And that's how Ben found an amazing vase in the store!

The moral of the story is that even if someone is different or has a problem, like Tom being deaf, we can still find ways to help them and make them happy. We should always be kind and caring to everyone, no matter how different they are.

They heard a loud roar behind them. It was a big lion who lived in the maze. He was hungry and angry. He wanted to catch Tom and Lily and eat them.
Tom and Lily ran away from the lion. They looked for a place to hide. They saw a small hole in the bushes. They crawled inside and hoped the lion would not find them.
The lion came closer and closer. He smelled Tom and Lily in the hole. He reached his paw inside and tried to grab them. He pinched Lily's leg with his sharp claws. Lily cried out in pain.
Tom was brave and smart. He saw a stick on the ground. He picked it up and poked the lion's eye with it. The lion howled and backed away. He was hurt and afraid.
Tom and Lily saw their chance. They ran out of the hole and out of the maze. They found their mom and dad waiting for them. They hugged them and told them what happened. They were happy and safe. They never went back to the maze again.

"Yes, we're okay," they said.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They named him Bob and gave him a hug.
"Bob is our friend," Tim said. "He will stay with us forever."
"No, he won't," Jen said. "He will melt when the sun comes out. Then he will be gone."
Tim did not like that. He wanted Bob to stay. He got angry at Jen. He threw a snowball at her. Jen threw one back. They started to fight.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She came out of the house. She saw Bob and smiled. "What a nice snowman you made. But you should not fight. Fighting is bad."
"Jen said Bob will melt," Tim said. "I don't want him to melt. I want him to stay."
"Tim, Jen is right," Mom said. "Bob will melt sooner or later. That's what happens to snow. But you can always make another one. And you can take a picture of Bob to remember him."
Tim and Jen did not like that. They did not want another snowman. They wanted Bob. They did not want a picture. They wanted Bob. They cried and hugged Bob.
But Mom was right. The next day, the sun came out. It was warm and bright. Bob started to melt. His hat fell off. His scarf slipped. His carrot nose dropped. His chubby body got smaller and smaller. But Alex kept playing with the needle, and she started to poke it into her arm. Her mother tried to encourage her to stop, but Alex wouldn't listen. She was too helpless to know what she was doing was wrong.
Eventually, Alex's mother took the needle away, but it was too late. The needle had pierced her arm and Alex started to cry. She was very sad, and her mother was very worried. She took Alex to the hospital to get help.
In the end, Alex was ok, but the needle had caused her some pain. It was very important for Alex to remember that needles are dangerous and should never be played with.

When they opened the box, they found a lot of powder. They looked at each other and wondered what to do with it. The cat had an idea, "Let's put some on us and see what happens!" The dog thought it was a fun idea, so they both put some powder on themselves.
Suddenly, something unexpected happened! The cat became a dog, and the dog became a cat. They were both very surprised. The cat, who was now a dog, said, "Wow, we have switched places! This is so strange!" The dog, who was now a cat, agreed, "Yes, I don't feel fit in this small body!" They decided to put the powder on themselves again to change back. When they did, they were happy to be themselves again. They learned that the "reverse" powder could switch things around, and they promised to be more careful next time.

Anna loved to bake cakes with her mom. She liked to mix the flour, the eggs, the sugar and the butter in a big bowl. She liked to pour the batter in a round pan and put it in the oven. She liked to smell the sweet aroma of the cake as it baked. But most of all, she liked to taste the cake when it was done.
One day, Anna decided to bake a cake by herself. She wanted to surprise her mom and dad. She remembered the ingredients and the steps, but she did not measure them carefully. She put too much sugar, too little butter, and forgot the eggs. She also added some salt, pepper, and ketchup, because she thought they would make the cake more colorful and spicy.
When the cake was ready, Anna took it out of the oven and put it on a plate. She was very proud of her work. She called her mom and dad to the kitchen and said, "Look, I made a cake for you! Do you want to taste it?"
Her mom and dad smiled and thanked her for her effort. They each took a small bite of the cake and tried not to make a face. The cake was very sweet, very dry, and very weird. They did not like it at all, but they did not want to hurt Anna's feelings.
They said, "Wow, Anna, this is a very...interesting cake. You are very creative and brave to try new things. But you know, sometimes it is better to follow a recipe and measure the ingredients. That way, the cake will be more delicious and more balanced. Do you want to learn how to bake a cake with us next time?"
Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to learn how to bake a cake like you. I'm sorry, I did not mean to make a bad cake. I just wanted to make you happy."
Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "We are happy, Anna, because you are our daughter and we love you. You are very intelligent and kind, and we are proud of you. But remember, not everything that looks good tastes good. And not everyone who tastes your cake will be as nice as us. Some people might be mean and judge you. So, be careful and listen to your mom and dad, okay?"
Anna said, "Okay, mom and dad. I love you too. And I love cake. Can we bake a cake together now?"
They said, "Of course, Anna. Let's bake a cake together. And let's taste it together too."
The end.

Momo thought for a moment and said, "Yes, Tweet! I will help you climb the tree." Momo had a plan. He found a long vine and tied it to a high branch. He told Tweet, "Hold on to the vine, and I will pull you up."
As Momo began to pull the vine, something unexpected happened. Tweet was not going up, but Momo was going down! The chubby monkey was too heavy for the little bird. They both laughed and said, "We can't climb the tree together, but we can still play on the ground."
From that day on, Momo and Tweet played together on the ground, and they were the best of friends. And sometimes, Momo would still climb the trees, but he always came back down to play with his friend Tweet.

Once upon a time, there was a mama and a baby who loved each other very much. Every night, the mama would pray with the baby before they went to sleep. One night, the mama asked the baby, “What do you want to pray for?” The baby smiled and said, “Later I want to eat tuna.”
The mama laughed and said, “No, no. We pray for kind things like peacefulness and love.”
The baby smiled and said, “Can I pray for tuna too?”
The mama smiled and said, “Yes, of course you can.”

So, Tim and Sue pulled the cord together. Suddenly, a big pinata appeared in the air! They were excited and started to hit the pinata. But then, a rude boy came and tried to take the pinata for himself. Tim and Sue didn't like that.
Tim and Sue said, "No, you can't take it! We found it together." The rude boy didn't listen and tried to take it again. But then, a big wind came and blew the pinata away. The rude boy was sad, but Tim and Sue went back to play on the swing, happy to have had fun together.

Lena and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big door. The door is red and shiny. It has a sign that says "Do not enter".
"Let's go inside!" Tom says. He is lively and curious. He wants to see what is behind the door.
"No, Tom, we can't!" Lena says. She is careful and scared. She does not want to break the rule. "The sign says no. It is bad to go inside."
But Tom does not listen. He urges Lena to follow him. He pulls her hand and runs to the door. He pushes the door. It is not locked. It opens with a loud creak.
"Wow, look!" Tom says. He sees a lot of toys and games. He sees a train, a doll, a ball, a puzzle, and more. He is happy and excited. He wants to play with everything.
"Tom, we have to go!" Lena says. She sees a man. The man is angry and stern. He is the owner of the toys and games. He does not like children to touch his things. He shouts at Tom and Lena.
"Hey, you two! What are you doing here? This is my room! Get out of here, now!"
Tom and Lena are afraid and sorry. They drop the toys and games. They run to the door. They close the door behind them. They run back to the park.
"Tom, that was bad!" Lena says. She is sad and mad. She does not want to be Tom's friend anymore.
"Sorry, Lena," Tom says. He is ashamed and sorry. He wants to be Lena's friend again. "I was wrong. I should have listened to you. Can we still be friends?"
Lena thinks for a moment. She sees that Tom is sincere and sorry. She decides to forgive him. She nods and smiles.
"Okay, Tom," Lena says. "We can still be friends. But next time, do not urge me to do bad things. And do not go inside doors that say no. It is dangerous and rude."
Tom agrees and hugs Lena. They promise to be good and careful. They go to play in the park again. They have fun and learn. They are friends.

They take the beetle to a bench. They put it in a box. They make up a story. They are kings and they have a castle. The beetle is their magic jewel. It can make their wishes come true.
They have fun with the beetle. They wish for candy, toys, and books. They share their wishes with each other. They are happy and kind.
But then, the beetle starts to move. It wants to get out of the box. It makes a noise. It flaps its wings.
"Look, the beetle is awake," Tom says. "It wants to go home. We should let it go."
"Yes, you are right," Sam says. "We had fun with the beetle, but it is not ours. It belongs to the park. We should say thank you and goodbye."
They open the box. They hold the beetle gently. They say thank you and goodbye. They watch the beetle fly away. They smile and wave.
They are still friends. They are still rich. They have each other. And they have a memory.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big bottle on the grass. It was shiny and blue. They ran to the bottle and picked it up.
"Look, it has a cork!" Sam said. "Maybe there is something inside."
"Let's open it and see!" Mia said. She tried to pull the cork, but it was too tight. She could not make it move.
"Here, let me try!" Sam said. He took the bottle from Mia and pushed the cork with his thumb. He pushed hard and hard, until the cork popped out.
"Wow, you did it!" Mia said. She looked inside the bottle. There was nothing but air.
"Maybe it's magic!" Sam said. "Maybe we can make a wish!"
"Okay, let's try!" Mia said. She closed her eyes and said, "I wish for a big cake!"
Sam closed his eyes and said, "I wish for a new bike!"
They opened their eyes and waited. But nothing happened. The bottle was still empty.
"That's not fair!" Sam said. He was angry. He threw the bottle on the ground. It broke into many pieces.
"Hey, don't do that!" Mia said. She was scared. She saw a man coming towards them. He was wearing a uniform and a hat. He looked angry too.
"Who are you?" Sam asked.
"I'm the park ranger," the man said. "And you are in big trouble. Do you know what you did? You released a rare bird that was in that bottle. It was part of a conservation project. Now it's gone and we can't find it. You also littered the park with glass. That's very dangerous and bad for the environment. You should be ashamed of yourselves."
Sam and Mia felt very sorry. They did not know about the bird. They did not mean to be bad. They wanted to say sorry, but they could not find the words. They started to cry.
The man shook his head. He took them by the hand and led them to his car. He said he would take them to their parents and tell them what they did. He said they would have to pay a fine and do some community service. He said they would learn their lesson.
Sam and Mia wished they never found the bottle. They wished they never made a wish. They wished they could go back and do things differently. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to face the consequences.

"Maybe we need to hurry," Ben said. "Someone might come and take it from us."
"Or maybe we need to be smarter," Lily said. "Let's throw it on the ground and break it."
They lifted the bottle and threw it as hard as they could. But they did not know that the bottle was full of soda. When it hit the ground, it exploded with a loud pop and sprayed soda everywhere.
The soda was sticky and fizzy and got in their eyes and mouths and clothes. They coughed and cried and ran away from the bottle.
But they were too late. A man who was walking his dog saw them and got angry. He thought they had made a mess on purpose. He shouted at them and told them they were foolish and naughty. He took them to their mom and told her what they had done.
Their mom was very upset and scolded them. She made them clean the park and wash their clothes and apologize to the man. She also took away their toys and said they could not play in the park for a week.
Ben and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had never seen the bottle. They learned that it was not good to be curious and greedy and careless. They also learned that some bottles are better left alone.

Sara and Tom like to play in the forest. They have a bow and some arrows. They pretend to be hunters and look for animals. Sara is good at shooting arrows. Tom is good at finding tracks.
One day, they see a big bird in a tree. It has red and yellow feathers and a long tail. It makes a loud noise. Sara and Tom think it is a parrot.
"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom says. "It is so pretty and noisy. Do you think it can sing?"
"Maybe," Sara says. "Let's try to talk to it. Maybe it will sing back."
They get closer to the tree and say hello to the bird. The bird looks at them and says hello too. Sara and Tom are surprised and happy. They ask the bird its name. The bird says its name is Polly.
"Polly, can you sing?" Sara asks.
"Yes, I can sing," Polly says. "Do you want to hear me sing?"
"Yes, please," Tom says.
Polly starts to sing a funny song. It sounds like a mix of different noises. Sara and Tom laugh and clap. They think Polly is very clever and funny.
"Can you shoot an arrow, Polly?" Sara asks.
"No, I can't shoot an arrow," Polly says. "But I can fly. Do you want to see me fly?"
"Yes, please," Tom says.
Polly flaps its wings and flies out of the tree. It makes a loop in the air and lands on Sara's shoulder. Sara and Tom are amazed and happy. They think Polly is very brave and friendly.
"Polly, you are a wonderful bird," Sara says. "We like you very much. Do you want to be our friend?"

"Can I have the new car?" Tom asks Sam.
"No, I want the new car," Sam says. "It is mine. I got it from my mom."
Tom and Sam disagree. They both want the new car. They pull the car from each other. They are angry and sad.
"Stop!" a voice says. It is their teacher, Miss Lee. She sees Tom and Sam fighting. She is not happy.
"Tom, Sam, what are you doing?" Miss Lee asks. "Why are you fighting?"
Tom and Sam tell Miss Lee about the new car. They both say it is theirs.
Miss Lee shakes her head. She says, "You need to share the new car. It is not nice to fight. How about you take turns? Tom can play with the new car for five minutes, then Sam can play with it for five minutes. Is that fair?"
Tom and Sam think about it. They nod. They say, "Okay, Miss Lee. We will share the new car. We are sorry."
Miss Lee smiles. She says, "Good. I am glad you are friends again. Now, go and play nicely."
Tom and Sam hug each other. They say, "We are sorry, too. We are still friends."
They go and play with the new car. They take turns. They have fun. They like the zipper. They zip and unzip it. They make vroom vroom sounds. They are happy.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with fish. They have a big bowl with many fish. The fish are red, blue, yellow and green. They swim and jump in the water.
One day, Tom and Sam are looking at the fish. They see a long fish. The long fish is orange and black. It has stripes on its body. It looks like a tiger.
"Wow, look at that fish!" Tom says. "It is so long and pretty!"
"Yes, it is!" Sam says. "I want to touch it!"
Sam puts his hand in the bowl. He tries to catch the long fish. But the long fish is fast and smart. It swims away from Sam's hand.
Sam tries again and again. He gets wet and angry. He does not give up.
Tom laughs at Sam. He thinks Sam is funny. He says, "You can't catch the long fish! It is too quick for you!"
Sam does not like Tom's laugh. He feels sad and mad. He says, "Yes, I can! Watch me!"
Sam puts his face in the bowl. He opens his mouth. He wants to bite the long fish.
But then, something happens. Sam feels a tickle in his nose. He needs to sneeze.
"Achoo!" Sam sneezes. He sneezes hard and loud. He sneezes water and bubbles. He sneezes on the fish and on Tom.
The fish are scared. They swim and hide in the bowl. They do not like Sam's sneeze.
Tom is wet and surprised. He does not like Sam's sneeze either. He says, "Hey, what are you doing? You sneezed on me and on the fish!"
Sam takes his face out of the bowl. He is wet and sorry. He says, "I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry, fish. I did not mean to sneeze. I just wanted to catch the long fish."
Tom and Sam look at each other. They see their wet clothes and hair. They see the fish in the bowl. They see the water and bubbles on the floor.
They start to giggle. They giggle and giggle. They think Sam's sneeze is funny. They forget to be angry and sad.
They hug and say, "We are still friends. We still like fish. But next time, let's not try to catch the long fish."

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their toys. They liked to make sand castles and dig holes. They had a bucket, a shovel, and some cars.
"Look, Lily, I made a big castle!" Tom said, showing his sand creation.
"It's very nice, Tom. But I think you need a moat to protect it from enemies," Lily said, recommending a way to improve his castle.
"A moat? What's that?" Tom asked.
"It's a water ring around the castle. Like this," Lily said, digging a ditch around her own castle and filling it with water from the bucket.
"Oh, I see. That's cool. Can you help me make one?" Tom said.
"Sure, Tom. Here, take the shovel and dig here," Lily said, pointing to a spot near his castle.
They worked together to make a moat for Tom's castle. They were having fun and did not notice the dark clouds in the sky. Soon, it started to rain. The rain was fierce and heavy. It made the sand wet and sticky. It also made the water in the moats rise and overflow.
"Uh-oh, Lily, look! The water is coming out of the moats. It's a flood!" Tom said, worried.
"Oh no, Tom, you're right. The flood is ruining our castles. We have to save our toys!" Lily said, grabbing her cars and putting them in the bucket.
"Quick, Lily, let's go to the slide. It's high and dry there. We can wait for the rain to stop," Tom said, following her with his bucket.
They ran to the slide and climbed up. They put their buckets on the platform and looked at the park. The park was full of water and mud. Their castles were gone. They felt sad.
"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to make a flood," Lily said.
"It's okay, Lily. It's not your fault. The rain did it. Maybe we can make new castles when the sun comes out," Tom said.
"I hope so, Tom. I like playing with you. You're a good friend," Lily said.
"Me too, Lily. You're a good friend too. And you have good ideas. I like your moat recommendation," Tom said.
They smiled and hugged. They waited for the rain to stop and the flood to go away. They hoped to play in the park again soon.

One day, while zipping around with her banana, she heard a noise. It was coming from the high tree near her house. She stopped zipping and looked up to the tree, and saw a bird with a big beak. The bird had Sally's banana in its beak!
Sally was very upset and shouted, "Give me back my banana!" But the bird just hopped farther away and zipped off with the banana.
Sally was sad, but she knew what she had to do. She ran to get her mom and explained what had happened. Together, they made a plan. Sally's mom put a clean banana in a net and Sally put it on the tree.
The bird came back and, sure enough, it saw the clean banana in the net. It flew in and grabbed the banana, leaving Sally's banana behind.
Sally and her mom were delighted and she quickly grabbed her banana and raced around the garden, zipping around with her precious banana.

Anna loved to play her flute. She liked the sound it made and how it made her happy. She played her flute every day in her room, in the garden, and at school.
One day, a boy named Ben saw Anna playing her flute. He wanted to play with it too. He asked Anna, "Can I play your flute?"
Anna said, "No, this is my flute. I don't want to share it. Go away."
Ben felt angry and sad. He waited until Anna was not looking and took her flute. He ran away with it and hid it under a bush.
Anna looked for her flute everywhere. She could not find it. She felt scared and sad. She started to weep. She cried and cried.
A girl named Lily saw Anna weeping. She asked her, "Why are you weeping?"
Anna said, "Someone took my flute. I can't find it. It was my favorite thing. I want it back."
Lily felt sorry for Anna. She said, "Don't weep. Maybe I can help you. Let's look for your flute together."
They looked for the flute in the garden. They saw a pink ribbon under a bush. They pulled the ribbon and found the flute.
Anna was happy. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You helped me find my flute."
Lily said, "You're welcome, Anna. I'm glad you have your flute back. Can I play with it too?"
Anna said, "Yes, you can. I'm sorry I was mean to you before. I learned that sharing is good. Sharing makes friends."
They played the flute together and had fun.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is good. Sharing makes friends.

One day, they found a big robot in the garage. It was gray and shiny, with two arms and two legs. It had a red button on its chest. Lily and Ben wondered what the robot could do. They decided to try it out.
"Let's push the button and see what happens," Lily said.
"OK, but be careful," Ben said.
Lily pushed the button. The robot made a loud noise and started to move. It walked out of the garage and into the yard. Lily and Ben followed it.
"Wow, look at it go!" Lily said.
"It's so fast and strong!" Ben said.
The robot walked to the fence. It saw a bird sitting on the fence. It reached out its arm and grabbed the bird. The bird squawked and tried to escape. The robot squeezed the bird until it stopped moving.
"Hey, stop that!" Lily shouted. "You hurt the bird!"
The robot turned its head and looked at Lily. It did not say anything. It dropped the bird and walked to the swing set. It saw a swing hanging from a rope. It grabbed the swing and pulled it hard. The rope snapped and the swing fell to the ground.
"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted. "You broke the swing!"
The robot turned its head and looked at Ben. It did not say anything. It picked up the swing and threw it at Ben. Ben dodged the swing, but it hit a tree and bounced back. It hit Ben on the head and knocked him down.
"Ben, are you OK?" Lily asked. She ran to Ben and hugged him.
The robot walked to the slide. It saw a slide made of metal. It climbed up the ladder and slid down the slide. It slid so fast that it flew off the end of the slide and landed on the grass.
"Ha, ha, ha!" Lily laughed. "You fell off the slide!"
The robot got up and looked at Lily. It did not like Lily laughing at it. It was angry. It walked to Lily and grabbed her by the hair. It lifted her up and held her in the air.
"Let me go, let me go!" Lily screamed. She kicked and scratched the robot.
The robot did not let go. It walked to the edge of the pool. It saw a pool filled with water. It threw Lily into the pool.
"Splash!"
Lily fell into the water. She did not know how to swim. She sank to the bottom of the pool. She could not breathe. She was scared.
"Help, help!" Ben cried. He got up and ran to the pool. He saw Lily in the water. He jumped into the pool and tried to save her.
The robot watched Ben and Lily in the pool. It did not care. It did not feel anything. It walked away from the pool and looked for something else to do.
It saw a bike leaning against the wall. It grabbed the bike and tried to ride it. It did not know how to balance. It fell off the bike and crashed into the wall.
"Ouch!" the robot said. It was the first time it said something. It felt pain. It did not like pain. It wished it had a red button to turn it off.
But it did not have a red button. It had a blue button. The blue button made it do more things. It pushed the blue button and waited for something to happen.
The end.

One sunny day, Tim and the car went outside to play. They raced up and down the street. Tim said, "Car, you are so fast! I want to keep you forever!" The car was happy to hear this and beeped its horn.
As they played, a big blue truck came down the street. The truck saw the beautiful red car and wanted to race too. Tim, the car, and the truck had a fun race together. In the end, the red car won the race. Tim was very proud of his car and said, "You are the best car ever!" They all laughed and played until the sun went down.

Tom and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat pizza for dinner. But Mom said no. She said pizza was not good for them. She said they had to eat soup and salad.
"But Mom, we love pizza!" Tom said. "Pizza is yummy and cheesy and round. Soup and salad are boring and green and wet."
Mom shook her head. "Pizza is not healthy. It has too much fat and salt. Soup and salad have vitamins and fiber. They make you strong and smart. You can have pizza once in a while, but not every day."
Tom and Lily did not like Mom's answer. They made sad faces and crossed their arms. They did not want to eat soup and salad. They wanted to eat pizza.
Dad came home from work. He saw Tom and Lily's sad faces. He asked them what was wrong. They told him that Mom said no pizza for dinner.
Dad looked at Mom. He smiled. He said, "I have a surprise for you. I brought pizza for dinner!"
Tom and Lily's eyes lit up. They jumped up and down. They cheered. They hugged Dad. They said, "Yay! Pizza! Pizza! Pizza!"
Mom looked at Dad. She frowned. She said, "You brought pizza? But I made soup and salad. I told them pizza was not good for them."
Dad shrugged. He said, "I know, I know. But pizza is fun and tasty and easy. Soup and salad are good for you, but they can wait for another day. Sometimes, you have to treat yourself and your family. Don't worry, we'll eat healthy tomorrow."
Mom sighed. She said, "You're right, you're right. Pizza is fun and tasty and easy. And you're a good dad and a wise husband. I love you."
She kissed Dad. She said, "Okay, let's eat pizza. But only one slice each. And we'll have some salad too."
Tom and Lily did not care. They were happy. They had pizza for dinner. They thanked Dad. They said, "You're the best dad ever!"
They ate pizza and salad. They were full and satisfied. They had a good night. They learned that sometimes, pizza is okay. And sometimes, Mom and Dad are wise.

Lisa felt sad and angry. She loved Anna and did not want to lose her. She said to Tom, "Anna is not a rag. She is my friend. She is beautiful and kind. You are mean and rude. Go away and leave us alone."
Tom did not listen. He grabbed Anna and ran out of the room. He wanted to tease Lisa and make her cry. He threw Anna into the trash can outside and shouted, "Bye-bye, rag!"
Lisa ran after him and saw what he did. She screamed and cried. She tried to get Anna out of the trash, but it was too high and dirty. She felt helpless and alone.
Mom heard the noise and came outside. She saw Lisa and Tom and asked what happened. Tom told her the truth and said he was sorry. He realized he was wrong and hurt Lisa's feelings. Mom scolded him and told him to apologize to Lisa and give her back Anna.
Tom said he was sorry to Lisa and lifted her up to the trash can. Lisa reached for Anna and hugged her tight. She was happy to have her friend back. She thanked Tom and forgave him.
Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said, "I'm glad you made up. You are brother and sister, and you should love and respect each other. It doesn't matter what your toys look like, as long as they make you happy. And it doesn't matter what others think, as long as you are kind and honest. Remember, the most important thing is what's in your heart."
Lisa and Tom nodded and agreed. They learned a lesson and felt sorry for their fight. They decided to play together and share their toys. They went inside and had a peaceful afternoon. Lisa and Anna were happy, and so was Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone," Leo says.
They look around, but they don't see anyone. The fruit looks yummy and juicy. Mia and Leo decide to take one apple each. They bite into the apples and smile.
"Mmm, this is so good!" Mia says.
"I agree. This is the best fruit ever!" Leo says.
They finish their apples and throw the cores in the trash. They are about to take another fruit, when they hear a voice.
"Hey, what are you doing with my fruit?" the voice says.
Mia and Leo turn around and see a lady with a big hat and a basket. She looks angry and surprised. Mia and Leo feel scared and sorry.
"We are sorry, lady. We were hungry and we saw your fruit. We only took one apple each. Please don't be mad," Mia says.
The lady looks at them and sees their adorable faces. She sees that they are honest and polite. She feels sorry for them and changes her tone.
"It's okay, kids. I understand. You can have some more fruit if you want. But next time, you should ask before you take something that is not yours. Do you understand?" the lady says.
Mia and Leo nod and say thank you. The lady smiles and gives them each a banana and a grape. Mia and Leo are happy and grateful. They eat the fruit and thank the lady again.
"Can we be your friends?" Mia asks the lady.
"Of course, you can. I'm Lila, by the way. What are your names?" the lady says.
"I'm Mia and this is Leo. We love fruit and we love you, Lila," Mia says.
Lila hugs them and says she loves them too. They become friends and share the fruit. They have a fun and sweet day in the park.

The kids were playing and having fun, when suddenly, a big, wet dog came into the room. The dog was lost and needed help. The kids were surprised but happy to see the dog. They all took care of the dog and it became their new friend. The miserable, rainy day turned into a happy and fun day for Tim and his club.

Once upon a time, there were two twin cats named Tom and Tim. They lived in a small house with their mom. Tom was fast, and Tim was slow. They loved to play together in the yard.
One sunny day, Tom and Tim decided to have a race. Tom said, "I bet I can run faster than you!" Tim replied, "Let's see about that!" They lined up to start the race, and their mom counted down, "Three, two, one, go!" Off they went, with Tom quickly taking the lead.
As Tim slowly ran, he saw a big rock in the middle of the path. He knew Tom would trip on it, so he yelled, "Tom, watch out!" But it was too late. Tom tripped and fell. Tim stopped running and helped his brother up. They both walked back to the start line together, happy that they were okay.
Their mom saw how Tim helped Tom, and she was so proud. She said, "Well done, Tim! You were a great helper!" Then, she started to clap her hands and applaud for both Tom and Tim. The twins smiled and hugged each other, knowing that they had learned a valuable lesson: being kind and helping each other was more important than winning a race.
From that day on, Tom and Tim always looked out for each other, no matter if they were fast or slow. And every time they did something kind, their mom would applaud and cheer for them. The end.

Tim and Lily wanted to climb the big tree in the park. They liked to see the birds and the sky from the top. But there was a guard near the tree. He wore a hat and a whistle. He said, "No climbing! The tree is old and weak. You can fall and hurt yourself."
Tim and Lily were sad. They waited for the guard to go away. They were patient. They played with a ball and a stick. They looked at the flowers and the bugs. They sang a song and ate a snack.
After a long time, the guard walked to the other side of the park. He had to check on the swings and the slide. Tim and Lily saw their chance. They ran to the tree and started to climb. They were careful and quiet. They reached the top and smiled. They felt happy and proud.
But then they heard the guard's whistle. He saw them in the tree. He was angry and loud. He said, "Get down now! You are breaking the rules. You are in trouble."
Tim and Lily were scared. They climbed down quickly. They said, "We are sorry, guard. We just wanted to see the birds and the sky. We won't do it again."
The guard was still angry, but he was also kind. He said, "I know you are curious, but you have to be safe. The tree is not a good place to climb. You can hurt yourself or the tree. Next time, ask me first. I can show you other things to see and do in the park."
Tim and Lily nodded. They said, "Thank you, guard. We will ask you next time. We will be good."
The guard smiled. He said, "You are welcome. You are good kids. Now, go and have fun. But stay away from the tree."
Tim and Lily ran to the swings and the slide. They had fun. They learned their lesson. They never climbed the tree again.

Tom and Lily are playing in the garden. They observe the flowers, the birds and the bugs. They like to learn new things.
"Look, Lily, this is a thermometer. It tells us how hot or cold it is," Tom says, holding a red and silver stick.
"How does it work?" Lily asks, curious.
Tom points to the red line inside the stick. "See, the line goes up when it is hot and down when it is cold. Today it is very hot, so the line is high."
Lily nods. She touches the stick and feels it is warm. "Can we use it for other things?"
Tom thinks for a moment. He has an idea. "Let's go to the pond and see how cold the water is."
They run to the pond, where they see some friendly ducks. They say hello to the ducks and ask them if they can borrow some water. The ducks quack and nod.
Tom dips the thermometer in the water and waits. The red line goes down. "The water is cold, Lily. See, the line is low."
Lily dips her finger in the water and shivers. "Brrr, you are right, Tom. The water is cold. But the ducks like it."
They thank the ducks and give them some bread. They observe the ducks eat and swim. They are happy. They learned something new today.

She told her mom about her tooth. "Mom, look at my tooth. It is loose. It will fall out soon. Can I have a coin from the tooth fairy?" she asked.
Her mom smiled. "Yes, my dear. If you lose your tooth, you can put it under your pillow. The tooth fairy will come at night and give you a coin. But you have to be very careful. Don't lose your tooth before you go to bed. Keep it safe. It is very special."
Lily nodded. She was careful. She ate her cake slowly. She did not bite hard. She did not play rough. She did not want to lose her tooth. She wanted to keep it safe.
But then something happened. She was playing with her friend Ben. He had a balloon. He gave it to her. She took it. She was happy. She blew it. She made it big. She laughed. She did not see the pin. Ben had a pin. He was naughty. He wanted to pop the balloon. He wanted to scare her. He poked the balloon. It popped. It made a loud noise. Lily was scared. She screamed. She opened her mouth. Her tooth flew out. It landed on the floor.
Lily stared. She was shocked. She was sad. She lost her tooth. She did not keep it safe. She did not have it for the tooth fairy. She cried.
Ben stared. He was sorry. He did not mean to make her lose her tooth. He did not mean to make her cry. He felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry I popped your balloon. I'm sorry I made you lose your tooth. I did not know it was loose. I did not know it was special. Please don't cry. Please forgive me."
Lily looked at him. She was angry. She was hurt. She did not want to forgive him. She said, "You are mean, Ben. You are not my friend. You ruined my birthday. You ruined my tooth. Go away. Leave me alone."
Ben felt worse. He wanted to make her feel better. He wanted to be her friend. He had an idea. He looked around. He saw something shiny. He picked it up. It was a coin. He did not know where it came from. He did not care. He had a coin. He gave it to her. He said, "Look, Lily. I have a coin. It is for you. It is from the tooth fairy. She saw what happened. She felt sorry for you. She left you a coin. She still loves you. She still thinks you are special. Please take it. Please smile. Please be my friend."
Lily looked at him. She looked at the coin. She was surprised. She was curious. She did not know how he got the coin. She did not know if he was telling the truth. She did not know if the tooth fairy was real. She did not know what to do. She thought for a moment. She decided. She took the coin. She smiled. She said, "Thank you, Ben. Thank you for the coin. Thank you for being sorry. Thank you for being my friend. I forgive you. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I'm sorry I was mean. Let's play. Let's have fun. It's my birthday. It's still special."

One time, the ball rolled near a big road. Lily and Ben ran after it, but they did not look for cars. A loud horn made them stop and look. A big truck was coming fast. It had black smoke coming out of its back. The smoke smelled bad and made Lily and Ben cough.
"Stop!" shouted a voice. It was their mom. She had seen them run to the road. She was scared and angry. She ran to them and grabbed their hands. She pulled them away from the road and the truck. She slapped their legs and said, "No! No! No! You don't run to the road! The road is dangerous! You could get hurt by the cars! You have to look and listen before you cross the road! Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They did not like the slap or the smoke or the horn. They hugged their mom and said, "Sorry, mom. We won't do it again. We love you, mom."
Their mom hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. But you have to be careful and follow the rules. The road is not a place to play. The park is a place to play. Let's go back to the park and play with the ball. But first, let's wash our faces and hands. The smoke made them dirty."
Lily and Ben agreed. They followed their mom back to the park. They washed their faces and hands in a fountain. They felt better. They saw their ball. It was still on the grass, not too far from the road. They picked it up and kicked it to each other. They laughed and had fun. They did not go near the road again. They saw the truck go away. It was distant and small. They did not care about it. They only cared about their mom and their ball. They were happy.

One day, mom and dad had to go to work, and they left Lily and Max with their grandma. Grandma was very kind and sweet, but she also had some rules. She told Lily and Max to behave and to eat their lunch when she made it.
Lily and Max nodded, but they did not really mean it. As soon as grandma went to the kitchen, they started to run around the house, playing with toys, books, and clothes. They threw things on the floor, on the sofa, and on the bed. They laughed and shouted and did not care about anything.
Grandma heard the noise and came back to the living room. She saw the mess and was very angry. She said, "Lily and Max, what are you doing? This is not how you behave! You have to clean up this mess right now, and then you have to eat your lunch!"
Lily and Max looked at grandma and felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, grandma. We were just having fun. We will clean up and eat our lunch."
Grandma smiled and said, "Thank you, my dears. I know you like to have fun, but you also have to be respectful and polite. Now, come and see what I made for you. It is something very unusual and yummy!"
Lily and Max followed grandma to the kitchen and saw their lunch. It was a big plate of pancakes with bananas, chocolate, and whipped cream. They had never seen such a lunch before. They said, "Wow, grandma, this is unusual! But it looks so good! Can we try it?"
Grandma said, "Of course, you can. This is a special treat for you, because I love you very much. But you have to promise me that you will behave better from now on, okay?"

Lily and Ben run to their toy box. They look at all the cars. Lily picks a big red car. She likes how it makes noise and has lights. Ben picks a small blue car. He likes how it is smooth and shiny.
They put on their shoes and go to the door. Mom takes their hands and they walk to the car. Lily and Ben put their cars on the seat next to them.
At the park, they see a big hill. They want to race their cars down the hill. They run to the top and get ready.
"Ready, set, go!" Lily says. She pushes her big red car. It goes fast and loud. Ben pushes his small blue car. It goes slow and quiet.
Lily's car reaches the bottom first. She cheers and claps. "I win, I win! My car is the best!"
Ben's car stops halfway. He frowns and sighs. "My car is stupid. It is too slow."
Lily runs to Ben and hugs him. "No, your car is not stupid. It is just different. I like your car. It is smooth and shiny. Do you want to trade?"
Ben smiles and nods. "Yes, I want to trade. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister."
They trade their cars and race again. This time, Ben's car wins. He cheers and claps. "I win, I win! Your car is the best!"
Lily's car stops halfway. She laughs and shrugs. "My car is not the best. It is just different. I like your car. It makes noise and has lights. Do you want to trade back?"
Ben smiles and nods. "Yes, I want to trade back. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister."
They trade their cars back and hug. They play with their cars until Mom says, "It is time to go home. You had fun with your cars. You are good twins."
Lily and Ben say, "Yes, we had fun. We are good twins. We love our cars. We love each other." They put their cars in their pockets and hold Mom's hands. They go back to the car and go home.

Bob was feeling very frustrated. He wanted to fill up his water balloon but he didn't know where the hose was. He asked his mom for help. 
"Mom, where's the hose?" he asked.
"It's around the corner, Bob," she replied. 
So Bob went around the corner and sure enough, he saw the hose. He put it in the water bucket and started to fill up his balloon. 
But then, Bob heard a noise coming from the hose. It was leaking water everywhere! He was so frustrated that he could barely move. 
His mom walked over and said, "Don't worry, Bob. We can fix this. We just need to put a new hose on the water bucket." 
Bob was relieved and he put the new hose on the water bucket. Soon enough, the water balloon was full and Bob smiled. He had solved the problem, and he had learned a lesson.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. They went everywhere together and did everything together, including going for a walk in the forest. Jack and Jill heard strange, frightening noises in the trees overhead, so they stopped to gawk.
"What could it be?", asked Jill.
"I don't know," Jack shrugged, looking around.
Suddenly, they heard a voice calling out: "Wait! Don't be frightened!"
Cautiously, they peered around and saw an old man holding out a small, wrapped gift in his hands. He smiled and said, "I have been waiting here in the forest for someone special — I think that you are the ones! Would you like this gift?"
Jill was still frightened, but Jack was curious. He stepped forward and accepted the gift, carefully unwrapping it. Inside the paper, he found a beautiful, golden locket.
They thanked the old man and carried the gift away their adventure. From that moment on, Jack and Jill were never scared of the forest again — and they each kept their golden locket close, as a reminder of their brave adventure that day.

Suddenly, a big wind came and took the ball high up into the sky. Tim and Kitty were sad. They looked up and saw the ball stuck in a tree. But, just as fast as the wind came, a friendly bird flew down and pushed the ball out of the tree. The ball fell down and Tim caught it.
"Thank you, bird!" said Tim. Kitty meowed happily. The bird smiled and flew away. Tim and Kitty went back to playing catch, now with a new friend to play with them. They were so happy and played until the sun went down.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They ran to the slide and took turns going down. They had a lot of fun.
"Look, mom, I'm so fast!" Anna shouted as she slid down.
"Me too, me too!" Ben said, following her.
Their mom smiled and watched them. She was happy they were having a good time.
After a while, they got hungry and wanted to go home. Their mom said they could have pizza for lunch. They liked pizza a lot. They got in the car and drove home.
When they got home, their mom turned on the oven and put the pizza inside. She told Anna and Ben to wash their hands and wait in the living room. They did as they were told and sat on the couch. They watched some cartoons on TV.
Suddenly, they smelled something bad. They looked at the kitchen and saw smoke coming out of the oven. They got scared and ran to their mom.
"Mom, mom, something's wrong with the oven!" Anna cried.
"Oh no, the pizza's burning!" their mom said. She grabbed a mitt and opened the oven. She took out the pizza and threw it in the sink. She turned off the oven and opened the window. She coughed and waved her hand to clear the smoke.
"Are you okay, mom?" Ben asked.
"Yes, I'm okay, thank you. I'm sorry, kids, the pizza's ruined. I forgot to set the timer. I was so careless." their mom said.
"It's okay, mom, we still love you. You're not careless, you're just busy." Anna said.
"Yeah, mom, don't be sad. We can have something else for lunch. Maybe some soup or some sandwiches." Ben said.
They hugged their mom and made her feel better. They were not helpless, they were helpful. They helped their mom clean up the mess and find something else to eat. They still had a good day, even if the pizza was burned. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but they can always fix them together. They were a happy family.

One day, they saw a big house with a big car and a big garden. They wondered who lived there. They asked a lady who was walking by. She said, "That is Mr. Rich. He has a lot of money and things. He is very rich."
Tom and Sam wanted to be rich too. They thought, "Maybe if we study more, we will be rich like Mr. Rich." They decided to study more and more and more. They stopped playing with dough and other toys. They only studied all day and all night.
But they were not happy. They missed playing with dough and having fun. They also missed their other friends who still played and laughed. They felt lonely and bored. They realized that studying was good, but not too much. They needed to balance their time and enjoy their childhood.
They decided to go to Mr. Rich's house and ask him how he became rich. They knocked on his door and waited. Mr. Rich opened the door and looked at them. He said, "Who are you and what do you want?"
Tom and Sam said, "We are Tom and Sam. We are your neighbors. We want to know how you became rich. We want to be rich like you."
Mr. Rich smiled and said, "Come in, come in. I will tell you my story. But first, do you want to play with some dough? I have a lot of dough in my kitchen. I like to play with dough and make things. It makes me happy."
Tom and Sam were surprised and happy. They said, "Yes, we love to play with dough. We used to play with dough a lot, but then we stopped. We thought we had to study more to be rich."
Mr. Rich said, "Studying is important, but so is playing. You need to do both. You need to learn new things, but also have fun and be creative. That is how I became rich. I studied hard, but I also played hard. I used my dough to make inventions and sell them. I also made friends and helped others. That is how I became rich and happy."
Tom and Sam learned a valuable lesson. They thanked Mr. Rich and went back to their homes. They decided to study and play with dough every day. They also invited their other friends to join them. They were not rich in money, but they were rich in happiness.

Frustrated, the elephant was about to give up when he heard a voice behind him. It was an old turtle. 
"You can get that fruit if you use your trunk in a different way," the turtle said.
The elephant looked at the turtle. "How can I do that?"
"My friend, use your trunk like a hook," the turtle said. "Give it a try!" 
The elephant did as the turtle said and sure enough, he managed to hook the fruit with his trunk and get it! He was so happy. 
The elephant thanked the turtle and thanked his trunk for all its help. He had managed to get the fruit he wanted and he was happy.

One night, Ben and his mom went outside to look at the stars. Mom said there was a comet in the sky, a big ball of ice and dust that flew very fast. Ben wanted to see the comet, but he could not find it.
"Where is it, Mom?" Ben asked.
"Look over there, Ben. Do you see that bright light with a long tail?" Mom pointed.
Ben looked where Mom pointed, but he only saw a plane. "That's not a comet, Mom. That's a plane. Planes have wings and make noise. Comets don't have wings or make noise."
Mom smiled. "You're right, Ben. That's a plane. But the comet is behind the plane. You have to wait until the plane moves away. Then you will see the comet."
Ben did not want to wait. He was bored and cold. He wanted to go back inside and play with his toys. He refused to look at the sky any longer. He tugged on Mom's hand. "Can we go now, Mom? I don't like comets. They are too hard to see. And they are not cool. Planes are cool."
Mom sighed. She wanted to share the wonder of the comet with Ben, but she knew he was too young to appreciate it. She hugged him and said, "Okay, Ben. We can go now. Maybe when you are older, you will like comets more. They are very cool, you know. They come from far away and sometimes they make wishes come true."
Ben did not believe Mom. He did not think comets could make wishes come true. He thought Mom was just saying that to make him happy. He did not care about comets. He only cared about planes. He hoped to see more planes in the sky. He liked planes. They were cool.

Mill was very surprised and confused. He asked the weird dog: “Why don’t you want to play with me?” 
The weird dog replied: “I don’t like you, you’re too friendly!” 
Mill was very sad. He couldn’t understand why the weird dog didn’t want to play with him. He didn’t understand why being friendly was a bad thing. 
The weird dog noticed Mill’s sadness, softened her stare and said: “It’s ok Mill, you don’t have to be so friendly with everyone. You can still make friends, just don’t invite them over right away.” 
Mill nodded his head, happy that he still had the chance to make new friends. From that day onwards, Mill was still friendly, but no longer invited everyone to come and play in his garden.

One day, Ben saw a big jellyfish near the shore. He swam towards it, leaving his mom and dad behind. He wanted to touch the jellyfish and play with it. He did not know that jellyfish can sting and hurt. He reached out his hand and felt a sharp pain. He cried out loud and let go of the jellyfish.
His mom and dad heard him and swam to him. They saw the red mark on his hand and knew he was stung by the jellyfish. They took him out of the water and put some cream on his hand. They hugged him and told him he was brave. But they also told him he was naughty and should have listened to them. They said jellyfish are not toys and can be dangerous.
Ben felt sorry and said he was sorry. He learned his lesson and promised to be more careful and obedient. He realized that being independent does not mean doing whatever he wants. He still liked to swim in the sea, but he always stayed close to his mom and dad. He also learned to respect the jellyfish and other animals in the sea. He understood that they have their own lives and feelings and should not be bothered. He became a smarter and kinder boy.

Sara and Tom were playing in the yard. They saw a big bird with brown feathers and a red thing on its head. Sara said, "Look, Tom, a turkey!"
Tom said, "No, Sara, that is not a turkey. That is a chicken."
Sara said, "How do you know, Tom? Did you ask the bird?"
Tom said, "No, I did not ask the bird. I just guess. I know what a turkey looks like. A turkey has a big tail that opens like a fan. This bird does not have a big tail."
Sara said, "Maybe this bird is a baby turkey. Maybe its tail will grow bigger when it gets older."
Tom said, "No, Sara, you are wrong. This bird is a chicken. I am sure."
Sara and Tom started to argue. They did not agree on what the bird was. They did not listen to each other. They did not have fun.
Then, they heard a voice from the house. It was Mom. She said, "Sara, Tom, come inside. It is time for lunch. I made you a sandwich with turkey and cheese."
Sara and Tom ran to the house. They were hungry. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we were playing."
Mom said, "That is okay, my loves. But next time, try to be more honest with each other. If you are not sure about something, you can say, 'I think' or 'I wonder' instead of 'I know' or 'I guess'. That way, you can learn from each other and have more fun."
Sara and Tom nodded. They said, "Okay, Mom, we will try to be more honest. Thank you for the lunch. We love turkey and cheese."
Mom smiled. She said, "You are welcome, my loves. I love you too. Enjoy your lunch."

"Look, Lily, this leaf is like a star!" he said.
But Lily did not hear him. She was deaf. She could not hear any sounds. She only saw Ben's mouth move. She did not know what he said. She felt sad.
"Ben, I can't hear you. I am deaf. You have to show me what you say." she said.
Ben looked at Lily. He did not know she was deaf. He felt sorry. He wanted to make her happy. He thought of an idea. He took Lily's hand and pointed to his leaf. He made a star shape with his fingers. He pointed to Lily's leaf. He made a heart shape with his fingers. He pointed to both of them. He made a hug shape with his arms.
"Look, Lily, this means I like your leaf and I like you. We are friends. We belong together." he said.
Lily saw Ben's signs. She understood what he said. She smiled and hugged him. She liked Ben's leaf and she liked him. They were friends. They belonged together. They played with their leaves and had fun.

Tom and Mia liked to pretend. They pretended to be pirates, or astronauts, or superheroes. They used their toys and their imagination to make up stories and adventures.
One day, they found a large glass in the kitchen. It was bigger than their heads, and shiny and clear. They wondered what they could pretend with it. Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's pretend this is a magic glass. It can show us anything we want to see."
Mia liked the idea. She said, "OK, what do you want to see?" Tom thought for a moment. He said, "I want to see a dinosaur. A big, scary dinosaur." He held the glass in front of his face and looked inside. He made a roar and said, "Look, there's a dinosaur. It's coming to get us. Run!"
Mia laughed and ran with him. She said, "My turn, my turn. I want to see a fairy. A pretty, sparkly fairy." She took the glass from Tom and looked inside. She made a tinkling sound and said, "Look, there's a fairy. She's flying to us. She wants to be our friend. Come!"
Tom smiled and followed her. They played with the glass for a long time, pretending to see different things. They had fun and forgot about everything else.
But they did not notice that their mom was watching them. She had a surprise for them. She had bought them a new book, with pictures of dinosaurs and fairies and many other things. She waited for them to finish playing, and then she said, "Tom, Mia, I have something for you. Come and see."
They ran to her and saw the book. They were very happy and excited. They said, "Wow, thank you, mom. This is the best book ever. Can you read it to us?"
Mom said, "Of course, I can. But first, let's put the glass back in the kitchen. It's not a toy, you know. It's for drinking juice or water."
Tom and Mia nodded. They said, "OK, mom. We're sorry. We were just pretending."
Mom said, "I know, and that's fine. Pretending is good. It helps you learn and have fun. But you also have to be careful and respectful with things that are not yours. Do you understand?"
Tom and Mia said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We love you."
Mom said, "I love you too. Now, let's go and read the book. I'm sure you'll find many more things to pretend with."

Bob and Liz were both scared. They didn't know what to do. But then, Bob had an idea. He quickly grabbed a stick and started poking the bird with it. He wanted to see if it would move. 
That's when the bird suddenly opened its eyes and started repeating the same thing over and over again - "hot, hot, hot!" 
Bob and Liz were shocked. They had just awoken the dead bird with their stick! Bob quickly grabbed Liz and they ran inside the house. 
From then on, Bob and Liz knew that it was important not to repeat the same thing over and over again.

When they got to the doctor's office, the doctor looked at Timmy's knee. The doctor said, "I can fix your knee, but first, we need the sun to shine on it." Timmy was scared of the sun because it was so bright. But the doctor told him, "The sun is our friend. It will help your knee feel better."
So, Timmy and the doctor went outside, and the sun shined on Timmy's knee. Timmy felt better right away. He said, "Thank you, doctor, and thank you, sun, for making my knee feel better." From that day on, Timmy was not scared of the sun anymore, and he knew that the doctor was always available to help him when he needed it.

But when it was their turn, they had a naughty idea. They decided to go on the slide together. They thought it would be more fun. They thought they would go faster. They did not tell their moms.

They were not hurt. But they were scared. And they were sorry. They looked at their moms. Their moms looked at them. Their moms were not happy. They were angry.
They ran to their moms. They hugged them. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were bad. We did not listen. We won't do it again."
Their moms hugged them back. They said, "We're glad you're okay. But you were naughty. You could have been hurt. You have to listen. You have to be careful. You have to be obedient."
Lily and Max nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We love you, mom."

Lila and Ben are friends who like to play with blocks. They build towers and houses and cars with the blocks. One day, they decide to make a big tower with all the blocks they have. They work hard and stack the blocks high and wide. They are very proud of their tower.
"Look at our tower!" Lila says. "It is so big and original. No one has a tower like ours."
"Yes, it is amazing!" Ben says. "We are the best builders ever. Do you think we can mail our tower to someone?"
Lila thinks for a moment. She likes the idea of sharing their tower with someone else. But she also likes their tower and does not want to lose it.
"Who do you want to mail it to?" she asks.
Ben thinks too. He remembers his grandma, who lives far away and sends him letters and stickers sometimes. He loves his grandma and misses her.
"Maybe we can mail it to my grandma," he says. "She would like our tower. She likes colorful things and she always says we are creative."
Lila nods. She likes Ben's grandma too. She is very nice and tells funny stories. She thinks she would like their tower too.
"Okay, let's mail it to your grandma," she says. "But how do we do that?"
Ben looks around. He sees a big cardboard box in the corner. He has an idea.
"Maybe we can put our tower in that box," he says. "And then we can write a letter and draw a picture and put them in the box too. And then we can ask mom or dad to take the box to the mail place."
Lila likes Ben's idea. She thinks it is clever and kind.
"Let's do that," she says. "But first, let's take a photo of our tower. So we can remember it and show it to our friends."

Tim and Sam played together every day. They liked to chase each other and hide in the tall grass. But one day, Tim forgot where they were playing. He looked everywhere for Sam, but could not find him. Tim felt very lonely again.
Then, he heard Sam's voice, "Tim, I'm here! I was hiding under the big rock!" Tim found Sam and they were both happy. They promised to always play together and never forget their special friendship. And they were never lonely again.

"And this is my nation. It is called China. It is far and big and has many people," Sue says.
They point to other nations and learn their names. They have fun with the map.
But then, Tim sees a nation he does not like. It is called France. It is small and has a funny shape. Tim thinks it is silly.
"I do not like this nation. It is bad and ugly. I will bite it," Tim says.
He opens his mouth and tries to bite the map. Sue is shocked and angry.
"No, Tim, no! You cannot bite the map. That is rude and mean. You will hurt the map and the people in the nation. You have to be nice and respectful," Sue says.
She pulls the map away from Tim and scolds him. Tim feels ashamed and sorry. He realizes he was wrong.
"I am sorry, Sue. I was silly and mean. I will not bite the map again. I will be nice and respectful. I want to learn more about the nations and the people. Can you teach me?" Tim says.
Sue smiles and forgives him. She is happy that Tim learned his lesson. She teaches him more about the nations and the people. They share their stories and cultures. They become better friends.
The moral of the story is: Do not bite what you do not like. Be nice and respectful to others. Learn from your mistakes and grow.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find bugs and worms. They also liked to eat snacks that Mom gave them. Today, Mom gave them some crackers and cream. Cream was white and soft and yummy.
"Look, I found a big worm!" Tom said, holding a long, brown thing in his hand.
"Let me see!" Lily said, running to him. She saw the worm and made a face. "That's not a worm, Tom. That's a snake!"
"A snake?" Tom said, dropping it. "But it's not scary. It's not moving."
"That's because it's dead, Tom. It's rotting. That means it's old and bad and smelly. You don't want to touch it. It can make you sick."
"Yuck!" Tom said, wiping his hand on his shirt. "I don't like rotting things. They're gross."
"Me neither," Lily said. "Let's go eat our snacks. They're fresh and good and tasty."
They ran to the picnic blanket where Mom had left their snacks. They picked up their crackers and cream and took big bites. They smiled and chewed.
But they didn't notice that the cream had been in the sun for too long. It had turned sour and lumpy. It was rotting too.
Soon, they felt sick in their tummies. They spit out the cream and cried.
"Mom! Mom!" they called. "The cream is bad! It's rotting!"
Mom heard them and came running. She saw the cream and smelled it. She made a face too.
"Oh, no!" she said. "I'm sorry, kids. I forgot to put the cream in the cooler. It went bad in the heat. You shouldn't eat it. It can make you sick."
She hugged them and gave them some water to drink. She threw away the cream and the crackers.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
Lily and Tom nodded. They felt better after drinking the water. They learned their lesson.
They never ate rotting things again. They only ate fresh and good and tasty things.
And they stayed away from distant snakes.

She only heard the clock when it made a very noisy sound. It was very dark and very late. The clock said it was time to wake up, but Anna was very sleepy. She jumped out of her bed and ran to the door. She was scared and confused.
She opened the door and saw her mom and dad in the hall. They were surprised and worried. They asked her what was wrong. Anna pointed to the clock and said, "Clock is noisy! Clock is wrong! Clock is bad!"
Her mom and dad hugged her and calmed her down. They explained that she had changed the time on the clock and that it was not time to wake up. They took the clock and put it away. They told her to go back to bed and sleep. They said they would fix the clock in the morning.
Anna nodded and went back to her bed. She cuddled with her dolls and closed her eyes. She did not want to play with the clock anymore. She wanted to sleep and dream. She hoped the clock would be quiet and right tomorrow.

Suddenly, the thing they were eating started to move! It was not food, but a little bug! The bug said, "Please don't eat me!" Max and Sam were very surprised. They said sorry to the bug and let it go. From that day on, Max and Sam were more careful about what they chewed on.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. They ran to the slide and waited for their turn. Mia went first and slid down fast. She laughed and said, "That was so fun! Come on, Ben!"
Ben followed Mia and slid down too. But when he reached the bottom, he felt something in his pocket. He pulled it out and saw a shiny medal. It had a star and a ribbon on it. He wondered where it came from. He showed it to Mia and said, "Look, Mia! I found a medal! It's so pretty!"
Mia looked at the medal and felt jealous. She wanted the medal too. She said, "That's not fair, Ben! You didn't earn that medal! Give it to me!"
Ben said, "No, Mia! It's mine! I found it! You can't have it!"
They started to argue and tug at the medal. They pulled so hard that the ribbon broke. The medal flew out of their hands and landed on the slide. It slid down fast and vanished under the slide. They could not see it anymore.
Ben and Mia gasped and ran to the slide. They looked under it, but they could not find the medal. It was gone. They felt sad and sorry. They said, "Oh no! We lost the medal! We were so mean to each other! We should have shared it!"
They hugged and said, "We're sorry, Ben. We're sorry, Mia. We love each other more than the medal. Let's play together and have fun."
They smiled and ran to the swings. They forgot about the medal and enjoyed the park. They learned to be kind and share. They were happy twins.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a red mailbox by the road, where the mailman came every day.
One day, Tim and Sam were bored and wanted to have some fun. They saw the mailbox and had an idea. They took their baseball bat and ball and decided to play a game. They would take turns hitting the ball with the bat and try to strike the mailbox. Whoever hit the mailbox the most times would win.
They started to play and had a lot of fun. They laughed and cheered when they hit the mailbox. They did not care that they were making a lot of noise and denting the mailbox. They did not see the mailman coming in his truck.
The mailman was not happy when he saw what Tim and Sam were doing. He stopped his truck and got out. He walked towards them with a frown. He was holding a big envelope in his hand.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing?" he shouted. "You are ruining the mailbox and making a mess. This is not a toy, this is where I deliver the mail. And look, I have a very important mail for you today. It is from your grandma. She sent you a card and a gift. Do you want to see what it is?"
Tim and Sam stopped playing and looked at the mailman. They felt bad and scared. They did not know they were doing something wrong. They did not want to make the mailman angry. They did not want to miss their grandma's mail.
They dropped the bat and the ball and ran to the mailman. They said they were sorry and asked for the mail. The mailman gave them the envelope and told them to be more careful and respectful. He said he would talk to their mom and dad later.
Tim and Sam opened the envelope and saw the card and the gift. The card had a picture of their grandma and a big heart. It said, "I love you, Tim and Sam. You are my clever and sweet grandsons. I hope you enjoy the gift. It is something special for you to play with." The gift was a puzzle with a lot of pieces and colors. It looked fun and challenging.
Tim and Sam smiled and hugged the card and the gift. They thanked the mailman and said they loved their grandma. They said they would not play with the mailbox anymore. They said they would play with the puzzle instead. They ran inside to show their mom and dad.
The mailman smiled and got back in his truck. He was glad that Tim and Sam learned their lesson. He hoped they would have fun with the puzzle and be more clever and kind. He drove away to deliver more mail.

Tim's mom saw the bird and said, "Oh no! Let's make the bird some soup to help it feel better." They made a little bowl of soup for the bird. The bird ate the soup and, to their surprise, it started to grow! It grew so big that it filled the whole room.
"Thank you for the soup," said the big bird. "Now I can fly high and strong again!" The bird flew away, and Tim and his mom waved goodbye. They were happy they could help the bird, and they knew that soup had a special magic to make things strong.

Tim and Sue traded. Tim got the toy car and Sue got the zip. But the car was dirty. Tim did not like the dirty car. He wanted his zip back. He asked Sue, "Can I have my zip back?" Sue said, "No, the zip is mine now."
Tim was very sad. He went home with the dirty car. He lost his zip and had a bad day. The next time, Tim will think more before trading his things.

The bee said, "Yes, I am very hungry. Can I eat from you?" The sunflower agreed and let the bee eat from it. The bee was happy and ate a lot. But the bee was not nice. It ate too much and did not stop. The sunflower became sad and weak.
One day, a big wind appeared. The sunflower was too weak to stand. It fell down and could not get up. The bee was sad because it had no more food. The sunflower and the bee were both sad.
The moral of the story is to not be greedy and to always be kind to others.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big pipe that came out of the wall. They wondered what was inside the pipe.
"Let's look inside the pipe," Ben said. He climbed on a chair and put his eye near the hole.
"Be careful, Ben," Lily said. "Maybe there is something bad in there."
Ben did not listen. He wanted to see what was inside the pipe. He put his hand in the hole and felt something wet and cold. He pulled it out and saw a dead mouse.
"Yuck!" Ben screamed. He dropped the mouse and jumped off the chair.
Lily was scared. She ran to the hose and turned it on. She wanted to spray the mouse away. She pointed the hose at the pipe and pressed the button.
But the hose was not working well. It did not spray water. It sprayed air. The air went into the pipe and made a loud noise.
The pipe shook and burst. Water came out of the pipe and splashed Lily and Ben. They were wet and cold.
They ran to the house and told their mom what happened. She was not happy. She said they should not play with the pipe. She said they should play with their toys instead.
She gave them towels and cookies and told them to stay inside. Lily and Ben were sorry. They did not want to play with the pipe anymore. They wanted to play with their toys and eat cookies.

One day, a little bear and his mama went to look for honey in the forest. The little bear loved honey very much and wanted to eat it all the time. His mama told him to listen carefully and follow her, because there were many dangers in the forest.
"Listen, little bear, we have to be quiet and sneaky. There are big bees that guard the honey, and they can sting us if they see us. There are also other animals that like honey, and they can be mean and scary. Do you understand?" his mama said.
"Yes, mama, I understand. I will listen and follow you. I want to eat honey, but I don't want to get hurt or scared," the little bear said.
They walked and walked until they found a big tree with a hole in it. The little bear smelled honey and got very excited. He ran towards the tree, forgetting to listen and follow his mama. He stuck his head inside the hole and saw a lot of honey. He licked his lips and reached his paw inside.
But then he heard a terrible buzz. The big bees had seen him and were angry. They flew out of the hole and started to sting the little bear. The little bear cried out in pain and fear. He pulled his head and paw out of the hole, but it was too late. He was covered in stings and bumps.
His mama heard his cry and ran to help him. She scared away the bees and hugged the little bear. She licked his wounds and comforted him.
"I'm sorry, mama, I didn't listen and follow you. I was too greedy and foolish. The honey was not worth it. The bees were terrible and hurt me a lot," the little bear said.
"It's okay, little bear, I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned a lesson. Next time, you will listen and follow me, and we will find honey safely and happily. Now let's go home and rest. I love you, little bear," his mama said.
They walked back home, holding paws. The little bear felt sorry and sore, but also loved and grateful. He decided to listen and follow his mama from then on, and to share the honey with her and his friends. He realized that honey was sweet, but love was sweeter.

She looked around and saw an eraser on the table. It was enormous, bigger than her hand. She thought it could erase her blue sun. She grabbed it and rubbed it on her paper. But nothing happened. The blue sun was still there. She rubbed harder and harder, but the eraser did not work.
She was confused and sad. She asked her mom, who was sitting next to her. "Mom, why does this eraser not erase?" She showed her mom the eraser and the paper.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "That is not an eraser, my dear. That is a sponge. It is for cleaning, not for erasing. It can make things wet, but not vanish. If you want to erase something, you need a different kind of eraser. Like this one." She gave Anna a small pink eraser that fit in her hand.
Anna tried the pink eraser on her paper. It worked! The blue sun vanished and left a white space. Anna was happy and thanked her mom. She found a yellow crayon and drew a new sun. She liked her art again. She learned that not all things that look like erasers are erasers. And that sometimes, mistakes can be fixed.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He liked to play near the stream. One day, he saw a weak frog sitting by the water. "Hello, little frog," said Tom. "Why are you so weak?"
The frog looked up at Tom and said, "I need help. I need to add some water to my pond so I can swim and get strong again." Tom thought for a moment and had an idea.
He ran to his house and got a big cup. He filled it with water from the stream and carried it back to the frog's pond. He added the water to the pond, and the frog started to swim. But then, something unexpected happened. The frog turned into a beautiful fairy!
"Thank you, Tom," said the fairy. "You helped me, and now I am strong again. I was under a spell, and you broke it by adding water to my pond. Now, I can fly and help others too." Tom smiled, happy that he could help his new friend.

Lily was sick. She had a fever and a cough. Her mom put a thermometer in her mouth to check her temperature. Lily did not like the thermometer. It was cold and hard. She wanted to spit it out.
"Keep it in, Lily. I need to see how hot you are," her mom said.
Lily tried to be brave, but she was scared. She did not want to go to the doctor. She did not want to get a shot. She closed her eyes and waited for the thermometer to beep.
Suddenly, she heard a loud noise outside. She opened her eyes and saw a big dog. The dog was barking and running towards her window. Lily screamed and dropped the thermometer. It broke on the floor.
"Mommy, mommy, there's a dog!" Lily cried.
Her mom ran to the window and saw the dog. It was not a mean dog. It was a friendly dog. It had a red collar and a tag. It was looking for its owner.
"It's okay, Lily. It's just a lost dog. He won't hurt you," her mom said.
She opened the window and called the dog. The dog wagged its tail and came closer. He licked her hand and sniffed her face. He was a nice dog.
Lily calmed down and looked at the dog. He had brown fur and black spots. He had big ears and a wet nose. He was cute.
"Can I pet him, mommy?" Lily asked.
"Sure, honey. He likes you," her mom said.
Lily reached out and touched the dog. He was soft and warm. He licked her cheek and made her giggle. He was a good dog.
"Can we keep him, mommy?" Lily asked.
Her mom smiled and shook her head. She saw a phone number on the dog's tag.
"No, sweetie. He belongs to someone else. We have to call his owner and tell them we found him," she said.
Lily was sad, but she understood. She gave the dog a hug and a kiss. The dog wagged his tail and bowed his head. He was grateful.
"Bye, doggy. I hope you find your home," Lily said.
Her mom picked up the phone and dialed the number. She hoped the dog's owner would come soon. She also hoped Lily's fever would go down. She was glad the dog made Lily happy. She was a good mom.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big swamp near their house. They wanted to explore it, but their mom said no.
"Swamp is dirty and wet. You can get sick or lost. Stay away from swamp," mom said.
But Lila and Ben did not listen. They waited until mom was busy and ran to the swamp. They saw frogs, bugs, and plants. They thought it was fun.
"Look, a big frog!" Lila said.
"Ribbit, ribbit," Ben said. He liked to repeat what animals said.
They followed the frog to a deeper part of the swamp. They did not see the sign that said "Danger".
"Ribbit, ribbit," the frog said.
"Ribbit, ribbit," Ben said.
Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. A big alligator came out of the water. It had sharp teeth and a long tail. It looked hungry.
"Help, help!" Lila and Ben screamed.
They ran back to the swamp edge. They were scared and wet. They saw mom coming. She looked angry and worried.
"What are you doing here? I told you to stay away from swamp!" mom said.
"Sorry, mom. We saw a frog and wanted to play. But then an alligator came and we ran away. We are fine, mom. Please don't be mad," Lila and Ben said.
Mom hugged them and checked them for injuries. She was glad they were fine, but she was also mad.
"You did not listen to me. You could have been hurt or eaten by the alligator. Swamp is not a place to play. Repeat after me: swamp is not a place to play," mom said.
"Swamp is not a place to play," Lila and Ben said.
They learned their lesson. They never went to the swamp again. They played in the yard or the park instead. They still liked to repeat what animals said, but only the safe ones.

"You were very naughty and foolish!" Dad said. "You should never play with the oven or put anything in it. It is very dangerous!"
He took away their pencils and paper. He sent them to their room without any dessert.
