Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and books. But today, they have a quiz at school. The quiz is about animals and their names.
Lily is good at the quiz. She knows the names of many animals. She says, "This is a cat. It says meow. This is a dog. It says woof. This is a cow. It says moo."
Tom is stubborn. He does not like the quiz. He thinks the names of the animals are silly. He says, "This is not a cat. It is a fur-ball. This is not a dog. It is a bark-machine. This is not a cow. It is a milk-factory."
The teacher is not happy with Tom. She says, "Tom, you have to learn the names of the animals. They are not fur-balls, bark-machines, or milk-factories. They are cat, dog, and cow. Why are you so stubborn?"
Tom shrugs. He says, "I like my names better. They are more fun. And I do not want to do the quiz. I want to play."
Lily shakes her head. She says, "Tom, you are silly. The quiz is easy and fun. And you have to do it. Or you will get in trouble. And you will not learn new things. Come on, try again. What is this?"
She points to a picture of a bird. Tom looks at it. He thinks for a moment. Then he says, "This is a bird. It says tweet."
Lily smiles. She says, "Good job, Tom. You see, you can do it. Now, what is this?"
She points to a picture of a fish. Tom looks at it. He says, "This is a fish. It says blub."
Lily claps. She says, "Very good, Tom. You are getting better. Now, what is this?"
She points to a picture of a lion. Tom looks at it. He says, "This is a lion. It says roar."
Lily cheers. She says, "Wow, Tom. You are amazing. You know all the names of the animals. You are not stubborn anymore. You are smart and brave."
Tom smiles. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. You helped me with the quiz. You are kind and patient."
The teacher smiles too. She says, "Well done, Lily and Tom. You both did a great job with the quiz. You learned the names of the animals. And you learned to work together. You are both stars."
Lily and Tom hug. They say, "We are stars. And we are friends."

Lila and Ben were restless. They did not want to nap. They wanted to play. They saw a big box in the corner. They opened it. Inside, they found many toys. They saw cars, dolls, blocks, and books. But they also saw something else. They saw a bag of shrimp.
"Look, Ben!" Lila said. "Shrimp! They are pink and small. They look yummy!"
"Let's eat them!" Ben said. He opened the bag. He took out a shrimp. He put it in his mouth. He made a face. He spit it out. "Yuck! They are not yummy! They are cold and salty!"
Lila laughed. She took out a shrimp. She did not eat it. She had an idea. She put the shrimp on the floor. She said, "Let's play march! We can be the shrimp army!"
"Okay!" Ben said. He put down the bag. He took out more shrimp. He put them on the floor. He said, "March, march, march! We are the shrimp army! We are strong and brave!"
Lila and Ben marched with the shrimp. They made noises. They had fun. They forgot about napping. They did not hear their mom coming. She opened the door. She saw the mess. She saw the shrimp. She saw Lila and Ben. She was not happy.
"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you playing with shrimp? Why are you not napping? You are making a big mess!"
Lila and Ben stopped marching. They looked at their mom. They felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were restless. We wanted to play. We found the shrimp. We played march. We are the shrimp army."
Mom sighed. She said, "You are not the shrimp army. You are my children. And you need to nap. And you need to clean up. Shrimp are not toys. Shrimp are food. Come on, let's put them back in the fridge. And then, let's go to bed."
Lila and Ben nodded. They helped mom. They put the shrimp back in the bag. They put the bag back in the box. They put the box back in the corner. They picked up their toys. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We love you."
Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too. Now, let's go to bed. And no more shrimp army, okay?"
Lila and Ben said, "Okay, mom." They went to bed. They were not restless anymore. They were sleepy. They closed their eyes. They dreamed of shrimp. But not of marching. Of eating. And they were yummy.

One morning, Tim wanted to make his own toast. He saw a knife on the counter and thought it would be fun to cut the bread. He did not know that the knife was sharp and could hurt him. He grabbed the knife and tried to slice the bread, but he cut his finger instead. He cried out in pain and dropped the knife.
Sam heard his brother's cry and ran to the kitchen. He saw Tim holding his finger and blood on the counter. He was scared and worried. He said, "Tim, what did you do? Why did you use the knife? It is sharp and dangerous. You should not play with it. You should ask Mom or Dad for help."
Tim felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I wanted to make toast by myself. I did not know the knife was sharp. It hurts a lot. I am sorry, Sam. I was silly and careless."
Sam hugged his brother and said, "It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. But you should be more careful next time. Knives are not toys. They are tools for grown-ups. Come on, let's go to Mom and Dad. They will clean your wound and put a band-aid on it. Then we can have some toast together. But not the one you cut. It is tough and hard. We can have some fresh and soft bread instead."
Tim nodded and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good brother. I love you."
They went to their parents and told them what happened. Their parents were glad that Tim was not badly hurt, but they also taught him a lesson. They said, "Tim, you should never touch a knife without permission. It is sharp and can cut you. You should always ask for help when you want to make toast or anything else. We are here to help you and keep you safe. We love you, but we also want you to be responsible and smart."
Tim learned his lesson and never played with knives again. He also thanked Sam for being kind and helpful. They enjoyed their toast and had a happy breakfast. They learned that being careful and asking for help are important, and that being tough and sharp are not always good.

One chilly day, Tom went outside to play. He grabbed his bike and went to explore. After some time, he noticed that his bike chain was not spinning very smoothly.
Tom looked closer and saw that the chain was covered in sticky oil. With a frown on his face, he knew he had to remove the oil.
Tom's mom, who was standing nearby, said, "What is wrong sweetie?"
Tom said, "My bike chain has too much oil and it's making it hard to ride".
His mom nodded her head, "Yes, I see. Here, take this cloth and I'll get some icy water."
Tom took the cloth and wiped the oil off the chain. He then sprinkled icy water from a bucket onto the chain to rinse it off. In no time, the chain was as good as new!
Tom thanked his mom and hopped back onto his bike. He was so excited and ready to keep exploring the icy weather.

Her mom said, "No, Jenny. The bird is wild. It might bite you or fly away. You have to protect yourself and the bird. Let's watch it from here."
But Jenny did not listen. She ran to the tree and climbed up. She reached for the bird. The bird got scared and pecked her hand. Jenny cried out in pain and let go of the branch. She fell to the ground and hurt her head.
Her mom ran to her and called for help. She hugged Jenny and said, "I'm sorry, Jenny. I told you not to touch the bird. You have to be careful. You could have died."
Jenny was bleeding and dizzy. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to see the bird. I love animals. I want to be a veterinarian."
Her mom said, "I know, Jenny. I love you. But you have to listen to me. You have to protect yourself and the animals. You can't be a veterinarian if you're dead."
Jenny closed her eyes and did not wake up. She died. The bird flew away.

Once there was a deaf bear who lived in a small cave near the forest. One day, the bear was feeling hot, so he decided to go for a bath in the river. 
He slowly made his way down the rocky path, but when he arrived at the river he found that the water was too deep for him to stand. He tried to turn around, but he had gone so far he couldn't make it back. 
He tried to call for help, but he was deaf, so nobody heard him. He looked around, and he saw a switch next to the river bank. He pressed the switch and a bridge appeared out of nowhere. With the bridge, the bear was able to cross the river and bathe in the cool water. 
When the bear was done bathing, he thanked the switch and scampered back home. He was squeezy clean and refreshed. It was the best bath he had ever had.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, slide and swing. They saw a big hill with colorful flowers. They wanted to climb the hill and smell the flowers.
"Come on, Ben, let's go up the hill!" Lila said.
"OK, Lila, but be careful. The hill is steep and there might be spikes on the flowers," Ben said.
They started to climb the hill. They held hands and helped each other. They saw many beautiful flowers. Some were red, some were yellow, some were blue. They smelled sweet and fresh.
"Wow, these flowers are so pretty! Can we pick some?" Lila asked.
"No, Lila, we can't. The flowers belong to the hill and the bees. If we pick them, they will die and the hill will be sad. And the bees might sting us if we take their food," Ben said.
"But I want to have a flower for Mommy. She will be happy if I give her a flower," Lila said.
"Lila, you don't need to give Mommy a flower to make her happy. She loves you no matter what. And you can draw her a picture of the flowers instead. That way, the flowers can remain on the hill and the bees can have their food," Ben said.
Lila thought about it. She realized that Ben was right. She didn't want to hurt the flowers or the bees. She wanted to be kind and respectful to nature. She smiled and hugged Ben.
"OK, Ben, you are a good brother. Let's go down the hill and draw Mommy a picture of the flowers. Maybe we can also draw a bee and a hill," Lila said.
They went down the hill and found some paper and crayons. They drew a colorful picture of the flowers, the bee and the hill. They wrote "We love you, Mommy" on the bottom. They ran to Mommy and gave her the picture. Mommy was very happy and proud. She hugged them and kissed them.
"Thank you, Lila and Ben, for this beautiful picture. You are very sweet and thoughtful. And I'm glad you didn't pick the flowers. You showed respect and care for the hill and the bees. That's a very good thing to do," Mommy said.
Lila and Ben smiled. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sometimes it's better to leave things as they are and enjoy them from a distance. They learned that nature is precious and needs our protection. They learned that love is more than a flower. It's a feeling that remains in your heart.

One day, Mina decided to go on an adventure. She started walking and soon came to a special place. All of a sudden, Mina noticed something in the distance. It was a man who was trying to get away from someone. 
Mina watched as the man stumbled and almost fell. Then she heard someone call out for help. She knew it was the man who had been trying to get away.
Mina felt very uncomfortable because she was scared of the man. She wanted to help him but was afraid. Eventually, Mina plucked up the courage and ran to the man. Together, they were able to escape.
Mina felt proud of herself for being brave. Even though it was uncomfortable, she was happy to have used her sight to help someone in need.

Tim was a lonely boy. He had no friends to play with. He only had his toys and his books. He liked to dream about going to the sea. He wanted to see the big waves and the fish and the boats. He wanted to taste the salt in the water and feel the sand on his feet.
One day, his mom said they could go to the sea. Tim was very happy. He packed his toys and his books in a bag. He put on his hat and his sunscreen. He got in the car with his mom and they drove to the sea.
When they got there, Tim ran to the water. He saw the big waves and the fish and the boats. He tasted the salt in the water and felt the sand on his feet. He was so happy. He said to his mom, "Mom, this is my dream. I love the sea. Can we stay here forever?"
His mom smiled and said, "No, Tim, we can't stay here forever. We have to go back home soon. But we can come back another day. Now, let's have some fun. Do you want to build a sandcastle?"
Tim nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I want to build a sandcastle. Can you help me?"
His mom said, "Of course, Tim, I will help you. Let's find a good spot."
They walked along the shore, looking for a good spot. They saw a big rock with a hole in it. Tim thought it looked like a cave. He said, "Mom, look, a cave. Can we build our sandcastle near the cave?"
His mom said, "Sure, Tim, we can build our sandcastle near the cave. But be careful, don't go inside the cave. It might be dangerous. There might be crabs or snakes or spiders inside."
Tim said, "OK, mom, I won't go inside the cave. I will stay with you."
They started to build their sandcastle near the cave. They used a bucket and a shovel and some shells and some seaweed. They made a big tower and a wall and a door and a flag. Tim was very proud of their sandcastle. He said, "Mom, look, our sandcastle is the best. It is bigger and prettier than the others. Can we take a picture of it?"
His mom said, "Yes, Tim, we can take a picture of it. Let me get my phone from the car. You stay here and watch our sandcastle. Don't let anyone destroy it. And don't go inside the cave. I will be right back."
His mom left to get her phone from the car. Tim stayed and watched their sandcastle. He was very happy. He thought, "This is the best day ever. I love the sea. I love my mom. I love our sandcastle."
But then, he heard a strange noise. It came from the cave. It sounded like a growl. Tim was curious. He wanted to see what was inside the cave. He thought, "Maybe it is not dangerous. Maybe it is a friendly animal. Maybe it is a dog or a cat or a bunny. Maybe it wants to play with me."
He forgot what his mom said. He forgot to be careful. He forgot to stay with their sandcastle. He walked towards the cave. He said, "Hello, who is there? Do you want to be my friend?"
He went inside the cave. He saw a dark shadow. He saw two yellow eyes. He saw sharp teeth. He saw a big bear. The bear was angry. The bear was hungry. The bear roared and attacked Tim.
Tim screamed. He was scared. He was hurt. He wanted his mom. He wanted to go back to their sandcastle. He wanted to go back to his dream. But it was too late. The bear ate him. He was gone.
His mom came back with her phone. She saw their sandcastle. She saw the cave. She saw the blood. She saw the bear. She screamed. She was sad. She was angry. She wanted her son. She wanted to go back to their home. She wanted to go back to their life. But it was too late. He was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat named Bob. Bob lived in a harbor with his boat friends. One day, Bob saw a big, shiny rock near the water. He wanted to show his friends the rock.
Bob called his friend, "Hey, look at this big rock!" His friend came over, but as he got close, he started to feel dizzy. "Oh no, I don't feel good," said his friend. But Bob didn't listen. He wanted to show the rock to all his friends.
One by one, Bob's friends came to see the rock. They all felt dizzy too. They knew something was wrong, but Bob didn't listen. He was so happy to show the rock. Then, it started to rain. The water became slippery, and the boats began to slip and slide in the harbor.
Bob's friends tried to tell him to stop, but he didn't listen. The rain got harder, and the boats slipped more and more. They all felt dizzy and scared. The big, shiny rock was not fun anymore.
In the end, all the boats slipped and crashed into each other. The harbor was a mess, and the boats were sad. Bob learned that he should have listened to his friends when they felt dizzy. Sometimes, things that look fun can be bad.

Ivy: "Yes they are very pretty!"

Mum: "The birds are singing and they are leading us around the garden."
Ivy and Mum held hands and started walking around the garden. Ivy saw a delicate butterfly and as she moved closer it flew away.
Mum: "Oh that's too bad. We must have been too noisy for the butterfly."
Ivy looked sad, so Mum said: "Let's go back inside, I have something special for you."
Mum opened a jar of creamy lotion and spread it all over Ivy's hands.
Mum: "Look how delicate and soft the lotion makes your hands feel."
Ivy smiled - everything felt so gentle and smooth. She laughed and hugged her Mum. She knew that everything would be alright.

From that day on, the little acorn and the small bird became best friends. They played together in the big dark forest every day. The little acorn was not sad anymore because it could speak and had a friend. All the animals in the forest were happy to see the little acorn and the small bird playing and having fun.

"Mmm, this is good!" Lily said.
"Yes, it is! I like it!" Ben said.
They ate more red balls and smiled. They had discovered a new fruit. They called it a berry. They decided to share some with their mom and dad. They ran to the house with their hands full of berries. They were proud and excited.

Mom said, “Joe, this is not a plan. You need to be careful and only buy one!”
Joe was fearful because he had never bought gum before. “Okay, mom”, he said nervously. He slowly looked at all the flavors and eventually chose his favorite one.
He went to the counter to pay for the gum and the cashier asked, “Is this your plan, Joe?”
Joe replied, “Yes, this is my plan.”
The moral of the story is: sometimes it's best to stick to your plan. Joe was smart to listen to his mom and it was a good plan to only buy one type of gum. This made him feel better and much less fearful.

The monkey was disappointed, but the parrot made him laugh by telling a funny joke. The monkey was so grateful to the parrot for cheering him up.

Ben and Mia were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes.
"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Ben said. "Do you like our town?"
The snowman did not say anything. He was very still and cold.
"Maybe he is shy," Mia said. "Or maybe he is dead."
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They did not know what dead meant. They had heard it on TV, but they did not understand.
"What is dead?" Ben asked.
Mia shrugged. She did not know either.
"Let's ask Mom," she said.
They ran to their house and knocked on the door. Mom opened it and smiled.
"Hi, kids. Did you have fun in the snow?"
"Yes, Mom. But we have a question," Ben said.
"What is it?"
"What is dead?" Mia asked.
Mom looked surprised. She knelt down and hugged them.
"Dead is when something is not alive anymore. When it does not breathe or move or feel. Like a flower that withers or a toy that breaks."
"Is Mr. Snowman dead?" Ben asked.
Mom shook her head.
"No, honey. Mr. Snowman is not dead. He is just frozen. Frozen is when something is very cold and hard. Like ice or snow. But frozen things can melt and change. Like when the sun comes out and makes the snowman smaller."
"Will Mr. Snowman come alive then?" Mia asked.
Mom smiled.
"No, sweetie. Mr. Snowman is not alive. He is just a fun thing we made with snow. But we can pretend he is alive and talk to him and play with him. And we can make him again next time it snows."
Ben and Mia nodded. They understood a little bit better.
"Can we go back and play with Mr. Snowman?" Ben asked.
"Sure, but wear your coats and gloves. It is very cold outside."
"Okay, Mom. Thank you," Mia said.
They kissed Mom and ran back to the snowman. They said hello to him and gave him a hug. They did not care if he was frozen or dead. They liked him anyway.

Sam liked to dream at night. He dreamed of many things. He dreamed of flying in the sky, or swimming in the sea, or playing with his toys. Sometimes he dreamed of scary things, like monsters or ghosts, but he knew they were not real.
One night, he dreamed of an alligator. The alligator was big and green and had many teeth. It was wet and slimy and made a loud noise. Sam was afraid of the alligator. He wanted to run away, but he could not move.
"Hello, little boy," the alligator said. "Do you want to be my friend?"
Sam shook his head. He did not want to be friends with the alligator. He wanted to wake up.
"Why not?" the alligator asked. "I am lonely. I have no friends. Everyone is afraid of me."
Sam felt sorry for the alligator. He did not like to be lonely. He had many friends at home and at school. He wondered why the alligator had no friends.
"Maybe you could be nicer to others," Sam said. "Maybe you could smile more and share your things and play nice games. Then maybe others would not be afraid of you."
The alligator thought about what Sam said. He had never tried to be nice to others. He had always been mean and greedy and angry. He wondered if he could change.
"Maybe you are right," the alligator said. "Maybe I could try to be nicer. Will you help me?"
Sam nodded. He decided to help the alligator. He taught him how to smile and share and play nice games. The alligator learned and had fun. He felt happy and grateful.
"Thank you, little boy," the alligator said. "You are a good friend. You have made me happy."
Sam smiled. He was happy too. He had made a new friend. He was not afraid of the alligator anymore.
They hugged and said goodbye. Sam woke up. He remembered his dream. He wondered if he would see the alligator again. He hoped so. He liked the alligator. He was his friend.

"Hello, sir," Lily and Tom say. "We like Max a lot, too. He is very playful. He makes our day."

"No, thank you, Mom," Lily said. She pushed her plate away. "Salad is yucky."
"No, no, no, Mom," Max said. He shook his head. "Salad is gross."
Mom sighed. She wanted her kids to eat well, but they were very picky. She decided to try a different approach.
"Okay, how about this?" Mom said. "If you eat some salad, I will tell you a story. A story about a big, scary monster who loves salad."
Lily and Max looked at each other. They liked stories, especially scary ones. They wondered what kind of monster liked salad.
"Okay, Mom, we will eat some salad," Lily said. She took a small bite. "But only a little bit."
"Okay, Mom, we will eat some salad," Max said. He took a tiny bite. "But only a tiny bit."
Mom smiled. She was happy that her kids were willing to try something new. She began to tell them the story.
"Once upon a time, there was a big, scary monster who lived in the woods. He had sharp teeth and claws and horns and a long tail. He liked to roam around the woods and look for food. But he did not like meat or fruit or nuts. He only liked salad. He liked to eat all kinds of salad: lettuce, spinach, kale, cabbage, carrots, tomatoes, cucumbers, and more. He liked to mix them all together and make a big salad bowl. He liked to add salt and pepper and vinegar and oil and make a tasty dressing. He liked to eat his salad with a big spoon and make loud noises. He liked to scream, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!'"
Lily and Max listened to the story with wide eyes. They imagined the big, scary monster and his big salad bowl. They wondered if he would eat them if he saw them.
"Did anyone ever see the monster, Mom?" Lily asked.
"Did he ever eat anyone, Mom?" Max asked.
Mom smiled. She had a surprise for them.
"Well, one day, a little girl and a little boy were walking in the woods. They were looking for berries and mushrooms. They did not know that the monster was nearby. They did not hear him scream, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' They did not see him coming. They did not notice his big spoon. They did not feel his breath. They did not see his teeth. They did not..."
"Mom, stop!" Lily and Max screamed. They were scared. They did not want to hear the end of the story. They did not want to know what happened to the little girl and the little boy.
Mom laughed. She hugged them and kissed them.
"Don't worry, kids, it's just a story. The monster is not real. The little girl and the little boy are fine. They ran away and hid behind a tree. The monster did not see them. He only saw their basket of berries and mushrooms. He thought they were part of his salad. He added them to his bowl and ate them. He screamed, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' And he was happy."
Lily and Max looked at each other. They were relieved. They were glad that the monster did not eat the little girl and the little boy. They were glad that he only ate berries and mushrooms. They were glad that he was happy.
"Mom, can we have some berries and mushrooms, too?" Lily asked.
"Mom, can we have some cheese and bread, too?" Max asked.
Mom nodded. She gave them some berries and mushrooms and cheese and bread. She also gave them some more salad.
"Here you go, kids. Enjoy your lunch. And remember, salad is good for you. Maybe you will grow up to be big and strong like the monster."
Lily and Max smiled. They ate their lunch. They ate some salad, too. They did not scream. They did not make loud noises. They did not say, 'Salad, salad, I love salad!' But they did say, 'Thank you, Mom, for the story and the food. We love you.'

She said, "A little bird came into the house and played with your toy. The bird didn't know it was a toy and thought it was a friend. When the bird tried to fly away, the toy fell and broke." Tim listened carefully and understood.
After dinner, Tim's mom fixed the broken toy. Tim was happy and thanked his mom. From that day on, whenever Tim ate broccoli, he remembered the story of the little bird and his broken toy.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had many old things inside, like books, hats, and a belt. Sara and Tom wanted to see what was in the box, so they opened it and took out the things.
Sara liked the belt. It was brown and shiny, and it had a buckle that made a noise when she moved it. She put it around her waist and pretended to be a cowboy. Tom liked the books. They had pictures and words, and he tried to read them. He opened one book and saw a story about a lion and a mouse.
Sara saw the book and wanted it too. She said, "Give me that book, Tom. It is mine." Tom said, "No, Sara. It is mine. I saw it first." Sara and Tom started to fight over the book. They pulled and tugged, and the book ripped in half. They both heard a loud tear and stopped.
They looked at the book and saw that it was ruined. The pages were torn and the cover was ripped. They felt sad and sorry. They had broken the book that they both liked. They wished they had shared it instead of fighting.
They heard their mom coming. They quickly put the book and the other things back in the box. They hoped their mom would not see the broken book. They hid the belt under Sara's shirt. They tried to act normal.
Their mom came in and said, "Hi, Sara and Tom. What are you doing?" Sara and Tom said, "Nothing, mom. Just playing." Their mom smiled and said, "That's good. Do you want some cookies? I made them for you. They are warm and yummy."
Sara and Tom said, "Yes, please, mom. We love cookies." They followed their mom to the kitchen. They felt the belt around Sara's waist. It was tight and uncomfortable. They felt the book in the box. It was torn and sad. They felt their hearts. They were heavy and guilty.
They decided to tell their mom the truth. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We found a box in the garage and we played with the things inside. We fought over a book and we tore it. We also took a belt and we hid it. We were wrong and we are sorry."
Their mom listened and said, "Thank you for telling me the truth, Sara and Tom. I am glad you are honest. The book and the belt belonged to your grandpa. He gave them to me when I was little. They were very special to him and to me. I was going to give them to you when you were older. But now they are broken and lost. That makes me sad."
Sara and Tom felt very sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We were selfish and greedy. We did not think about you or grandpa. We only thought about ourselves. We are sorry, mom. Can you forgive us?"
Their mom hugged them and said, "Of course I forgive you, Sara and Tom. I love you very much. But you have to learn to share and care for your things and for others. That is what grandpa taught me. That is what I want to teach you. Sharing and caring are more important than fighting and breaking. Do you understand?"
Sara and Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We will try to share and care more. We will try to be like you and grandpa. We love you, mom." Their mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara and Tom. Now, let's have some cookies. They are still warm and yummy." They ate the cookies and felt warm and happy. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to share and care.

"I will paint this big white cloud," said Tom. "It looks like a bunny."
"I will paint this small gray cloud," said Sue. "It looks like a mouse."
They started to paint their clouds on their papers. They were happy and proud of their work.
But then, they saw something in the sky. It was a big, dark, unknown cloud. It was not like any cloud they had seen before. It was moving fast and making loud noises. It scared them.
"What is that?" asked Tom.
"I don't know," said Sue.
They dropped their brushes and papers and ran to their mom. They told her about the unknown cloud. She hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. That is a storm cloud. It brings rain and thunder and lightning. It can be scary, but it is also good. It helps the plants and animals grow. It will go away soon."
She took them to the couch and gave them blankets and cookies. They snuggled with her and watched the storm cloud pass by. They saw flashes of light and heard booms of sound. They felt the raindrops on the window. They were still a little scared, but they also felt curious and amazed.
They learned something new about the sky and the clouds. They decided to paint the storm cloud next time. They thought it would be fun and exciting. They smiled and said, "We love to paint."

He flew down and started to work on the triangle. But just then, another bird flew down and said,
“That triangle is mine! I was going to complete it myself.”
Bob was a bit surprised but he said,
“I want to help. Let’s complete it together.”
The other bird smiled and said,
“Okay then! Let’s do it.”
So Bob and the other bird worked together. After a few seconds, the triangle was complete. They both cheered in delight and thanked each other for the help.
From then on, they were the best of friends. They looked after each other and worked together to complete all their difficult tasks. Bob was so proud of his intelligent friend.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys. Anna has a doll and Ben has a car. They like to act like the doll and the car are talking to each other.
"Hello, car. I am a doll. Do you want to be my friend?" Anna says in a high voice.
"Vroom, vroom. Yes, doll. I want to be your friend. Let's go for a ride." Ben says in a low voice.
They make the doll and the car move around the floor. They have fun.
But then, Ben sees another toy. It is a big truck. He likes the truck. He wants to play with it.
"Bye, doll. I am going to play with the truck now." Ben says. He drops the car and grabs the truck.
"Hey, that's not fair!" Anna says. She is sad. She likes the car. She wants to keep playing with it.
"Give me back the car, Ben. You can't take it away. We were playing with it." Anna says.
"No, I want the truck. You can have the doll. The truck is better." Ben says.
They start to argue. They are not happy.
Mom hears them. She comes to see what is wrong.
"What's going on, Anna and Ben? Why are you fighting?" Mom asks.
"Ben took the car away from me. He is not fair." Anna says.
"I want the truck. Anna can have the doll. The truck is mine." Ben says.
Mom looks at them. She thinks for a minute. She has an idea.
"How about this? You can take turns with the toys. Anna, you can play with the car for five minutes. Then, you can give it to Ben. Ben, you can play with the truck for five minutes. Then, you can give it to Anna. That way, you can both enjoy the toys. Is that fair?" Mom says.
Anna and Ben think about it. They nod.
"OK, Mom. That sounds fair. We can take turns." Anna says.
"OK, Mom. That sounds fair. We can share." Ben says.
Mom smiles. She gives them a hug.
"Good. I'm glad you agree. Now, let's set the timer for five minutes. And remember, be nice to each other." Mom says.
Anna and Ben say thank you to Mom. They start to play with the toys again. They act like the doll, the car, and the truck are friends. They have fun. They are happy.

Suddenly, the bottle bumped into a group of strong whales. Furious, the whales chased after baby shark.

Using their strength, mommy and daddy shark pushed the whales away and saved baby shark. 
The mommy and daddy shark hugged their baby and made sure he was okay. "You need to listen to us and behave," said mommy and daddy shark. "You could have gotten hurt if we hadn't been here." 
From that day onwards, baby shark no longer behaved badly and always listened to his mommy and daddy shark. 
The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and behave no matter what.

Anna and Ben groaned. They did not want to wait. They wanted to play now. They ate their cereal very fast and brushed their teeth very fast. They put on their hats and sunscreen very fast. Then they grabbed their ball and ran outside.
They kicked and threw the ball to each other. They had a lot of fun. They laughed and shouted. They did not notice that the sun was getting higher and hotter. They did not notice that they were getting thirsty and tired.
"Anna, catch!" Ben said. He threw the ball high in the air. Anna looked up and saw the ball. She also saw the sun. It was very bright. It hurt her eyes. She blinked and closed her eyes. She did not see the ball.
The ball hit her on the head. She fell down. She dropped the ball. She cried.
"Anna, are you okay?" Ben said. He ran to her. He was worried. He was sorry. He did not mean to hurt her.
Anna opened her eyes. She saw Ben. He looked sad. She felt a bump on her head. It hurt. She was angry. She did not want to play with him anymore.
"Go away!" she said. "You are mean. You hit me with the ball. You are not my friend."
Ben felt bad. He did not know what to say. He picked up the ball. He wanted to hug Anna and say sorry. But she did not want him. She turned away from him. He walked away. He felt lonely.
Their mom heard them. She came outside. She saw Anna crying and Ben walking. She knew something was wrong. She went to Anna first. She checked her head. She gave her a kiss and a band-aid. She asked her what happened.
"Ben hit me with the ball. He did it on purpose. He is mean. I don't like him." Anna said.
Their mom shook her head. She knew that was not true. She knew Ben loved Anna. She knew it was an accident. She knew they were both hot and tired. She knew they needed a break.
She called Ben. He came back. He looked down. He did not want to talk.
"Ben, did you hit Anna with the ball on purpose?" their mom asked.
Ben shook his head. He did not.
"Did you say sorry to Anna?" their mom asked.
Ben nodded. He did.
"Did Anna forgive you?" their mom asked.
Ben shook his head. She did not.
Their mom sighed. She knew they were both upset. She knew they needed some love.
She hugged them both. She told them she loved them. She told them they were both good kids. She told them they should love each other too. She told them they should say sorry and forgive each other. She told them they should play nicely and share the ball. She told them they should drink some water and rest in the shade. She told them they should enjoy the day.
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry. They felt silly. They felt sorry for being silly. They said sorry to each other. They hugged each other. They forgave each other. They smiled at each other. They felt better.
They drank some water and rested in the shade. They felt comfortable. They watched the ball. They wanted to play again. They asked their mom if they could.
Their mom smiled. She said yes. She was happy. She watched them play. They were happy too. They played nicely and shared the ball. They enjoyed the day. They did not drop the ball again. They did not drop their friendship either.

"Look, Ben, I made a fire!" Lily said, holding the stick in the air. She smiled and waved it around.
"Be careful, Lily, don't burn yourself!" Ben said. He was a helpful brother. He always looked after Lily.
Lily nodded, but she did not listen. She wanted to make the fire bigger and brighter. She ran to the pile of leaves and threw the stick on it. The leaves caught fire and made a lot of smoke.
"Oh no, Lily, what did you do?" Ben shouted. He ran to the tent and grabbed the flashlight. He turned it on and pointed it at the fire. He hoped it would scare the fire away.
But the fire did not go away. It grew and grew. It reached the tent and burned it. It reached the map and burned it. It reached the flashlight and burned it.
Lily and Ben were scared. They cried and hugged each other. They did not know what to do.
Then they heard a siren. It was a fire truck. It came to the yard and sprayed water on the fire. The fire went away. The firemen came out and checked on Lily and Ben.
"Are you okay, kids?" one of them asked.
"Yes, we are okay, thank you," Ben said.
"Why did you start a fire?" another one asked.
"It was an accident, we were playing," Lily said.
"Playing with fire is very dangerous, you know. You could have hurt yourself or others. You should never do that again," the fireman said.
"We are sorry, we won't do that again," Lily and Ben said.
The firemen were nice. They gave Lily and Ben a hug and a sticker. They told them to be careful and to listen to their parents. They also told them to smile and be happy.
Lily and Ben smiled and thanked the firemen. They learned their lesson. They decided to play something else next time. Maybe they would pretend to be astronauts or pirates. But they would never play with fire again.

Suddenly, he heard a voice from above: "That's my tooth!"
Noah looked up and saw a friendly-looking cloud smiling down at him.
The cloud said, "If you give me back my tooth, I'll reward you with something special." 
Noah happily handed the tooth back to the cloud. As the cloud took the tooth, it began to melt. Little droplets of golden liquid rained down, forming a big pool around Noah's feet. 
The cloud said, "Now, that is your reward. Have fun playing!" Noah thanked the cloud, and jumped into the pool. He felt amazed - he'd never felt anything like it before!
The cloud smiled and said, "See you soon!" before disappearing into the sky. 
Noah remained in the pool, feeling dependable in his newfound luck.

Once upon a time, there was a compassionate whale. He swam across the ocean. One day, he decided to take a break and stop for a rest. As he arrived at a small island, he noticed a little girl sitting alone on the beach.
The whale swam closer and said, "hello!"
The girl was startled by the whale's unexpected greeting. She smiled and replied, "hello!"
The whale asked, "why are you here all alone?"
The girl looked at the whale with a sad expression and said, "I was on a boat trip with my parents. But then a big storm came and now I can't find them. I'm scared and alone."
The whale felt sad for the little girl. He said in a gentle voice, "I understand how you feel. Don't worry, I'm here with you. You are not alone."
The girl hugged the whale. She smiled and thanked the whale for being so compassionate. 
From that day on, the whale became the little girl's best friend. They both lived happily together on the island.

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big mop and a bucket of water. They wanted to have fun with them.
"Let's mop the floor!" Tom said. "It will be like a slide!"
"OK!" Lily said. "But don't make too much mess!"
They took the mop and dipped it in the water. Then they dragged it on the floor. The floor became wet and slippery. They laughed and slid on the floor.
But then Mom came in. She saw the water and the mop. She was not happy.
"What are you doing?" Mom asked. "You made a big mess!"
Tom and Lily stopped playing. They felt bad. They regretted mopping the floor.
"We're sorry, Mom," Tom said. "We just wanted to have fun."
"We didn't mean to make a mess," Lily said.
Mom sighed. She was not angry, but she was tired. She had a lot of work to do. She was poor and had no help.
"I know, kids," Mom said. "But you have to be careful. The mop and the water are not toys. They are for cleaning. And the floor is not a slide. It is for walking. You could have hurt yourself or broken something."
Tom and Lily nodded. They understood. They wanted to help Mom.
"Can we help you clean, Mom?" Tom asked.
"Yes, please," Mom said. "That would be very nice."
Tom and Lily took some towels and dried the floor. Then they hugged Mom and said they loved her.
Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said she loved them too. She was glad they were sorry and wanted to help. She was proud of them.

Many people were scared and did not want him to go. But the King was brave and he wanted to prove his bravery. He carried a sword and a shield and set out on the journey.
When the King arrived at his destination, he met an evil monster. The monster was huge and very dangerous! The King was scared but he did not want to show it. He took a deep breathe and walked right up to the monster.
The King started to talk to the monster and said, ‘I am brave and I will stand up to you!’ The monster was surprised and stepped back. Then the King and the monster talked for a long time about being brave and about friendship.
In the end, the King and the monster became friends. The King went home and everyone was happy. The King had proven himself to be brave and everyone loved and respected him. 
The King taught everyone an important lesson: no matter how dangerous something may seem, if you are brave and talk about it, it can always have a happy ending.

One day, Anna wants to play with the big red truck. But Ben has it. He says, "No, it is mine. You play with the doll."
Anna says, "No, I want the truck. You had it yesterday. Give it to me."
They pull and tug on the truck. They are both angry. They do not listen to each other.
Then, Ben pushes Anna. Anna falls on the floor. She cries. She hurts her knee.
Mom hears the noise. She is alert. She runs to the bedroom. She sees Anna and Ben. She is not happy.
She says, "What is going on here? Why are you pushing and crying? You need to share and be kind."
She helps Anna up. She hugs her. She puts a band-aid on her knee. She says, "I'm sorry you got hurt, Anna. Ben, you should not push your sister. That is not nice. You need to say sorry."
Ben feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was wrong. Do you want to play with the truck?"
Anna says, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. Yes, I want to play with the truck. But we can take turns. You can play with the doll, too."
Mom smiles. She says, "That's better. I'm glad you are making up. Now, play nicely and have fun."
She leaves the bedroom. Anna and Ben hug. They play with the truck and the doll. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily picked up the pencil and the book. She felt the difference in her hands. She nodded. She understood.
"Can I weigh other things?" Lily asked.
"Sure, you can. But be careful not to break anything," Mom said.
Lily ran to her room. She found a toy scale that she got for her birthday. She put the pencil on one side of the scale and a stuffed bear on the other side. The scale tipped to the bear's side.
"The bear weighs more than the pencil," Lily said to herself.
She tried other things. She weighed a ball, a flower, a cookie, and a necklace. She had fun comparing them.
Then she saw her cat sleeping on her bed. She wondered how much the cat weighed. She was very curious. She picked up the cat and put it on the scale. The cat did not like it. It meowed and scratched Lily's arm. It jumped off the scale and ran away.
"Ow!" Lily cried. "That hurt!"
Mom heard Lily and came to her room. She saw the scratch on Lily's arm and the scale on the floor.
"What happened, Lily?" Mom asked.
"I wanted to weigh the cat, but the cat was angry," Lily said.
Mom hugged Lily and cleaned her wound. She explained to Lily that the cat did not like to be weighed. She said that some things are better left alone.
"I'm sorry, Mom. I was just curious," Lily said.
"I know, Lily. Curiosity is good, but you have to be gentle and respectful with living things. They have feelings too," Mom said.
Lily nodded. She learned something new. She said sorry to the cat and gave it a treat. She decided to weigh only things that did not mind. She still liked to be curious, but she also liked to be kind.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog runs to them and wags his tail.
"Hello, dog!" Lila says. "Do you want to play with us?"
The dog barks and licks Lila's face. He is happy. Ben is scared. He thinks the dog will bite him.
"Go away, dog!" Ben says. "You are big and scary!"
The dog does not go away. He sniffs Ben's pocket. He smells something good. Ben has a sandwich with meat in his pocket. The dog wants the meat.
"Hey, that's mine!" Ben says. He tries to pull his sandwich away from the dog. The dog growls and pulls harder.
Lila sees that Ben and the dog are fighting. She does not like fighting. She wants them to be peaceful.
"Stop, stop!" Lila says. "Ben, share your sandwich with the dog. He is hungry. He is not scary. He is friendly. He wants to be your friend."
Ben listens to Lila. He thinks for a moment. He does not want to be mean to the dog. He breaks his sandwich in half and gives one half to the dog.
"Here, dog. You can have this. But you have to be nice to me. And you have to play with us."
The dog takes the meat and eats it. He is happy. He wags his tail again. He licks Ben's face. He is thankful.
"Thank you, Ben. You are kind. You are my friend. Can I play with you and Lila?"
Ben smiles. He is not scared anymore. He likes the dog. He pets the dog.
"Sure, dog. You can play with us. What is your name?"
The dog barks. He does not have a name.
"Can we give you a name?" Lila asks.
The dog nods. He likes that idea.
"How about Brownie?" Lila suggests.
The dog barks. He likes that name.
"OK, Brownie. Welcome to our park. Welcome to our game. Welcome to our friendship."
Lila, Ben and Brownie play together. They have fun. They are peaceful. They are happy.

Tom and Lily stayed behind the fence for a while. They calmed down and looked at their cars. One was broken and the other was dirty. They felt sorry for Max. He was not a bad dog, he was just scared and confused.

"Maybe," Tom said. "But he should not have bitten our car."

The girl replied, "I just want to be happy, but I can't seem to find joy anywhere".
The bear said, "Come closer, I may be able to help you find happiness". 
So the girl stepped closer and the bear said, "All you need to do is demand joy for yourself. Find what makes you happy and you will find joy"! 
The girl thanked the bear and promised to always remember her advice. With that, each of them went their own way. The girl was much happier and never felt so miserable again!

Tom and Lily were bored. They had no toys to play with and no books to read. Their mom was busy in the kitchen and their dad was at work. They looked out the window and saw a big slide in the park. They wanted to go there and have fun.
"Mom, can we go to the park and slide?" Tom asked.
"Not now, dear. I have to finish cooking. Maybe later," Mom said.
Tom and Lily did not listen. They put on their coats and shoes and ran out of the door. They did not tell Mom where they were going. They crossed the street and ran to the park. They saw the big slide and smiled.
"Let's go, Lily. I'll go first and you follow me," Tom said.
He climbed up the ladder and sat on the top of the slide. He pushed himself down and felt the wind in his hair. He laughed and shouted, "Whee!"
Lily climbed up the ladder and sat on the top of the slide. She saw Tom waiting for her at the bottom. She pushed herself down and felt the wind in her hair. She laughed and shouted, "Whee!"
But then something bad happened. The slide was broken and had a sharp edge. Lily did not see it and slid over it. It cut her leg and made her bleed. She screamed and cried, "Ow! Ow! Ow!"
Tom heard her scream and ran to her. He saw her leg and felt scared. He did not know what to do. He shouted, "Help! Help! Help!"
Mom heard the shouts and looked out of the window. She saw Tom and Lily in the park and felt angry. She also saw Lily's leg and felt worried. She grabbed her phone and ran to the park. She called Dad and the doctor. She hugged Lily and Tom and said, "Why did you go to the park without telling me? You could have been hurt or lost. You were very naughty and made a big mistake."
Tom and Lily felt sorry and sad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We were bored and wanted to slide. We didn't mean to make you angry or worried. We didn't know the slide was broken. Please don't be mad at us."
Mom said, "I'm not mad at you, but I'm very disappointed. You have to listen to me and follow the rules. You have to be careful and safe. You have to ask me before you go anywhere. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We understand, Mom. We won't do it again. We love you, Mom."
Mom said, "I love you too, but you have to learn from your mistake. Now let's go to the hospital and get Lily's leg fixed. And no more sliding for a while."
Tom and Lily followed Mom to the car and went to the hospital. They felt dull and sore. They wished they had stayed at home and played with their toys and books. They learned a hard lesson that day.

The people were sad. They wished Lily and Ben had not chased the man. They wished Lily and Ben had stayed in the park.

One day, Spot found a big stick. He wanted to share it with his friends, so he tried to split it into smaller pieces. But it was too hard for him to do. Spot started to worry. He thought, "How can I share this stick with my friends if I can't split it?"
Just then, a wise old bird named Mr. Feather saw Spot's worry. He flew down and said, "Don't worry, Spot. I have an idea!" Mr. Feather called all of Spot's friends to come and help. Together, they all pulled on the stick until it split into many pieces.
Spot was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Feather and friends!" They all took a piece of the stick and played together. The day was filled with laughter and fun, and Spot learned that sharing and working together made everything better.

Anna and Ben like to play with beans. They have a big jar of beans in different colors. They like to pour the beans on the floor and make shapes and patterns with them.
One day, Anna has an idea. She says to Ben, "Let's count the beans. How many beans do we have?"
Ben nods and says, "OK. Let's count. You count the red beans and I count the green beans. Then we can see who has more."
They start to count the beans. Anna says, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. I have ten red beans."
Ben says, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve. I have twelve green beans. I have more than you."
Anna says, "No fair. You have more regular beans. I have some small beans and some big beans. They are not the same size. Let me count again."
She counts the red beans again. She says, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven. I have eleven red beans. I have one more than before."
Ben says, "How did you get one more? Did you take one of my beans?"
Anna says, "No, I did not. I found one more red bean under the jar. It was hiding. See, it is a small bean. It is hard to see."
Ben says, "Oh, I see. You are right. It is a small bean. Now we have the same number of beans. Ten plus one is eleven. Eleven plus eleven is twenty-two. We have twenty-two beans in total."
Anna says, "Wow, that is a lot of beans. We are good at counting. Counting is fun."
They smile and hug each other. Then they start to make new shapes and patterns with the beans. They are happy.

One day, Sam's tablet ran out of power. He tried to plug it in, but it did not work. He looked for another plug, but he could not find one. He was very sad and angry. He cried and shouted. He did not know what to do without his videos.
His mom came to see what was wrong. She saw Sam's tablet and his tears. She felt sorry for him, but she also wanted to teach him a lesson. She said, "Sam, you watch too many videos. You need to do other things, like play, read, and help. Videos are fun, but they are not everything. You need to balance your time and your activities. Do you understand?"
Sam nodded, but he still felt unhappy. He did not like to hear his mom's words. He felt uncomfortable. He wanted his videos back. He said, "But mom, I love videos. They make me happy. Can I have my tablet back, please?"
His mom said, "No, Sam. Not today. Today, you will do something else. You will help me dry the dishes. It is easy and fun. You will see." She took Sam to the kitchen and gave him a towel. She showed him how to dry the dishes and put them away. She smiled and praised him when he did a good job.
Sam did not like it at first. He thought it was boring and hard. He missed his videos. But as he dried the dishes, he started to enjoy it. He liked to see the dishes shine. He liked to hear his mom's voice. He liked to feel useful and proud. He realized that drying the dishes was not so bad. It was actually fun.
He finished drying the dishes and hugged his mom. He said, "Thank you, mom. I'm sorry I was rude. I learned my lesson. I will not watch videos all day. I will do other things, too. I will play, read, and help. I will balance my time and my activities. I understand now."
His mom hugged him back and said, "I'm proud of you, Sam. You are a good boy. You learned a valuable lesson. Videos are fun, but they are not everything. There is more to life than videos. You need to explore, learn, and grow. You need to be happy and healthy. You need to be yourself."
Sam smiled and said, "I love you, mom. You are the best. Can I watch one video now?"
His mom laughed and said, "Okay, Sam. Just one. But only after you eat your lunch. Deal?"
Sam agreed and said, "Deal. Thank you, mom. You are the best."
The end.

"Well, I'm sorry, but you'll have to wait until the dishwasher is done. Or you can play something else," mom said.
Lily and Ben were very upset. They wanted to make soup, not something else. They looked at each other and had an idea.
"Let's go to the store and buy a teaspoon!" Ben whispered.
"OK, let's go!" Lily whispered back.
They put on their shoes and coats and grabbed their piggy banks. They sneaked out of the house and walked to the corner store. They saw many things in the store: candy, toys, books, and more. But they only wanted a teaspoon. They found one that was shiny and small and perfect for soup. They took it to the cashier and paid with their coins.
"Thank you, come again!" the cashier said.
Lily and Ben were very happy. They ran back to their house with their new teaspoon. They stirred their soup and tasted it. It was delicious. They shared it with their mom, who was surprised and proud.
"Where did you get this teaspoon?" mom asked.
"We bought it at the store!" Lily and Ben said.
"You did? That's very clever of you. But next time, please ask me before you go out, OK? It's not safe to go alone," mom said.
"OK, mom. We're sorry. We just really wanted a teaspoon," Lily and Ben said.
Mom hugged them and smiled.
"I understand. You are very creative and adventurous. But you are also very young. And I love you very much," mom said.
Lily and Ben hugged her back and smiled.
"We love you too, mom. And we love our teaspoon!" they said.

Everyone in the town saw the cat with the hat on its tail. They laughed and clapped. The cat was surprised, but it liked the attention. So, the cat kept wearing the hat on its tail. And the yellow cat with the hat on its tail was the happiest cat in town.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big flower with many colors. Lily wanted to smell it, but Ben said no.
"That flower is fake. It is not real. It is made of paper and glue. It is for people to look at, not to touch," Ben said.
Lily was sad. She liked the flower. She thought it was pretty. She did not believe Ben. She went closer to the flower.
Suddenly, a bee came out of the flower. It buzzed and flew around Lily's head. Lily was scared. She screamed and ran away.
Ben laughed. He thought it was funny. He said, "I told you the flower was fake. The bee was fake too. It was a toy. I put it there to trick you. It was a joke."
Lily was angry. She did not like Ben's joke. She said, "That was not a joke. That was mean. You made me feel bad. You are not a good friend."
Ben felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. I was just having fun. Please forgive me. I will not do it again."
Lily looked at Ben. She saw he was sincere. She said, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But next time, be nice. Do not play tricks on me. Or on anyone else."
Ben nodded. He said, "You are right, Lily. I will be nice. I will not play tricks. I will be a good friend."
Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Do you want to play with me?"
Ben smiled too. He said, "Yes, Lily. I want to play with you. What do you want to play?"
Lily said, "How about we play with the slide? It is fun and real."
Ben agreed. He said, "OK, let's play with the slide. It is fun and real. And no more fake flowers or bees."
They held hands and ran to the slide. They played and laughed. They were happy.
The moral of the story is: Do not play tricks on your friends. It is not nice. It can hurt their feelings. Be honest and kind. That is how you make good friends.

One day, they decide to have a race with their cars. They find a long road near their house and draw a line with a stick. They put their cars behind the line and get ready to start.
"Are you ready, Sam?" Tom asks.
"Yes, I am ready, Tom," Sam answers.
"OK, let's go! One, two, three, go!" Tom shouts.
They push their cars as hard as they can. The cars zoom along the road. Tom's car is faster than Sam's car. It reaches the end of the road first. Tom is happy. He jumps and cheers.
"I win, I win!" Tom says.
Sam is sad. He walks to the end of the road and picks up his car. He looks at Tom's car and sighs.
"Your car is better than mine, Tom. It is big and fast. My car is small and slow. You are wealthy. I am poor," Sam says.
Tom hears Sam and feels sorry for him. He likes Sam and does not want him to be sad. He thinks for a moment and then smiles.
"Sam, do you want to play another game?" Tom asks.
"What game, Tom?" Sam asks.
"Let's play match. We can match our cars by color. You have a blue car and I have a red car. We can find other cars that are blue and red and put them together. It will be fun," Tom says.
Sam thinks and then nods.
"OK, Tom, let's play match. That sounds fun," Sam says.
Tom and Sam run to their house and look for other cars that are blue and red. They find many cars and match them by color. They make a big pile of blue cars and a big pile of red cars. They laugh and have fun. They forget about the race and the wealthy and the poor. They are just friends who like to play with cars.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big vine that grew on the wall. It had many green leaves and purple flowers.
"Let's climb the vine!" Tim said. "It looks like fun!"
Lily was not sure. "But what if we fall? Or what if Mom and Dad get angry?"
Tim shrugged. "Don't be scared. They won't see us. And the vine is tough. It can hold us."
He grabbed the vine and started to pull himself up. Lily followed him, but she felt nervous. The vine was high and wobbly.
They reached the top of the wall and looked around. They saw the neighbor's dog, a big and black one. It barked at them and ran towards the wall.
"Uh-oh!" Tim said. "The dog is mad at us! We have to go down!"
They tried to slide down the vine, but it was not easy. The vine was rough and scratchy. It hurt their hands and legs. The dog jumped and snapped at them.
"Help!" Lily cried. "Mom! Dad!"
Mom and Dad heard them and came outside. They saw Tim and Lily on the vine and the dog on the ground. They were shocked and worried.
"Tim! Lily! What are you doing?" Mom shouted. "Get down from there!"
Dad grabbed a stick and scared the dog away. He helped Tim and Lily down from the vine. They were dirty and bleeding.
Mom hugged them and checked their wounds. She was angry and sad.
"Why did you climb the vine?" she asked. "You could have been hurt badly! Or bitten by the dog! You know you are not allowed to do that!"
Tim and Lily looked down. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"We wanted to have fun," Tim said. "We thought the vine was tough."
"But it was not safe," Lily said. "We were wrong."
Mom and Dad took them inside and cleaned their wounds. They gave them a hug and a kiss.
"We love you, Tim and Lily," they said. "But you have to be careful and listen to us. We only want you to be safe and happy."
Tim and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They never climbed the vine again.

Tom liked to whistle. He whistled when he walked, when he played, and when he was happy. He learned to whistle from his dad, who whistled a lot too. Tom wanted to whistle like his dad, who could make different sounds and tunes with his mouth.
One day, Tom and his dad went to the park. They saw a big, modern building with glass and metal. Tom thought it looked shiny and cool. He asked his dad what it was.
"That's a museum, Tom. It's a place where people can see old and new things, like paintings and statues and machines. Do you want to go inside and look?" his dad said.
"Yes, please!" Tom said. He was curious and excited.
They went inside the museum and saw many things. Tom liked the colorful paintings and the funny statues. He also liked the machines that moved and made noises. He whistled along with some of them. His dad smiled and whistled with him.
They came to a room that had a sign that said "Rocks and Minerals". Tom saw many stones of different shapes and colors. Some were shiny, some were dull, some were smooth, some were rough. He wanted to touch them and feel them.
"Can I touch the stones, dad?" he asked.
"Sure, but be careful. Some of them are very old and fragile. And don't take any of them with you, okay? They belong to the museum," his dad said.
"Okay, dad," Tom said. He touched some of the stones gently. He liked how they felt in his hand. He saw one stone that was round and white. It had a hole in the middle. It looked like a donut. He thought it was funny and cute. He picked it up and put it in his pocket. He forgot what his dad said.
They left the museum and went back to the park. Tom and his dad played catch with a ball. Tom was happy and whistled. He felt the stone in his pocket. He wanted to show it to his dad.
"Dad, look what I found in the museum!" he said. He took out the stone and showed it to his dad.
"Tom, that's not yours. That's a fossil. It's a very old stone that has the shape of an animal that lived a long time ago. It's very rare and valuable. You can't take it from the museum. That's stealing. You have to give it back," his dad said. He was angry and disappointed.
Tom felt bad. He didn't know it was a fossil. He didn't mean to steal. He liked the stone, but he didn't want to make his dad mad. He wanted to do the right thing.
"I'm sorry, dad. I didn't know. I'll give it back. Please don't be mad at me," he said. He started to cry.
His dad hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you told me the truth. You made a mistake, but you can fix it. Let's go back to the museum and return the fossil. Maybe they'll let you whistle with the machines again."
Tom nodded and smiled. He wiped his tears and whistled. He held his dad's hand and walked back to the museum. He hoped they would forgive him. He learned a lesson. He would never take anything that wasn't his again. He would only whistle.

Once upon a time there were two brothers. One brother was called John and the other one was called Joe. John owned a reliable car and Joe owned a toy tooth. 
John and Joe got in a fight because Joe wanted to use John's car. John told Joe that he could not have the car because he owns a toy tooth. 
Joe was sad and did not understand why he could not have the car. He asked John why he could not have the car. 
John explained that he could not give him the car because it is important to be reliable and dependable. He said that he only wanted to lend his car to people who are reliable. 
Joe thought about this for awhile. He realized that it is important to be dependable and reliable so that when others need your help, you can give it to them. 
Joe decided to put away his toy tooth and work on gaining John's trust by being reliable and dependable. From that day forth, Joe and John became the best of friends. 
The moral of the story is that it is important to be reliable and dependable in order to be trusted by others.

"I want to see the crane," Lily said. "It is big and cool."
"You can't be here, it is dangerous," the man said. "The crane can hurt you, or you can fall. And there is fire over there, it can burn you. Go back to your house, now!"
Lily saw the fire. It was orange and red, and it was making smoke. It was coming from a pile of wood and metal. Lily felt scared. She did not like the fire. It was hot and bad.
"OK, I will go," Lily said. She climbed down from the fence and ran to her house. She did not want to see the crane anymore. She wanted to be safe and warm.
She told her mom what she saw. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm glad you are OK, Lily. You should never go near the crane or the fire. They are not for playing. They are for working. And you should always listen to the man in the yellow hat. He knows what is best."
Lily nodded. She learned her lesson. She was still curious, but she knew some things were better to watch from far away. She decided to play with her toys instead. She liked her toys. They were fun and nice.

Sam and Mia like to play in the park. They like to swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass. One day, they see a new thing in the park. It is a pitch. It has a big net and a small ball.
"Look, Mia, a pitch!" Sam says. "Let's play with the ball!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we play?" Mia asks.
Sam picks up the ball and throws it to Mia. Mia catches it and throws it back. They do this for a while, and then Sam has an idea.
"Let's swing the ball!" he says. "I will swing it to you, and you will swing it to me!"
"OK, Sam, but how do we swing the ball?" Mia asks.
Sam shows Mia how to swing the ball. He holds the ball in one hand, and swings his arm back and forth. Then he lets go of the ball, and it flies to Mia.
"Wow, Sam, you swing the ball so well!" Mia says. She tries to swing the ball back to Sam, but she swings too hard, and the ball goes over the net.
"Oh no, Mia, the ball is gone!" Sam says. "How will we get it back?"
They run to the net, and see that the ball is on the other side. There is a gate, but it is closed.
"Maybe we can open the gate," Mia says. She pushes the gate, but it does not move.
"Maybe we can climb the net," Sam says. He tries to climb the net, but it is too high.
They are sad, and do not know what to do. Then they hear a voice.
"Hello, kids, do you need some help?" the voice says.
They look up, and see a man. He is wearing a hat and a shirt with a logo. He is holding a big bag.
"Who are you?" Sam asks.
"I am the coach," the man says. "I work here at the pitch. I teach people how to play with the ball."
"Can you help us get our ball back?" Mia asks.
"Sure, I can," the coach says. "The gate is locked, but I have the key. Follow me."
The coach opens the gate, and walks to the other side. He picks up the ball, and gives it to Sam and Mia.
"Here you go, kids, your ball," he says. "Do you like to play with the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say. "We like to swing the ball."
"That's great," the coach says. "Do you want to learn more about how to swing the ball?"
"Yes, we do," Sam and Mia say.
"OK, then, come with me," the coach says. "I will show you some tips and tricks. And maybe you can join my team someday."
Sam and Mia are happy, and follow the coach. They learn how to swing the ball better, and have fun. They make a new friend, and find a new game. They like the pitch.

Lily loved to draw. She drew many things: flowers, animals, stars, and people. She used many colors and made her pictures bright and happy. She wanted to show her drawings to everyone.
One day, her teacher said they would have a drawing contest. The children could display their drawings on the wall and a judge would pick the best one. Lily was very enthusiastic. She thought she could win the contest. She worked hard on her drawing and made it very big and beautiful.
The next day, the children brought their drawings to school. Lily saw that the other children had different kinds of drawings. Some were small and simple, some were dark and scary, some were funny and silly. Lily thought her drawing was the best. She put it on the wall and waited for the judge.
The judge came and looked at all the drawings. He smiled and nodded and said nice things. He said he liked all the drawings because they showed the children's imagination and feelings. He said there was no best drawing, because every drawing was special and unique. He gave every child a sticker and a hug.
Lily felt confused. She thought her drawing was better than the others. She wanted to win the contest. She wanted the judge to say her drawing was the best. She felt angry and sad.
Her teacher saw her face and came to talk to her. She said, "Lily, why are you unhappy? You have a wonderful drawing and a sticker and a hug. You should be proud of yourself."
Lily said, "But I wanted to win. I wanted to have the best drawing. I worked so hard on it."
Her teacher said, "Lily, drawing is not a competition. Drawing is a way to express yourself and have fun. It doesn't matter if your drawing is big or small, bright or dark, happy or scary. What matters is that you enjoy drawing and share it with others. Everyone has a different style and a different story to tell. You can learn from other people's drawings and appreciate their creativity. You can also be happy for them and celebrate their achievements. That is the true meaning of drawing."
Lily thought about what her teacher said. She looked at the other children's drawings and saw that they were all different and interesting. She realized that she had been selfish and rude. She felt sorry and ashamed.
She said, "Teacher, I'm sorry. You are right. Drawing is not a competition. I was wrong to think that my drawing was the best. I should have been more respectful and kind to the other children. I want to apologize to them and tell them that I like their drawings."
Her teacher said, "That's very brave and mature of you, Lily. I'm proud of you. I'm sure the other children will forgive you and be your friends. Go ahead and talk to them. They are waiting for you."
Lily smiled and thanked her teacher. She went to the wall and looked at the other children's drawings. She found something nice to say about each one. She said sorry and gave them hugs. The other children smiled and thanked her. They said they liked her drawing too. They said they were happy to be her friends.
Lily felt happy and relieved. She learned a valuable lesson. She learned that drawing is not a competition, but a way to express yourself and have fun. She learned that everyone has a different style and a different story to tell. She learned that she should respect and appreciate other people's creativity. She learned that she should be happy for them and celebrate their achievements. She learned that drawing is a way to make friends and share joy. She learned that drawing is a wonderful thing.

Tim and Liz were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Let's enter the tree!" Tim said.
"OK, but be careful!" Liz said.
They crawled into the hole and found a dark and cozy space. They saw a trunk with a lock on it.
"Wow, what is in the trunk?" Liz wondered.
"Maybe it is a treasure!" Tim guessed.
They tried to open the trunk, but it was too hard. They pushed and pulled, but nothing happened.
Suddenly, they heard a voice.
"Who is there? What are you doing in my tree?" The voice was angry and loud.
Tim and Liz were scared. They saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was the owner of the tree and the trunk.
"We are sorry, sir. We were just playing. We did not mean to bother you." Tim said.
"You should not enter other people's homes without permission. That is rude and wrong. And you should not touch other people's things. That is stealing and bad." The man said.
Tim and Liz felt ashamed. They knew they had made a mistake.
"We are very sorry, sir. We will not do it again. Please forgive us." Liz said.
The man looked at them. He saw they were young and curious. He decided to be kind.
"OK, I forgive you. But you have to promise me to respect other people's property and privacy. And you have to leave now. This is my home, not a playground." The man said.
Tim and Liz nodded. They thanked the man and crawled out of the hole. They ran back to their parents and told them what happened. They learned a lesson that day. They never entered the tree again.

"Look, Tom, I have a whistle!" she said.
Tom looked at her and laughed. "That is not a whistle, Lila. That is a twig. You cannot whistle with a twig. You need a hole in it, like this." He showed her his whistle, which was a small plastic tube with a hole in the middle.
"Wow, can I try?" Lila asked.
"Sure, here you go." Tom gave her his whistle and took her twig. He blew on the twig, but nothing happened. He smiled and said, "See? It does not work."
Lila put the whistle in her mouth and blew hard. She made a loud sound that scared some birds. She was very happy and said, "Look, Tom, I can whistle!"
Tom clapped and said, "Good job, Lila! You are very smart. Can I have my whistle back?"
Lila nodded and gave him his whistle. They took turns whistling and laughing. They did not see a hidden squirrel that was watching them from a tree. The squirrel was curious and wanted to try the whistle too. It waited until Lila and Tom were busy with something else, and then it jumped down and grabbed the whistle. It ran away with it, making a funny noise.
Lila and Tom heard the noise and looked around. They saw the squirrel with the whistle in its mouth. They were surprised and said, "Hey, that is our whistle! Give it back, squirrel!"
They chased the squirrel, but it was too fast and too clever. It climbed up another tree and hid the whistle in a hole. Lila and Tom could not reach it. They were sad and said, "Oh, no, we lost our whistle. How will we whistle now?"
They looked at each other and had an idea. They put their lips together and blew. They made a sound that was like a whistle, but softer and sweeter. They smiled and said, "Look, Tom, look, Lila, we can whistle with our mouths!"
They whistled with their mouths and forgot about the whistle and the squirrel. They were happy and had fun. The squirrel watched them and felt sorry. "Help! Help!" they shouted. "We are lost in the maze!"

They ran out of the maze and hugged each other. They also saw their mom and dad waiting for them. They were worried and angry.
"Where were you, Ben and Lily?" mom asked. "We were looking for you everywhere. You should not go into the maze without us. It is dangerous and you could get hurt."
"We are sorry, mom and dad," Ben and Lily said. "We wanted to have fun, but we got lost and dizzy. We learned our lesson. We will not go into the maze again without you."
Mom and dad hugged them and forgave them. They also praised them for finding the fountain and the sign. They said they were brave and smart.
Ben and Lily felt happy and loved. They learned that the maze was not as fun as they thought, and that they should always listen to their parents and stay together. They also learned that water can help them when they are thirsty and dizzy. They thanked the fountain and the sign for helping them. They went home and had a nice nap.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They had a small house made of wood and a big box of toys. They liked to pretend they were animals and make noises.
"Let's be lions today," said Tom. "We can roar and hunt and feed on other animals."
"Okay," said Lily. "But I want to be a nice lion, not a mean one."
They put on their lion masks and ran around the garden. They saw a bird on a tree and tried to catch it, but it flew away. They saw a cat on the fence and tried to scare it, but it hissed and scratched them. They saw a dog on the street and tried to chase it, but it barked and ran away.
They were hungry and tired. They went back to their small house and looked for something to eat. They found a bowl of soup that Mom had left for them. It smelled good and looked yummy.
"Let's feed on this soup," said Tom. "It will make us strong and happy."
They took a spoon each and dipped it in the soup. They put it in their mouths and made a face. The soup was very hot and spicy. It burned their tongues and made them cough.
"Ow, ow, ow!" they cried. "This soup is not good for lions. It is too spicy. It hurts."
They spit out the soup and ran to the tap. They drank some water and felt better. They looked at the bowl of soup and had an idea.
"Let's escape from this soup," said Lily. "We can give it to someone else who likes spicy food."
They picked up the bowl and carried it to the fence. They saw the cat that had scratched them before. It was licking its paws and looking bored.
"Hey, cat," said Tom. "Do you want some soup? It is very tasty and good for you."
The cat looked at the bowl and sniffed it. It smelled the spices and licked its lips. It liked spicy food. It jumped off the fence and took the bowl.
"Thank you, lions," said the cat. "This soup is perfect for me. It is not too spicy. It is just right."
The cat ate the soup and purred. Lily and Tom smiled and waved. They were glad they had found a friend who liked spicy food. They went back to their small house and played some more. They decided to be different animals tomorrow.
