"Yes, please!" Sam said. "It looks yummy. Thank you for sharing."
They pretended to eat the cake. They made funny noises with their mouths. They laughed and smiled.
Suddenly, they saw a big dog. It was brown and furry. It had a long tail and a wet nose. It appeared from behind a tree. It ran towards them. It wanted to play.
"Wow, a dog!" Lily said. "Hello, dog. What is your name?"
The dog barked. It wagged its tail. It licked Lily's face. She giggled.
"Hi, dog. You are friendly. Do you want to play with us?" Sam said.
The dog nodded. It sniffed their cake. It looked tasty. It took a bite.
"Hey, that's our cake!" Lily said. "You can't eat that. It's not real. It's made of leaves."
The dog spit out the leaves. It made a funny face. It did not like the taste. It looked sorry.
"It's okay, dog. We forgive you. You didn't know." Sam said. "But you can't have our cake. You can have this stick instead. Do you like sticks?"
The dog barked. It liked sticks. It took the stick from Sam. It ran away. It came back. It dropped the stick. It wanted Sam to throw it.
"Okay, dog. Let's play fetch. Ready?" Sam said.
He threw the stick. The dog ran after it. It caught it. It brought it back. They played fetch for a long time.
Lily and Sam had fun with the dog. They were happy. They made a new friend. They forgot about their cake. They did not mind. They had something better. They had a dog.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with her dolls and dress up in her mom's clothes. She had a pretty veil that she found in a box in the attic. It was white and soft and had flowers on it. She liked to wear it and pretend she was a princess or a bride.
One day, her mom told her they were going to visit her aunt and uncle and their new baby. Lily was excited to see the baby, but she was also nervous to meet new people. She decided to wear her veil to feel more confident and pretty. She put it on and looked at herself in the mirror. She smiled and said, "I am a princess today."
Her mom saw her and said, "You look lovely, Lily, but you have to be careful with the veil. It is very old and delicate. It belonged to your great-grandma. She wore it on her wedding day. It is a special thing that we have to keep safe. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I will behave and take good care of the veil. I promise."
They got in the car and drove to her aunt and uncle's house. Lily held the veil gently in her lap and looked out the window. She saw trees and flowers and birds. She felt happy and curious.
When they arrived, her aunt and uncle greeted them warmly and invited them in. They showed them the baby, who was sleeping in a crib. He was small and cute and had a lot of hair. Lily wanted to touch him, but she was afraid to wake him up. She stayed close to her mom and said hello in a quiet voice.
Her aunt and uncle had a big dog, who was friendly and playful. He saw Lily and ran to her, wagging his tail and barking. He wanted to say hello and play with her. He jumped on her and licked her face. Lily was scared and tried to push him away. She dropped the veil on the floor. The dog saw it and thought it was a toy. He grabbed it with his teeth and ran away.
Lily screamed and cried. She ran after the dog and tried to get the veil back. She was very upset and angry. She forgot to behave and be careful. She yelled, "Bad dog! Give me back my veil! It is mine!"
Her mom and her aunt and uncle heard her and came to help. They saw the dog and the veil and understood what happened. They called the dog and took the veil from him. They checked it and saw that it was torn and dirty. They felt sorry and sad.
They hugged Lily and said, "We are sorry, Lily. The dog didn't know it was a special thing. He thought it was a fun thing. He didn't mean to hurt it or you. He was just being a dog. He likes you and wants to be your friend. Can you forgive him?"
Lily looked at the dog and saw that he was wagging his tail and looking at her with big eyes. He seemed to say, "I am sorry, Lily. I like you. Can we play?"
Lily felt her anger and sadness go away. She realized that the dog was not bad, just silly. She also realized that the veil was not the most important thing. The most important thing was her family and the baby and the dog. She smiled and said, "It's okay, dog. I forgive you. Let's play."
She hugged the dog and gave him a kiss. She hugged her mom and said, "I am sorry, mom. I didn't behave and take good care of the veil. I broke my promise."
Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are still my princess. And you know what? I have something for you. A surprise."
She took out a box from her bag and opened it. Inside was a new veil, just like the old one, but shiny and clean. It had a note that said, "To Lily, from your great-grandma. She wanted you to have this. She loved you very much."
Lily gasped and said, "Wow! Thank you, mom! Thank you, great-grandma! This is the best surprise ever!"
She put on the new veil and felt happy and proud. She showed it to her aunt and uncle and the baby and the dog. They all said, "You look beautiful, Lily. You are a princess today."
Lily said, "Thank you. I love you all. And I love the veil. But I will be more careful with it. I promise."

Max did not listen. He tried to grab the rock from Lily. They both pulled and pushed. The rock fell on the ground. It broke into two pieces.
Lily and Max both cried. They were sad and tired. They had lost their pretty rock.
Mom came and saw them crying. She said, "What happened, Lily and Max?"
Lily and Max told Mom what happened. Mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily and Max. You both made a mistake. You should not fight over a rock. You should be kind and gentle to each other. You are friends, not enemies."
Lily and Max said, "We're sorry, Mom. We're sorry, Lily. We're sorry, Max."
Mom said, "It's okay, Lily and Max. I forgive you. Do you forgive each other?"
Lily and Max nodded. They hugged each other. They said, "We forgive you, Lily. We forgive you, Max."
Mom said, "That's good, Lily and Max. Now, let's go home and have some juice and cookies. You must be thirsty and hungry."
Lily and Max said, "Yes, Mom. We are thirsty and hungry. And we are tired too."
Mom said, "Then let's go home and rest. You can play again tomorrow. Maybe you will find another pretty rock. Or something else."
Lily and Max said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom."
They held Mom's hand and walked home. They were still sad about the rock, but they were happy to have each other. They learned a lesson. They learned to share and not to demand.

Lily liked to sign with her hands. She learned sign from her mom, who was deaf. Lily could hear, but she loved to talk with her mom in sign. She also liked to teach sign to her friends at school.
One day, a new boy came to her class. His name was Ben. He was very big and had a lot of weight. He looked mean and scary. He did not talk to anyone. He just sat in his seat and frowned.
Lily wanted to be nice to Ben. She thought maybe he was lonely or sad. She walked up to him and smiled. She said hello with her voice and her hands. She asked him his name in sign.
Ben looked at her and laughed. He said, "What are you doing with your hands? Are you crazy? That's not how you talk. You talk with your mouth, like this." He made a loud and rude noise with his mouth.
Lily felt hurt and angry. She ran away and cried. She did not understand why Ben was so mean. She did not want to be his friend.
The next day, Lily's mom came to her class. She wanted to show the kids how to sign. She said sign was a beautiful and fun way to communicate. She said sign was for everyone, not just for deaf people. She said sign was a gift that Lily shared with her.
Lily was happy to see her mom. She hugged her and signed, "I love you, mom." She also saw Ben. He was sitting in his seat and frowning. He did not look happy.
Lily's mom asked the kids if they wanted to learn some sign. All the kids raised their hands and said yes. Except for Ben. He said no. He said sign was stupid and silly. He said he did not want to learn it.
Lily's mom looked at him and smiled. She said, "That's okay, Ben. You don't have to learn sign. But you should know that sign is not stupid or silly. It is a way to express yourself and connect with others. It is a way to show respect and kindness. It is a way to make friends. Maybe one day, you will change your mind and want to try sign. I hope you do. Because sign is not just for deaf people. It is for people who want to listen with their hearts."
Lily's mom then taught the kids some sign. They learned how to say hello, goodbye, thank you, and sorry. They learned how to say their names and their favorite colors. They learned how to say they were happy, sad, angry, or scared. They had a lot of fun.
Lily looked at Ben. He was still sitting in his seat and frowning. He did not join the fun. He did not learn any sign. He did not make any friends.
Lily felt sorry for Ben. She thought maybe he was lonely or sad. She walked up to him and smiled. She said goodbye with her voice and her hands. She said, "I hope you have a good day, Ben. Maybe tomorrow, you will want to learn sign with us. Maybe tomorrow, you will want to be my friend."
Ben looked at her and did not say anything. He did not laugh or make a rude noise. He just watched her walk away. He saw her sign with her mom and her friends. He saw her happy and ordinary. He felt something in his chest. He did not know what it was. He wondered if it was his heart. He wondered if it wanted to listen.

Lily gives the shell to Ben. He holds it to his ear and listens.
"I hear the sea!" Ben says.
Lily wants to hear too. She takes the shell back and puts it to her ear.
"I hear it too!" Lily says.
They smile and laugh. They put the shell in their bucket with other shells. They want to take them home and show Mom and Dad.
But then they see something in the water. It is big and long and has a fin. It is a shark!
"Look, Lily, a shark!" Ben says.
Lily and Ben are scared. They drop the bucket and run to Mom and Dad.
"Mom, Dad, there is a shark in the water!" Lily and Ben say.
Mom and Dad look at the water. They see the shark too. It is far away and does not come close to the shore.
"Don't worry, Lily and Ben, the shark is not going to hurt you. It is just swimming and looking for food. It is not interested in you or your shells," Mom says.
"Are you sure, Mom?" Lily asks.
"Yes, I am sure, Lily. Sharks are animals that live in the sea. They are not bad, they are just different. Sometimes they rise to the surface to breathe or to see what is around them. But they usually stay away from people," Dad says.
Lily and Ben feel better. They go back to their bucket and pick up their shells. They still like the shells, but they also like to watch the shark. They think it is cool and amazing. They learn something new about the sea.

One day, Tom finds a pen on the table. He picks it up and looks at it. He thinks it is a magic pen. He wants to write with it. He opens a book and writes on a page. He writes his name and a smiley face.
"Tom, what are you doing?" Mom asks. She sees Tom with the pen and the book. She is not happy. She takes the pen and the book from Tom. "This is not your pen. This is my pen. And this is not your book. This is a library book. You cannot write on library books. You have to be careful with books. They are not toys."
Tom feels sad. He did not know he did something bad. He likes books. He does not want to hurt them. He says sorry to Mom. He says sorry to the book. He hugs the book.
Mom sees Tom is sorry. She hugs Tom. She says, "It's okay, Tom. I know you love books. But you have to respect them. You can read them, but you cannot write on them. If you want to write, you can use your own paper and crayons. And you can ask me before you use my pen. Do you understand?"
Tom nods. He understands. He says, "Yes, Mom. I understand. Can I read another book?"
Mom smiles. She says, "Yes, you can. But first, let's return this book to the library. And let's say sorry to the librarian. Maybe she will let you borrow another book. A lively book with lots of colors and sounds. Would you like that?"
Tom smiles. He says, "Yes, Mom. I would like that. Thank you, Mom. You are the best."
Mom and Tom go to the library. They return the book and say sorry to the librarian. The librarian is kind. She says, "It's okay, Tom. I'm glad you like books. Here, you can borrow this book. It's a lively book. It has animals and music and jokes. I think you will enjoy it."
Tom takes the book. He says, "Thank you, librarian. This book looks fun. I will read it and take good care of it. I will not write on it. I promise."
Mom and Tom go home. They sit on the couch. They read the lively book together. They laugh and sing and learn. They have a good time. They love books. And they love each other.

When they got to the big boat, they saw a man with a sad face. He was sitting on the deck and looking at a map. He had a big hat and a long coat. He looked like a pirate.
"Hello, sir," Lila said. "We are Lila and Ben. We came to see your boat. Can we look around?"
The man looked at them and smiled a little. "Hello, Lila and Ben. I am Jack. I am a pirate, but not a bad one. You can look around, but be careful. There are many things on this boat that are not for children."
"Thank you, Jack. Why are you sad?" Ben asked.
Jack sighed and pointed at the map. "I am sad because I am looking for a treasure. It is on a small island far away. But I do not know how to get there. The map is old and hard to read. I have been sailing for a long time, but I have not found the island. I am troubled and tired."
Lila and Ben looked at the map. They saw a picture of an island with a big X on it. They also saw some words and numbers. They did not know what they meant, but they tried to help.
"Maybe we can help you, Jack. We know some things about the water and the sky. We can look for signs that show us where to go. Maybe we can find the island together," Lila said.
Jack looked at them and smiled more. He felt a little hope in his heart. He liked Lila and Ben. They were brave and kind. He decided to let them help him.
"Thank you, Lila and Ben. You are good friends. Maybe you are right. Maybe we can find the island together. Come, let us sail and see what we can find." He took them by the hand and led them to the helm. He showed them how to steer the boat and look for clues. They sailed away from the beach and into the blue sea. They hoped to find the island and the treasure. They were happy and excited. They had met a pirate and started an adventure.

Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around for Ben, but she could not see him. She heard a noise behind a big tree. She ran to the tree and shouted, "I found you, Ben!"
But it was not Ben. It was a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. The dog barked at Lily and wagged its tail. Lily was scared and ran away. She forgot about Ben and the game. She wanted to find her mom.
Ben was hiding under a slide. He heard Lily scream and the dog bark. He wondered what happened. He waited for Lily to come back and find him, but she did not. He felt lonely and sad. He wanted to play with Lily. He wanted to hear her voice.
He crawled out from under the slide and looked for Lily. He saw her running to her mom, who was sitting on a bench. He followed her and called her name. Lily heard Ben and turned around. She saw him and smiled. She ran to him and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was scared of the dog. It reminded me of the bad dog that bit me once. Are you mad at me?"
Ben shook his head and said, "No, I'm not mad. I was worried about you. I'm glad you're okay. The dog was not bad. It was just clumsy. It wanted to play with you, too. But I understand. Sometimes I'm scared of things that remind me of bad things, too. Like the dark and the silence. They remind me of the night when the storm came and the lights went out."
Lily nodded and said, "I don't like the dark and the silence, either. They make me feel alone. But we're not alone. We have each other. And we have our mom. She loves us and protects us. She's not scared of anything."
Ben and Lily hugged their mom and thanked her for being there. They decided to play a different game, one that did not involve hiding or dogs. They played tag and laughed and had fun. They forgot about their fears and enjoyed their day. They were happy.

"Maybe she is looking for a new home," Lily said.
"Maybe she is visiting her friends," Ben said.
They heard mom calling them again.
"Come on, kids, time's up! Lunch is ready!"
Lily and Ben said goodbye to the ants and ran to the house. They were hungry and curious. They wanted to learn more about the ants and the queen. They decided to come back to the garden later and look for them again.

"My doll is not ugly," Tom said to Sara. "He has a stitch because he is brave. He is special."
Sara did not listen. She grabbed Tom's doll and ran away. She wanted to open the stitch and see what was inside.
"Give me back my doll!" Tom shouted. He chased Sara around the room.

Tom shook his head. He smiled.
"There is nothing inside," he said. "Only stuffing. And love. My grandma said the stitch is a sign of love. She loves me and I love her. And I love my doll. Do you want to play with him?"
Sara nodded. She felt sorry. She wanted to be friends with Tom.
"OK," she said. "But can I play with your doll's hair?"
Tom laughed. He nodded.
"OK," he said. "But can I play with your doll's dress?"
They smiled. They opened the door and went to play. They shared their dolls and their stories. They learned to be kind and respectful. They became good friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play games. One day, they find a big box of cards in the attic. The cards have pictures of animals, fruits, and shapes.
"Look, Ben, these cards are interesting. Let's play with them," Lily says.
"OK, Lily, but how do we play?" Ben asks.
Lily thinks for a moment. She has an idea. "Let's play dare. I pick a card and show it to you. You have to do what the card says. If you don't, you lose. Then you pick a card and show it to me. I have to do what the card says. If I don't, I lose. The one who does more cards wins. Do you want to play?"
Ben nods. He likes challenges. He says, "Yes, I want to play. You go first, Lily."
Lily picks a card. It has a picture of a monkey. She shows it to Ben. She says, "Dare. You have to act like a monkey. You have to make monkey sounds and jump around."
Ben laughs. He thinks it is funny. He says, "OK, Lily, I can do that." He starts to make monkey sounds and jump around. Lily claps. She says, "Good job, Ben. You did it. Now it is my turn."
Ben picks a card. It has a picture of a banana. He shows it to Lily. He says, "Dare. You have to eat a banana. You have to peel it and bite it."
Lily makes a face. She does not like bananas. She says, "No, Ben, I don't want to do that. I don't like bananas. They are yucky."
Ben smiles. He says, "Sorry, Lily, but you have to do it. It is the rule. If you don't, you lose."
Lily thinks. She does not want to lose. She says, "OK, Ben, I will do it. But you have to give me something else to eat after. Something sweet."
Ben agrees. He says, "OK, Lily, I will give you something sweet after. But you have to eat the banana first."
Lily takes the banana. She peels it and bites it. She makes a sour face. She says, "Blech. I don't like it. It is mushy and sticky."
Ben gives her a glass of water. He says, "Here, Lily, drink some water. It will help."
Lily drinks the water. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Now, what is the sweet thing you have for me?"
Ben picks another card. It has a picture of a candy. He shows it to Lily. He says, "Dare. You have to eat this candy. You have to unwrap it and put it in your mouth."
Lily smiles. She likes candy. She says, "Yes, Ben, I want to do that. I like candy. It is yummy."
Ben gives her the candy. She unwraps it and puts it in her mouth. She says, "Mmm. I like it. It is sweet and crunchy."
Ben says, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. You are a good friend. You did the dare. You are brave."
Lily says, "Thank you, Ben. You are brave too. You did the monkey dare. That was funny. I had fun playing with you."
Ben says, "Me too, Lily. I had fun playing with you. These cards are interesting. Let's play again tomorrow."
Lily says, "OK, Ben, let's play again tomorrow. But next time, let's pick different cards. Maybe we will find something more fun."
They hug and put the cards back in the box. They go downstairs to find their moms. They are happy. They are friends.

Max's friend, a little girl named Lily, saw him chewing the stick. She wanted to play with Max. So, she ran to her house and came back with a big mug. She filled the mug with water and said, "Max, let's play with this mug!"
Max wagged his tail and stopped chewing the stick. He looked at the mug and barked, "Okay, Lily! I want to play with the mug!" Max and Lily played with the mug all day. They splashed water on each other and laughed.
When the sun went down, Max and Lily were tired but happy. They said goodbye and went to their homes. Max knew he had a great friend in Lily, and he couldn't wait to play with her and the mug again.

Sam and Lily were playing soldiers in the garden. They had sticks for guns and hats for helmets. They liked to order each other and march around.
"Sam, you are the captain," Lily said. "You can order me what to do."
"OK, Lily, you are a good soldier," Sam said. "First, we have to march to the big tree. Then, we have to hide behind it and look for enemies. Are you ready?"
"Yes, captain, I am ready," Lily said. "Let's march!"
They marched to the big tree, holding their sticks and hats. They made loud noises with their mouths, like guns and bombs. They felt very jolly and brave.
But when they reached the big tree, they saw something that made them stop. It was a big, furry, black dog. It was wagging its tail and licking its lips. It looked very friendly, but also very hungry.
"Uh-oh, captain, what do we do?" Lily asked. "Is that an enemy?"
Sam looked at the dog and thought for a moment. He had an idea.
"No, Lily, that is not an enemy. That is a friend. A friend who needs some food. Let's order him some food from the kitchen. Maybe he will join our army."
"Good idea, captain," Lily said. "Let's order him some food."
They ran to the kitchen and asked their mom for some food for the dog. Their mom gave them some bread and cheese and a bowl of water. They took the food and ran back to the garden.
"Here, doggy, we have some food for you," Sam said. "We are soldiers and we want you to be our friend. Do you want to play with us?"
The dog barked happily and ate the food. He licked Sam and Lily's faces and wagged his tail. He followed them as they marched around the garden. He was a jolly dog and a good soldier. Sam and Lily were very happy. They had a new friend.

Tom takes the brush off his head and says, "I'm okay, Sara. It was just a little bump. But your brush is not pretty anymore. It is dirty and bent. Do you want to clean it?"
Sara nods and says, "Yes, Tom, thank you. Let's go to the sink and wash it. And let's put the car away. It is too wild for us."
Sara and Tom go to the sink and wash the brush. Then they put the car and the blocks back in the box. They hug and say, "We are still friends, right?"
They smile and say, "Yes, we are still friends. And we still like to play with cars. But maybe not with that one."

Sam and Lily nodded. They started to pick up their toys and put them back in the box. But Sam saw something shiny on the floor. It was a stamp. A big stamp with a picture of a lion on it.
"Wow, look at this!" Sam said, holding the stamp. "It's so big and pretty!"
"Where did you find it?" Lily asked, coming closer.
"It was under the sofa," Sam said. "Maybe it fell from one of the books."
"Can I see it?" Lily asked, reaching for the stamp.
"No, it's mine!" Sam said, pulling the stamp away. "I found it first!"
They both wanted the stamp. They started to tug and pull on it. They did not hear Mom coming back.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said, taking the stamp from them. "This is not a toy. This is a special stamp that Dad gave me. It's very old and rare. You could have damaged it or lost it."
"Sorry, Mom," Sam and Lily said, feeling ashamed.
Mom looked at the stamp. She saw that it had a mark on the back. It said "reverse".
"Do you know what this means?" Mom asked, showing them the mark.
Sam and Lily shook their heads.
"It means that this stamp is even more special. It was printed the wrong way. The lion is facing the opposite direction. That makes it very valuable and unique. Dad was very lucky to find it."
"Wow," Sam and Lily said, looking at the stamp with wonder.
Mom smiled. She decided to let them keep the stamp, but only if they promised to be careful with it and share it.
"Thank you, Mom," Sam and Lily said, hugging her.
They put the stamp in a safe place. They decided to play with their cars again, but this time they were more gentle and tidy. They also learned a new word: reverse.

Jack and Jane listened to their mom and decided to share the toy. They hugged each other, happy to have such a special new toy. They promised to share all their future toys. From then on, Jack and Jane had many happy days exploring the modern mall.

Ben screams. He feels pain. He sees blood. He is scared.

The moms hear the screams. They run to the cage. They see the bear and Ben. They are shocked. They are angry.
They call for help. They pull Ben away from the cage. They wrap his hand with a cloth. They take him to the doctor.
The bear does not care. He licks his lips. He lies down again.

Mom nodded and said, "Yes, Anna, you can bounce later, when the rain stops. But for now, let's go to the kitchen and have some fun."
Anna smiled and said, "OK, mom, let's go. Maybe bouncing is not the only fun thing to do."

The end.

"Yes, they are polite!" they say together.
Their mom shakes her head. She says, "Polite means you follow the rules and respect others. The school has a rule that you wear blue and red. If you wear different colors, you might make the teacher and the other kids unhappy. They might think you are rude or silly."
Tim and Anna do not want to make anyone unhappy. They do not want to be rude or silly. They want to be polite.

Tim and Anna think about it. They like the idea of having a weekend uniform. They nod and say, "Okay, mom. That sounds good."

"No, it is mine, I saw it first!" Ben yelled.
They pulled and tugged at the jewel, but it was too hard to break. They got angry and sad, and forgot to have fun.
A lady who was walking her dog saw them and came over. She smiled and said, "Hello, children. Why are you fighting over this jewel?"
Lily and Ben stopped and looked at her. They felt ashamed and said, "We both want it, it is so pretty."
The lady nodded and said, "I understand, but do you know what this jewel is? It is not a real jewel, it is a candy. You can eat it, but only if you share it."
She took the jewel and broke it in half. She gave one half to Lily and one half to Ben. They looked at the candy and saw that it was dry and hard. It did not taste very good, but they were polite and said, "Thank you, lady."
The lady said, "You are welcome, children. Next time, remember to be kind and generous. Sharing is better than fighting, and real jewels are not always what they seem."
Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We are sorry, lady. We will share and be nice to each other."
They hugged and said sorry to each other. Then they threw away the candy and went to play on the swings. They learned their lesson and had a happy day.

Lily and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a big pond with many birds. Lily liked the white birds with long necks. Mom said they were swans. Ben liked the brown birds with big beaks. Mom said they were ducks.
"Can we buy a swan, Mom?" Lily asked. She wanted to take one home and play with it.
"No, dear, we can't buy a swan. Swans are wild animals. They belong to the pond. They would not be happy in our house," Mom said.
"But they are so pretty and soft," Lily said. She reached out her hand to touch a swan that came close to the shore.
"Careful, Lily, swans can be rough. They might bite you if you bother them," Mom said.
Just then, the swan hissed and snapped at Lily's hand. Lily pulled back and cried. Ben laughed and said, "See, Lily, swans are not nice. Ducks are better. They are friendly and quack."
Mom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily, the swan didn't hurt you. It was just scared of you. Swans are not toys, they are living creatures. We can admire them from a distance, but we can't touch them or buy them."
Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She looked at the swan and said, "Sorry, swan, I didn't mean to make you angry. You are very beautiful, but I will leave you alone."
The swan swam away and joined the other swans. Lily and Ben watched them for a while, then they fed some bread to the ducks. The ducks were happy and quacked. Lily and Ben smiled and had fun. Mom took a picture of them and said, "What a lovely day at the park!"

Frank thought about it for a moment and decided it was a good idea. He hopped out from under the bush and followed the rabbit. 
The two friends eventually made it to the far end of the field, safe and warm.  When the storm passed, the bright sunlight shone down and made the field come alive again. 
The moral of this story is that it is always better to tell the truth. Lying can cause you to feel scared and lonely. An honest friend is a dead friend and one honest word can be worth more than a thousand false ones.

Sara loved books. She liked to look at the pictures and listen to the stories. She had many books at home, but she always wanted more. One day, she went to the library with her mom. She saw a brilliant book on the shelf. It had a shiny cover and a big dragon on it. She wanted to take it home.
"Mom, can I have this book?" she asked.
"Sure, honey, but you have to pay for it," her mom said.
"Pay? What is pay?" Sara asked.
"Pay means you give something to get something. If you want this book, you have to give the librarian some money. Then you can borrow the book for a few weeks. But you have to bring it back, or you have to pay more money," her mom explained.
Sara nodded. She took the book to the librarian. The librarian scanned the book and told Sara how much money she had to pay. Sara gave the librarian some coins from her piggy bank. The librarian gave her a receipt and a date. She said Sara had to return the book by that date, or she would have to pay a fine.
Sara thanked the librarian and hugged the book. She was so happy. She went home with her mom and read the book. She loved the story and the pictures. She read the book every day until the date came. Then she remembered what her mom and the librarian had said. She had to bring the book back, or she had to pay more money.
Sara did not want to pay more money. She also did not want to keep the book from other children who might want to read it. She decided to do the right thing. She put the book in her backpack and went to the library with her mom. She gave the book to the librarian and said goodbye to the dragon. The librarian smiled and said Sara was a good girl. She did not have to pay any fine. She also gave Sara a sticker and a new book to borrow.
Sara was proud of herself. She learned that paying was fair and that returning was kind. She also learned that there were many brilliant books in the library. She could not wait to read them all.

Tom and Lily were playing in the backyard. They had a big box that they pretended was a spaceship. They took turns being the pilot and the co-pilot.
"Tom, it's my turn to be the pilot now," Lily said. "You have been the pilot for a long time."
"No, I want to be the pilot more," Tom said. "You can be the co-pilot again."
"But that's not fair," Lily said. "We have to share the box. And the co-pilot seat is uncomfortable. It has a hole in it."
Tom did not listen to Lily. He stayed in the pilot seat and made spaceship noises. Lily was angry. She got out of the box and walked away.
"Fine, then I will play something else," she said.
She saw a ball on the grass. She picked it up and threw it at the box. The ball hit the box hard and made a loud sound. Tom was scared. He jumped out of the box and looked at Lily.
"Why did you do that?" he asked. "You broke our spaceship."
"I didn't break it," Lily said. "I just wanted to pay you back for being mean to me. You didn't share the box with me."
Tom felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He went to Lily and gave her a hug.
"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "You are right. We have to share the box. Do you want to be the pilot now?"
Lily smiled. She forgave Tom. She took his hand and they went back to the box.
"OK, I will be the pilot now," she said. "But you can be the pilot again later. And we can fix the hole in the co-pilot seat."
They got into the box and resumed their spaceship adventure. They were happy and had fun. They learned to share and be nice to each other.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys, but they do not like to share. One day, they find a big book in the attic. The book has many pictures and words. It is a quiz book about ancient things.
Tim wants to look at the book. He likes to learn new things. He opens the book and sees a picture of a pyramid. He reads the question: "What is the name of this ancient building?" He thinks hard.
Sam wants to look at the book too. He likes to see the pictures. He tries to grab the book from Tim. He says: "Give me the book! It is my turn!"
Tim does not want to give the book. He says: "No, it is not your turn! I found the book first! Go away!"
Sam does not go away. He pulls the book harder. Tim pulls the book harder too. They both shout and cry.
Mom hears the noise. She comes to the attic. She sees Tim and Sam fighting over the book. She is angry. She says: "Stop it, both of you! You are being very naughty! You need to share and take turns!"
She takes the book from them. She says: "This book is too old and fragile for you. You might break it or tear it. It is an ancient book. It belongs to Grandpa. He gave it to me when I was little. He loves this book very much."

The thunder got louder and the sky got darker. Jack was scared, but he asked his mom, "Can I raise the window and see?"
His mom said, "Yes, you can, but be very brave. The thunder can be loud, but it won't hurt you."
Jack carefully opened the window and saw dark clouds in the sky. He was amazed. He saw lightning and he heard thunder, but he wasn't scared. He was brave.
When the storm passed, Jack smiled. He said, "Mom, look. The sky is bright now. I'm so glad I was brave!" 
His mom said, "I'm proud of you, Jack. Now, it's time for bed."
Jack smiled and went back to sleep. He was brave and he was happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They ran to the slide and took turns going down. "Whee!" they shouted.
But then, they saw something else. Behind the slide, there was a door. It was small and brown and had a sign that said "Do not enter". Tom and Lily were curious. They wanted to see what was behind the door. They looked at their mom, who was talking on her phone. She did not see them.
"Let's go," Tom said. "Maybe there is a secret place."
"Okay," Lily said. "But be careful. It might be scary."
They opened the door and went inside. It was dark and cold. They saw some stairs going up. They decided to climb them. They held hands and walked slowly. They heard some noises. They sounded like growls and hisses.
"What is that?" Lily asked. "I don't like it."
"Me neither," Tom said. "Maybe we should go back."
But it was too late. As they reached the top of the stairs, they saw a big cage. And inside the cage, there was an unknown animal. It had fur and claws and teeth. It looked angry and hungry. It saw Tom and Lily and roared.
"Help!" Tom and Lily screamed. "Mom!"
Their mom heard them and ran to the door. She saw the animal and the cage and the stairs. She was shocked and scared. She grabbed Tom and Lily and pulled them out of the door. She slammed it shut and locked it.
"Are you okay?" she asked. "What were you doing in there?"
"We were sorry, mom," Tom and Lily said. "We wanted to see the secret place. But it was not fun. It was bad. There was an unknown animal. It was scary."
Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you're safe. But you should never go to places you don't know. They can be dangerous. You should always listen to the signs and to me. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We won't do it again."
Mom smiled and said, "Good. Now let's go home and have some cookies. And forget about the unknown animal."
But they never forgot. They always wondered what it was and why it was in the park. And they never went near the door again.

She stumbled upon a vegetable patch in the corner of the garden. She had never seen anything like it before. All the vegetables were wonderfully unusual looking! Jessica had never seen vegetables like this before and was filled with enthusiasm and excitement.
She slowly squatted down and started to lay each vegetable down onto the grass. She could not believe her luck. She paused for a minute, wondering what would happen next.
Just then, she heard a voice say "Hello Jessica, I am the magical vegetable fairy." Jessica was absolutely delighted. 
The magical vegetable fairy smiled at her and said, "I have given you these unusual vegetables so you can explore the wonderful world of vegetables!" Jessica was amazed and thanked the magical vegetable fairy. 
Jessica had the best time exploring her garden and the magical world of vegetables. She could not wait to see what other wonderful surprises the vegetable fairy had in store for her.

"Wow, look at that cloud!" Lily says. "It is so orange and funny!"
"Maybe it is a magic cloud," Ben says. "Maybe it can make wishes come true."
Lily and Ben run to the cloud. They want to touch it and talk to it. They hope it will be nice to them.
"Hello, orange cloud!" Lily says. "We are Lily and Ben. We like you. Do you like us?"
The orange cloud does not say anything. It just floats in the sky. Lily and Ben feel sad. They want the cloud to be their friend.
"Please, orange cloud, say something!" Ben says. "We want to play with you. We want to invite you to our house. We have cookies and toys and books. You will like them."
The orange cloud still does not say anything. It just moves away from Lily and Ben. It goes to another part of the sky. Lily and Ben feel very sad. They do not understand why the cloud does not want to be their friend.
"Maybe the cloud is shy," Lily says. "Maybe it does not know how to talk. Maybe it is lonely."
"Maybe we can try again tomorrow," Ben says. "Maybe the cloud will be happier then. Maybe it will say hello to us."
Lily and Ben hug each other. They are still friends. They go back to their house. They hope the orange cloud will come back. They hope it will be their friend too.

Missy and Tim were excited about their new find. They decided to keep the coal and play with it. They had a lot of fun rolling it, throwing it, and hiding it. But soon, it was time for dinner. "I'll miss playing with our coal," said Missy. "Me too," said Tim. "But we can play again tomorrow!" And they happily went inside to eat, looking forward to more adventures with their new friend, the coal.

Once upon a time there was a prince who wore a shiny crown on his head. But one day, he suddenly felt so tired. He was so tired that he wished he could just close his eyes and fall asleep.
But his crown kept getting in the way. No matter how he moved his head, he couldn't get comfortable with it on. He thought for a moment, and finally had an idea.
He quickly opened the clasp at the back of his crown. He carefully took it off his head and placed it on a table. Immediately, the prince sighed in relief; he was much more comfortable now!
But before he could drift off to sleep, his crown suddenly began to glow. Out of the crown came a beautiful fairy! She said that the prince must not take off his crown, for it was where his power came from. Without it, he could not be the ruler of his kingdom.
The prince was so sad. He asked the fairy if there was any way he could be comfortable with his crown, and she said yes! She taught the prince how to close the clasp of his crown so he could still wear it, but keep it comfortable on his head.
The prince thanked the fairy and quickly closed the clasp. He was now able to wear his crown without feeling uncomfortable. And the kingdom was happy, because their prince was able to rule with his crown on. The end.

"Let's become something else," Ben said. "What do you want to be?"
Lily thought for a moment. She saw a red jar on a shelf. It had a picture of a pepper on it. She was curious.
"I want to be a pepper," she said. "A spicy pepper."
Ben laughed. "That's silly. How can you be a pepper?"
Lily climbed on a stool and reached for the jar. She opened it and smelled it. It made her nose tickle. She took a pinch of the red powder and put it in her mouth.
"Wow!" she cried. "It's hot! It's spicy!"
She ran to the water bucket and drank some. Ben followed her and tried some too. He made a funny face.
"Yuck!" he said. "That's not good. That's not fun."
Lily agreed. She spat out the powder. She felt her tongue burn.
"Let's not be peppers," she said. "Let's be something else."
Ben nodded. He looked around the barn. He saw a basket of eggs. He had an idea.
"Let's be chickens," he said. "Chickens are fun. They cluck and lay eggs."
Lily liked that. She forgot about the spicy powder. She followed Ben to the basket. They pretended to be chickens. They clucked and flapped their wings and laid eggs. They had fun.
They were happy they became chickens. They decided they liked chickens better than peppers. Peppers were too spicy. Chickens were just right.

As Bob told the story, the sunflower grew taller and taller. The sunflower liked the story so much that it wanted to hear more. So, Bob told more stories every day. The sunflower became the biggest and tallest one in the whole town.

Once there was a spider named Sam. Sam supported his family by spinning webs. But one day, as he was spinning, he felt uncomfortable.
Sam wondered why he felt so strange. He asked his Mom, ''Mom, why do I feel uncomfortable?''
His Mom answered, ''Sam, life can be difficult at times. But you are strong and must support your family.''
Sam tried his best to spin, but the uncomfortable feeling stayed. As he looked up at the sky, he saw thunderclouds rolling in.
''Uh oh,'' he thought, ''It looks like a storm is coming!''
He felt even more uncomfortable as the storm grew closer. Soon, a huge gust of wind blew through and knocked down Sam's web!
The uncomfortable feeling suddenly made sense. His Mom was helping him prepare for the storm by making sure he was strong enough to support his family during tough times. 
Sam smiled, for he now knew the reason for the uncomfortable feeling. He spun a new web, this one even stronger than before, and the spider family was able to stay safe during the storm.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they find a big toy bus in the park. It is red and yellow and has many seats.
"Wow, look at this bus!" Sara says. "It is so cute!"
"Can we play with it?" Tom asks.
"Yes, let's play!" Sara says. "I will be the driver and you will be the passenger."
They climb on the bus and pretend to drive around the park. Sara makes honking noises and Tom waves to the birds and the flowers. They have a lot of fun.
But then, they hear a loud voice.
"Hey, kids, that's my bus!" the voice says. "Give it back to me!"
They look and see a man running towards them. He is wearing a blue uniform and a hat. He is the real driver of the bus.
"Oh, no, we are sorry!" Sara says. "We did not know it was your bus. We just wanted to play."
The driver reaches the bus and looks at them. He is angry at first, but then he sees their scared faces. He softens a bit and smiles.
"It's okay, kids, I understand," he says. "But this bus is not a toy. It is my job to drive people around the city. You can't play with it. It is dangerous."
He helps them get off the bus and gives them each a sticker. The sticker has a picture of a bus and says "I love buses".
"Here, take these stickers," he says. "They are cute, too. And next time, if you want to ride on a bus, you can ask me. I will let you sit in the front and see everything. But only if you promise to be good and listen to me. Deal?"
Sara and Tom nod and say "Deal". They thank the driver and apologize again. They stick the stickers on their shirts and wave goodbye to him. They run back to their parents, who are waiting for them.
They tell them what happened and show them the stickers. Their parents are glad that they are safe and that they learned a lesson. They hug them and say "We love you".
Sara and Tom are happy. They learned something new and made a new friend. They still like to play with cars and trucks, but they also like to ride on buses. They think buses are cute, too.

"Hey, little bird, I am going to catch you!" Tom said. The little bird was scared and flew away. Tom chased the bird, but he could not catch it. He was sad and tired. Then, he met a big dog named Max.
Max saw Tom and said, "Why are you so sad, bossy cat?" Tom told Max about the little bird he wanted to catch. Max had an idea. "Let's work together to catch the bird," Max said. Tom agreed, and they became friends.
Max and Tom tried to catch the bird together, but the little bird was too fast for them. Then, something unexpected happened. The little bird came back and said, "Why are you trying to catch me? I just want to be friends." Tom and Max were surprised, but they liked the idea. So, the bossy cat, the big dog, and the little bird became friends and played together every day. And they all lived happily ever after.

Anna was a gifted girl. She could do many things that other kids could not. She could read big books, play the piano, and draw beautiful pictures. But her favorite thing to do was to fly.
She had a special furniture in her room. It was a big chair with wings. She called it her flying chair. She liked to sit on it and pretend that she was flying in the sky. She would imagine that she was a bird, or a fairy, or a superhero.
One day, she decided to try something new. She wanted to fly outside her window. She put on her helmet and her goggles, and she tied a rope to her chair. She opened the window and pushed her chair out. She held on to the rope and jumped after it.
She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She saw the trees, the houses, and the cars below. She waved to the birds and the clouds. She was so happy and free. She flew higher and higher, until she reached the stars.
She looked at the stars and wondered what they were. She wanted to touch them and talk to them. She let go of the rope and reached out her hand. But then, she realized that she had made a mistake. She had no way to get back to her chair. She started to fall.
She screamed and cried. She was scared and sorry. She wished she had not been so silly. She wished she had stayed in her room. She closed her eyes and waited for the end.
But then, she felt something soft and warm. She opened her eyes and saw that she was in her bed. She looked around and saw that she was in her room. She saw her flying chair, her books, her piano, and her pictures. She realized that it was all a dream.
She was relieved and grateful. She hugged her teddy bear and said a prayer. She learned a lesson. She decided that she would never fly outside her window again. She decided that she would only fly in her imagination. She decided that she was still a gifted girl, but also a wise one.

Tim and Mia learned a lesson. They learned that climbing the tower was a bad idea. They learned that daring someone to do something dangerous was not nice. "Look, Ben, a pepper! Can we have it?" Lily asked.
Ben shook his head. "No, Lily, that is a hot pepper. It will hurt your mouth. Mama said so."
Lily did not listen. She reached for the pepper and pulled it off the plant. She took a big bite and smiled. But then, she felt a fire in her mouth. She spit out the pepper and cried.
"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, it hurts!" Lily screamed.
Ben ran to get Mama. Mama heard Lily's cry and entered the garden. She saw Lily holding her mouth and the pepper on the ground.
"Oh, Lily, what did you do? You ate a hot pepper. That was not a good idea. Come here, let me help you." Mama said.
She took Lily inside and gave her some water and milk. She hugged her and kissed her cheek.
"I'm sorry, Mama. I was silly. I won't eat hot peppers again." Lily said.
Mama smiled. "It's okay, Lily. You learned your lesson. Next time, listen to Ben and me. We only want you to be safe and happy." Mama said.
Lily nodded. She felt better. She said sorry to Ben and gave him a hug. They went back to the garden and played with some nice flowers. They did not touch the peppers anymore.

One day, they saw a new place to hide. It was a small house made of wood and stone. It had a door and a window, but no one lived there. Tom and Lily ran to the house and opened the door. It was dark and dusty inside.
"Wow, this is a great place to hide!" Tom said. "Let's go in and explore!"
"OK, but be careful. It might be scary," Lily said.
They went in and looked around. They saw a table, a chair, a bed and a shelf. On the shelf, there was a box. It was old and rusty, and had a lock on it.
"What's in the box?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Maybe a treasure, or a toy, or a secret," Lily said.
"Let's open it and see!" Tom said. He tried to break the lock with a stick, but it was too strong.
"Stop, Tom! You might break something!" Lily said.
But Tom did not listen. He hit the lock harder and harder, until it snapped. He opened the box and looked inside.
There was nothing in the box, except a small ball of light. It floated out of the box and flew around the room. It made a soft sound, like a whisper.
"Wow, what is that?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. It looks like a spirit," Lily said.
"A spirit? What is a spirit?" Tom asked.
"A spirit is a thing that has no body, but has feelings and thoughts. Sometimes, spirits are nice and friendly, and sometimes, they are mean and scary," Lily said.
"Is this spirit nice or mean?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Let's say hello and find out," Lily said.
They said hello to the spirit, and the spirit said hello back. It had a cheerful voice, and it smiled.
"Hello, children. I'm glad you found me. I've been lonely for a long time," the spirit said.
"Who are you? Where did you come from?" Tom asked.
"I'm a fairy. I used to live in the forest, with my friends and family. But one day, a bad man came and caught me. He put me in this box and locked me up. He wanted to use my magic for his own selfish purposes. He was very cruel and greedy," the spirit said.
"That's terrible! How long have you been in the box?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. A very long time. I lost track of the days and the seasons. I missed the sun and the moon, the flowers and the birds, the wind and the rain. I missed my home and my people. I was sad and lonely," the spirit said.
"I'm sorry. That's very sad," Lily said.
"Can we help you? Can we set you free?" Tom asked.
"Yes, you can. You already did. By opening the box, you broke the spell that kept me trapped. Now I can go back to the forest, and find my friends and family. You are very kind and brave, children. Thank you very much," the spirit said.
"You're welcome. We're happy to help you. We're your friends, too," Tom said.
"Can we go with you? Can we see the forest and the fairies?" Lily asked.
"Of course. I would love to show you my home and my people. They will be happy to meet you, too. Come, follow me. Let's go," the spirit said.
The spirit took Tom and Lily by the hand, and led them out of the house. They flew in the air, with the spirit's magic. They saw the park, the town, the river and the hills. They saw the forest, green and bright. They saw the fairies, colorful and cheerful. They played and danced and sang with them. They had a lot of fun.
Tom and Lily never forgot that day. They never forgot the spirit, their friend. They never forgot the forest, their adventure. They never forgot the magic, their gift. They always remembered to be kind and brave, and to help those in need. They always remembered to be happy and grateful, and to enjoy life. They always remembered to play hide and seek, and to laugh and shout. They always remembered to be children, and to dream.

Sue and her mom looked around and found a big tree with lots of normal-sized pins under it. Sue's mom said, "These pins are too big for the duck to eat. We need to find something else." Sue looked sad, but she kept looking.

The squirrel ran up the tree and came back with a small bag of seeds. Sue and her mom were very surprised, but they were happy. They thanked the squirrel and went to feed the duck. The duck was very happy too, and they all had a fun day at the park.

Sam and Mia were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. But then Sam saw something on the window. It was a big bird with black feathers and a yellow beak. It looked angry and hungry.
"Look, Mia, a bird!" Sam said, pointing at the window.
Mia looked up and gasped. She was scared of the bird. She thought it might break the window and hurt them.
"Let's hide, Sam!" Mia said, grabbing her car and running to the couch.
Sam followed her, but he did not want to hide. He wanted to see the bird. He thought it was cool and brave. He left his car on the floor and crawled to the window. He wanted to touch the bird.
"Sam, come back!" Mia whispered, but Sam did not listen.
He reached the window and put his hand on the glass. The bird saw him and squawked. It pecked at the glass, trying to get to Sam. Sam was not scared. He laughed and wiped the glass with his hand, making the bird more angry.
"Go away, bird!" Sam said, wiping harder.
But the bird did not go away. It pecked harder and harder, until the glass cracked. Sam was surprised and stopped wiping. He saw the crack and felt the wind. He heard the bird flap its wings and fly inside. He was in trouble.
"Help, Mia, help!" Sam screamed, as the bird chased him around the room.
Mia heard Sam and got up from the couch. She saw the bird and the broken window. She felt helpless. She did not know what to do. She wanted to help Sam, but she was too scared of the bird.
She looked around and saw Sam's car on the floor. She had an idea. She picked up the car and threw it at the bird. The car hit the bird on the head and made it fall. The bird was stunned and stopped moving.
"Sam, run!" Mia shouted, as she ran to the door.
Sam saw Mia and the car and the bird. He realized what Mia did. He was proud of her. He ran to the door and joined her. They opened the door and ran outside. They were safe.
They hugged each other and thanked each other. They looked at the window and the bird. They felt sorry for the bird. It was hurt and lost. It did not belong in their land. They hoped it would fly away and find its home.
They decided to never play with the window again. They learned their lesson. They went back inside and played with their cars on the floor. They were happy and careful. They were friends.

"Look, Tom, a swan!" Lila said. "It can soar high and low. It is so pretty!"
Tom nodded. He liked the swan too. He wanted to touch it. He ran to the pond where the swan was landing. He reached out his hand.
"Tom, no!" Lila shouted. "The swan can bite you. It is not nice. Come back!"
But Tom did not listen. He got closer to the swan. The swan saw him and hissed. It opened its beak and snapped at Tom. Tom screamed and ran away. He was scared and hurt.
Lila ran to him and hugged him. She was sorry for him. She saw a piece of wood on the ground. It was weird. It had a shape like a swan. It had a head and a neck and a body and wings. It was a toy.
"Look, Tom, a toy!" Lila said. "It is a swan too. But it can not bite you. It can only soar in your hand. Do you want it?"
Tom nodded. He liked the toy. He took it and smiled. He forgot the bad swan. He waved the toy in the air. He made it soar high and low. He was happy.
Lila and Tom played with the toy. They had fun. They liked the weird wood swan. It was so pretty.

Once upon a time, there was a small beetle named Pat. Pat was always busy examining the world. He had never seen anyone like him before so he felt quite alone. One day, Pat was examining a tiny, brown leaf. Suddenly he saw something moving. It was a small worm named Liz.
Pat smiled and shouted "hi". Liz looked up and said "Hello Pat". Pat was so happy that he had found someone like him that he ran over to Liz, and rubbed her back with his tiny antennae.
Liz was delighted. She said to Pat, "You know, sometimes it's helpful to have a friend to examine the world with. We can learn so much together!" Pat agreed and they vowed to explore the world together. Pat gave Liz a big hug and they flew off to explore their next big adventure.
The moral of this story is to always be helpful and kind to your friends. You never know what kind of adventure you might have together if you lend a helping hand.

Lily and Tom were twins. They liked to play with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big white bear. The bear was soft and cuddly, and they named him Snowy.
One day, Mom said, "Lily and Tom, I have to go to the store. Be good and don't make a mess. I will be back soon." She gave them a kiss and left.
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Okay, Mom." They continued to play with Snowy. They pretended he was a king, a pirate, and a superhero. They had a lot of fun.
But then, Tom had an idea. He saw a bottle of red paint on the table. He said, "Lily, let's make Snowy more colorful. He is too white. Red is a nice color."
Lily said, "No, Tom. That is a bad idea. Mom will be mad. And Snowy will be sad. He likes to be white. White is a useful color. It goes with everything."
Tom said, "No, Lily. You are silly. Red is a better color. It is bright and happy. And Snowy will be happy too. He will look like a fire truck or a strawberry. Come on, let's do it."
Lily said, "No, Tom. Stop. Don't spoil Snowy. He is our friend. We love him."
But Tom did not listen. He grabbed the bottle of paint and poured it all over Snowy. The paint dripped and splashed on the bear, the carpet, and the couch. Snowy was no longer white. He was red and wet and sticky.
Lily cried, "Tom, what did you do? You ruined Snowy. And the living room. Mom will be very angry. And Snowy will be very sad. You are a bad brother."
Tom looked at what he did. He felt sorry. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I thought it would be fun. But it was not. It was a big mistake. I'm sorry, Snowy. I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Mom."
Lily said, "Tom, you have to fix this. You have to clean up. And you have to say sorry to Snowy and Mom. And you have to be nice to Snowy. He is still our friend. He is still our bear."
Tom said, "Okay, Lily. I will. I will try to make it better. I hope Snowy and Mom will forgive me. And I hope you will too."
They hugged each other and Snowy. They got some towels and water and tried to clean up the mess. They hoped Mom would not be too mad. They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful with their toys and their paint. And they learned to love their white bear.

Ben says, "Maybe. Let's leave it here. Maybe they will like it."

"Look, a bell!" Tom says. "Let's pull the rope and make it ring!"
"OK!" Mia says. "But we have to be careful. The bell is very high. We have to jump to reach the rope."
Tom and Mia run to the bell. They take turns to jump and pull the rope. The bell makes a loud sound. Ding-dong, ding-dong. Tom and Mia laugh and clap. They feel lively and happy.
But then, they hear a voice. It is the park keeper. He is angry. He does not like the noise.
"Hey, you two! Stop pulling the bell! You are disturbing the birds and the people!" he shouts. "Go away from the bell, or I will call your parents!"
Tom and Mia are scared. They let go of the rope. They run away from the bell. They say sorry to the park keeper. They do not want to get in trouble.
They find a quiet spot in the park. They sit on a bench. They are still friends. They hug and smile.
"Next time, let's play something else," Tom says.
"OK," Mia says. "But the bell was fun, right?"
"Yes, it was," Tom says. "But maybe too loud."
They giggle and nod. They look for a new game to play. They are still lively and happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and white. The dog has a red collar.
"Look, a dog!" Lily says. "Can we pet it?"
"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe it is not nice."
Lily and Ben go near the dog. The dog wags its tail. It licks Lily's hand. Lily smiles. She pets the dog.
"Hello, dog," she says. "You are kind and soft."
The dog barks. It jumps on Ben. Ben falls down. He cries. The dog bites Ben's arm. Ben has a cut. It hurts.
"Help, help!" Ben calls. "The dog is bad!"
Lily runs to Ben. She hugs him. She sees the cut. She is scared.
"Let's go to mom," she says. "She can help."
Lily and Ben run to mom. Mom is on a bench. She sees the cut. She is worried.
"What happened?" she asks.
"A dog bit me," Ben says. "It was not kind."
Mom takes Ben to the car. She drives to the doctor. The doctor looks at the cut. He cleans it. He puts a bandage on it.
"You are brave," he says. "The cut will heal soon."
Lily and Ben say thank you. They go back to mom. Mom hugs them.
"I'm sorry, Ben," she says. "Are you okay?"
"I'm okay," Ben says. "But I don't like dogs anymore."
Lily thinks. She remembers the dog. It was kind and soft at first. Then it was bad and hurtful.
"Maybe the dog was scared too," she says. "Maybe it did not know us. Maybe it wanted to play, but it played too rough."
Ben nods. He understands.
"Maybe you are right," he says. "But we should be careful. We should not pet dogs we don't know. We should ask their owners first."
Lily and Ben agree. They learn a lesson. They are still friends. They are kind to each other.

Ben and Mia were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they decided to have a picnic. They brought some bread, cheese, fruit and juice. They found a nice spot under a big tree and spread a blanket on the grass.
"Let's eat!" Ben said. He took a piece of bread and put some cheese on it.
"Wait!" Mia said. "We have to say thank you first. Thank you for the food and the sun and the park."
"Okay, okay," Ben said. He put his bread down and folded his hands. "Thank you for the food and the sun and the park."
They ate their picnic and drank their juice. They were happy and full.
"Let's play now!" Mia said. She picked up a ball and threw it to Ben.
"Okay!" Ben said. He caught the ball and threw it back.
They played catch for a while. Then, they saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was black and brown and had sharp teeth. It looked fierce.
"Look out!" Ben shouted. He dropped the ball and ran behind the tree.
"Help!" Mia cried. She grabbed the blanket and wrapped it around her.
The dog reached the picnic spot and sniffed the food. It liked the smell of cheese. It took a bite of Ben's bread and cheese. Then, it saw the ball. It liked the ball too. It picked up the ball and ran away.
"Hey!" Ben said. "That's my ball! Give it back!"
He came out from behind the tree and chased the dog.
"Ben, no!" Mia said. "The dog is fierce! It might bite you!"
She followed Ben and tried to stop him.
The dog ran faster and faster. Ben and Mia ran after it. They ran across the park and out of the gate. They ran into the street and saw a car coming.
"Stop!" Mia screamed. "The car!"
Ben and Mia stopped and jumped back. The car honked and passed by. The dog kept running and disappeared.
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They were scared and sad. They had lost their ball and their picnic.
They hugged each other and cried.
A lady saw them and came over. She was kind and gentle.
"What's wrong, children?" she asked.
"A dog took our ball and our picnic," Ben said.
"It was a fierce dog," Mia said.
"Oh, I'm sorry," the lady said. "That's not nice. Do you want to come with me? I have some cookies and milk at home. And I have a ball too. You can play with it if you want."
"Really?" Ben asked.
"Really," the lady said. "I don't own the ball. It belongs to my son. But he's at school now. He won't mind if you play with it. He likes to share."
"Thank you," Mia said.
"Thank you," Ben said.
They took the lady's hand and walked with her. They felt better. They had found a new friend. And they still had each other.

When he arrived, he saw a beautiful pool of bubbling water. He was so amazed that he decided to take a drink from it. "This water is so refreshing," the elderly man said. 
Just then, he heard a deep rumble coming from within the volcano. The man quickly jumped into the pool and watched as molten lava began to fill the volcano's crater. He swam to the top of the pool and looked around. 
Just then, an elderly lady appeared. "These waters are magical," she said. "Come, drink from them and be blessed with eternal youth." 
The man was hesitant at first, but then he took a sip and was filled with strength and joy. The elderly lady smiled and vanished, leaving the man to enjoy the beauty of the volcano forever.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play games. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they decided to play a game of hide and seek in the house.
Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Ben. She checked under the bed, behind the sofa, in the closet, but she could not find him. She sighed and thought, where could he be?
Ben was hiding in the kitchen, inside the refrigerator. He had opened the door quietly and climbed in. He thought it was a good hiding spot, because Lily would never look there. He smiled and waited for Lily to give up.
But Lily did not give up. She searched every room in the house, except the kitchen. She was getting tired and hungry. She decided to go to the kitchen and get a snack. She walked to the refrigerator and opened the door.
She saw Ben sitting inside, holding a carton of juice. She was surprised and angry. She said, "Ben, you cheated! You can't hide in the refrigerator! That's not fair!"
Ben said, "I didn't cheat! I just found a clever spot! I win!"
Lily said, "No, you don't! You broke the rules! I win!"
They started to argue and shout. They did not notice that their mom came into the kitchen. She heard them and said, "What are you two doing? Why are you in the refrigerator? You could get sick or hurt!"
Lily and Ben stopped arguing and looked at their mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were playing hide and seek and we got too competitive."
Mom said, "I'm glad you like to play games, but you have to be safe and respectful. Hiding in the refrigerator is not a good idea. And you don't have to fight over who wins or loses. The most important thing is to have fun and be kind to each other."
Lily and Ben nodded and hugged their mom. They said, "We love you, mom. And we love each other, too. Can we have some juice, please?"
Mom smiled and said, "Of course you can. But first, let's close the refrigerator and clean up the mess."

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys. Anna has a doll that can talk. Ben has a car that can move. They need batteries for their toys.
One day, they find a new pack of batteries in the kitchen. They are happy. They want to use the batteries for their toys. But there is a problem. The pack has only two batteries. And they need four.
"Anna, give me the batteries. I need them for my car," Ben says.
"No, Ben. I need them for my doll. She is gifted. She can say many things," Anna says.
They start to fight. They pull the pack of batteries. They yell at each other.
Mom hears them. She comes to the kitchen. She sees them fighting. She is not happy.
"Anna, Ben, stop! Why are you fighting?" Mom says.
"Mom, we need batteries for our toys. But there are only two. And we need four," Anna says.
"Mom, we found the batteries in the kitchen. They are ours. We want to use them," Ben says.
Mom shakes her head. She says, "The batteries are not yours. They are mine. I bought them for my flashlight. I need them for the night. You cannot use them."
Anna and Ben are sad. They do not have batteries for their toys. They do not know what to do.
Mom sees them sad. She feels sorry for them. She says, "I have an idea. Why don't you share the batteries? You can take turns. Anna, you can use the batteries for your doll for one hour. Then you can tie a ribbon around the pack and give it to Ben. Ben, you can use the batteries for your car for one hour. Then you can tie a bow around the pack and give it back to Anna. And so on. How does that sound?"
Anna and Ben think about it. They like the idea. They agree to share the batteries. They say, "Thank you, Mom. You are smart. You are kind."
Mom smiles. She says, "You are welcome, Anna and Ben. You are good. You are sweet."
They hug Mom. They hug each other. They go to play with their toys. They are happy. They have learned to share.

Bella and Ben were twins who liked to bounce. They bounced on their beds, on the sofa, on the trampoline. They bounced everywhere they could, even when their mom said no. They thought bouncing was the best thing ever.
One day, their mom made broccoli for dinner. Bella and Ben hated broccoli. They said it was yucky and green and smelled bad. They did not want to eat it. They wanted to bounce some more.
"Please, mom, can we bounce instead of eating broccoli?" they asked.
"No, you have to eat your broccoli. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy. And you have bounced enough today. You need to rest," their mom said.
"But mom, we don't like broccoli. We like bouncing. Bouncing is fun. Broccoli is not," they said.
"I don't care. You have to eat your broccoli. No more bouncing until you finish your plate. And no more arguing," their mom said.
Bella and Ben were very unhappy. They did not want to eat their broccoli. They wanted to bounce. They looked at each other and had an idea. They pretended to eat their broccoli, but they hid it under their napkins. Then they asked to go to the bathroom. Their mom said yes, but told them to hurry back.
Bella and Ben ran to the bathroom, but they did not go inside. They sneaked to their bedroom, where their beds were waiting for them. They jumped on their beds and bounced as high as they could. They laughed and giggled and had a lot of fun.
But they did not know that their mom had seen them. She had followed them and saw them bouncing on their beds. She was very angry. She opened the door and shouted at them.
"Bella and Ben, what are you doing? You lied to me. You did not eat your broccoli. You hid it under your napkins. And you bounced on your beds when I told you not to. You are very naughty. You are in big trouble. No more bouncing for you. Ever."
Bella and Ben stopped bouncing. They looked at their mom and felt very scared. They knew they had done something very bad. They wished they had eaten their broccoli. They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they could bounce again. But it was too late. Their mom took away their beds and their trampoline and their sofa. She gave them only hard chairs to sit on. She said they had to eat broccoli every day. She said they had to learn their lesson.
Bella and Ben were very sad. They had no more fun. They had no more bouncing. They had only broccoli. They hated broccoli. They hated their life. They wished they could bounce again. But they could not. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Aaron and Becca. Every morning they would meet at the beach and look for waves to surf. 
Becca had grown tired of Aaron's behavior. He always took the best waves, even if it meant being selfish. Becca felt miserable and unimportant when they were together. 
"My friend Becca," said Aaron, "why don't you surf too?" 
Becca sadly replied, "Because you're always taking the best waves and leaving me with nothing." 
Aaron felt ashamed and knew he had to change his behavior. 
The next morning Aaron let Becca pick the first wave. He helped her paddle and gave her plenty of space to surf the wave.
Becca's whole mood changed. She was no longer miserable and felt important again. 
From that day forward, Aaron and Becca always took turns surfing. They made sure to always behave in a respectful way towards each other. 
The moral of the story is that it's important to be thoughtful and polite to your friends!

The stars listened to the cool moon and started to twinkle brightly. They made a path for the little bird to follow. The bird saw the stars and knew they were supporting it. It followed the path of stars all the way back to its nest.
The cool moon and the stars were happy that they could support the little bird. The bird thanked them and went to sleep in its cozy nest. From that day on, the bird knew that the cool moon and the stars would always be there to support it. Once upon a time, there was a shy little otter. She was very modest, and she kept to herself every day. She would often play alone in the lake, or explore the shore. One day, while exploring the shore, she met a kind lady. The lady asked her, "Hello there little otter. Can I give you something?"
The otter was a bit shy, so she shook her head no. But the lady told her, "Don't worry, I have something for you. Come closer little one and I'll give it to you." With that, the otter hesitantly placed a paw in the lady's outstretched hand. 
The lady smiled and said, "Here, this is for you!" She held out a shiny, golden coin. "This is to show that kindness is always better than being shy." 
The otter smiled and thanked the lady, then put the coin in her pocket. From then on, she stayed modest but wasn't afraid to be brave and kind.

Lily and Tom were brother and sister. They liked to play outside in the sun. One day, they saw a creek near their house. It had clear water and shiny rocks. They wanted to go closer and touch it.
"Mom, can we go to the creek?" Lily asked.
"No, you can't. The creek is dangerous. It can be very powerful and fast. You might fall in and get hurt. You have to behave and stay away from it." Mom said.
But Lily and Tom did not listen. They waited until Mom was busy and ran to the creek. They thought it was fun and pretty. They threw rocks and sticks in the water. They tried to catch fish and frogs.
"Look, I found a big rock. I can jump on it." Tom said.
He jumped on the rock, but it was slippery. He lost his balance and fell into the creek. The water was cold and strong. It pulled him away from the shore. He screamed and cried.
"Lily, help me! I can't swim!" Tom said.
Lily was scared and sad. She wanted to help Tom, but she did not know how. She ran to Mom and told her what happened.
"Mom, Tom fell in the creek. He is in trouble. Please help him." Lily said.
Mom was angry and worried. She ran to the creek with Lily. But it was too late. Tom was gone. The creek had taken him away. Mom and Lily cried and hugged. They wished they had behaved and stayed away from the creek.

Lily wanted to touch the crab. She was not afraid of it. She was independent and curious. She walked slowly to the crab and reached out her hand. The crab saw her and snapped its claws.
"Ouch!" Lily said. She pulled back her hand. It hurt a lot. She started to cry. The crab ran away and hid under a rock.
Mommy heard Lily cry and ran to her. She saw her hand was red and swollen. She picked up Lily and hugged her.
"What happened, sweetie?" Mommy asked.
"I touched a crab and it bit me," Lily said.
"Oh, no. I'm sorry, honey. Crabs don't like to be touched. They are scared and defensive. You have to be careful with them," Mommy said.
She took Lily to the water and washed her hand. Then she rubbed some cream on it. The cream made the pain go away.
"Thank you, Mommy," Lily said.
"You're welcome, Lily. I love you," Mommy said.
They went back to their blanket and had a snack. Lily learned a lesson. She decided not to touch crabs anymore. She was still independent and curious, but she was also respectful and careful. She played with her sand castle and her shells and had a fun day on the beach.

One night, she heard a mysterious sound from her crib. It was like a soft whisper, but she could not understand what it said. She was curious and scared at the same time. She got out of her bed and tiptoed to her crib. She peeked inside and saw a tiny fairy sitting on her pillow.
"Hello, Lily," the fairy said. "I am Faye, and I am here to be your friend. I can show you many wonderful things in your dreams, if you sleep in your crib."
Lily was surprised and happy. She had never seen a fairy before. She wanted to see the wonderful things the fairy could show her. She asked, "What kind of things can you show me, Faye?"
Faye smiled and said, "I can show you the stars, the moon, the flowers, the animals, the rainbows and more. I can also tell you stories and sing you songs. But you have to sleep in your crib, or I will disappear."
Lily thought for a moment. She still did not like her crib very much, but she liked Faye a lot. She decided to give it a try. She said, "OK, Faye, I will sleep in my crib tonight. But you have to promise to stay with me and not leave me alone."
Faye nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. I will stay with you and not leave you alone. Now, let's go to sleep and have some fun."
Lily climbed into her crib and snuggled with Faye. She felt warm and safe. She closed her eyes and waited for Faye to show her the wonderful things in her dreams. She did not know that Faye was a magic fairy who could make her crib bigger, brighter and more comfortable. "Let's go to the tower," Tom said. He wanted to be brave.
"No, it's too high and wobbly," Lily said. She was afraid.
"Come on, it will be fun," Tom said. He took Lily's hand and pulled her to the tower.
They climbed up the steps and reached the rope bridge. It was long and shaky. Tom went first and crossed the bridge. He waved at Lily.
"Your turn," he said.
Lily looked down and saw the ground far below. She felt dizzy and scared. She wanted to go back.
"No, I can't," she said. She started to cry.
Tom saw that Lily was sad and scared. He felt sorry for her. He crossed the bridge again and hugged her.
"It's okay, Lily. You don't have to do it. Let's go back," he said.
They climbed down the steps and ran to the slide. They slid down together and laughed.
They played on the other equipment until it was time to go home.
They had fun, but they never went to the tower again.
The end.

Lily did many jobs to save money. She helped her mom and dad, and her neighbors too. After some time, she had enough money to pay for the trip. Lily was excited and went to find the magic man.
When she found the magic man, he was happy to help her. He gave Lily a magic stone and told her to take it back to her town. The magic stone would make the mist go away and make her town fun and bright.
Lily went back to her town and used the magic stone. The mist went away and her town became fun and bright, just like she wanted. Everyone was happy, and they all thanked Lily for her hard work. From that day on, the town was never boring again.
