Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big bean on the ground. It was green and shiny and looked yummy.
"Wow, look at this bean!" Lily said. "I want to eat it!"
"No, I want to eat it!" Tom said. "I saw it first!"
They both grabbed the bean and tried to pull it away from each other. They began to fight over the bean. They shouted and pushed and tugged.
"Give me the bean!" Lily said.
"No, it's mine!" Tom said.
They fought so hard that they did not see the big dog that came into the garden. The dog was hungry and smelled the bean. It ran towards Lily and Tom and barked loudly.
"Roof! Roof!" the dog said.
Lily and Tom were scared of the dog. They let go of the bean and ran away. The dog picked up the bean and ate it in one bite. It wagged its tail and licked its lips.
Lily and Tom hid behind a tree and looked at the dog. They felt sorry for fighting over the bean. They realized that the bean was not worth losing their friendship.
"I'm sorry, Tom," Lily said. "The bean was not that important. You can have it next time."
"I'm sorry, too, Lily," Tom said. "The bean was not that yummy. You are my friend and I don't want to fight with you."
They hugged and made up. They decided to play something else in the garden. They learned that fighting over a bean was a terrible idea.

Lily liked to watch cartoons on TV. She liked the funny animals and the songs. She did not like to share the TV with her brother Ben. Ben liked to watch other shows. He liked the cars and the robots.
One day, Lily and Ben were home with their mom. Mom said they could watch TV for a little while, but they had to take turns. Lily went first. She chose her favorite cartoon. She laughed and clapped. Ben waited patiently. He played with his toys.
When Lily's cartoon was over, Ben said, "My turn now, Lily. Please give me the remote." Lily did not want to give him the remote. She wanted to watch another cartoon. She said, "No, Ben. I want to watch more cartoons. Go away!" She held the remote tightly.
Ben felt sad and angry. He said, "That's not fair, Lily. You had your turn. You have to share. Mom said so." Lily did not listen. She said, "Shut up, Ben. I don't care what mom said. I don't care what you want. I only care about me and my cartoons." She turned up the volume.
Mom heard the noise. She came to the living room. She saw Lily and Ben fighting over the remote. She saw Lily being rude and selfish. She saw Ben being humble and polite. She was very upset. She said, "Lily, how could you be so mean to your brother? You should be ashamed of yourself. You have to learn to share and be kind. You are not the only one who likes to watch TV. You have to respect others. Give me the remote right now. You are in big trouble, young lady. You are not watching any more cartoons today. You are going to your room. And you are going to apologize to Ben."
Lily realized she had made a big mistake. She felt sorry and scared. She cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. I was selfish. Please forgive me. Please let me watch cartoons." But it was too late. Mom took the remote and turned off the TV. She took Lily by the hand and led her to her room. She said, "No, Lily. You have to face the consequences of your actions. You have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will be more humble and generous. Maybe next time you will think of others before yourself."
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being humble is better than being selfish. Respect others and they will respect you.

Lia and Sam were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were hunters in the jungle. They had sticks that they used as spears. They threw them at the trees and the bushes.
"Look, Sam, I found a big bird!" Lia said. She pointed at a gray and white creature with a long neck and legs. It was eating some grass near the fence.
"That's not a bird, Lia, that's a giraffe!" Sam said. He had seen one in a book. "It's very unusual. It has spots and horns and a long tongue."
"Can we catch it?" Lia asked. She wanted to touch it and see how it felt.
"I don't know. It's very tall and fast. Maybe it will run away or kick us." Sam said. He was a little scared of the giraffe.
They decided to try anyway. They crept closer to the fence, holding their spears. They waited for the right moment to throw them.
But the giraffe saw them. It lifted its head and looked at them with big brown eyes. It made a funny sound, like a whistle.
"Hello, children," it said. "What are you doing with those sticks?"
Lia and Sam dropped their spears. They were very surprised. They did not know that giraffes could talk.
"Uh, we were playing," Lia said. "We're sorry, we didn't mean to hurt you."
"That's all right," the giraffe said. "I'm not hurt. I'm just curious. Why do you want to catch me?"
"We wanted to see you up close," Sam said. "You're very unusual. We've never seen a giraffe before."
"Well, you can see me now," the giraffe said. "But you don't need to throw sticks at me. You can just ask me nicely. I'm very friendly."
"Can we touch you?" Lia asked.
"Sure, you can touch me," the giraffe said. "But be gentle. And don't pull my tail."
Lia and Sam smiled. They walked up to the fence and reached out their hands. The giraffe bent down and let them stroke its fur and horns. It felt soft and warm.
They liked the giraffe. It was unusual, but nice. They decided to be friends with it. They asked it many questions and learned many things. They had a lot of fun.
The end.

Lily was scared and hurt, so she closed her eyes and started to pray. When she opened her eyes, she saw Max had turned into a big, soft pillow! Lily had landed on Max-pillow and didn't get hurt. They went back home, and Lily thanked Max for being so reliable. From that day on, Lily always listened to Max, and they had many more adventures together.

The dad and the daughter reached out and touched the cat gently. The cat seemed to be so relieved that it stopped chewing the rope and purred. The dad scooped the cat up and hugged it tightly.

One day, a friendly dog named Spot saw a shiny pan on the street. He wanted to play with it, so he picked it up with his mouth and started to march around. He felt very happy and proud of his new toy.
He met a cat named Fluffy, who was sitting on a fence. Fluffy saw the pan and said, "That is not a toy, that is a pan. You should not play with it, you should give it back to the person who lost it."
Spot did not listen to Fluffy. He said, "No, this is my toy. I found it, so I can keep it. It makes a nice sound when I march with it. Go away, cat, you are not friendly."
Fluffy felt sad and angry. He said, "You are not friendly, either. You are selfish and rude. You do not care about other people's things. You do not know how to share. You will get in trouble if you keep the pan."
Spot did not care. He marched away with the pan, making a lot of noise. He did not see the big truck that was coming fast on the road. He did not hear the horn that was honking loud. He only heard the sound of the pan.
The truck hit Spot and the pan. Spot was hurt and scared. The pan was bent and broken. The driver of the truck was sorry and angry. He said, "You silly dog, why did you march on the road with a pan? You could have been killed. You should have listened to the cat. He was right, you should have given back the pan. It was mine, I dropped it by mistake. It was a special pan, a gift from my mother. Now it is ruined. You are a bad dog."
Spot felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Fluffy. He wished he had been friendly and shared the pan. He learned a lesson that day. He learned that playing with other people's things is wrong. He learned that being selfish and rude is not fun. He learned that being friendly and caring is better. He said, "I am sorry, sir. I am sorry, Fluffy. I was a bad dog. I will not do it again. I will be a good dog. I will be a friendly dog."
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty bee. He flew around everywhere, never settling in one spot. One day, he heard a voice calling to him from the ground. He flew down and saw an old ant. The ant urged him to stay with him for a rest. The bee didn't want to listen and so he kept flying away.
As the days went on, he got more and more tired from never staying in the same spot. He could feel himself getting weaker and weaker. Eventually, he spotted the ant again and decided to take him up on his offer. 
The ant was happy to see the bee and brought him lots of food to eat. The bee enjoyed his rest and slowly got back his strength. Once rested, the bee understood how important it was to stay in one spot and not be too naughty and fly around too much. And so the moral of the story is that it is important to rest and stay in the same spot sometimes.

They decided to play with their toys. Mia picked up her doll and Ben picked up his car. They made noises and stories with them. They had fun and forgot about the chocolate for a while.
But then, Ben saw the chocolate again. He felt hungry and curious. He said to Mia, "Can we have a little bite? Just a little one. Mom won't know."
Mia shook her head. She said, "No, Ben. We have to remember what mom said. We have to be good and play nicely. If we eat the chocolate now, we will be naughty and sad."
Ben frowned. He said, "But I want some chocolate. It looks so yummy. Please, Mia. Just a little bite."
Mia said, "No, Ben. We have to wait. If we wait, we will be happy and proud. And the chocolate will taste even better."
Ben thought about it. He knew Mia was right. He said, "Okay, Mia. You are smart. We will wait. Let's play some more."
Mia smiled. She said, "Okay, Ben. You are kind. Let's play some more."
They put the chocolate away and played with their toys again. They were peaceful and good. They remembered what mom said. They waited for lunch and then they ate the chocolate. Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with many animals. The truck says "Zoo". Sara and Ben want to see the animals.
They run to the truck and peek inside. They see a lion, a monkey, a zebra and a snake. The lion is sleeping. The monkey is jumping. The zebra is eating. The snake is hissing.
"Wow, look at the animals!" Sara says.
"They are so cool!" Ben says.
But then, the snake sees Sara and Ben. It is angry. It wants to escape. It pushes the door of the truck with its tail. The door opens. The snake slithers out.
"Help! The snake is out!" Sara screams.
"Run, run, run!" Ben shouts.
Sara and Ben run away from the snake. They are scared. The snake chases them. It is fast. It wants to bite them.
But then, a man sees the snake. He is the zookeeper. He has a net. He throws the net over the snake. He catches the snake.
"Got you, you naughty snake!" the zookeeper says.
He puts the snake back in the truck. He closes the door. He locks it.
"Are you okay, kids?" the zookeeper asks Sara and Ben.
"Yes, we are okay. Thank you, mister," Sara says.
"That was a close one. You should not go near the truck. The animals are not for playing. They are for the zoo. They can be dangerous," the zookeeper says.
"Sorry, mister. We were curious. We wanted to see the animals," Ben says.
"I understand. But you have to be careful. The animals are not like your toys. They have their own feelings and needs. They can be weird sometimes. They can gain or lose their temper. They can escape or attack. You have to respect them," the zookeeper says.
"We will, mister. We will respect the animals. We will not go near the truck again," Sara and Ben say.
"Good. Now, go back to your parents. They must be worried. And have fun in the park. But stay safe," the zookeeper says.
Sara and Ben nod. They run back to their parents. They hug them. They tell them what happened. Their parents are glad they are okay. They are also proud of them. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect the animals. They learned to be careful. They learned to be brave.

Lily was surprised. She did not know swans could talk.
"How can you talk?" Lily asked.
"I can talk because I am a magic swan. I used to be a prince, but a witch turned me into a swan. She said I have to suffer until someone breaks the spell," the swan said.
"That's not fair. How can someone break the spell?" Lily asked.
The swan sighed.
"I don't know. The witch said only true love can break the spell. But who would love a weird swan like me?" the swan said.
Lily felt sorry for the swan. She wanted to help him.
"I love you, swan. You are not weird. You are beautiful and brave. Maybe I can break the spell," Lily said.
She hugged the swan gently. The swan felt a warm feeling in his heart. He felt something change in his body. He looked at his reflection in the water. He was not a swan anymore. He was a boy.
"Wow, you did it! You broke the spell! Thank you, Lily. You are my true love," the boy said.
Lily smiled. She liked the boy. He had brown hair and blue eyes. He looked like a prince.
"You're welcome, boy. What is your name?" Lily asked.
"My name is Leo. What is yours?" the boy asked.
"My name is Lily. Do you want to play with me and Ben?" Lily asked.
"Yes, I do. But first, can I kiss you?" Leo asked.
Lily nodded. Leo kissed her on the cheek. Lily giggled.
Mom saw Lily and Leo. She was shocked.
"Lily, who is that boy? Where did he come from?" Mom asked.
Lily and Leo ran to Mom. They told her the story of the magic swan and the witch.
Mom did not believe them at first. She thought they were making it up. But then she saw the black spot on Leo's neck. It was the same as the swan's.
Mom realized it was true. She was amazed and happy.
She hugged Lily and Leo.
"I'm glad you found each other. You are both very special. Now, let's go home and have some cake," Mom said.
Lily and Leo agreed. They held hands and followed Mom. Ben joined them too. He liked Leo. He wanted to be his friend.
They all went home and had cake. They were happy. They did not see the witch. She was watching them from a distance. She was angry and jealous. She wanted to curse them again. But she could not. One day, a little girl came to the garden. She was only three years old and was very excited to see the loyal hoop. She asked if she could pick it up and the hoop was happy to let her. The little girl looked intently at it, and the two of them were soon best friends. 
The little girl started bringing it some of her own food from home. She shared tasty snacks like carrots and apples. Even when her parents called her to go home, the loyal hoop refused to be separated from the little girl. 
From that day on, the loyal hoop followed the little girl everywhere she went. It ate snacks with her, played games and even slept in her bed. The two were inseparable and were loyal friends for life.

"I don't care! I want to play with them!" Max said. He grabbed some blocks and threw them at Lily and Ben.

Then, Mom came. She saw the mess and the fight. She was not happy.
"What is going on here?" Mom said. "Why are you fighting?"
"Max broke our tower!" Lily said.
"Max took our blocks!" Ben said.
"Max, is that true?" Mom said.
Max looked down. He felt bad. He knew he was wrong.
"Yes, Mom. I'm sorry." Max said.
Mom made Max say sorry to Lily and Ben. She made him help them restore their tower. She gave them more blocks to make it bigger and better. She told them to play nicely and share.
Lily and Ben forgave Max. They let him join their game. They showed him how to make a fit tower. They had fun together.
Mom smiled. She was happy. She gave them a hug and a kiss. She told them she loved them.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the backyard. They liked to make vroom-vroom noises and pretend they were racing. Sara had a red car and Ben had a blue car.
"Let's see who is faster," Sara said. "We can race to the fence and back."
"OK," Ben said. "But first we need to fill our cars with fuel."
They ran to the shed and found a can of water. They poured some water into their cars and said it was fuel.
"Ready, set, go!" Sara shouted. They pushed their cars along the grass and tried to reach the fence first.
But something was wrong. Sara's car stopped halfway and made a terrible noise. It sounded like it was broken.
"What happened?" Ben asked. He stopped his car and ran to Sara.
"I don't know," Sara said. She looked at her car and saw water dripping from it. "Maybe the fuel was bad."
She picked up her car and shook it. More water came out.
"That's not fuel, that's water!" Ben said. He looked at the can and saw a label that said "Water. Do not drink."
"Oh no," Sara said. "We made a mistake. We used the wrong can."
She felt sad and angry. She liked her car and did not want it to be broken.
"Why did you use this can?" she questioned Ben. "Did you not read the label?"
Ben felt sorry and scared. He did not read the label. He did not know how to read.
"I'm sorry, Sara," he said. "I did not know. I just saw a can and thought it was fuel."
He hugged Sara and said he was sorry again.
Sara hugged him back and said it was OK. She knew he did not mean to hurt her car.
"Maybe we can fix it," she said. "Let's go and ask Dad. He knows about cars."
They took their cars and the can and ran to the house. They hoped Dad could help them. They learned a lesson. They should always check what they use before they play.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They saw a lizard on a rock. It was green and brown and had a long tail.
"Wow, look at the lizard!" Lily said. "It is so cool. Can we touch it?"
Ben was scared of the lizard. He thought it might bite or scratch them. He shook his head.
"No, Lily, we can't touch it. It is not a toy. It is a wild animal. It might run away or hurt us."
But Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to see the lizard up close. She had an urge to touch it. She moved slowly towards the rock.
"Come on, Ben, don't be a baby. It is just a lizard. It is not a lion or a snake. It is cute and small. I want to pet it."
Ben tried to stop Lily. He grabbed her arm.
"Lily, stop! You are being silly. The lizard does not want to be petted. It wants to be left alone. You are scaring it. Come back here!"
But Lily pulled her arm away from Ben. She reached out her hand to the lizard. The lizard did not like Lily's hand. It felt threatened. It opened its mouth and showed its teeth. It hissed and jumped at Lily.
"Aaaah!" Lily screamed. She was surprised and scared. She fell back and dropped her hand. The lizard ran away and hid under a bush.
Ben ran to Lily. He hugged her and checked her hand. She had a small scratch on her finger. It was bleeding a little bit.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked. "Did the lizard hurt you?"
Lily nodded. She was crying. She felt sorry and stupid.
"Yes, Ben, I am okay. But the lizard hurt me. It was angry at me. I should have listened to you. You were right. I was wrong. I was silly. I am sorry, Ben."
Ben smiled and kissed her cheek. He took her hand and wrapped it with a leaf.
"It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are not silly. You are curious. But you have to be careful. Some animals don't like to be touched. They need their space. Next time, we can look at the lizard from far away. Okay?"
Lily smiled and nodded. She hugged Ben and said thank you.
"Okay, Ben. Thank you for being my friend. You are very smart and brave. And tall. I like you."
They walked back to the house. They saw their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Their mom and dad were glad they were okay. They gave them a hug and a cookie. They said they were proud of them for being honest and kind. They said they loved them very much.

As he reached the carrot, he heard a voice. It was a big, scary wolf. The wolf said, "Surrender, little bunny, or I will eat you!" Ben was scared, but he did not want to give up. He thought of a plan to trick the wolf.
Ben looked at the wolf and said, "If you are hungry, I can show you where there are more carrots. We can share them." The wolf thought about it and agreed. Ben led the wolf far away from the valley. When they got there, Ben quickly hopped away and hid.
The wolf was too busy eating the carrots to notice Ben was gone. Ben went back to the valley, safe and sound. From that day on, Ben and his friends lived happily in the valley, without any fear of the big, scary wolf.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Ben. Ben loved to explore and was always curious about everything. One day, he stumbled upon history books in his grandparents house.
Ben held one of the books and asked his Grandpa, “What’s this?”
Grandpa smiled. “This is a book about history," he said. 
Ben looked confused and asked, “What is history?”
Grandpa looked up and said, “History is something we can lift up to become better. It teaches us lessons and makes us smart. It’s full of stories.”
Ben didn’t understand and he said, “It looks so dull.”
Grandpa lifted Ben up onto his chair and said, “It’s not dull. It’s a part of your identity. It’s your past, present and future.”
Ben smiled and he suddenly understood the importance of learning history.
The moral of this story is that history can teach us valuable lessons. We can lift it up to become better and to avoid mistakes from the past.

Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park, draw pictures and read books. One day, they found a big letter on the ground. It was red and shiny and had a star on it.
"Wow, what an amazing letter!" Anna said. "I wonder what it says."
"Let's open it and see," Ben said. He tore the letter and looked inside. There was a piece of paper with some words on it.
"What does it say?" Anna asked.
Ben tried to read the words, but they were too hard. He only knew some of them. He read: "This is a magic letter. If you say the word 'disappear', you will go to a wonderful place. But be careful, you can only come back if you say the word 'appear'."
"Wow, that sounds fun!" Anna said. "Let's try it. Maybe we will go to a place with candy and toys and animals."
"OK, but we have to remember the word 'appear'," Ben said. "Or we will be stuck there forever."
They held hands and said together: "Disappear!"
Suddenly, everything went dark. They felt a strange wind and heard a loud noise. They opened their eyes and saw a new place. It was not wonderful at all. It was scary and ugly and cold. There were no candy and toys and animals. There were only rocks and thorns and monsters.
"Help!" Anna cried. "This is a bad place. I want to go home."
"Me too," Ben said. "Let's say the word 'appear' and go back."
They held hands and said together: "Appear!"
But nothing happened. They said it again and again, but nothing changed. They were still in the bad place. They looked at the piece of paper, but it was gone. They had lost it when they tore the letter.
They realized they had made a big mistake. They had opened a bad letter that lied to them. They had said a bad word that trapped them. They had forgotten a good word that could save them.
They started to cry. They wished they had never found the letter. They wished they had never said 'disappear'. They wished they could see their home and their parents and their friends again.
But they couldn't. They were stuck in the bad place forever. The end.

One day, the sky turned dark and grey. It started to rain very hard. Tom was still under the cherry tree, but he did not want to leave. The rain made Tom sad and he frowned. The squirrel came back and said, "You should go home, Tom. It's not safe here."
Tom didn't listen to the squirrel. He stayed under the cherry tree, even though he was cold and wet. The rain got stronger and stronger. Suddenly, a big wind came and blew the cherry tree down. Tom was hurt and cried. He should have listened to the squirrel and gone home.

He took the bird home and made a small nest for him. He closed the window so the bird wouldn't fly away and fed him his favorite snacks. He also wrote a note of his own explaining that he had taken the bird in. 
The little bird was very grateful and they became the best of friends. Living with him made Carlos forget all his worries and sadness, even on the gloomiest of days.

Tom makes some food with his toys. He puts them on a big plate. He calls Lily. "Lily, come and serve the food!" he says.
Lily comes with a tray. She puts the plate on the tray. She smiles. "I will serve the food to our guests," she says.
She walks to the table where their teddy bears are sitting. She puts the plate in front of them. "Here you go, teddy bears. Enjoy your food," she says.
But then, she sees something on the plate. It is a test. A test with many questions and answers. Lily is surprised. She looks at Tom. "Tom, why did you put a test on the plate?" she asks.
Tom laughs. He says, "I wanted to see if you are honest, Lily. If you are honest, you will tell the teddy bears that this is not food. This is a test. If you are not honest, you will pretend that this is food and try to make them eat it."
Lily thinks for a moment. She knows that lying is bad. She wants to be honest. She says, "Tom, you are silly. This is not food. This is a test. Teddy bears cannot eat a test. They cannot read a test. They only want to hug and cuddle."
Tom stops laughing. He says, "You are right, Lily. You are honest. I am sorry for tricking you. Let's make some real food for the teddy bears. They must be hungry."
Lily nods. She says, "OK, Tom. Let's make some real food. And let's eat some too. I am hungry too."
They hug and say sorry. They make some real food with their toys. They serve the food to the teddy bears and to themselves. They have a lot of fun. They are happy. They are friends.

"Wow, Daddy, we have so many books! We can read them all and learn many things," Lily said.
"Yes, we can, Lily. But I still wonder who sent them to us. And why they sent so many. And how we are going to pay for them," he said.

Suddenly, he heard something. It was a soft, gentle whistle coming from somewhere deep in the woods. Johnny decided to follow the sound, and he started to walk in its direction.
The whistle grew louder and louder, and soon he spotted a clearing in the woods. In the middle of the clearing was a big tree and standing next to it was a fox. The fox was whistling softly and when it saw Johnny, it stopped and gave him a friendly welcome.
Johnny was surprised and scared, but the fox seemed friendly. Johnny waved and smiled at the fox, and it smiled back. The two of them were now friends, and it was the start of a beautiful friendship.

In his house, Jimmy asked his mummy about the roaring. His mummy said "Oh Jimmy, that wasn't a real lion. It was a fake lion. It's made of plastic and it's just pretending to roar".
Jimmy wasn't scared anymore and he ran back to the street. He was ready to look at the fake lion! When Jimmy got back to the street, he saw the lion. It was so big and colourful that Jimmy was very excited. He smiled and said: "Hello, fake lion". 
Jimmy and fake lion became friends. Every day they would meet in the street and they would roar together. It made Jimmy really happy!

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Josh. He was very hungry, so his Mommy made him a steak. Josh bit into it, but it was very tough. He wasn't able to chew it.
Mommy said, "What's wrong, Josh?"
Josh replied, "My steak is too tough. I can't eat it."
Mommy smiled and said, "Let's count to 10 before you eat it, ok?"
Josh nodded and started counting. He got to 10 and tried the steak again. This time it was much easier to chew!
Josh smiled and said, "Thank you Mommy, that was much better!"
Mommy said, "See, how great it is to take our time and count? Patience is a great lesson to learn and it can help us in many situations. Always remember to count before making a decision!"
 Josh nodded and smiled as he enjoyed his steak. He'd learned a valuable lesson and was happy that he can now always count on his Mommy!

"Look, a squirrel!" Sara says. "Let's go and say hello."
"OK," Ben says. "But be quiet. We don't want to scare it."
They walk slowly and softly towards the squirrel. The squirrel sees them and stops eating. It looks at them with big eyes.
"Hello, squirrel," Sara says. "We are Sara and Ben. We are your friends. Can we play with you?"
The squirrel does not answer. It makes a funny noise and runs away. It jumps from one tree to another.
"Hey, come back!" Ben says. "We just want to play."
They chase the squirrel, but the squirrel is too fast. It disappears in the leaves.
"Where did it go?" Sara says. "I can't see it."
"Me neither," Ben says. "Maybe it went home."
They feel sad. They wanted to play with the squirrel.
But then they hear a rustle behind them. They turn around and see the squirrel. It is hanging from a branch, holding a big nut. It looks at them and smiles.
"Hello, Sara and Ben," the squirrel says. "I'm sorry I ran away. I was shy. But now I see you are nice. Do you want to share my nut?"
Sara and Ben are surprised and happy. They smile back.
"Yes, please," they say. "Thank you, squirrel."
They sit under the tree and eat the nut with the squirrel. They talk and laugh and have fun. They make a new friend.

Ben said, "No, Anna, I was playing it first. You can play the flute or the guitar."
Anna said, "But I don't want to play the flute or the guitar. I want to play the drum. It is the most fun."
Ben said, "Well, I want to play the drum too. It is the most fun."
They started to argue and tug at the drum. They made a lot of noise and their mom heard them. She came to their room and said, "Anna and Ben, what are you doing? You are making too much noise and you are not sharing. You need to settle down and take turns."
Anna and Ben looked at their mom and felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were fighting over the drum. We both like it a lot."
Mom said, "I know you both like the drum, but you can't play it at the same time. You have to share and be fair. How about you play the drum for five minutes, and then you switch with your sister or brother? That way, you can both enjoy the drum and the other instruments."
Anna and Ben thought that was a good idea. They said, "Okay, mom. We will do that. Thank you for helping us."
Mom smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you settled your problem. Now, you can play music nicely and have fun."

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big sack in the shed. They opened it and saw many fireworks inside. They were shiny and colorful and had funny names.
"Wow, look at these!" Tom said. "Let's take some and play with them."
"No, Tom, we can't!" Lily said. "Mum and Dad said fireworks are dangerous. They can hurt us and make loud noises. We have to wait for them to light them for us on Bonfire Night."
But Tom did not listen. He was naughty and wanted to have fun. He took some fireworks and hid them in his pocket. He told Lily to follow him to the park.
At the park, Tom found a stick and a match. He lit the match and touched it to the stick. Then he put the stick in a firework and threw it in the air.
"Look, Lily, look!" he shouted. "It's going to make a big bang!"
But the firework did not go up. It fell down and landed on a pile of dry leaves. The leaves caught fire and made a lot of smoke. The smoke made Lily and Tom cough and cry.
"Help, help!" they screamed. "Fire, fire!"
Some people saw the fire and called the firemen. The firemen came with a big red truck and a loud siren. They used a hose to put out the fire. They also found the sack of fireworks and took it away.
The firemen were angry and asked Lily and Tom who did it. Lily told them the truth. She said Tom was naughty and took the fireworks without asking. Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said he was sorry and he would never do it again.
The firemen told Lily and Tom to go home and tell their parents what they did. They said fireworks are not toys and they should never play with them. They said they were lucky they did not get hurt or burn the park.
Lily and Tom nodded and ran home. They were scared and sad. They knew Mum and Dad would be very cross with them. They wished they had listened to Lily and left the fireworks alone. They learned a hard lesson that day.

Ben knocks harder. "Anna, come on! You're taking too long!"

One day, a little girl named Lucy came to the pond. She saw Fred and said, "Hello, frog! You are so lovely. Can you be my friend?" Fred smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to be your friend!"
Lucy and Fred played together every day. They had so much fun. One day, a big bird came near the pond. The bird wanted to eat Fred! Lucy saw the bird and said, "No, bird! You cannot eat my friend!" Lucy protected Fred from the big bird. The bird flew away, and Fred was safe.
Fred was so happy that Lucy protected him. They were best friends forever. They played and laughed together at the pond every day.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big duck pond in the park. They wanted to feed the ducks.
Lily had some bread in her bag. She broke it into small pieces and threw them to the ducks. The ducks came closer and quacked. Lily was happy. She gave some bread to Ben and said, "Here, you feed them too."
Ben took the bread and threw it to the ducks. But he threw it too hard. One piece hit a duck on the head. The duck was angry. It flapped its wings and chased Ben. Ben was scared. He ran away from the duck. He dropped the bread and bumped into Lily. Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She cried.
Ben felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to hurt you or the duck. Are you okay?"
Lily looked at her knee. It was red and sore. She looked at Ben. He looked sad and sorry. She looked at the duck. It was graceful and calm. It had stopped chasing Ben and was eating the bread. Lily thought for a moment. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You didn't do it on purpose. And the duck is fine too. See, it's happy now."
Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You're a good friend. Can I help you up?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, please. And can we still play in the park?"
Ben said, "Of course. Let's go to the swings. They're fun and safe."
Lily and Ben held hands and walked to the swings. They forgot about the duck and the bread. They laughed and played. They were best friends again.

Tom and Lily went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But their favorite was the seal pool. The seals were big and gray, and they swam and jumped in the water.
"Look, mom, the seals are so funny!" Lily said, pointing at a seal that was playing with a ball.
"Yes, they are, sweetie. Do you want to feed them?" mom asked.
"Yes, yes, please!" Tom and Lily said together.
Mom bought some fish from a man and gave them to Tom and Lily. They walked to the edge of the pool, where some seals were waiting.
"Be careful, kids. Don't touch the seals, they might bite. Just throw the fish to them," mom said.
Tom and Lily nodded and threw the fish to the seals. The seals caught the fish with their mouths and made happy noises.
"Wow, they are so smart!" Tom said.
But Lily wanted to touch a seal. She saw a seal that was close to her. It looked friendly and cute. Lily reached out her hand and touched the seal's head.
"Ouch!" Lily cried. The seal bit her finger. It hurt a lot.
Mom ran to Lily and took her hand. She saw blood on her finger.
"Oh, no, Lily, what did you do?" mom asked.
"I touched the seal, mom. I wanted to pet it," Lily said, sobbing.
Mom hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, honey, but you can't touch the seals. They are wild animals, not pets. They don't like to be touched by strangers. You have to be careful and listen to me."
Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't touch the seals again."
Mom took Lily to a nurse, who cleaned and bandaged her finger. Tom followed them, feeling nervous.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Tom asked.
Lily smiled and said, "I'm okay, Tom. Thank you. The seal didn't mean to hurt me. It was just scared."
Tom hugged Lily and said, "I'm glad you're okay, Lily. I love you."
"I love you too, Tom," Lily said.
Mom smiled and said, "I love you both, kids. Now, let's go see some other animals, okay?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom."
They left the seal pool and went to see some other animals. They had fun, but they never touched the seals again.

Tom and Anna were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Tom was a lion and Anna was a bird.
"Roar!" Tom said, jumping on the couch. "I am the king of the jungle!"
"Tweet!" Anna said, flying around the room. "I am the fastest bird in the sky!"
They laughed and chased each other until they heard their mom call them.
"Tom! Anna! It's time for dinner!" Mom said from the kitchen.
Tom and Anna ran to the table and sat down. They saw their mom had made their favorite food: spaghetti and meatballs. They smiled and said thank you.
"Mom, this is yummy!" Tom said, twirling his fork.
"Mom, this is delicious!" Anna said, taking a big bite.
Mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it. And guess what? I have a surprise for you after dinner."
"What is it?" Tom and Anna asked, curious.
Mom winked and said, "You'll see. But you have to finish your plates first."
Tom and Anna ate quickly, eager to find out the surprise. They wondered what it could be. A new toy? A book? A game?
When they were done, mom brought out a big tray with four bowls. In each bowl, there was a scoop of ice cream, some whipped cream, and a cherry on top.
"Dessert!" Tom and Anna exclaimed, clapping their hands.
Mom nodded and said, "Yes, dessert. I made it for you because you have been such good kids today. You can choose your flavor: chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, or mint."
Tom and Anna looked at the bowls and thought hard. They both liked all the flavors, but they had different favorites.
"I want chocolate!" Tom said, reaching for a bowl.
"I want strawberry!" Anna said, grabbing another bowl.
But then they realized they had both taken the same bowls. They looked at each other and frowned.
"Hey, that's mine!" Tom said, pulling the bowl.
"No, that's mine!" Anna said, tugging the bowl.
They started to fight over the bowl, spilling some ice cream on the table. They were upset and angry.
"Stop it!" Mom said, raising her voice. "You can't have the same bowl. There are two more flavors. Why don't you trade?"
Tom and Anna looked at the other bowls. They saw vanilla and mint. They didn't like them as much as chocolate and strawberry, but they knew they had to share.
"Fine," Tom said, letting go of the bowl. "I'll take vanilla."
"Fine," Anna said, pushing the bowl. "I'll take mint."
They swapped the bowls and started to eat. They were still upset, but they didn't want to waste their dessert.
They ate in silence, until they heard a knock on the door.
"Who is it?" Mom asked, getting up.
She opened the door and saw their dad standing there. He had a big smile and a bag in his hand.
"Hi, everyone!" Dad said, coming in. "I'm home from work. And I have a surprise for you!"
He opened the bag and took out two boxes. He gave one to Tom and one to Anna.
"What is it?" Tom and Anna asked, excited.
They opened the boxes and saw two cupcakes. One was chocolate and one was strawberry. They had frosting and sprinkles and candles on top.
"Cupcakes!" Tom and Anna shouted, jumping up.
Dad nodded and said, "Yes, cupcakes. I bought them for you because I love you. And because today is a special day. Do you know what day it is?"
Tom and Anna thought for a moment. Then they remembered.
"It's our birthday!" Tom and Anna said, smiling.
Dad hugged them and said, "That's right. It's your birthday. You are four years old today. Happy birthday, my twins!"
Mom joined them and said, "Happy birthday, my sweeties!"
They lit the candles and sang happy birthday. Then they blew them out and made a wish.
Tom and Anna wished for the same thing: to be happy and to have more dessert.

Tommy was a dog who loved to run and play. He had a red collar that his owner gave him. He was very proud of his collar and liked to show it to other dogs. One day, he saw a big park with many trees and flowers. He wanted to explore it and have fun.
He asked his owner, "Can I go to the park, please?"
His owner said, "Yes, you can, but be careful. Don't go too far and come back when I call you."
Tommy was very excited and ran to the park. He saw many things that he liked: a pond, a bridge, a slide, a swing. He chased a butterfly, jumped over a log, slid down the slide, and swung on the swing. He was having a great time.
But he did not notice that his collar was loose. When he was on the swing, his collar slipped off his neck and fell on the ground. He did not see it and kept playing.
After a while, his owner called him, "Tommy, come here. It's time to go home."
Tommy heard his owner and ran back to him. But when he got there, his owner looked worried.
"Tommy, where is your collar?" his owner asked.
Tommy felt his neck and realized that his collar was gone. He felt sad and scared. He did not know where his collar was. He said, "I'm sorry, I lost my collar. I was playing and I did not see it."
His owner said, "Oh, Tommy, you should have been more careful. Your collar is important. It has your name and my phone number on it. If you lose it, someone might not know who you are or where you live. You could get lost or in trouble. You have to be more responsible and pay attention to your things."
Tommy felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, I was too excited and I forgot. Can we find my collar, please?"
His owner said, "We can try, but it might be hard. The park is big and there are many people and dogs. Someone might have taken it or thrown it away. But we can look for it together. Maybe we will succeed."
They went back to the park and searched for the collar. They asked other people and dogs if they had seen it. They looked under the slide, behind the log, near the pond, and on the bridge. They did not give up.
Finally, they found the collar. It was on a bench, next to a lady who was reading a book. She had seen the collar and picked it up, hoping to find the owner. She was happy to see Tommy and his owner.
She said, "Is this your collar? I found it on the ground. It's a nice collar. It has your name and your owner's phone number on it. You are a lucky dog."
Tommy and his owner thanked the lady and took the collar. Tommy was very happy and relieved. He put the collar back on his neck and felt safe and proud again.
He said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. I'm so glad we found my collar. I'm sorry I lost it. I will be more careful next time. I will not forget."
His owner said, "You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome. I'm glad too. I'm proud of you for looking for it and not giving up. You learned a good lesson today. You have to be responsible and pay attention to your things. They are part of who you are and what you love. You have to respect them and take care of them."
Tommy nodded and hugged his owner. He learned a good lesson and he was happy. He still loved to run and play, but he also loved his collar and his owner. He did not want to lose them again. He was a good dog.

"Let's fix our house, Lily," Ben said. "We can use these sticks and this mud."
"OK, Ben," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Max might knock it down again."
They worked hard to fill the hole with sticks and mud. They were happy when they finished. They went inside their house and pretended to have tea and cookies.
But they did not see that someone was watching them. It was Mrs. Jones, their nosy neighbor. She did not like children or dogs. She thought they were noisy and messy. She always complained to their parents.
She saw the hole in the wall and the sticks and mud. She was angry. She thought they had ruined the garden. She decided to tell their parents.
She walked to their house and knocked on the door. She waited for their parents to come out.
But before they did, Max saw her. He did not like her either. He ran out of the garden and barked at her. He jumped on her and licked her face.

Ben and Lily heard the noise and came out of their house. They saw Mrs. Jones and Max. They were scared. They did not want her to be mad at them.
They ran to her and tried to help her. They said they were sorry.
"Sorry, Mrs. Jones," Ben said. "We did not mean to make you angry. We were just repairing our house."
"Sorry, Mrs. Jones," Lily said. "We did not mean to make you dirty. We were just playing in the garden."
Mrs. Jones looked at them. She saw their innocent faces and their dirty hands. She felt a little sorry for them. She realized they were just children having fun.
She sighed and smiled. She said she was not angry. She said she was sorry too.
"Sorry, Ben and Lily," Mrs. Jones said. "I was too nosy. I should have let you play in peace. Your house is very nice. And your dog is very friendly."
She got up and dusted herself off. She picked up her purse and her glasses. She said goodbye to them and walked away.
Ben and Lily waved at her. They were happy. They hugged Max and thanked him. They went back to their house and played some more.

"Because he poked my tower!" Anna said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry to each other and hugged. Then they decided to build a tower together, without poking. Mommy smiled and gave them a kiss. She was glad they were friends again.

"Can we play with him?" Tom asks.
"Sure, you can. He likes to fetch and run," the man says. He gives them a ball.

"Spot, come back!" the man calls.

"Spot, stop!" Sara and Tom shout.
But Spot does not stop. He runs out of the park. He crosses the street.
"Spot, no!" the man yells.

But Spot does not look. He is too excited.

Spot is safe. He is not hurt. He is lucky.

Spot nods. He barks. He agrees.

Spot nods. He barks. He agrees.

Tim quickly grabbed the coffee and ran back to his mom. He gave her the coffee and said, "Mom, I pushed the big, red button in the kitchen and now the house is shaking!" His mom looked at him and said, "Oh no, Tim! That button was not for playing. Now our house will fall down." And just like that, their house fell down with a big crash.
The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and not touch things you are not supposed to.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they were playing with their blocks and cars in the living room. Sara wanted to build a big tower with the blocks, but Ben wanted to drive his cars around the tower and make noises.
"Ben, stop!" Sara said. "You are making my tower fall down!"
"But I want to play with my cars!" Ben said. "They are fun and fast!"
Sara and Ben started to argue and shout. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.
Mom came into the living room and saw the mess and the noise. She was not happy.
"Sara and Ben, what are you doing?" she asked. "It is time for lunch. Why are you fighting?"
Sara and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They felt bad.
"We are sorry, mom," they said. "We wanted to play different things and we did not agree."
Mom nodded and said, "I understand. Sometimes it is hard to share and cooperate. But you are twins and you love each other, right?"
Sara and Ben nodded and hugged each other.
"Right, mom," they said. "We love each other."
Mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now, let's go to the kitchen and have some lunch. I made your favorite sandwiches and fruit salad."
Sara and Ben followed their mom to the kitchen. They were hungry and happy.
"Mom, you are so thoughtful," Sara said. "Thank you for making us lunch."
"Yes, mom, you are the best," Ben said. "Can we request something?"
Mom looked at them and said, "Sure, what is it?"
Sara and Ben said, "Can we help you clean up the living room after lunch? We want to show you that we are sorry and that we can work together."
Mom hugged them and said, "Of course, you can. That is very kind and responsible of you. I am proud of you, Sara and Ben."
Sara and Ben smiled and ate their lunch. They learned that it is better to share and cooperate than to fight and argue. They also learned to appreciate their mom and her thoughtful gestures. They had a good day.

They went home. Sara put her tooth in a pink envelope. She wrote her name on it. She put it under her pillow. She brushed her teeth and went to bed. She dreamed of the tooth fairy.
The next morning, she woke up and looked under her pillow. She found a shiny coin. She was very happy. She ran to her mom and dad and showed them her coin. They smiled and said, "The tooth fairy came, Sara. She liked your tooth. She left you a coin."
Sara said, "Thank you, tooth fairy. Thank you, mom and dad. I love you." She gave them a big hug and a kiss. She put her coin in her piggy bank. She wondered when her next tooth would fall out.

"That's good, Tom, but mine is higher!" Lily said, smiling. She added another block to her tower, too.
They kept building and building, until they ran out of blocks. Then they looked at their towers and compared them.
"Wow, they are both very high!" Tom said. "But I think mine is a little bit higher. I win!"
"No, Tom, mine is higher. You can't see it well, but the top block is bigger than yours. I win!" Lily said.
They started to argue and get angry. They wanted to measure their towers, but they didn't have a ruler or a tape. They looked around the room, but they couldn't find anything to help them.
"Maybe we can ask Mom to help us," Tom said.
"OK, let's go find her," Lily said.
They left their towers on the floor and ran to the kitchen, where Mom was making lunch.
"Mom, Mom, can you help us?" Tom said.
"What is it, sweeties?" Mom said.
"We need to measure our towers. We want to know who made the highest one," Lily said.
"Your towers? Where are they?" Mom said.
"They are in the living room, on the floor," Tom said.
Mom smiled and said, "OK, I'll come and see them. But you have to wait a little bit. I need to finish making lunch first. Can you delay your game for a few minutes?"
Tom and Lily nodded. They knew Mom was busy and they had to be patient.
"OK, Mom, we'll wait. But please hurry, we really want to know who won," Tom said.
"Sure, sweeties, I'll be there soon. Why don't you go back to the living room and play something else? Maybe you can read a book or draw a picture," Mom said.
Tom and Lily agreed. They ran back to the living room and looked at their towers. They were still standing, tall and proud.

"Wow, let me see!" Tim said, reaching for the pebble. But Lily pulled it away.
"No, it is mine! I dug it up!" she said, hugging the pebble.
Tim was angry. He wanted to see the pebble too. He tried to grab it from Lily, but she ran away. They started to fight and yell.
"Quit it! Quit it!" they both shouted.
A lady who was sitting on a bench nearby heard them. She was their teacher, Miss Rose. She came over to them and asked them what was wrong.
"Tim and Lily, why are you fighting?" she said. "You are friends, aren't you?"
They both looked down and said nothing. They felt bad for fighting.
Miss Rose smiled and said, "Why don't you share the pebble? You can take turns holding it and looking at it. Maybe you can even find more pebbles underground if you work together."
Tim and Lily thought about it. They liked to share and play together. They said sorry to each other and hugged.
"OK, we will share the pebble," Tim said.
"And we will dig more together," Lily said.
They gave the pebble to Miss Rose and asked her to hold it for them. Then they took their shovels and buckets and went back to the sand. They dug and dug, and found more shiny rocks. They were happy and comfortable. They thanked Miss Rose for helping them.
The end.

"Ow!" Tom said, dropping the stick. He felt scared and sorry. He had hurt the turtle and its home.

Mom smiled and said, "That is good, Tom. Come on, let's go home and change your clothes. And maybe next time, you can play with Lily and the turtle nicely."

"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say.
The man takes out a small bag from his pocket. He opens it and gives them each a biscuit. They hold the biscuits in their hands.
"Say 'sit', Rex," the man says.
"Sit, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex sits down. He looks at them with his big eyes.
"Give him the biscuit," the man says.
Tom and Lily give Rex the biscuit. Rex takes it gently. He crunches it in his mouth. He licks his lips. He looks at them again.
"Say 'good boy', Rex," the man says.
"Good boy, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
Rex barks. He jumps up and down. He wags his tail.
"Thank you, Rex," Tom and Lily say.
"Thank you, sir," they say to the man.
"You're welcome," the man says. "Rex likes to make new friends. He thinks you are very nice."
Tom and Lily smile. They hug Rex. They say goodbye to him and the man. They go back to play in the park. They are happy. They think Rex is a wonderful dog. They think his biscuit is delicious.

Buddy was very worried, so he went and spoke to the pup. He said, “Please be careful my friend! Eaters can get sick when they don’t eat the same food each day.” But the pup didn’t listen. 
Soon the pup was very ill. The other animals were sad and even the old dog was very worried. Buddy had to look for a way to help his friend. 
Suddenly he had an idea. He quickly found some of his old food and brought it to the pup. The pup ate it, and soon he was feeling better. 
Buddy and the pup shared a peaceful moment, and the pup learned a valuable lesson: eat the same food every day and stay healthy!

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. But it was a very hot day and the sun was bright. They felt tired and thirsty.
"Let's find some shade," Anna said to Ben. "We can rest and drink some water."
They looked around and saw a big tree with many green leaves. They ran to the tree and sat under it. The shade was cool and nice. They drank some water from their bottles and felt better.
"Look, what is that?" Ben pointed to something shiny on the ground. It was a small metal ring with a red stone in it. It sparkled in the sun.
"Maybe it is a treasure," Anna said. She picked up the ring and examined it. She turned it around and looked at the stone. It was smooth and bright.
"Can I see it?" Ben asked. He reached out his hand.
"OK, but be careful," Anna said. She gave the ring to Ben. He examined it too. He rubbed the stone and felt its warmth.
"It is very pretty," Ben said. "Do you think someone lost it?"
"Maybe," Anna said. "Or maybe it is a magic ring. Maybe it can make wishes come true."
"What would you wish for?" Ben asked.
Anna thought for a moment. She looked at the ring, then at Ben, then at the park. She smiled.
"I would wish for more days like this," she said. "More days to play with you and have fun."
Ben smiled too. He nodded.
"Me too," he said. He put the ring on his finger. It fit perfectly.
They held hands and closed their eyes. They made their wish together. Then they opened their eyes and laughed.
They did not know if the ring was magic or not. But they felt happy and lucky. They decided to keep the ring as a secret. They put it in their pocket and got up.
"Let's play some more," Anna said.
"OK, let's go," Ben said.
They ran to the slide and slid down. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their skin. They were not tired anymore. They were having the best day ever.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with clay. They had many colors of clay, but their favorite was gray. They said gray clay was the best because it had a soft texture and could make any shape.
One day, they decided to make a big castle with gray clay. They worked hard and used all their gray clay to build the walls, the towers, and the gate. They were very proud of their castle and put it on the table to dry.
But then, they saw that their little brother, Sam, had taken some of their gray clay and made a ball. He was bouncing the ball on the floor and laughing.
"Hey, that's our clay!" Anna shouted. "Give it back!"
"No, it's mine!" Sam said. "I like the ball!"
Ben ran to Sam and tried to grab the ball, but Sam was faster and ran away. Anna and Ben chased him around the house, but they could not catch him. They were angry and sad.
Mom saw what was happening and called them to the living room. She asked them why they were fighting over the clay.
"Because he took our clay!" Anna and Ben said.
"But you have so much clay!" Mom said. "Can't you share with your brother?"
"No, we can't!" Anna and Ben said. "We need all the gray clay for our castle!"
Mom looked at their castle and smiled. She said it was very beautiful and creative, but she also said that clay was meant to be played with, not to be kept on the table.
She told them a story about how she and her sister used to play with clay when they were little. They made different things every day and had fun. They also shared their clay with their friends and learned new ideas. She said that playing with clay was more fun when you share and learn from others.
She asked them if they wanted to try that with Sam. She said that maybe they could teach him how to make a castle, or learn how to make a ball. She said that sharing and learning would make them happy and smart.
Anna and Ben thought about it and agreed. They said they were sorry to Sam and asked him if he wanted to play with them. Sam was happy and said yes. They went to the table and started to play with the gray clay. They made a bigger castle, a ball, and some other things. They had fun and laughed.
They learned that sharing and learning is better than fighting and settling. They also learned that gray clay can make many things, not just one. They thanked Mom for her story and her advice. Mom hugged them and said she was proud of them. She said that gray clay was the best because it had a soft texture and could make any shape, but also because it could make them happy and smart.

Sam and Tom were happy and relieved. They hugged each other, and thanked the black car. They decided to play with the black car more often, because it was brave and helpful. They also decided to be more careful, and look out for dogs and other things on the sidewalk. They learned that sometimes, old and dirty things can be useful and fun.

She took him to a big room, where there were many toys and books. Tom saw a big train set, a doll house, a rocking horse, and a pile of blocks. He was very happy, and wanted to play with everything.
"Wow, thank you, auntie!" he said. "Can I play with the train?"
"Of course, Tom. But be gentle with it. It is very old and fragile. It was your grandfather's train, when he was a boy like you."
Tom nodded, and went to the train set. He turned on the switch, and watched the train go around the tracks. He smiled, and tried to make the train go faster and slower. He was having so much fun, that he did not notice that he was pulling the wires too hard.
Suddenly, there was a loud snap, and a spark. The train stopped, and smoke came out of the engine. Tom gasped, and felt scared. He had broken the train!
"Oh no, oh no, oh no!" he cried. "I'm sorry, auntie, I'm sorry!"
He ran to his aunt, who was sitting on a sofa, reading a book. He hugged her, and sobbed.
"Auntie, I broke the train! I'm so clumsy, I'm so bad!"
His aunt put down her book, and looked at him. She saw his tears, and felt sorry for him. She also saw the smoke, and felt worried.
"Tom, don't cry. It's okay. It was an accident. You didn't mean to break the train. You were just playing."
She kissed him, and wiped his tears.
"Come on, let's go and see if we can fix the train. Maybe it's not too bad. Maybe we can make it work again."
She took his hand, and led him to the train set. She looked at the wires, and the engine. She smiled, and said:
"Tom, you are very lucky. The train is not broken. It just needs a new battery. I have one in the drawer. Let me get it, and we can put it in the train. Then, it will run again."
She went to the drawer, and got a new battery. She opened the train, and replaced the old battery with the new one. She closed the train, and turned on the switch. The train started to move, and whistle. Tom clapped, and cheered.
"Yay, the train works! Thank you, auntie, thank you!"
He hugged her, and kissed her. He was very happy, and relieved.
"You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad the train works. You can play with it as much as you want. But remember, be gentle with it. It is very old and fragile. It was your grandfather's train, when he was a boy like you."
Tom nodded, and smiled. He went back to the train set, and played with it. He was gentle with it, and careful with the wires. He enjoyed the train, and the other toys. He had a wonderful time, in the big palace, with his aunt. He was not clumsy, he was not bad. He was a good boy, and a happy boy.

One day, they were playing hide and seek again. Anna counted to ten and said, "Ready or not, here I come!" Timmy ran to the kitchen and opened the small door. He crawled inside the cupboard and closed the door behind him. He was very quiet and still. He heard Anna's footsteps in the hall, then in the living room, then in the bedroom. He smiled. She would never find him here.
But then, he heard a loud noise. It was the door of the big cupboard. Someone was opening it. Timmy was scared. He hoped it was not Anna. He hoped it was Mommy or Daddy. He peeked through a crack and saw a face. It was not Mommy or Daddy. It was a stranger. A man with a mask and a bag. He was looking for something to take. He saw Timmy.
"Hey, what are you doing here?" the man said. He grabbed Timmy by the arm and pulled him out of the cupboard. Timmy screamed. He wanted Anna. He wanted Mommy. He wanted Daddy. He wanted to be hidden.
"Shut up, kid!" the man said. He put his hand over Timmy's mouth. He looked around. He saw a phone on the counter. He picked it up and dialed a number. He said, "I found something in the kitchen. A kid. What should I do with him?"
Timmy heard another voice on the phone. It was Anna. She said, "Let him go, or I'll call the police. I saw you from the window. I have your picture. I have your license plate. You have no choice. Surrender."
The man dropped the phone. He looked at Timmy. He looked at the window. He looked at the door. He was trapped. He was scared. He let go of Timmy and said, "OK, OK, you win. I surrender. Don't call the police. Please."
Timmy ran to the door. He opened it and saw Anna. She hugged him and said, "You're safe, Timmy. You're brave. I'm sorry I couldn't find you sooner. I love you."
Timmy hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Anna. You're smart. You're strong. You saved me."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted the toys. She said, "No, they are ours now. We found them. Come on, help me carry the sack."
Ben felt bad. He did not want to hurt Lily, but he did not want to do something wrong. He said, "No, Lily, I don't want to. It is not fair. Let's leave the sack here and go home. Maybe the owner will come back and find it."
Lily got angry. She said, "Fine, then I will take the sack by myself. You are not my friend anymore. Go away!"
She grabbed the sack and ran away. Ben was sad. He watched Lily go. He hoped she would change her mind.

She decided to take the sack back to the park and look for Ben. She hoped he would forgive her. She hoped they could be friends again. She hoped they could watch the sunset together and say how sweet it was.
The moral of the story is: Do not be selfish and take what is not yours. Be honest and kind. Friendship is more important than toys.

Max was angry, but then he saw how much fun Lucy and Lily were having. He thought maybe he could have fun too if he shared his toys. So Max walked over and asked, "Can I play with you?"

Soon, she saw a rabbit hop into the garden. It smelled the carrots and lettuce and followed the trail. It reached the basket and jumped inside. Anna ran out and closed the basket. She caught the rabbit!
She was very happy and proud. She showed her mom the rabbit and told her what she did. Her mom was surprised and impressed. She said Anna was very clever and brave. She also said it was difficult to keep a rabbit as a pet. She asked Anna what she wanted to do with it.

She took the basket to the edge of the garden and opened it. The rabbit hopped out and ran away. Anna waved goodbye and smiled. She hoped the rabbit would not steal her vegetables again. Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play on the farm with the animals. One day, they see a big cow in the field. The cow is black and white and has a bell around her neck.
"Look, a cow!" Sam says. "Can we pet her?"
Ben nods. "Yes, let's go. Maybe she will give us some milk."
They run to the cow and try to touch her. But the cow does not like it. She moos loudly and shakes her head. She kicks her legs and runs away.
"Hey, come back!" Ben shouts. "We just want to be your friends."
But the cow does not listen. She runs to the fence and jumps over it. She runs to the road, where there are many cars and trucks.
"Oh no!" Sam says. "The cow is in danger. She might get hit by a car. We need to help her."
They run after the cow, but they are too slow. The cow is faster and runs across the road. The cars and trucks honk and brake. The drivers are angry and scared.
"Stop, cow, stop!" Sam and Ben yell. "You are not safe there. Come back to the farm."
But the cow does not stop. She runs to the woods, where there are many trees and animals. She thinks she is free and happy.
Sam and Ben are sad and worried. They do not know what to do. They need to find the cow and bring her back. They need to tell their dad what happened. They hope the cow is okay.
They look around and see a man on a bike. He is wearing a helmet and a bright vest. He is alert and smart. He sees the cow and the boys.
"Hey, kids, what are you doing here?" he asks. "Do you know that cow?"
Sam and Ben nod. "Yes, she is from our farm. She ran away and we followed her. But we can't catch her. She is too fast and wild."
The man smiles. "Don't worry, I can help you. I have a rope and a whistle. I can call the cow and tie her to my bike. Then we can take her back to your farm. Do you want to come with me?"
Sam and Ben smile. "Yes, please. Thank you, mister. You are very kind and brave."
They get on the bike with the man. He blows his whistle and waves his rope. The cow hears him and stops. She is curious and tired. She comes closer and lets him tie her to the bike.
"Good girl, cow," the man says. "You are safe now. Let's go home."
They ride back to the farm. The cow moos softly and follows the bike. Sam and Ben are happy and relieved. They hug the cow and the man.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you," they say. "You saved the cow and us. You are our hero."
The man laughs. "You're welcome, kids. You are very brave and caring. You love the cow and the farm. You are good friends."
They reach the farm and see their dad. He is surprised and glad. He sees the cow and the man and the boys.
"What happened?" he asks. "Where did you go? How did you find the cow?"
Sam and Ben tell him everything. They tell him how the cow ran away and how the man helped them. They tell him how they learned a lesson.
"We are sorry, dad," they say. "We did not mean to scare the cow. We just wanted to pet her. But we learned that we need to be gentle and respectful with the animals. We need to listen to them and watch them. We need to keep them safe and happy."
Dad smiles and hugs them. "I'm proud of you, boys. You did the right thing. You helped the cow and the man. You are good sons."
He thanks the man and gives him some milk and cheese. He invites him to stay for dinner. He is grateful and friendly.
They all go inside the house. They eat and talk and laugh. They are a big family. The cow is in the barn. She is calm and warm. She has a new friend. She is a happy cow.

Once upon a time, there was an angry frog hopping around a pond. Suddenly, he spotted something sparkly on a rock near the pond.
The frog hopped over and peered at the sparkly thing. It was very shiny, and the frog wanted it very badly. He started to try and take the sparkly thing away.
Suddenly, there was a loud noise, and the frog heard a voice. It was the voice of a wise old turtle. The turtle warned the frog, “You should never try and take things that don't belong to you.”
The frog felt sad and stopped. Instead, he decided to create something special. He found some clay near the pond and rolled it into a ball. Then he used twigs from nearby trees to make two arms and two legs. 
With the help of the old turtle, the frog finally created a beautiful clay frog. He was so proud of it. He decided to leave the sparkly thing at the pond and brought the clay frog home with him.
The moral of this story is that it's better to create something positive instead of taking something that doesn't belong to you.

The cheese laughed and clapped his hands. It loved to see everyone having so much fun. After a while, everyone slowed down and stopped spinning. They were all out of breath and worn out, but they had a great time. 
The Cheese knew it would always remember the fun they had spinning together.

Tom and Lily are friends who like to joke with each other. They play games and try to make each other laugh. Sometimes they are competitive and want to win.
One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big cooler with drinks and snacks. They are thirsty and hungry, so they run to the cooler.
"Can I have a juice, please?" Tom asks his mom.
"Me too, me too!" Lily says.
Their moms give them each a juice box and a cookie. They sit on the grass and enjoy their treats.
"Hey, Lily, do you want to hear a joke?" Tom says.
"Sure, Tom, tell me a joke," Lily says.
"Okay, here it goes. Why did the chicken cross the road?" Tom says.
"I don't know, why?" Lily says.
"To get to the cooler!" Tom says and laughs.
Lily thinks for a moment, then shakes her head.
"That's not a joke, Tom, that's silly. The chicken would not want a juice or a cookie. The chicken would want seeds or worms," Lily says.
Tom frowns. He thinks his joke is funny.
"No, Lily, you don't get it. It's a joke because it's unexpected. The chicken does something different than usual. That's what makes it funny," Tom says.
Lily shrugs. She does not think it's funny.
"Well, I have a better joke, Tom. Do you want to hear it?" Lily says.
"Okay, fine, tell me your joke," Tom says.
"Okay, here it goes. What do you get when you cross a cooler and a competitive kid?" Lily says.
"I don't know, what?" Tom says.
"A cool kid!" Lily says and laughs.
Tom rolls his eyes. He thinks his joke is better.
"That's not a joke, Lily, that's lame. The cooler and the kid have nothing to do with each other. That's what makes it boring," Tom says.
Lily smiles. She thinks her joke is clever.
"No, Tom, you don't get it. It's a joke because it's a pun. The cooler and the kid sound the same. That's what makes it funny," Lily says.
Tom and Lily look at each other. They realize they have different kinds of jokes. They decide to agree to disagree.
They finish their juice and cookies and go back to playing. They still like to joke with each other, but they also respect each other's humor. They are friends who have fun.

One day, it was very cold outside. Max's mom said, "Max, you must wear your coat today!" Max did not want to wear the coat, but he wanted to go outside and play. Max struggled to put on the coat, but he did it. He was still a stubborn dog, but he knew he needed to wear the coat to play outside.
When Max went outside, he saw his friend, a cat named Luna. Luna was wearing a warm coat too. Max and Luna played in the cold, but they did not feel cold because they wore their coats. Max learned that sometimes it is good to listen to his mom, even if he is a stubborn dog.

Once upon a time there lived an old chubby mouse. He lived a long and happy life but one day something strange happened. He took a deep breath and gasped for oxygen. All the other animals noticed his big breaths and wondered why he was breathing so hard. 
The mouse knew he was running out of oxygen and had a plan to save himself. He snuck into the nearby village and found a small red balloon. He tied it to his back and jumped into the air. As he flew he caught a breeze and soared into the sky. 
The mouse was so happy that he began to laugh. But soon he realized his balloon was shrinking. He looked down to see the chubby mouse was beginning to plummet. With a loud pop, the balloon burst which sent the mouse crashing to the ground. 
But luckily, the mouse had enough oxygen left in his balloon to save him! He landed safely back on the ground and everyone around cheered. The mouse learned a valuable lesson that day and was able to live another long and happy life.

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a lot of toys, but their favorite ones were the magic wand and the magic hat. They pretended to be wizards and witches and made up spells and adventures.
One day, they wanted to make a cake with their magic. They took some flour, sugar, eggs, and butter from the kitchen and put them in a big bowl. Then they waved their wand and said, "Magic, magic, make a cake!"
But nothing happened. The bowl was still full of flour, sugar, eggs, and butter. They tried again and again, but nothing changed.
Lila and Tom were frustrated. They wanted to eat a cake, but their magic did not work. They wondered why their magic did not work. They hoped their magic would work soon.
They decided to ask their mom for help. They went to the living room, where their mom was reading a book. They showed her the bowl and the wand and the hat.
"Mom, can you help us?" Lila asked. "We want to make a cake with our magic, but it does not work."
Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "I'm sorry, my loves, but magic is not real. You can't make a cake with a wand and a hat. You need to use the oven and a recipe."
Lila and Tom were surprised. They thought magic was real. They liked to pretend with their magic toys. They felt sad and confused.
"But mom, we like magic. We have fun with magic. Can we still play with magic?" Tom asked.
Their mom nodded and kissed them. She said, "Of course you can. Magic is not real, but it is fun. You can use your imagination and creativity to make up stories and games with your magic toys. But when you want to make a cake, you need to use the oven and a recipe. And I can help you with that. How about we make a cake together?"
Lila and Tom smiled. They liked the idea of making a cake with their mom. They said, "Yes, please. We want to make a cake with you."
They followed their mom to the kitchen, where they put the bowl and the wand and the hat aside. They took out a new bowl and a recipe book. They helped their mom measure, mix, and bake the ingredients. They waited for the cake to be ready. They hoped the cake would be yummy.
They were happy. They learned that magic is not real, but it is fun. They learned that they can use their imagination and creativity to play with their magic toys. They learned that they can use the oven and a recipe to make a cake. They learned that they can have fun with their mom.
They ate the cake and enjoyed it. They said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. You are our magic."

"What do they do on the ship?" Anna asked.
"They carry things, like food, clothes, or toys, from one place to another. Sometimes they also help people who are in trouble on the water," dad said.

"Wow, look at these!" Tom said. "They are from history. They are very old and special. I want them all!"
"No, Tom, you can't have them all!" Sam said. "We have to share. Maybe someone else needs them. They are not ours."
Tom did not listen. He grabbed the hat, the map, the coin, and the medal. He ran away from Sam. He was very happy. He thought he was successful.
But Sam was very sad. He felt lonely and angry. He followed Tom to his house. He knocked on the door. He wanted to talk to Tom.
"Tom, please open the door!" Sam said. "We are friends. We have to be nice to each other. You have to accept that you can't have everything. You have to give some things back."
Tom heard Sam. He felt sorry. He knew he was wrong. He opened the door. He gave Sam the hat, the map, the coin, and the medal. He said sorry to Sam.
"Sam, I am sorry. You are right. I was greedy and mean. I don't need these things. They are from history. They belong to someone else. I accept that I can't have everything. I want to share with you. Can we still be friends?"
Sam smiled. He hugged Tom. He said yes. They were friends again. They decided to return the box to the park. They hoped someone would find it and learn from history. They learned that being successful is not about having everything, but about being kind and generous.

The little girl was very happy to receive her toy back. She said "Thank you, blue fish!" The blue fish smiled and swam away. All the friends of the blue fish clapped and cheered. The blue fish learned that helping others can make you feel good too.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Ben brings a new toy to Mia's house. It is a microscope. Ben says, "Look, Mia, this is a microscope. It can make small things big. Do you want to try?"
Mia nods and smiles. She likes to see new things. Ben puts a slide with a flower on the microscope. He turns a knob and the flower becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Wow, Ben, the flower is so pretty. It has many colors and shapes. Can I see more?"
Ben nods and smiles. He puts another slide with a bug on the microscope. He turns another knob and the bug becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Eek, Ben, the bug is so ugly. It has many legs and eyes. It is scary. I don't like it."
Ben laughs and says, "Don't be scared, Mia, it is just a toy bug. It can't hurt you. It is interesting to see how different things are. Do you want to see something else?"
Mia nods and says, "Yes, Ben, but something nice, not scary." Ben puts another slide with a candy on the microscope. He turns the knob and the candy becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Mmm, Ben, the candy is so sweet. It has many crystals and colors. It looks yummy. Can I have some?"
Ben laughs and says, "Sorry, Mia, you can't eat the candy. It is too small. But I have a real candy for you. Here, take one. It is sweet and yummy. We can share."
Mia takes the candy and says, "Thank you, Ben, you are a good friend. I like your microscope. It is a fun toy. We can see many things with it. But I like candy more."
Ben and Mia eat the candy and laugh. They are happy. They like to play with the microscope and with each other. They are good friends.
