Tom loved his bicycle. He rode it every day in the park with his dad. He liked to go fast and feel the wind on his face. He also liked to ring the bell and wave to the other kids.
One day, Tom saw a big hole in the ground. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He got off his bicycle and walked to the hole. He leaned over and saw something shiny. He reached out his hand and touched it. It was a metal box.
Tom wanted to open the box and see what was inside. He tried to pull it out of the hole, but it was too heavy. He looked around and saw a shovel. He had an idea. He took the shovel and started to dig around the box. He thought he could make the hole bigger and then lift the box.
But he did not see his dad coming. His dad was looking for him and saw him digging in the hole. His dad was angry and shouted at him. He said, "Tom, what are you doing? You are making a mess and you are ruining the grass. And where is your bicycle?"
Tom felt scared and sad. He dropped the shovel and pointed to his bicycle. He had left it next to the hole, but he did not see that a dog had come and taken it away. The dog had dragged it to a corner and started to chew on it. The bicycle was broken and dirty.
His dad saw the bicycle and was even more angry. He said, "Tom, you are very naughty. You did not take care of your bicycle and you lost it. Now you have no bicycle and you have to go home. And you have to help me bury this hole and fix the grass."
Tom cried and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I just wanted to see the box. I did not mean to lose my bicycle. Please don't be harsh with me."
His dad sighed and said, "I know, Tom. But you have to learn to be careful and responsible. Come on, let's go and find the dog and get your bicycle back. Maybe we can fix it and ride it again. And maybe we can come back another day and see what is in the box. But only if you promise to listen to me and not dig in the ground again."
Tom nodded and said, "I promise, dad. I love you and I love my bicycle. Can we still be friends?"
His dad smiled and said, "Of course, Tom. We are always friends. Now let's go and find that dog and your bicycle."

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park after school. One day, Sara had a new toy. It was a big, red ball. She wanted to show it to Tom.
"Look, Tom, I have a new ball. Do you want to play with me?" Sara asked.
"Yes, please. Your ball is very nice. Can I kick it?" Tom said.
Sara nodded. She was happy to share her ball with Tom. They took turns kicking the ball in the grass. They had a lot of fun.
But then, the sun started to go down. It was evening. The sky was dark and the park was quiet. Sara and Tom felt cold and scared.
"Let's go home, Sara. It's too dark and scary here," Tom said.
"OK, Tom. But where is my ball? I can't see it," Sara said.
They looked around, but they could not find the ball. It was gone. Someone had taken it.
"Who took my ball? That's not fair. I liked my ball," Sara said. She started to cry.
Tom felt sorry for Sara. He wanted to help her. He had an idea.
"Sara, don't cry. I have something for you. It's not a ball, but it's something nice. Do you want to see it?" Tom said.
He reached into his backpack and took out a small, yellow teddy bear. He had won it at the fair. He liked it, but he liked Sara more.
"Here, Sara. This is for you. I offer you my teddy bear. You can keep it. It's soft and warm and friendly. It will make you feel better," Tom said.
He gave the teddy bear to Sara. Sara stopped crying. She smiled. She hugged the teddy bear.
"Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. I like your teddy bear. It's very nice. You are my best friend," Sara said.
They held hands and walked home. They were not scared anymore. They were happy. They had each other.

But Tim was serious. He asked his friends to help him. They all tried to lift the truck, and it started to move! The truck driver was happy. He said, "Thank you, Tim, for your help!" The people in the town learned that even a little boy can make a big difference. The moral of the story is that everyone can help, no matter how small they are.

In the end, Tim learned that it's essential to be careful with the things he finds and always keep clean. He felt happy and safe knowing that his mom was there to guide him. She showed her story to her brother Max. Max was older and he liked to read. But he was also bossy. He looked at Lily's story and said, "This is not a good story. The princess is too small and the dragon is too big. And you spelled some words wrong. You should write like me."
Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "This is my story. I can write how I want. You are not the boss of me. Go away!"

The rabbit looked at Sara and twitched its nose. It smelled the carrot and came closer. It took a bite and nibbled happily. Sara smiled and stroked its soft fur. She said, "You are very cute and delicate. I like you. What is your name?"
The rabbit did not answer, but it licked Sara's hand and cuddled with her. Sara felt happy and warm. She said, "I will call you Fluffy. Do you want to be my friend?"
The rabbit nodded and snuggled with Sara. Sara said, "I recommend that you come back tomorrow. I will bring you more carrots and we can play together. OK?"
The rabbit agreed and hopped away. Sara waved goodbye and ran to her mom. She told her about Fluffy and how they shared a carrot. Her mom hugged her and said, "That sounds wonderful, Sara. You are very kind and generous. I am proud of you."

Cat was sitting by a tree. "Cat, did you send the big barrel?" Bo asked. Cat shook her head. "No, I did not send it," Cat said. They all went back to the barrel and looked at it, feeling confused.
Then, they heard a small voice from inside the barrel. "Help, help!" it said. Bo, Tim, and Cat all looked at each other. Bo used his big paw to open the barrel.
Out came a little bunny named Sue. "Thank you for helping me!" Sue said. "I was stuck in the barrel and could not get out." Bo, Tim, and Cat were happy they could help Sue. They all became good friends and played together every day.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toy boats in the harbor. They liked to watch the big boats come and go, and make noises like horns and engines. Sometimes they saw fish and birds in the water, too.
One day, they saw a new boat that was very big and shiny. It had a lot of flags and people on it. Sara and Tom wanted to see it closer, so they ran to the edge of the harbor. But they were not careful, and they dropped their toy boats on the ground.
"Oh no!" Sara cried. "Our boats are broken! They are fragile and the ground is hard!"
Tom was sad, too. He picked up his boat and saw a big crack in it. He tried to fix it, but it did not work. He looked at Sara's boat and saw that it was worse. It had lost its mast and its sail.
"Maybe we can ask the people on the big boat to help us," Tom said. "They have tools and glue and stuff."
Sara nodded. She liked Tom's idea. She saw a man on the big boat who was wearing a hat and a uniform. He looked like he was in charge. She waved her hand and called to him.
"Excuse me, sir! Can you help us, please? Our toy boats are broken and we don't know what to do!"
The man heard Sara's voice and looked down. He saw the two children and their toy boats. He smiled and walked to the side of the big boat. He leaned over and said:
"Hello, there! I'm sorry to hear that your toy boats are broken. They look very nice. What are their names?"
Sara and Tom told him their boat names. Sara's boat was called Lily and Tom's boat was called Max. The man nodded and said:
"Well, Lily and Max are very lucky to have you as their owners. You know what? I have some spare parts and some glue in my cabin. Why don't you come up and I'll see what I can do to fix them?"
Sara and Tom were very happy. They thanked the man and followed him to the big boat. He helped them climb up and took them to his cabin. There, he had a lot of things that looked like toys, but they were for real boats. He found some pieces that matched Lily and Max and glued them together. He also gave them some stickers and some paint to decorate them.
"There you go," he said. "Lily and Max are good as new. Maybe even better. They are very strong and beautiful now. You can take them back to the harbor and play with them again."
Sara and Tom were overjoyed. They hugged the man and thanked him again. They took their toy boats and ran back to the harbor. They put them in the water and watched them float and sail. They were very careful not to drop them or bump them. They knew they were fragile, but they also knew they were loved.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a long, pink rag that she liked to pretend was a scarf. Ben had a big, blue truck that he liked to drive around. They were having fun until Ben saw Sara's rag and wanted it.
"Give me your rag!" Ben said to Sara.
"No, it's mine!" Sara said to Ben.
"Why?" Ben asked.
"Because it's pretty and soft and I like it," Sara explained.
"But I want it too," Ben said. "It can be a flag for my truck."
He tried to grab the rag from Sara, but she held on tight. They started to pull and tug on the rag, making loud noises.
"Stop it, you two!" their mom said, coming into the room. "What are you doing?"
"Sara won't share her rag with me," Ben said.
"Ben tried to take my rag from me," Sara said.
Mom looked at them with a stern face. "You both need to learn to share and be nice to each other. Rag is just a thing. Friends are more important. How would you feel if someone took your toy away?"
Sara and Ben thought for a moment. They felt sorry for being mean to each other.
"I'm sorry, Sara," Ben said. "You can have your rag back."
"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara said. "You can play with my rag if you want."
They hugged and smiled. Mom was happy to see them make up.
"That's better," she said. "Now, why don't you play together nicely? I'll make you some cookies for a snack."
Sara and Ben nodded and went back to their toys. They decided to use the rag as a bridge for the truck. They were having fun again until they heard a loud rip. They looked at the rag and saw that it was torn in half.
"Oh no!" Sara cried.
"Oh no!" Ben cried.
They had pulled the rag too hard and broke it. They felt sad and angry. They blamed each other for the rag's ruin.
"It's your fault!" Sara said to Ben.
"No, it's your fault!" Ben said to Sara.
They started to fight again, hitting and kicking each other. Mom heard the noise and came back into the room. She saw the rag and the children.
"What happened?" she asked.
"They broke my rag!" Sara said.
"They broke my flag!" Ben said.
Mom was very disappointed and angry. She took away their toys and sent them to their rooms. She told them they had to stay there until they learned to share and be nice to each other.
Sara and Ben went to their rooms, crying and sulking. They wished they had listened to Mom and not fought over the rag. They realized they had lost their toy and their friend. They felt lonely and sorry.
The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and selfish. Share and be nice to your friends. Things can break, but friends can last.

He runs to the pond and shouts at the duck. He waves his stick and tries to scare the duck. But the duck does not listen. It swims faster and farther. Tom follows the duck. He forgets to be careful.
Mia sees Tom go too close to the pond. She is scared. She calls Tom to stop. She tells him to come back. But Tom does not hear her. He only sees the duck and the ball.
He reaches the edge of the pond and leans over. He tries to grab the ball from the duck. But the duck is clever. It releases the ball and bites Tom's hand. Tom screams and drops his stick. He loses his balance and falls into the pond.
Mia runs to help Tom. She sees him splash and cry in the water. She grabs his stick and pulls him out. She hugs him and tells him to calm down. She says he is lucky. The pond is deep and he could have drowned.
Tom is wet and cold and sore. He is sorry for being silly. He says thank you to Mia for saving him. He says sorry to the duck for being mean. He does not care about the ball anymore. He just wants to go home and get warm and dry.
Mia and Tom walk back to their friends. They tell them what happened. Their friends are glad they are okay. They say they can share their ball and play hockey together. They say they will not go near the pond again. They say they will be careful and have fun.

They take the cookies and run to the garden. They find a wide tree with thick branches. They climb up the tree and sit on a branch. They open the box and start to eat the cookies. They are very sweet and crunchy.
"These are the best cookies ever," Tom says. "We are so lucky to find them."
"Yes, they are," Ben says. "But maybe we should save some for later. We might get sick if we eat too many."
"No, we won't," Tom says. "We can eat them all. They are ours. We don't have to share with anyone."
They eat and eat and eat. They eat until the box is empty. They feel very full and happy. They smile at each other and wipe their mouths.
"That was fun," Tom says. "Let's do it again tomorrow."
"OK," Ben says. "But we have to hide the box. We don't want anyone to find out."
They throw the box down the tree and jump down. They run back to the house. They think they are very smart and clever.
But they are not. The next day, they wake up with a big problem. They have a bad stomach ache. They feel very sick and unhappy. They can't play with cars and balls. They have to stay in bed and drink water. They cry and moan.
"What happened to us?" Tom asks. "Why do we feel so bad?"
"Maybe it was the cookies," Ben says. "Maybe we ate too many. Maybe we were greedy and selfish."
"Yes, maybe you were," a voice says. It is Mom. She is standing at the door. She looks very angry and sad. She has the empty box in her hand. She knows what they did.
"Did you take the cookies from the kitchen?" she asks. "Did you eat them all by yourselves?"
Tom and Ben nod. They are very ashamed and sorry. They know they did something wrong.
"Those cookies were for your sister's birthday party," Mom says. "They were a special treat for her and her friends. You ruined her surprise. You were very naughty and mean."
Tom and Ben feel very bad. They love their sister. They don't want to make her sad. They wish they could take back what they did.
"We are sorry, Mom," they say. "We are sorry, sister. We made a mistake. We won't do it again. Please forgive us."
Mom sighs. She is not happy, but she loves them. She knows they are young and they need to learn.
"I forgive you, boys," she says. "But you have to gain your sister's forgiveness too. You have to do something nice for her. You have to show her that you care. And you have to share with others. Sharing is caring. Do you understand?"
Tom and Ben nod. They understand. They want to be good and kind. They want to be better friends. They hug Mom and say thank you. They hug each other and say sorry. They learn their lesson.
The end.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big fountain with many coins in the water. Tom wanted to take some coins and put them in his pocket.
"Look, Lily, shiny pennies!" he said. "Let's get some!"
"No, Tom, we can't do that!" Lily said. "That's not nice. Mom will be angry. And the pennies are for wishes. People throw them and hope for good things."
But Tom did not listen. He ran to the fountain and reached for a penny. He did not see the sign that said "Do not touch the water".
Suddenly, a loud voice warned him. "Hey, kid, stop that! You can't take the coins! That's stealing!"
Tom was scared. He looked up and saw a man in a blue uniform. He was a guard. He had a big hat and a whistle.
"Sorry, sir, I didn't know," Tom said. He dropped the penny and ran back to Lily.
The guard followed him. He looked angry. He wanted to tell Tom's mom what he did.
But Lily was compassionate. She felt sorry for Tom. She knew he made a mistake. She did not want him to get in trouble.
"Please, sir, don't be mad at Tom," she said. "He's only three. He didn't mean to be bad. He just liked the pennies. He won't do it again. I promise."
The guard looked at Lily. He saw her big eyes and her sweet smile. He softened a bit. He decided to give Tom a chance.
"Okay, okay, I'll let it go this time," he said. "But you have to promise me something. You have to make a wish with the penny you dropped. And you have to wish for something good. Something that will make you a better person. Can you do that?"
Tom nodded. He felt ashamed. He did not want to steal anymore. He wanted to be good.
"Thank you, sir," he said. "I'm sorry. I'll make a wish."
He picked up the penny and threw it back into the fountain. He closed his eyes and wished.
"I wish I could be more like Lily," he said. "She's kind and smart and compassionate. She's the best sister ever."
Lily hugged him. She was proud of him. She loved him.
Mom came back from the bench. She did not know what happened. She saw Tom and Lily smiling.
"Did you have fun, kids?" she asked.
"Yes, mom, we did," they said.
They did not tell her about the pennies. They kept it as a secret. A secret wish.

One day, they saw a big boat on the lake. It was white and shiny. It had a flag and a horn. Sara and Tom wanted to see it up close. They ran to their small boat and got in.
"Let's go to the big boat!" Sara said.
"OK, but be careful. It might be a bad boat," Tom said.
They pushed their small boat into the water and started to row. They got closer and closer to the big boat. They could hear the horn and see the people on the deck.
"Hello!" Sara shouted.
"Hello!" a man shouted back. He had a hat and a beard. He smiled at them.
"Who are you?" Tom asked.
"I'm the captain of this boat. Do you want to come aboard?" the man asked.
Sara and Tom looked at each other. They were curious and excited. They nodded.
"OK, but you have to guess the name of my boat first. It's a playful word that rhymes with boat," the man said.
Sara and Tom thought hard. They tried to think of words that rhymed with boat.
"Is it goat?" Sara asked.
"No, that's not it," the man said.
"Is it coat?" Tom asked.
"No, that's not it either," the man said.
"Is it float?" Sara asked.
"Close, but no," the man said.
"Is it note?" Tom asked.
"No, no, no," the man said.
Sara and Tom were running out of words. They looked at the boat again. They noticed something on the side. It was a picture of a fish with a big smile.
"Is it moat?" Sara asked.
"No, but you're very warm," the man said.
"Is it...gloat?" Tom asked.
"No, but you're almost there," the man said.
Sara and Tom looked at each other. They had one more word in their minds. They said it together.
"Is it...dote?"
"Yes, that's it! You guessed it! Dote is the name of my boat. It means to love and care for someone very much. I named it after my wife, who is very playful and sweet. You're very smart and brave. Come aboard, I have some treats and toys for you," the man said.
Sara and Tom cheered. They had guessed the name of the boat. They were happy and proud. They climbed aboard the big boat and met the captain's wife. She was very playful and sweet. She gave them cookies and juice and showed them her dolls and books. They had a wonderful time on the dote boat. They made new friends and learned new words. They thanked the captain and his wife and went back to their small boat. They waved goodbye and rowed back to the shore. They had a lot of fun.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a big bucket and a small shovel to make sand castles. They worked together and had fun.
One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a red truck and a blue hat. He came over to Anna and Ben and said, "Hello, can I play with you?"
Anna and Ben said, "Yes, you can play with us. We are making sand castles. Do you want to help?"
The new boy said, "Yes, I want to help. But I want to use your bucket and shovel. They are better than mine."
Anna and Ben did not like that. They said, "No, you cannot use our bucket and shovel. They are ours. You can use your truck and hat."
The new boy got angry. He said, "No, I want to use your bucket and shovel. Give them to me now!"
He tried to grab the bucket and shovel from Anna and Ben. They held on tight and said, "No, go away!"
They started to quarrel. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The sand castles they made were ruined. They were not happy.
A lady who worked in the park saw them. She came over and said, "Stop, stop, what are you doing? Why are you quarreling? You should share and be nice to each other."
She took the bucket and shovel and the truck and hat. She said, "You cannot play with these toys until you calm down and say sorry. Go and sit on that bench and think about what you did."
Anna and Ben and the new boy felt ashamed. They went and sat on the bench. They did not look at each other. They were quiet.
After a while, Anna said, "I'm sorry. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I like to play with you. You are my friend."
Ben said, "I'm sorry too. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I like to play with you. You are my friend."
They looked at the new boy. He said, "I'm sorry too. I did not mean to quarrel with you. I was rude and selfish. I want to play with you. Can you be my friends?"
Anna and Ben smiled and said, "Yes, we can be your friends. You can play with us. We can share our toys. We can make new sand castles together."
They hugged and said, "We are sorry, lady. We will not quarrel again. We will be nice to each other."

Lily and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They know they have to tidy up.
"Sorry, Mom," Lily and Ben say. "We were playing with the file. It is very nice. But we will put it back and clean up the living room."
Mom nods. She is glad that Lily and Ben are sorry and that they want to tidy up. She helps them to put the toys and books in their places and the file on the shelf. She hugs them and kisses them.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park and look for treasure. One day, they found a big box under a tree. It was locked with a padlock. They wondered what was inside.
"Maybe it has gold and jewels," Ben said.
"Or toys and candy," Lily said.
They tried to open the box, but it was too hard. They needed a key. They looked around and saw a shiny metal thing on the ground. It was a key!
"Look, Lily, a key!" Ben said. He picked it up and ran to the box. He put the key in the padlock and turned it. The box opened with a click.
Inside the box, there was a map. It was old and torn, but it had impressive drawings of mountains and rivers and stars. It also had a big red X on it.
"What is this?" Lily asked.
"It's a map, silly," Ben said. "It shows us where the treasure is. Maybe it's buried somewhere in the park. Let's follow it!"
They took the map and ran to the other side of the park. They followed the stars and the mountains and the rivers until they reached a big hill. There was a red X on the map where the hill was.
"This is it, Lily, we found it!" Ben said. He took a shovel from the box and started to dig. Lily helped him. They dug and dug until they hit something hard.
They cleared the dirt and saw a wooden chest. It had a lock on it, too. But the key they had didn't fit.
"Oh no, Ben, we need another key," Lily said.
"Maybe it's somewhere on the map," Ben said. He looked at the map again. He saw a small drawing of a key next to a flower. He looked around and saw a flower near the hill. He ran to it and looked under it. There was another shiny metal thing. It was another key!
"Look, Lily, another key!" Ben said. He picked it up and ran to the chest. He put the key in the lock and turned it. The chest opened with a creak.
Inside the chest, there was treasure. There was gold and jewels and toys and candy. Ben and Lily were so happy. They hugged each other and laughed.
"We did it, Lily, we found the treasure!" Ben said.
"We did, Ben, we did!" Lily said.
They shared the treasure and played with it. They had the best day ever. They thanked the map and the keys and the box and the chest. They were the best treasure hunters in the world.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big and impressive rainbow in the sky. It had many colors and it was very bright.
"Wow, look at the rainbow!" Tom said. "It is so pretty!"
"I want to touch it!" Lily said. "Maybe it has magic!"
They ran towards the rainbow, hoping to reach it. But the rainbow was very far away. They had to step over rocks and puddles and grass. They got tired and wet and dirty.
"Are we there yet?" Tom asked. "I can't see the rainbow anymore!"
"Me neither!" Lily said. "Maybe it is hiding!"
They stopped and looked around. They were lost. They did not know where their home was. They felt scared and sad.
"Mommy! Daddy!" they cried. "Where are you?"
They heard a voice. It was their dog, Spot. He had followed them from their home. He barked and wagged his tail. He was happy to see them.
"Spot!" Tom and Lily said. "You found us!"
They hugged their dog and followed him back to their home. Their parents were waiting for them. They were worried and angry.
"Where have you been?" Mommy asked. "We were looking for you!"
"We were chasing the rainbow!" Tom said.
"We wanted to touch it!" Lily said.
Mommy and Daddy shook their heads. They explained to Tom and Lily that rainbows are not things you can touch. They are made by light and water in the sky. They are beautiful, but they are not magic.
They also told them that they should never run away from home without telling them. They said that it was dangerous and foolish. They said that they loved them and wanted them to be safe.
Tom and Lily felt sorry. They said they were sorry. They hugged their parents and thanked Spot for saving them.
They learned their lesson. They never chased rainbows again. They still liked to look at them, but they knew they were better off at home.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars. One day, they find a big box in the park. They want to see what is inside.
"Let's open it!" Tom says.
"OK!" Jen says.
They pull and push the box. It is very heavy. They hear a beep.
"What is that?" Jen asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a toy." Tom says.
They pull and push harder. The box opens. They see a lot of wires and a red button.
"Wow! Look at this!" Tom says.
He reaches for the button.
"Tom, don't touch it!" Jen says.
"Why not? It looks fun." Tom says.
He presses the button. The box beeps louder.
"Repeat. Repeat. This is a bomb. You have ten seconds to run away. Repeat. Repeat. This is a bomb. You have ten seconds to run away." A voice says from the box.
Tom and Jen are scared. They do not know what a bomb is. They do not know what to do.
"Tom, what is a bomb?" Jen asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a bad toy." Tom says.
They look at the box. It has a screen. It shows a number. The number is nine.
"Nine. Eight. Seven." The voice says.
Tom and Jen start to cry. They want to run away. But they are too late.
The box explodes. It makes a loud noise. It makes a big fire. It hurts Tom and Jen.
They fall to the ground. They do not move. They do not play anymore.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Mabel. She lived in the countryside, near a large vineyard. Her mother knew that Mabel was curious and loved to explore, so she asked her neighbor to lend Mabel their horse.
"Of course," said her neighbor. "Just make sure that she comes back before dark!"
Mabel thanked him, before running excitedly over to where the horse was waiting. She was delighted to spot a big vine, hanging down from the tree next to it. She quickly put her hand up to reach it and started to pull the vine downwards. Suddenly, the vine snapped in two and Mabel felt ashamed of what she had done.
"Why did you do that, Mabel?" her neighbor asked.
Mabel hung her head. "I'm sorry. I just wanted to see what the vine was like."
Her neighbor smiled. "I know how curious you can be. That's why I wanted to lend you the horse so you could explore and have fun."
Mabel smiled. She realized that although she had made a mistake, it wasn't a problem. From then on, she explored the countryside with her neighbour's horse whenever she was allowed.

One day, Sammy's best friend, a little bird named Billy, said, "Sammy, come up and see the view from the tree! It's so pretty!"
Sammy was scared but wanted to be brave, so he climbed up the tree very slowly. As he climbed higher and higher, he could see more and more of the forest. When he reached the top, he saw the beautiful view. The sky was blue, and the trees were green and tall. Sammy was so happy that he forgot to be scared.
But then, Sammy looked down and saw how high he was. He started to weep because he was scared to climb down. Billy saw Sammy weep and said, "Don't worry, Sammy! I will help you." Billy held onto Sammy's tail, and they both climbed down the tree together. When they reached the ground, Sammy was so happy and thanked Billy for helping him. From that day on, Sammy was no longer scared of heights, and he loved to see the view from the trees with his friend Billy.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big rocket that could fly to space. They pretended to be astronauts and explored the stars and planets.
One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Sam and he was very pale. He had been sick for a long time and could not go outside much. He saw Tom and Lily playing with their rocket and wanted to join them, but he was shy and afraid they would not like him.
He knocked on their door and said, "Hello, I am Sam. I live next door. Can I play with you?"
Tom and Lily looked at him and smiled. They said, "Hello, Sam. We are Tom and Lily. We are twins. You can play with us. We are going to space. Do you like space?"
Sam nodded and said, "Yes, I love space. I have many books about space. Can I see your rocket?"
Tom and Lily welcomed him into their room and showed him their rocket. They told him how it worked and what they saw in space. They gave him a helmet and a suit and invited him to fly with them.
They had a lot of fun together and became good friends. They learned many things from each other and shared their toys and books. They realized that it did not matter how they looked or where they came from. They only cared about how they treated each other.
The moral of the story is: Be kind and welcoming to new people. You can make new friends and learn new things. Everyone is special and has something to offer.

Sara and Tom were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. But they were not allowed to go too far, because there might be sharks in the deep.
One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It had a sign that said "Shark Tour". Sara and Tom wanted to go on the boat and see the sharks. They asked their mom and dad, but they said no. They said it was too dangerous and scary.
"But we want to see the sharks!" Sara and Tom said. "They are not scary, they are cool!"
"No, they are not cool, they are dull," their mom and dad said. "They have no colors, no smiles, no fun. They only have sharp teeth and fins. They are not nice to other fish or people. You would not like them."
Sara and Tom were sad and angry. They did not understand why their mom and dad did not let them see the sharks. They thought their mom and dad were dull and boring.
They decided to sneak away from their mom and dad and go on the boat. They ran to the boat and climbed on board. They saw a man with a hat and a net. He was the shark tour guide.
"Hello, kids," he said. "Are you ready to see the sharks?"
"Yes, we are!" Sara and Tom said. "We love sharks!"
The man smiled and took them to the side of the boat. He pointed to the water and said, "Look, there they are!"
Sara and Tom looked and saw many sharks swimming around the boat. They were big and gray and had sharp teeth and fins. They looked dull and scary.
Sara and Tom felt afraid. They did not love sharks anymore. They wanted to go back to their mom and dad.
"Can we go back, please?" they asked the man.
"Sorry, kids, you can't," the man said. "You have to stay here and watch the sharks. That's what you wanted, right?"
Sara and Tom realized they made a mistake. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They wished they had accepted their mom and dad's words and not gone on the boat.
They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharks are not cool, they are dull and dangerous. They learned that their mom and dad are not dull and boring, they are wise and caring. They learned that they should accept their mom and dad's rules and not do things that might hurt them. They learned that sometimes, the best things are not on the boat, but on the beach.

The little duck looked at Tom and said, "Yes, please. I would like that very much."

The other animals looked at the little duck and said, "No, we will not play with you. We refuse."
The little duck was sad, but he did not give up. He went to the river and started to practice swimming very fast. Day after day, he practiced and got better and better. One day, a big storm came to the country. The river started to flood, and the other animals were scared.
The little duck saw the animals in trouble and swam very fast to save them. One by one, he brought them to safety. After the storm, the animals were very grateful to the little duck.
"Thank you, little duck," they said. "We were wrong to refuse to play with you. From now on, we will be your friends."
And so, the little duck and the other animals lived happily ever after on the farm, and they all became the best of friends.

But one day, they saw a sign on the oak tree. The sign said: "Do not climb. The tree is sick. It can break and hurt you." Anna and Ben were sad. They loved the oak tree.
"Let's climb anyway," Ben said. "The sign is silly. The tree is strong. It won't break."
"No, Ben," Anna said. "We have to listen to the sign. It is there to help us. If we climb, we can get hurt. And we can make the tree worse. And we can get punished."
"Punished by who?" Ben asked. "No one is watching. Come on, Anna. Don't be scared. It will be fun."
Ben did not listen to Anna. He ran to the oak tree and started to climb. Anna followed him. She did not want to be alone. She hoped nothing bad would happen.
But something bad did happen. When Ben reached a high branch, he heard a loud crack. The branch broke under his weight. Ben fell down and landed on the ground. He cried out in pain. He had a big cut on his leg. It was bleeding.
Anna was scared. She climbed down quickly and ran to Ben. She saw his cut and felt sorry for him. She tried to comfort him. She said: "Ben, are you okay? I'm sorry. We should not have climbed. We should have listened to the sign."
Ben was in pain. He was also ashamed. He knew he had been wrong. He said: "Anna, you were right. I was silly. I did not listen to the sign. I did not listen to you. I'm sorry. I hope the tree is okay. I hope we don't get punished."
Anna and Ben hugged each other. They hoped the tree would get better. They hoped their parents would not be angry. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect the signs and the trees. They learned to be careful and kind.

"Oh no!" he said. "I need to clean myself. I want to look nice and shiny."
He jumped into the water and started to scrub his fur with his paws. He splashed and played and had fun. He felt happy and fresh.
But then he heard a voice behind him. It was a serious owl, who was sitting on a branch.
"Fox, what are you doing?" the owl asked. "You are wasting time and water. You should be hunting and learning, not playing and cleaning. You are a wild animal, not a pet."
The fox felt ashamed. He got out of the water and shook his fur.
"I'm sorry, owl," he said. "I just wanted to look nice and shiny. I didn't mean to be silly."
The owl looked at him with his big eyes.
"Fox, you don't need to look nice and shiny. You need to be smart and strong. That's what makes you a good fox. And you are not silly. You are curious and playful. That's what makes you a happy fox. But you also need to balance your fun and your work. That's what makes you a wise fox."
The fox nodded. He understood what the owl said.
"Thank you, owl," he said. "You are a good friend. You teach me a lot. Can I ask you a question?"
"Of course, fox," the owl said. "What do you want to know?"
The fox smiled.
"Can I clean myself again tomorrow?" he asked.

"Hello, sweetie," Tom said. "You look very pretty."

"And our box?" Mom asked.
Lisa and Tom looked at each other. They knew they were in trouble. They wished they had not touched the lock.

"Look at this bug, Lily!" Tom said. He pointed to a bug that was different from the others. It had six legs, two wings and a long tail. It was black and shiny and had red spots on its back. "It is so pretty!"
Lily looked at the bug and nodded. "It is pretty, Tom. But I don't know what it is. Maybe it is a new bug. Can we keep it?"
Tom smiled and said, "Yes, we can keep it. But we have to be careful. Maybe it can bite or sting. We have to give it some food and water and a name. What do you want to call it?"
Lily thought for a moment and said, "How about Spot? Because it has red spots."
Tom agreed and said, "Spot is a good name. Let's go and find some food and water for Spot. Maybe he likes leaves or flowers or bread."
They left the jar on the grass and ran to the house. They did not see that Spot was not happy in the jar. He wanted to get out and fly away. He used his tail to break the lid of the jar. He flew out and looked for a place to hide. He saw a big tree and flew to it. He landed on a branch and saw a lot of other bugs. They were green and had no wings. They were eating the leaves of the tree. Spot was hungry and decided to eat them. He used his tail to sting them and make them fall. He ate them one by one. He felt good and grew bigger and bigger. He became enormous.
Tom and Lily came back with some food and water for Spot. They looked for the jar and saw that it was broken. They looked for Spot and saw him on the tree. He was enormous and scary. He saw them and flew to them. He opened his mouth and showed his teeth. He wanted to eat them too.
"Run, Lily, run!" Tom shouted. He dropped the food and water and ran to the house. Lily was scared and followed him. But Spot was faster and caught her. He stung her with his tail and made her fall. He ate her in one bite. Tom saw this and cried. He ran to the house and locked the door. He hoped that Spot would go away. But Spot did not go away. He spread his wings and flew to the house. He broke the windows and the roof. He found Tom and ate him too. He was full and happy. He flew away and looked for more food. He spread his terror to the whole town. No one was safe from Spot. He was the baddest bug ever. The end.

Tim ran to the kitchen and saw three bowls. Each bowl had a different sauce. Tim's mom told him to point at the one he wanted to eat. Tim pointed at the red sauce, and his mom put it on his food. Tim was very happy and started to eat.
As Tim ate the red sauce, he made a funny face. It was very spicy! Tim did not expect the sauce to be so hot. He quickly drank some water to cool his mouth. Tim's mom laughed and said, "Surprise! I made a new sauce for you to try." Tim laughed too, and they both enjoyed the rest of their meal.

Lily did not like yellow clothes. She liked pink and purple and blue. But today, her mom gave her a yellow dress to wear. Lily did not want to wear it. She said, "No, no, no! I do not like yellow!"
Her mom said, "Lily, you have to wear this dress. It is a gift from your grandma. She made it for you with love. She will be very sad if you do not wear it."
Lily did not care. She threw the dress on the floor and ran to her room. She cried and cried. She did not want to wear the yellow dress.
Her mom followed her and knocked on the door. She said, "Lily, please open the door. I want to talk to you."
Lily opened the door. She saw her mom holding the yellow dress. She said, "Go away! I do not want to see that dress!"
Her mom said, "Lily, I know you do not like yellow. But you have to be kind and grateful. Your grandma worked very hard to make this dress for you. She loves you very much. She wants you to be happy. How do you think she will feel if you do not wear it?"
Lily thought for a moment. She remembered her grandma. She remembered how she hugged her and kissed her and gave her cookies. She remembered how she read her stories and sang her songs. She loved her grandma very much. She did not want to make her sad.
Lily said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was very rude. I will wear the yellow dress. I love grandma. I want to make her happy."
Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "I'm proud of you, Lily. You are a good girl. You learned to resist your own feelings and think of others. That is a very important lesson. Come on, let's go and see grandma. She will be very happy to see you in the yellow dress."
Lily put on the yellow dress. She looked at herself in the mirror. She still did not like yellow. But she liked her grandma more. She smiled and said, "Let's go, mom. I'm ready."

Anna and Ben were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.
Anna wanted to make the tallest tower ever. She stacked the blocks as high as she could, but she needed more. She saw a big box of blocks on the shelf. She asked Ben to help her lift the box.
"Ben, can you help me lift the box? I want more blocks for my tower," she said.
Ben nodded and went to the shelf. He tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy for him. He pulled and pushed, but the box did not move. He felt frustrated and angry.
He decided to use a chair to reach the box. He dragged the chair to the shelf and climbed on it. He grabbed the box and tried to lift it again. But he lost his balance and fell off the chair. The box fell with him and hit the floor. The blocks spilled out of the box and made a loud noise.
Anna and Ben were both scared by the noise. They looked at the mess of blocks and the broken box. They heard their mom coming to the living room. They knew they were in trouble. They felt ashamed of what they had done.
"What happened here?" their mom asked in a stern voice. She saw the chair, the box, and the blocks. She saw Anna and Ben hiding behind the couch. She was shocked by the scene.
"Anna, Ben, come here right now," she said. "You need to explain what you were doing and why you made such a mess. And you need to apologize and clean up."
Anna and Ben came out of their hiding place. They looked at their mom with sad eyes. They said they were sorry and that they just wanted to play with the blocks. They said they would help to clean up.
Their mom was not happy, but she was also glad that they were not hurt. She hugged them and said she loved them. She said they should not lift things that were too heavy for them. She said they should ask for help and be careful. She said they should not use the chair to climb on the shelf. She said they should respect their toys and not break them.
Anna and Ben nodded and said they understood. They said they would not do it again. They helped their mom to pick up the blocks and put them back in the box. They learned their lesson and felt better. They decided to play with something else. They still liked the blocks, but they did not want to lift the box anymore.

Ben and Lily were going to the zoo with their mom. They had to take the bus to get there. Ben liked the bus. He liked to look out the window and see the cars and the trees and the people. Lily did not like the bus. She thought it was too loud and too bumpy and too crowded. She worried that she would get sick on the bus.
"Mom, I don't want to go on the bus," Lily said. "Can we walk to the zoo?"
"No, sweetie, it's too far to walk. The bus will take us there faster and easier. Don't worry, you'll be fine. Just hold my hand and breathe slowly," Mom said.
But Lily still worried. She closed her eyes and tried not to think about the bus. She hoped they would get to the zoo soon.
The bus stopped at a red light. Ben saw a big truck next to them. The truck had a picture of a cow on it. Ben liked cows. He pointed at the truck and said, "Look, Lily, a cow!"
Lily opened her eyes and looked at the truck. She saw the cow, but she also saw something else. The truck had a hole in the back. And out of the hole came a lot of brown stuff. It looked like mud, but it smelled very bad. It was cow poop!
Lily screamed. "Ew, ew, ew! That's disgusting! Mom, make it go away!"
Mom looked at the truck and saw the poop. She made a face and said, "Oh, yuck! That's gross! Don't look, kids, don't look!"
But it was too late. Lily had seen enough. She felt her stomach turn and her mouth fill with spit. She leaned over and threw up on the floor of the bus.
Ben saw Lily throw up and he felt sorry for her. He also felt a little sick himself. He said, "Lily, are you okay?"
Lily nodded, but she was not okay. She was still worried. She worried that the bus would never get to the zoo. She worried that the poop truck would follow them. She worried that she would throw up again.
She wished they had walked to the zoo.

She put on her coat and hat and took a basket. She walked to the store and found the milk and eggs. She put them in the basket and went to the cashier. The cashier was a nice lady who smiled at her and gave her some change.
"Thank you, lady," Lily said.
"You're welcome, sweetie. Be careful on your way home," the lady said.
Lily nodded and left the store. She walked to the street and looked both ways. She saw a lot of cars and buses and bikes. She waited for the green light, but it seemed to take a long time. She started to feel impatient and bored.
She saw a boy on the other side of the street. He waved at her and said, "Hey, Lily, come here. I have something to show you."
Lily wanted to see what he had, but she knew she had to wait for the light. She said, "No, I can't. I have to wait for the light."
The boy said, "Oh, come on. It's not that far. Just run across. It's easy."
Lily looked at the street again. She saw a gap between the cars. She thought maybe she could make it. She said, "OK, I'll try."
She put down her basket and ran across the street. But she didn't see a bike coming fast from the other side. The bike hit her and knocked her down. She felt a lot of pain and started to cry.
The boy ran to her and said, "Oh, no, Lily, I'm sorry. Are you OK?"
Lily said, "No, I'm not OK. I'm hurt. And I lost my milk and eggs. And my mom will be mad at me."
The boy said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have told you to run across. It was a bad idea. I hope you feel better soon."
A man who saw what happened called an ambulance. The ambulance came and took Lily to the hospital. The lady from the store saw the basket and the milk and eggs on the street. She picked them up and followed the ambulance. She told the doctors what happened and gave them Lily's mom's phone number.
Lily's mom came to the hospital and hugged Lily. She said, "Lily, I'm so glad you're alive. I was so worried about you. What happened?"
Lily told her mom what happened. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't wait for the light. I listened to the boy. He said it was easy. But it wasn't. It was dangerous. I was stupid."
Lily's mom said, "Lily, you're not stupid. You're a good girl who made a mistake. You learned a hard lesson today. You have to be careful on the street. You have to wait for the light. You have to listen to your mom. Do you understand?"
Lily said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you."
Lily's mom said, "I love you too, Lily. And I'm proud of you. You managed to be brave and honest. You managed to say sorry and learn from your mistake. You're a good girl, Lily. And I'm here for you."
The lady from the store came in and gave Lily the milk and eggs. She said, "Lily, I'm sorry you got hurt. I hope you get well soon. Here's your milk and eggs. I saved them for you. You did a good job buying them."
Lily said, "Thank you, lady. You're very kind. You did a good job helping me."
The lady said, "You're welcome, Lily. You're very sweet. You did a good job thanking me."
Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, lady. Thank you, mom. I'm happy you're here."
The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many green leaves. They ran to the tree and looked for acorns. Acorns were brown and round and had little hats.
"Look, I found an acorn!" Lily said. She picked up an acorn and showed it to Ben.
"Me too!" Ben said. He found another acorn and held it in his hand.
They heard a noise in the tree. They looked up and saw a squirrel. The squirrel had a bushy tail and black eyes. It was holding an acorn in its mouth.
"Hello, squirrel!" Lily said. She waved to the squirrel.
The squirrel looked at Lily and Ben. It was not happy. It wanted to keep all the acorns for itself. It made a loud sound and shook its tail.
"Go away, go away!" the squirrel said. It threw an acorn at Lily and Ben.
"Ouch!" Lily said. The acorn hit her on the head.
"Hey, that's not nice!" Ben said. He threw an acorn back at the squirrel.
The squirrel dodged the acorn and ran to another branch. It threw another acorn at Lily and Ben.
Lily and Ben ran away from the tree. They found a bench and sat down. They still had their acorns.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.
"Yes, I'm okay. That squirrel was mean." Lily said.
"Maybe the squirrel was hungry. Maybe the acorns are yummy." Ben said.
He bit his acorn. It was hard and bitter. He made a face and spit it out.
"Yuck! This is not yummy!" Ben said.
Lily laughed. She bit her acorn. It was also hard and bitter. She made a face and spit it out.
"Yuck! You're right, this is not yummy!" Lily said.
They threw their acorns away. They did not want them anymore.
"Let's go and play on the swings. The swings are fun." Lily said.
"Okay, let's go. The swings are fun." Ben said.
They ran to the swings and pushed each other. They forgot about the squirrel and the acorns. They had a good time.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was a bunny and the other was a fox. Bunny and Fox were walking across a bridge, when suddenly Bunny noticed that it was very dirty.
Bunny said to his friend, "Fox, this bridge is so dirty. What shall we do?"
Fox thought for a minute and then came up with a great idea. He said, "Let's give the bridge a clean up and make it look more beautiful". 
So Bunny and Fox got to work. They gave the bridge a scrub, collected all the trash, and swept away all the dirt. Soon the bridge was shining bright. It was so clean that the sun was reflected off its surface!
The two friends smiled. They were proud to see that their hard work had made a difference. 
The End.

Tom and Lily were playing hide and seek in the park. Tom was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran to a big tree and hid behind it. She hoped Tom would not find her.
Tom looked around the park. He saw the swings, the slide, the sandbox and the fountain. He did not see Lily. He was anxious. He wanted to find Lily and win the game. He called out, "Lily, where are you? Come out, come out, or I will count to ten!"
Lily heard Tom's voice. She was scared. She did not want to lose the game. She did not want to come out. She stayed behind the tree and kept quiet.
Tom counted to ten. He said, "Lily, I counted to ten. You have to surrender or you lose the game. Do you surrender?" He waited for Lily to answer.
Lily did not answer. She did not want to surrender. She wanted to win the game. But she also did not want to make Tom sad. She thought for a moment. Then she had an idea. She said, "Tom, I have a pass. I can stay hidden for one more minute. Then I will come out. OK?"
Tom heard Lily's voice. He was surprised. He said, "A pass? What is a pass? How do you have a pass?"
Lily said, "A pass is a special thing. It lets you do something different. I have a pass because I am your sister. And I love you. Do you love me?"
Tom smiled. He said, "Yes, I love you, Lily. And I love your pass. OK, you can stay hidden for one more minute. But then you have to come out. Deal?"
Lily smiled too. She said, "Deal. Thank you, Tom. You are a good seeker. And a good brother."
They both laughed. They were happy. They enjoyed the game. And they loved each other.

Tom did not like that. He wanted to play with the doll, the house, and the cake. He said, "That is not fair. You have so many things, and I have none. Why can't we share and have fun?"

Tom did not want to help. He wanted to play. He said, "You are not the boss. You are just bossy. You are not a good friend. I don't want to play with you anymore." He got up and left.
Lily was sad. She looked at all her things and realized that they were not fun without a friend. She wished she had been nicer to Tom. She decided to make something for him. She made a card from paper and crayons, and wrote, "I am sorry. Can we be friends?" She ran after Tom and gave him the card.
Tom was surprised. He looked at the card and smiled. He said, "Thank you. That is very nice of you. I am sorry, too. Can we play together?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, please. We can share and have fun. You can play with anything you want."
Tom and Lily hugged. They went back to Lily's house and played with the doll, the house, and the cake. They made more things and shared them. They were happy and not bossy. They were good friends.

They saw a big tree and ran under it for some space to hide from the rain. Tom said, "Let's wait here until the rain stops." Spot wagged his tail and sat down. While waiting, Tom found a lemon on the ground. He picked it up and took a bite. "Yuck!" he said. "This is sour!"
After a while, the rain stopped. Tom and Spot were very happy. They played with their ball and had lots of fun. Tom threw the ball far away and Spot ran to catch it. They played until the sun went down. Then, they went home, tired but happy.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun, but they also made a big mess. There were blocks, cars, dolls, and books everywhere.
"Mommy will be mad if she sees this," Ben said. "We have to clean up."
"But I don't want to clean up," Lily said. "I want to play more."
Just then, they heard a squeak from under the sofa. They looked and saw a little mouse. The mouse had a piece of cheese in its mouth. It was trying to run away.
"Look, a mouse!" Ben shouted. "Let's catch it!"
They ran after the mouse, but it was too fast. It ran behind the curtains, under the table, and into the kitchen. Ben and Lily followed it, making more noise and more mess.
"Stop, mouse!" Lily yelled. "We want to play with you!"
The mouse was scared. It did not want to play with the big kids. It wanted to eat its cheese and hide. It saw a hole in the wall and ran towards it.
But before it could reach the hole, Ben grabbed it by the tail. He lifted it up and smiled.
"Got you, mouse!" he said. "You are so cute and soft. I will give you a name. How about Cheese?"
The mouse did not like being held. It dropped its cheese and bit Ben's finger. Ben screamed and let go of the mouse. The mouse ran into the hole and disappeared.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "The mouse bit me! It was mean!"
Lily picked up the cheese and looked at it. She shrugged and said, "Can I have it?"
Ben glared at her and said, "No, you can't. It's mouse cheese. It's yucky."
They heard footsteps coming from the stairs. It was their mommy. She looked at the living room and the kitchen. She saw the mess they had made. She was not happy.
"Ben, Lily, what have you done?" she asked. "Why is everything so messy?"
Ben and Lily looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They pointed at the hole in the wall and said, "The mouse did it."

She points to a small purple plant with fuzzy leaves. "This is a lavender. It is a cool plant. It can make you feel calm and sleepy if you smell it."
She points to a tall yellow plant with a round head. "This is a sunflower. It is a cool plant. It can follow the sun and make seeds that you can eat."
Lily and Sam are amazed. They think the plants are very cool. They want to learn more about them.

"Of course, you can," Sam's grandma says. "You are always welcome here. I have more plants to show you next time."
Lily and Sam smile. They hug Sam's grandma and say goodbye. They are happy to have a new friend and a new hobby. They love plants.

The mouse agreed and the elephant took a marker out of his pocket. He drew a big star on the oat, so they could find it easily.
The two friends then went their separate ways, but the mouse kept thinking about the oat. When he went back to the river to look for it, it was nowhere to be seen. 
He asked the other animals if they had seen it, but nobody had. The mouse was disappointed and a little sad, so he decided to go back home.

The mouse thought about the elephant's words and he realised that they were true. From that day forward, the mouse always thought twice before taking something that didn't belong to him.

Jay listened to the wise old man and waited for the bees to leave. When all the bees were gone, Jay quickly removed the banana and ate it right away. He was so happy that he had been able to get the yummy banana without getting stung by the bees.

One day, a little squirrel named Lily wanted to find some nuts to eat. She saw a big tree with many nuts on it. She ran to the tree and started to pick some nuts. She did not see her mother, who was watching her from another tree.
"Lily, be careful!" her mother called. "Do not wander too far from me. There are bad animals in the forest who might hurt you."
But Lily did not listen. She wanted more nuts. She wandered away from the big tree and found another tree with even more nuts. She was very happy and forgot about her mother.
"Hello, little squirrel," a voice said. Lily looked up and saw a big fox. He had sharp teeth and a long tail. He smiled at Lily, but he did not look nice. He looked bad.
"Who are you?" Lily asked.
"I am your friend," the fox said. "I have some more nuts for you. Come with me and I will show you."
Lily was curious. She liked nuts. She followed the fox, who led her to a dark hole.
"Here are the nuts," the fox said. "Go inside and take them."
Lily was scared. She did not like the dark hole. She wanted to go back to her mother.
"Wait," she said. "I want to go home."
But the fox did not let her. He blocked the hole with his body. He was not her friend. He was a bad animal who wanted to eat her.
"Help!" Lily cried. "Mother, help!"
Her mother heard her cry. She ran to the hole and saw the fox. She was angry and brave. She bit the fox's tail and made him run away.
She hugged Lily and took her back to the big tree.
"Lily, I am so glad you are safe," she said. "You should never wander away from me. You should never trust bad animals who lie to you. You should always listen to me, because I love you and I want to protect you."
Lily was sorry. She learned her lesson. She thanked her mother and promised to be a good squirrel. She ate some nuts and felt happy. She never wandered away again.

"Look, Lila, I found a root!" Tom said. He held up a long, brown thing that came out of the ground. "It is very big and hard. What is it for?"
Lila looked at the root. She remembered what her mom had told her. "It is for the plant, Tom. The root helps the plant get water and food from the dirt. It is like a straw for the plant."
"Oh, I see. Can I pull it out?" Tom asked.
"No, Tom, you can't. If you pull out the root, you will hurt the plant. The plant needs the root to live. It is not an ordinary thing. It is very important." Lila said.
Tom nodded. He did not want to hurt the plant. He liked the plant. It had pretty flowers and smelled nice. He put the root back in the dirt and covered it with more dirt. He patted it gently.
"Sorry, plant. I did not know. I will not pull your root again." Tom said.
Lila smiled. She was proud of Tom. He was a good brother. He learned fast. She gave him a hug.
"Good job, Tom. You helped the plant. You are very kind." Lila said.
They continued to play in the garden. They had fun. They found more bugs and worms. They did not pull any more roots. They helped the plants. They were happy.

One day, he was walking through the forest and came across a bush with juicy-looking strawberries. The elephant couldn't resist and started eating them all!
When the elephant heard a voice behind him, he was startled. It was a little girl, with a stern expression. She said, "Why are you eating all the strawberries? That's not very nice."
The elephant was a bit embarrassed and replied nervously, "I'm sorry. I just couldn't help it. I shouldn't have behaved in such a messy way."
The little girl smiled. "It's okay", she said, "But next time, remember to be more behaved."
The elephant was thankful for the girl's kindness and thanked her before he carried on his journey. From that day on, the elephant always tried his best to be more behaved when walking through the forest.

Tom and Lily were playing outside in the garden. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw a big, powerful rainbow in the sky. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.
"Wow, look at the rainbow!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and bright!"
"I want to drink the rainbow!" Tom said. "Maybe it tastes like candy or juice!"
"No, you can't drink the rainbow!" Lily said. "It is too high and too far. And it is not for drinking. It is for looking."
Tom did not listen to Lily. He ran to the shed and got a ladder. He put the ladder against the fence and climbed up. He reached out his hand to touch the rainbow.
"Tom, stop! Come down!" Lily shouted. "It is not safe! You will fall and hurt yourself!"
But Tom did not hear Lily. He wanted to drink the rainbow. He leaned forward and opened his mouth.
Suddenly, a big cloud came and covered the sun. The rainbow disappeared. Tom lost his balance and fell off the ladder. He landed on the grass with a thud.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. He felt pain in his arm and his leg.
Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She was scared and sorry.
"Tom, are you okay?" Lily asked. "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to yell at you. I just wanted to protect you."
Tom looked at Lily and sniffed. He felt sad and silly.
"I'm sorry, too," Tom said. "I was wrong. You can't drink the rainbow. It is not for drinking. It is for looking. And for sharing with you."
Lily smiled and kissed Tom's cheek. She helped him get up and go inside. They told their mom what happened. She gave them a band-aid and a hug. She also gave them a glass of water and a cookie.
"Next time, listen to your sister," Mom said. "She loves you and knows what is best for you."
Tom and Lily nodded and said sorry. They drank their water and ate their cookie. They looked out the window and saw the sun come out again. They saw a new, powerful rainbow in the sky. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.
They smiled and held hands. They learned their lesson. They did not want to drink the rainbow. They just wanted to look at it. And to share it with each other.

The bear was sad to see his friend go, but he was also very excited to see what would happen. The next morning, the caterpillar had gone and in its place was a beautiful butterfly with iridescent wings the colour of avocado.

One day, Lily and Max went to the park with Spot and Fluffy. Lily put a leash on Spot, so he would not run away. Max put Fluffy in a basket, so he would not get scared. They walked to the swings and took turns to swing high and low. They had a lot of fun.
"Look at me, Lily! I can swing higher than you!" Max said.
"No, you can't, Max! I can swing higher than you!" Lily said.
They laughed and swung faster and faster. They did not see a big hole in the ground. Spot saw the hole and barked. He wanted to warn them. But Lily and Max did not hear him. They were too busy swinging.
Suddenly, Lily's swing broke. She fell off and landed in the hole. She hurt her knee and cried. Max stopped swinging and ran to help her. He saw Spot pulling on the leash. He understood that Spot was trying to help. He thanked Spot and gave him a hug.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Max asked.
"It hurts, Max. I want to go home." Lily said.
"I'm sorry, Lily. It was my fault. I should have listened to Spot. He is a good dog." Max said.
"It's okay, Max. You are a good friend. You came to help me. Spot is a good dog, too. He saved me." Lily said.
They got out of the hole and walked back to the basket. Fluffy was still sleeping. He did not know what happened. They picked up Fluffy and Spot and went home. They learned a lesson. They learned to pay attention to their surroundings and to their pets. They were lucky that nothing worse happened. They were lucky to have each other and their pets. They hugged and said sorry and thank you. They were still best friends.

One day, Tom rides his bicycle to the park. He sees Lily sitting on a bench with her doll. He wants to show off his bicycle. He rides around Lily and says, "Look at me! Look at my bicycle! It is fast and cool. You don't have a bicycle. You only have a doll. Dolls are boring. Bicycles are fun."
Lily feels sad and angry. She does not like Tom's words. She thinks Tom is mean. She says, "Stop it, Tom! Stop teasing me! I don't care about your bicycle. I love my doll. She is pretty and soft. You are rude and loud. Go away!"
Tom does not stop. He is stubborn. He thinks he is better than Lily. He rides closer to Lily and says, "No, you go away! This is my park. This is my bicycle. You can't play here. You can't touch my bicycle. You are silly and weak."
Lily has had enough. She stands up and grabs Tom's bicycle. She pushes it away from him. She says, "No, you are silly and weak! This is not your park. This is our park. You can't bully me. You can't keep your bicycle. I will take it from you."
Tom is shocked and scared. He does not expect Lily to do that. He runs after Lily and tries to get his bicycle back. He says, "Hey, give me back my bicycle! That is mine! You are mean and bad!"
Lily and Tom fight over the bicycle. They pull and push and shout. They do not see the big dog coming. The big dog likes bicycles. He sees Tom's bicycle and thinks it is a toy. He runs to the bicycle and bites it. He makes a loud noise. He breaks the bicycle.
Lily and Tom stop fighting. They look at the big dog and the broken bicycle. They feel sorry and scared. They say, "Oh no! Oh no! What have we done? What will we do?"
The big dog runs away with the bicycle. Lily and Tom cry. They hug each other. They say, "I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I was wrong. You are my friend. I don't want to fight with you."
They go home and tell their parents what happened. Their parents are not happy. They say, "You should not tease each other. You should not fight over things. You should share and care. You should be kind and gentle."
Lily and Tom learn their lesson. They promise to be good friends. They promise to respect each other. They promise to never tease again.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of dolls and cars and blocks. But she did not like to share them with anyone. When her brother Ben came to her room and asked if he could play with her, she said no. She said they were all hers and he had to go away.
Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to play with Lily and have fun. He did not think it was fair that she kept all the toys for herself. He tried to grab a car from her hand, but she pulled it back. They started to fight and yell. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong.
She saw Lily and Ben tugging and pushing and shouting. She was not happy. She told them to stop and calm down. She said they had to share their toys and be nice to each other. She said that was the right thing to do. She said if they did not, they would have to go to time out.
Lily did not want to go to time out. She liked her room and her toys. But she did not want to share them either. She tried to resist her mom and keep the car. She said it was hers and she did not care. She wrapped her arms around her neck and held on tight.
But her mom was stronger and gentler. She pried Lily's arms off her neck and hugged her. She said she loved her and she understood that she liked her toys. But she said she had to learn to share and be kind. She said that was how to make friends and be happy. She said she could play with Ben and have more fun. She asked her to try.
Lily looked at her mom and then at Ben. She saw that he was still sad and angry. She felt sorry for him. She thought maybe her mom was right. Maybe sharing was not so bad. Maybe playing with Ben was not so bad. She decided to give it a try. She let go of the car and gave it to Ben. She said he could play with it. She said she was sorry for being mean.
Ben smiled and thanked her. He said he was sorry for grabbing the car. He said he wanted to play with her. He asked her if she wanted to play with his blocks. She said yes. They went to his room and played with his blocks. They built a tower and a bridge and a house. They had fun. They were happy.
Their mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them. She said they did a good job. She said they learned to share and be nice. She said that was the best thing to do. She said she loved them both. She gave them a kiss and a hug. They said they loved her too. They were a happy family.

Ben did not like that. He wanted to make the water low. He tried to turn the faucet the other way, but Lily pushed his hand away.
"Stop it, Ben! I want high water!" Lily said.
"No, I want low water!" Ben said.
They began to pull and push each other, trying to get to the faucet. They did not notice that the water was getting too high and spilling over the tub. They also did not notice that their mom was coming to check on them.
"Mommy, help! They are quarreling!" their baby sister, Mia, said from her crib in the next room.
Mom heard Mia and hurried to the bathroom. She saw the mess and the twins fighting. She was very angry and scared.
"Lily and Ben, stop it right now!" she shouted. "Look what you have done! You have made a flood in the bathroom! You are in big trouble!"
Lily and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They saw the water on the floor and the toys floating. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"We are sorry, Mommy," they said.
Mom turned off the faucet and drained the tub. She took the twins out of the bathroom and dried them off. She told them to go to their room and think about what they had done. She also told them to say sorry to each other and to Mia.
Lily and Ben did as they were told. They hugged and said sorry to each other and to Mia. They learned their lesson and promised to share the faucet and not quarrel anymore.

"No, I don't want to!" Sam said.
"You have to!" Tom said. "Or I will hit you with the hammer!"
Sam was scared and confused. He did not know why Tom and Lily were angry at him. He did not remember taking or breaking the doll. He ran to his room and locked the door.
Tom and Lily followed him and banged on the door. They shouted and cried. They wanted to punish Sam. They did not listen to him.
Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Lily with the hammer and the book. She saw the broken doll on the floor. She saw Sam hiding in his room.
She was very angry and sad. She took the hammer and the book from Tom and Lily. She made them sit on the couch and wait. She went to talk to Sam and calm him down.
She came back and told Tom and Lily that they were wrong. Sam did not take or break the doll. It was an accident. The doll fell from the shelf and Sam tried to fix it. He was sorry and scared. He wanted to tell them, but they did not listen.
Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They realized that they were mean and unfair. They wanted to say sorry to Sam, but he did not want to talk to them. He was still scared and confused.
Mom told them that they had to learn to be kind and honest. They had to respect and listen to others. They had to say sorry and forgive. She said that playing pretend was fun, but not when it hurt someone.
The story has a bad ending because Tom and Lily lost their brother's trust and friendship. The story has a moral value because it teaches that being mean and unfair is wrong and that being kind and honest is right.

"Sorry, Tom, but I like my shirt and pants. They are soft and loose and easy to move in. You can keep the suit. It makes you look very smart," Sam said, as he smiled and winked.
Tom felt sad and angry. He did not want to wear the suit anymore. He wanted to be comfortable and flexible like Sam. He thought of a plan to get what he wanted. He waited until Sam was not looking, and then he grabbed the toy phone and ran away. He hid behind the curtains and called Sam.

"Yes, Sam, I am sure. They are very sneaky and fast. They could be here any second. Please, Sam, offer me your shirt and pants. It is the only way to save me," Tom said, in a desperate voice.
Sam felt sorry for Tom. He did not want him to be scared or hurt. He decided to offer him his shirt and pants, even though he liked them very much. He took them off and threw them to Tom.
"Here, Tom, take my shirt and pants. They are flexible and comfortable. You can wear them and escape from the bad guys. I will wear the suit and distract them. Be careful, Tom. I love you," Sam said, in a brave voice.
Tom caught the shirt and pants and put them on. He felt happy and relieved. He had what he wanted. He did not care about the bad guys anymore. He did not care about Sam anymore. He did not say thank you or I love you. He just smiled and ran away.
Sam put on the suit and looked for the bad guys. He did not see them. He realized that Tom had tricked him. He felt sad and angry. He had given up his shirt and pants for nothing. He had been a good brother, but Tom had been a bad brother. He wished he had not offered him his shirt and pants. He wished he had not played spies with the suit. But then, a big cloud comes and covers the sun. The shadows disappear. Lila and Tom are sad.
"Where did our shadows go?" Lila asks.
"They went away with the sun," Tom says.
"Will they come back?" Lila asks.
"Maybe, if the cloud goes away," Tom says.
They wait and wait, but the cloud does not go away. It gets darker and colder. Lila and Tom shiver.
"Let's go home, Lila," Tom says.
"OK, Tom," Lila says.
They hold hands and walk to their mom. She is sitting on a bench. She has a big smile and a warm hug for them.
"Did you have fun, my loves?" she asks.
"Yes, mom, we did. We played with our shadows," Lila says.
"But then they went away," Tom says.
"Don't worry, my loves. Your shadows will come back when the sun comes back. They always stay with you, even when you can't see them. They are your friends," mom says.
"Really, mom?" Lila asks.

"Yummy, mom. Thank you, mom," Lila and Tom say.

"Look, mom, our shadows are back!" Lila and Tom say.
"I see them, my loves. They are happy to see you, too," mom says.
Lila and Tom smile and wave back. They are happy, too. They love their shadows. They love their mom. They love each other. The end.

Anna and Ben ran to the castle. They took off their shoes and climbed on it. They bounced high and low. They laughed and shouted. They had a lot of fun. But they did not see the other kids who wanted to bounce too. They did not share the castle. They bounced and bounced and bounced.
The other kids were sad. They waited and waited and waited. They wanted to bounce too. But Anna and Ben did not let them. They said, "This is our castle. Go away!" They were not nice. They were not kind.
Mom and dad saw what was happening. They were not happy. They called Anna and Ben. They said, "Anna and Ben, come here. You have to share the castle. The castle is for everyone. You have to be nice and kind. You have to take turns. That is the right thing to do."
Anna and Ben felt bad. They knew they were wrong. They said sorry to the other kids. They said, "We are sorry. We were not nice. We were not kind. You can bounce too. Let's share the castle. Let's have fun together."
The other kids smiled. They said, "Thank you. You are nice. You are kind. Let's bounce together. Let's have fun together." They put on their shoes and climbed on the castle. They bounced high and low. They laughed and shouted. They had a lot of fun. Anna and Ben had more fun too. They made new friends. They learned to share. They were happy.

Mom picked up a tall strip from the kitchen table. She asked Sally, “Do you want to tie it?”
Sally smiled and nodded. She grabbed the strip, but it was too long for her little hands to handle. 
Mom said, “I can help you.” She took the strip and knelt down to the floor. She showed Sally how to make a knot with the end. Then she looped it around her hands and made another knot. 
Sally clapped. “That looks like a butterfly!” 
Mom smiled and said, “Yes, it does! You’re so clever! Now we can hang it in the tree.”
They went outside and found the tallest tree in the garden. Mom and Sally placed the strip around the tallest branch. As they stood back to admire it, the bright strip blew gently in the breeze. 
Mom said, “We made a beautiful butterfly!”
Sally hugged Mom and said, “Thanks for helping me Tie!”

One day, a boy named Tom and his old dog Spot went for a walk in the park. They liked to play with the ball and run on the grass. But soon, the sky became dark and noisy. Tom saw flashes of lightning and heard loud thunder. He was scared and wanted to go home.
"Come on, Spot, let's go home!" Tom said to his dog. "It's going to rain and we don't want to get wet!"
But Spot did not listen. He saw a big puddle and jumped into it. He splashed and rolled in the water. He was having fun and did not care about the lightning.
"Spot, stop it!" Tom shouted. "You are making a mess and you will get sick!"
But Spot did not stop. He ran out of the puddle and shook his fur. He sprayed water all over Tom and made him wet and dirty.
"Spot, you are a bad dog!" Tom cried. "Now we have to wash and change our clothes!"
Tom grabbed Spot's collar and dragged him home. He was angry and sad. He did not want to play with Spot anymore.
But when they got home, Tom's mom was waiting for them. She saw how wet and dirty they were and smiled.
"Looks like you had a lot of fun in the park!" she said. "Don't worry, I'll help you wash and dry. Then we can have some cookies and milk and watch a movie. How does that sound?"
Tom looked at his mom and then at Spot. He saw that Spot was wagging his tail and licking his face. He realized that Spot was not a bad dog. He was just a playful dog. He felt sorry for yelling at him.
"I'm sorry, Spot," he said. "You are a good dog. I love you."
Spot barked and licked him some more. He loved Tom too.
Tom's mom hugged them both and took them to the bathroom. She turned on the faucet and filled the tub with warm water. She added some soap and bubbles. Lily nodded. She ate her dinner, but she did not like it. It was green and mushy. She took a bath, but she did not like it. It was too hot and bubbly. She wanted to go to bed.

"Lily, what is this?" her mom asked. "Did you take this toy from your friend?"
Lily nodded. She felt ashamed. She knew she did something bad.
"That was not nice, Lily," her mom said. "You need to say sorry to your friend and give it back. How would you feel if someone took your toy?"
Lily felt sorry. She knew how she would feel. She hugged her mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, friend. I will give it back tomorrow."

Lily smiled. She liked stories and songs. She snuggled with her mom and listened to her voice. She felt calm and happy. She relaxed in her clean sheet and fell asleep.
