The cat said, "Yes, you can touch my tail. But be gentle." The boy was very happy. He touched the cat's tail softly. It felt nice and warm.
They became good friends. They played together in the park every day. The boy always touched the cat's beautiful tail, and they both had lots of fun.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they want to visit the farm. The farm has many animals. Lily and Ben like animals.
They ask their moms to take them to the farm. Their moms say yes. They get in the car and drive to the farm. They see a big gate. The gate has a sign. The sign says "Welcome to the farm".
Lily and Ben are happy. They get out of the car and open the gate. They walk into the farm. They see cows, sheep, pigs, chickens, and horses. They hear the animals make noises. They say hello to the animals.
They go to the cow. The cow is big and black and white. The cow says "moo". Lily and Ben touch the cow. The cow is soft and warm. They go to the sheep. The sheep is small and white and fluffy. The sheep says "baa". Lily and Ben hug the sheep. The sheep is woolly and cozy.
They go to the pig. The pig is pink and fat and dirty. The pig says "oink". Lily and Ben laugh at the pig. The pig is funny and snorty. They go to the chicken. The chicken is brown and red and feathery. The chicken says "cluck". Lily and Ben feed the chicken. The chicken is hungry and pecky.
They go to the horse. The horse is tall and brown and shiny. The horse says "neigh". Lily and Ben stroke the horse. The horse is smooth and strong. The farmer comes and says hello. He asks them if they want to ride the horse. Lily and Ben say yes. They are excited.
The farmer helps them get on the horse. He holds the horse's reins. He walks with the horse around the farm. Lily and Ben feel the horse's back move. They see the farm from high up. They wave to the animals. They smile and giggle.
They have a fine time at the farm. They thank the farmer and the horse. They say goodbye to the animals. They close the gate. They get in the car and drive back home. They tell their moms about their visit. They say they want to go to the farm again. Their moms say maybe. Lily and Ben are happy. They are friends. They like to play together.

The girl and her friend started to struggle. They were trying to find a safe place, but it seemed like the wind was too strong.
The girl shouted to her friend. "I'm scared! I don't like the sound of thunder!"
The girl's friend hugged her and said, "It'll be okay. We'll be safe soon."
Then, they saw a tree with sheltering branches. They ran to it and stayed under the branches.
The storm eventually passed, and the gray sky opened up to blue again. The girl and her friend had struggled in the storm, but they made it safely through together.

Suddenly a voice startled her, saying "Whatcha doing?"
Bree looked up to see a 3 year old child standing nearby. When Bree tried to explain about the fair case, the child simply opened it up, took out the gem, and put it in her pocket.
Bree watched with amazement as the child smiled and said, "Come with me! Let's soar together!" So, with one flap of her wings, Bree flew after the child, happily soaring away into the sky.

"It is rain," Mia says. "Rain is water that falls from the sky. It makes the sand wet and the sea big."
"Big sea?" Tim asks. "How big?"
"Very big," Mia says. "The tide is high. The tide is when the sea goes up and down. When the tide is high, the sea comes close to the sand. When the tide is low, the sea goes far from the sand."
"Can we play in the sea?" Tim asks.
"No, we can't," Mia says. "The sea is too big and too fast. It can push us and hurt us. We have to be careful. We have to stay away from the sea."
"OK," Tim says. "Let's go back to the house. We can play inside. We can read books and draw pictures. Maybe the rain will stop soon."
"OK," Mia says. "That sounds fun. Let's go." They hold hands and run to the house. They are wet and cold, but they are happy. They like to play on the beach, but they also like to play inside. They are careful and smart. They know how to be safe.

"Go away, dog!" Lily shouted. "You are not nice!"

"Help, help!" Ben cried. "We are stuck!"
Then they saw a man coming. He had a leash in his hand. He was the dog's owner.
"Sorry, kids," the man said. "My dog is not mean, he just wants to play. He is very friendly, see?"
The man whistled and the dog came to him. He put the leash on the dog and patted his head.
"His name is Rex," the man said. "He likes to chase things, but he does not hurt them. Do you want to pet him?"
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They were still scared, but they were also curious. The dog wagged his tail and licked the man's face.
"Maybe he is not so bad," Lily said.
"Maybe," Ben said.
They slowly walked to the man and the dog. They reached out their hands and touched the dog's fur. It was soft and warm. The dog licked their hands and nuzzled their cheeks.
"See? He likes you," the man said. "He is a good dog, he just needs to settle down a bit."
Lily and Ben smiled. They felt better. They liked the dog, even if he was filthy.
"Can we play with him?" Lily asked.
"Sure, why not?" the man said. "But be careful, he might make you fall. He is very strong and fast."
Lily and Ben nodded. They took turns throwing a ball for the dog. The dog ran and fetched the ball and brought it back. They laughed and had fun. They forgot their fear.
They played until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the man and the dog.
"Thank you for letting us play with Rex," Lily said.
"Yes, thank you," Ben said.
"You're welcome, kids," the man said. "Come back anytime. Rex likes you."
Lily and Ben waved and left. They were happy. They had made a new friend.

Then, Mia had an idea. She went to the porch and tried to unlock a small box that was there. The key worked! Inside the box, they found a sour lemon. Mia's mom said, "Let's make lemonade!" They squeezed the lemon, added sugar and water, and made delicious lemonade. They drank it together on the porch, happy that they had unlocked the secret of the sour lemon.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread, so they asked their mom for some.
"Here you go, boys. But be careful, don't go too close to the water. There might be an alligator hiding there," their mom said.
Ben and Sam nodded and ran to the pond. They threw some bread to the ducks and fish, who came to eat. They were having fun, but soon they ran out of bread.
"Let's go back to mom and get more bread," Sam said.
"No, I want to stay here. Look, there is a big log in the water. Maybe we can stand on it and see more ducks and fish," Ben said.
He pointed to a long, brown thing in the water. Sam thought it looked like a log, too. He followed Ben to the edge of the pond.
"Be careful, Ben. Don't drop in the water. It might be hot," Sam said.
Ben laughed. "Don't be silly, Sam. The water is not hot. It is cool and nice. Watch me, I can stand on the log."
He stepped on the log, but it was not a log. It was an alligator. The alligator opened its big mouth and snapped at Ben. Ben screamed and jumped back. He dropped his hat in the water.
"Help, help! It's an alligator!" Ben cried.
Sam was scared, too. He ran to their mom and told her what happened. Their mom came to the pond and saw the alligator. She grabbed Ben and hugged him.
"Are you okay, Ben? You are very lucky. The alligator could have hurt you. You should have listened to me and stayed away from the water," she said.
Ben was sorry. He realized he was wrong. He hugged his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. I won't go near the water again."
Sam hugged his brother and said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I should have stopped you. I'm glad you are safe."
Their mom smiled and said, "It's okay, boys. I'm glad you are safe, too. Let's go home and have some ice cream. But remember, always be careful and listen to your mom."
Ben and Sam learned their lesson. They never went near the water again. They also never saw their hat again. The alligator kept it as a souvenir.

She hugged Lily. She said she was very brave and smart. She did the right thing. She trusted Mom. She helped Tom. She thanked her.
Lily was happy. She loved Mom. She loved Tom. She hoped he would be okay. She hoped he would trust her next time.

The boy was so sad, he wanted to eat the olive. He decided to wait outside until it got dark. Then he tried the long stick he had found. It worked! He opened up the olive and ate it with a big smile. Now he knew olives weren't a problem anymore.

Tom and Lily were playing in the yard. They liked to pretend they were heroes who could protect the world from bad guys. They had a fan that they used as a weapon. It made a loud noise and blew air.
"Look, Lily, I can make the fan spin faster!" Tom said. He pushed a button on the fan and it whirred louder.
"Wow, Tom, that's cool!" Lily said. "But be careful, don't break it. Mom said it's not a toy."
Tom didn't listen. He wanted to see how fast the fan could go. He pushed another button and the fan spun even faster. It made a very loud noise and blew a lot of air.
"Tom, stop it, you're making a mess!" Lily said. She saw the fan blowing dirt and leaves all over the yard. "Mom will be mad!"
Tom still didn't listen. He pushed the last button and the fan spun so fast that it flew out of his hands. It hit a rock and broke into pieces. The noise stopped and the air stopped.
"Tom, look what you did!" Lily said. She was scared and angry. "You broke the fan! Mom will be so mad!"
Tom was scared too. He saw the broken fan and the dirty yard. He knew he was in trouble. He tried to pick up the pieces, but it was too late. Mom came out of the house and saw the mess.
"Tom, Lily, what happened here?" Mom said. She was very mad. "Did you break the fan? Do you know how much it cost? How could you be so careless?"
Tom and Lily looked at each other. They didn't know what to say. They knew they had done something bad. They wished they had listened to Lily and not played with the fan. They wished they had protected the fan instead of breaking it. They wished they could be heroes, but they felt like losers.

Anna was shy. She did not know Ben. She wondered if he liked waffles too. She decided to bring him one of her waffles as a gift. She wrapped it in a napkin and put it in a basket.
She and her mom walked to Ben's house and knocked on the door. Ben's dad opened it and smiled. He said hello and invited them in. He said Ben was in his room, playing with his toys.

Ben's eyes lit up. He said, "I love waffles! Thank you, Anna. That's very nice of you. Do you want to play with me?"
Anna smiled. She said, "Yes, I do. Can I see your cars and trucks?"
Ben nodded. He said, "Sure. Come on, I'll show you. They are very cool."
Anna and Ben sat on the floor and played with the cars and trucks. They shared the waffle and talked about their favorite things. They became friends.

The moral of the story is: Sharing and being kind can help you make new friends.

"Ouch!" Lily says. "The bench is sticky. It hurts my legs."
"Me too!" Max says. "The bench is wet. It makes my pants dirty."

Ben was scared. He did not want the barber to cut his hair. He liked his hair long and curly. He did not know the barber. He wanted his dad.
"Dad, I don't want to. I want to go home. Please, dad," Ben cried.
His dad smiled and hugged him. "It's okay, Ben. The barber is a nice man. He knows how to make your hair look good. It won't hurt, I promise. You'll be done soon. Do you want a sticker when you're done?"
Ben sniffed and nodded. He liked stickers. He liked the ones with cars and animals. He hoped the barber had those.

"Oh no!" cried Lily, as she saw her doll floating in the water. She picked up Daisy and dried her off. Lily learned that she needed to be more careful when giving her toys a bath. From that day on, she always made sure to hold the cup steady and not let it tip over.

One day, True meets a new friend in the park. His name is Spot and he is a cat. Spot is curious and friendly. He says hello to True and asks him what he is doing.
"I am drinking water," True says. "I drink water every day. It is good for me and it makes me happy. Do you want to drink some water with me?"
Spot thinks for a moment. He does not drink water as much as True. He prefers milk or fish. But he wants to be polite and try something new. He nods and follows True to the fountain.
True and Spot drink some water from the fountain. True drinks a lot and makes a loud slurping sound. Spot drinks a little and makes a soft purring sound. They look at each other and smile.
"Water is not bad," Spot says. "But I still like milk and fish more. Thank you for sharing with me, True."
"You are welcome, Spot," True says. "I am glad you tried it. Maybe next time I can try some milk or fish with you."
True and Spot become good friends. They drink water together sometimes, but they also drink other things. They learn from each other and have fun. They are both enthusiastic and happy.

Lily liked fashion. She liked to wear pretty dresses and shoes and hats. She liked to look at magazines and see what other people wore. She wanted to be like them.
One day, Lily saw a fashion show on TV. She saw models walk on a long stage. They wore different clothes and colors. They looked happy and beautiful. Lily wanted to follow them. She wanted to be a model too.
She ran to her room and opened her closet. She picked out her favorite dress and shoes and hat. She put them on and looked in the mirror. She smiled and said, "I am a model!"
She went to the living room and saw her mom and dad. They were watching the TV. Lily said, "Look at me! I am a model! I want to follow the fashion show!"
Her mom and dad looked at her and smiled. They said, "You look very pretty, Lily. But you know, the fashion show is not real. It is just for fun. The models wear different clothes for different seasons and places. They change their clothes many times. They do not wear the same clothes every day."
Lily did not understand. She said, "But I like these clothes. I want to wear them every day. I want to be like the models."
Her mom and dad said, "You can wear them today, if you want. But tomorrow, you might want to wear something else. Something more comfortable and warm. Something that suits the weather and the occasion. Fashion is not just about clothes. It is also about being yourself and expressing your personality."
Lily thought about it. She said, "I see. But I still like these clothes. Can I wear them outside?"
Her mom and dad said, "Sure, you can. But be careful. It is raining outside. You might get wet and dirty. And your clothes might get ruined. Do you want that?"
Lily said, "No, I do not want that. I want to keep my clothes nice and clean. But I also want to go outside and play. What can I do?"
Her mom and dad said, "Why don't you wear a raincoat and boots over your clothes? That way, you can protect them from the rain and the mud. And you can still have fun outside. How does that sound?"
Lily said, "That sounds good. Thank you, mom and dad. You are very smart. You know a lot about fashion."
Her mom and dad said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are very sweet. And you have a lot of fashion sense too."
Lily put on her raincoat and boots and went outside. She followed the fashion show in her own way. She walked on the sidewalk like a stage. She twirled and posed and smiled. She did not care if she got wet or dirty. She was happy and beautiful. She was a model.

But this time, it wasn't the big and shiny bear she was looking for. Instead, she saw a small and weak toe sticking out of the ground! Sarah was so excited and asked the toe:
"Can you lead me home?"
The toe was surprised and answered:
"I wish I could little one, but I'm too weak. Maybe you should look for a stronger animal. Look for a horse, or maybe even a deer!"
After a few more minutes of searching, Sarah found a deer that was very strong and proud. She thanked the little toe and followed the deer all the way home. 
The end.

Lily and Tom went to a big place with many people and many tables. They sat with Mom and Dad and looked at the pictures on the paper. The paper had many things to eat and drink.
"What do you want, Lily?" Mom asked.
"I want fish," Lily said. She liked fish. It was yummy and soft.
"What do you want, Tom?" Dad asked.
"I want fish, too," Tom said. He liked fish, too. But he liked it a different way.
The man who worked at the big place came to their table. He had a pen and a paper.
"Hello, what can I get for you?" he asked.
Mom and Dad told him what they wanted. Then they told him what Lily and Tom wanted.
"Lily wants fish with rice and peas," Mom said.
"Tom wants fish with fries and ketchup," Dad said.
The man nodded and wrote on his paper.
"How do you want your fish?" he asked Tom.
"Rare," Tom said.
"Rare?" the man asked. He looked surprised.
"Yes, rare," Tom said. He liked his fish rare. It was pink and juicy.
"Are you sure?" the man asked.
"Yes, I'm sure," Tom said.
"Okay, rare fish for Tom," the man said. He smiled and went away.
Lily looked at Tom. She did not like rare fish. She liked her fish well done. It was white and flaky.
"Why do you like rare fish?" she asked Tom.
"Because it's good," Tom said.
"No, it's not," Lily said.
"Yes, it is," Tom said.
They started to argue. Mom and Dad told them to stop.
"Everyone can like different things," Mom said.
"That's right," Dad said. "Let's enjoy our food and be nice to each other."
Soon, the man came back with their food. He gave them plates and forks and spoons. He gave Tom his rare fish. It was pink and juicy. He gave Lily her well done fish. It was white and flaky.
They ate their fish and their sides. They drank their drinks. They said thank you to the man. They were full and happy.
They liked fish. But they liked it different ways. And that was okay.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with dough and paint. They make shapes and colors with their hands. They are happy and playful.
One day, they go to Ben's house. Ben's mom says they can play in the kitchen. She gives them dough and paint. She says, "Have fun, but be careful. Do not make a mess."
Lily and Ben say, "Okay, mom." They start to play with dough and paint. They make animals and flowers and cars. They laugh and talk.
But soon, they get bored. They want to do something else. They look around the kitchen. They see a big cake on the table. It is for Ben's dad's birthday. It has white frosting and candles.
Lily says, "Let's paint the cake. It will be more fun." Ben says, "No, mom will be mad. It is dad's cake." Lily says, "Don't be silly. It will be a surprise. Mom will like it."
She takes some paint and brushes. She paints the cake with red and blue and green. She makes dots and stripes and stars. She says, "Look, Ben. It is pretty. Come and help me."
Ben is scared. He does not want to paint the cake. But he does not want to make Lily sad. He takes some paint and brushes. He paints the cake with yellow and pink and purple. He makes circles and hearts and letters. He says, "Okay, Lily. It is done. Let's stop now."
They look at the cake. It is not white anymore. It is a rainbow of colors. It is messy and sticky and wet. They think it is funny. They giggle and clap.
But then, they hear a sound. It is Ben's mom. She is coming back to the kitchen. She says, "What are you doing? What have you done?"
She sees the cake. She is shocked and angry. She says, "How could you? You ruined the cake. It was for dad's birthday. He will be sad. You are very naughty. You have to go to your room. No more dough and paint for you."
She takes the cake and throws it in the trash. She takes the dough and paint and puts them away. She takes Lily and Ben and sends them to their room. She says, "You have to stay there until I say so. You have to think about what you did."
Lily and Ben are sad and sorry. They cry and hug. They wish they did not paint the cake. They wish they listened to mom. They wish they could say sorry to dad. They wish they could play with dough and paint again. But they can't. They have to stay in their room. They have no fun. They have a bad ending.

After a few seconds, a small voice called out, “Can you help me?” The fisherman was surprised and looked around. He saw a little boy, standing next to the broken boat.
The fisherman smiled, "Yes, I can help, but why don't you tell me what happened here?"
The little boy was deaf, so he spoke slowly. "I wanted to go fishing, so I took my boat out. But I don't know how to repair it."
The fisherman was touched by the little boy's courage. He put down his toolbox and said, "Let me help you. It won't take very long."
Together, the fisherman and the little boy fixed the boat. Once the boat was fixed, the Fisherman said goodbye and the little boy thanked him. The little boy jumped into the boat, holding his fishing poles and with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. She was very curious and always wanted to explore the world around her. One day she saw a fisherman in the river, she was so amazed and wondered what he was doing there. She followed the fisherman and watched him catch lots of fish. Then, Sally got really excited and decided to help the fisherman catch more fish. She grabbed a rod, found some bait, and casted out into the water. 
The fisherman was stunned that this little girl was helping him and smiled. Suddenly, the river started to get quiet. Sally hadn't noticed but the fisherman knew something was wrong. Suddenly, a giant wave came crashing down and knocked both Sally and the fisherman off their feet. Sally was terrified and ran away. The fisherman managed to climb back up the river bank, but Sally was too scared to go back.
The moral of this story is to always listen to people around you who know more. Even though Sally wanted to help the fisherman, if she had listened to his advice she would have not been put in danger. It's important to respect the wisdom of those more experienced than us and not get too curious and adventurous.

Anna and Ben are playing with their dolls in the living room. Anna likes to make her doll talk and act like a teacher. She says, "Hello, class. Today we are going to learn about colors. Repeat after me: red, blue, yellow, green."
Ben tries to copy her, but he forgets some of the colors. He says, "Red, blue, green, red." Anna laughs and says, "No, Ben. That's wrong. You have to say yellow, not red again. Yellow is like the sun and the bananas. Try again."
Ben feels embarrassed. He does not like when Anna laughs at him. He thinks she is mean. He looks at his doll and sees that it has a spot on its face. He says, "Look, Anna. Your doll has an itch. It has a red spot on its face. Maybe it has chicken pox."
Anna looks at her doll and sees the spot. She feels scared. She does not want her doll to be sick. She says, "No, Ben. That's not an itch. That's a sticker. You put a sticker on my doll. That's not nice. Take it off."
Ben smiles and says, "No, Anna. That's an itch. You have to scratch it. Scratch, scratch, scratch." He makes his doll scratch Anna's doll's face. Anna gets angry and says, "Stop it, Ben. You are hurting my doll. Give it back to me."
They start to pull and tug on the doll. They make a lot of noise. Their mom hears them and comes to the living room. She sees them fighting over the doll. She says, "What's going on here? Why are you two not playing nicely?"
Anna and Ben stop and look at their mom. They feel ashamed. They say, "Sorry, mom." They give each other the doll and hug. They say, "We are sorry, Anna. We are sorry, Ben. We are friends." They go back to playing with their dolls. They repeat the colors and the stickers. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there were two friends: Peter and Jimmy. They were walking in the park and saw a puddle of mud. Peter wanted to jump in it, but Jimmy said: "It's not a good idea, Peter. The mud will make us very dirty".
Peter said: "I don't care! I still want to jump in it!"

One day, their mom said they had to share a room, because their grandma was coming to visit. Ben and Lily did not like this idea. They wanted to have their own space and their own things. They started to argue and fight.
"Mom, Lily is always singing in the room. She makes too much noise. I can't sleep or play," Ben complained.
"Mom, Ben is always playing with his cars and trucks. He makes a mess. I can't read or dress," Lily whined.
Their mom was tired of their bickering. She said, "Ben and Lily, you have to learn to get along. You are twins, but you are also different. And that's okay. You can like different things, but you can also respect each other. You can share the room, and take turns to do what you like. You can also try to do something together, and maybe you will find something new that you both enjoy."
Ben and Lily did not want to listen. They wanted to do their own thing. They tried to resist their mom's words. But their mom was firm. She said, "If you don't stop fighting, you will have to go to bed early, and you will miss the movie night with grandma. Is that what you want?"
Ben and Lily did not want to miss the movie night. They loved their grandma, and they loved to watch movies with her. They looked at each other, and sighed. They decided to give their mom's idea a chance. They agreed to share the room, and take turns to do what they liked. They also agreed to try to do something together, and maybe they would find something new that they both enjoyed.
That night, they watched a movie with their grandma. It was a movie about cars and trucks, but it also had songs and dresses. Ben and Lily were surprised. They liked the movie. They liked the cars and trucks, and they liked the songs and dresses. They laughed and sang together. They realized that they had something in common, after all. They hugged each other, and said, "Sorry, for fighting. We love you."
Their mom smiled, and said, "I'm proud of you, Ben and Lily. You learned to respect each other, and to appreciate your differences. You also learned to try new things, and to have fun together. That's what being twins, and being family, is all about."

"That's not good. You should not touch the stove. It is dangerous," Mia said.

One day, Sara finds a new thing in her mommy's makeup bag. It is a furry brush. Sara wonders what it is for. She picks it up and rubs it on her face. It feels soft and tickly. She giggles and puts some powder on the brush. Then she paints her cheeks, nose, chin, and forehead with the powder. She looks in the mirror and smiles. She thinks she looks like a bunny.
But then she hears her mommy coming. She gets scared and hides under the bed. Her mommy opens the door and sees the mess on the floor. She sees the makeup bag, the mirror, and the powder. She frowns and calls Sara's name.
"Sara, where are you? What did you do with my makeup?"
Sara does not answer. She hopes her mommy will not find her. But her mommy sees her furry ears sticking out from under the bed. She bends down and pulls Sara out. She looks at Sara's face and tries not to laugh.
"Sara, what have you done? You look like a furry bunny!"
Sara looks at her mommy and says, "I'm sorry, mommy. I just wanted to play with your makeup. I like your furry brush. Can I keep it?"
Her mommy shakes her head and says, "No, Sara. You can't keep it. That is my makeup brush. You can't use my makeup without asking me. It is not for children. It can hurt your skin and eyes. And you made a big mess. You have to clean it up."
Sara feels bad and says, "I'm sorry, mommy. I won't do it again. Can you help me clean it up?"
Her mommy nods and says, "Yes, Sara. I will help you clean it up. But first, let's wash your face. You don't want to be a furry bunny all day, do you?"
Sara says, "No, mommy. I want to be your little girl."
Her mommy smiles and says, "That's better. Come on, let's go to the bathroom. And next time, if you want to play with makeup, ask me first. Maybe I can show you how to use it properly. Or we can find some makeup that is safe for children. OK?"
Sara nods and says, "OK, mommy. Thank you. I love you."
Her mommy hugs her and says, "I love you too, Sara. You are my pretty girl, with or without makeup."

Mia and Sam were curious. They wanted to see the ball. They walked towards the stranger, but their mom saw them and called them back. "Mia, Sam, come here. Don't go to the stranger. He is not our friend. We don't know him."
Mia and Sam ran back to their mom. They were scared and confused. They did not understand why the stranger was not nice. Their mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, my loves. The stranger was trying to trick you. He wanted to take you away from me. You should never go to a stranger, even if he has something fun. You should always stay with me or someone you know and trust."
Mia and Sam nodded. They felt better. They said sorry to their mom and thanked her for keeping them safe. They decided to play some more, but they stayed close to their mom. They did not look at the stranger anymore. He left the park soon after.
Mia and Sam were tired after playing. They were sleepy and hungry. Their mom said, "Let's go home, my loves. We can have some snacks and read a story. Then we can settle in our beds and have a nice nap." Mia and Sam agreed. They liked to nap with their mom. They held her hand and walked home. They were happy and safe.

Ben told Mom what happened. He said, "The book is bad. It does not like to be questioned. It thinks it is popular. It does not want to go back on the shelf."
Mom looked at the book. She said, "This book is not for you. It is for older kids. It is too hard and too scary for you. I will take it away and give it to someone else. You can read the other books on your shelf. They are nice and fun and they like to be questioned."

One day, a beautiful dog was walking in the park. The dog had a tiny flea on its back. The flea liked to jump and play on the dog's fur. The dog and the flea were best friends.
The dog said to the flea, "I have a hurt paw. Can you help me heal it?" The flea jumped onto the dog's paw and looked at it. The flea said, "I will try my best to help you."
The flea saw a big leaf nearby. The flea had an idea. It jumped onto the leaf and started to sing a magic song. As the flea sang, the leaf started to glow. The flea put the glowing leaf on the dog's paw. The dog's paw began to heal.
The dog was so happy and said, "Thank you, flea. You are the best friend ever!" The flea smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm happy I could help you."
From that day on, the dog and the flea played happily in the park every day. They knew that they could always count on each other to help when they needed it.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big ball on the grass. It was red and blue and yellow.
"Let's kick the ball!" Lily said.
"OK!" Ben said.
They took turns to kick the ball. They kicked it high and low and far and near. They had fun.
Then they saw something in the sky. It was a rainbow. It had many colors. It was bright and beautiful.
"Wow! Look at the rainbow!" Ben said.
"It's so pretty!" Lily said.
They ran to the rainbow. They wanted to touch it. But it was too far away.
They tried to kick the ball to the rainbow. But the ball could not reach it.
They felt sad.
Then they heard a voice. It was a fairy. She was flying near the rainbow. She had wings and a wand.
"Hello, children!" the fairy said. "Why are you sad?"
"We want to touch the rainbow, but we can't," Lily said.
The fairy smiled. She waved her wand. She said some magic words.
"Zim zam zoom! I give you a gift. You can kick the ball to the rainbow. But you have to be careful. The ball is very powerful. It can break things. Only kick it once. Then it will come back to you."
Lily and Ben were happy. They thanked the fairy.
They kicked the ball to the rainbow. The ball flew in the air. It touched the rainbow. It made a big splash. The rainbow sparkled.
Lily and Ben clapped their hands. They saw the ball coming back to them. They caught it.
They looked at the fairy. She winked at them. She flew away.
Lily and Ben hugged each other. They were glad. They had a magical day.

One day, Tim and Lily are making a big castle with a moat and a flag. They are very proud of their castle and want to show it to Mom and Dad. They run to the blanket where Mom and Dad are sitting and say, "Look, look, we made a castle!"
Mom and Dad smile and say, "Wow, that's a very nice castle! You did a great job!"
Tim and Lily are happy and say, "Thank you! Can we go back and finish it?"
Mom and Dad say, "Sure, but be careful of the waves. They are getting bigger and stronger. Don't go too far from the shore."
Tim and Lily say, "OK, we will be careful." They run back to their castle and start to add more sand and shells.
But while they are busy, a big wave comes and washes away their castle. Tim and Lily are sad and cry, "Oh no, our castle is gone! The wave was bad and ruined it!"
Mom and Dad hear them and run to them. They hug them and say, "It's OK, don't cry. The wave didn't mean to be bad. It's just part of the sea. Sometimes it makes things and sometimes it breaks things. But you can always make another castle. Maybe even bigger and better."
Tim and Lily stop crying and say, "Really? Can we make another castle?"
Mom and Dad say, "Of course you can. But first, let's have some lunch. You must be hungry after all that work."
Tim and Lily say, "OK, let's have lunch. Then we can make another castle. And we will watch out for the waves."
Mom and Dad say, "That's a good plan. Come on, let's go to the blanket. We have sandwiches and juice and cookies."
Tim and Lily say, "Yay, we love sandwiches and juice and cookies!" They follow Mom and Dad to the blanket and have a nice lunch. Then they go back to the sand and make another castle. And they have fun at the beach. The end.

Lily looked around. She saw a red scarf on a bench. It belonged to a lady who was reading a book. Lily ran to the bench and took the scarf.
"Hey, that's mine!" the lady shouted. She was angry. She got up and chased Lily.
Lily was scared. She ran back to Ben with the scarf. The lady followed her.
"Give me back my scarf, you crazy girl!" the lady said. She reached for the scarf.
But Lily did not want to give it back. She wanted to use it for a flag. She held it tight and ran around the castle.
"Stop, stop!" Ben said. He did not like the lady. He did not like the shouting. He wanted to relax and play with the castle.
He had an idea. He took some sand and threw it at the lady. The sand got in her eyes and mouth. She coughed and blinked.
"Ow, ow, ow!" she said. She dropped the book and rubbed her eyes.
Lily and Ben saw their chance. They put the scarf on the castle as a flag. They smiled and hugged.
"We did it!" they said. "We have the best castle ever!"
They relaxed and admired their work. They did not care about the lady or the book. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a bee, and he was very gentle. He flew around the garden, buzzing and looking for flowers. He was happy.
Suddenly he noticed something funny happening in a corner of the garden. He flew over to take a closer look and saw a little boy who looked about three years old. The little boy was carefully pushing some dirt into a pile, and talking to himself.
The little boy looked up and saw the bee. "Hello!" he said. He pointed at the pile of dirt and said: "I'm putting this here, do you want to help?"
The bee was very gentle, so he nodded his head and landed softly on the pile of dirt. Together they worked to make the dirt higher and higher. When they were finished, the little boy stepped back and smiled.
Suddenly, the bee heard loud buzzing coming from the pile of dirt. "Look!" said the little boy. He put his hands in the dirt and dug out a big, buzzing hive of bees! 
The little boy had put the dirt there for a reason--he knew that it was a great place for bees to make their hive. The bee was impressed by the little boy's gentle and caring nature. It seemed that he was always looking out for his little friends. The bee gave the little boy a grateful nod before flying off to join the others.

Lily and Tom were playing with clay. They liked to make shapes and animals with the clay. Lily made a big ball and Tom made a long snake. They put their clay on the table.
"Look, I made a ball!" Lily said. "It is round and smooth."
"Look, I made a snake!" Tom said. "It is long and wiggly."
They looked at each other's clay and smiled. They were happy.
Then, Tom had an idea. He took his snake and wrapped it around Lily's ball. He pressed hard and made the ball flat.
"Hey, what are you doing?" Lily asked. "You ruined my ball!"
"I made a pancake!" Tom said. "It is flat and yummy."
He lifted his snake and looked at the pancake. He saw a big crack in the middle. He was sad.
"You broke my snake!" Tom said. "You made a crack!"
He threw his snake on the floor and started to cry. He was grumpy.
Lily looked at the pancake and the snake. She felt sorry for Tom. She did not like to see him cry.
"I'm sorry, Tom," Lily said. "I did not mean to make a crack. Can we fix it?"
She picked up the snake and the pancake. She rolled them together and made a new ball. She gave it to Tom.
"Here, Tom," Lily said. "We can make a new shape. We can make a star or a heart or a flower. What do you want to make?"
Tom stopped crying and looked at the ball. He saw the clay was soft and smooth. He smiled.
"Thank you, Lily," Tom said. "You are a good friend. I want to make a flower. We can spread the clay and make petals."
They took the ball and spread the clay. They made a beautiful flower. They put it on the table and admired it.
"Look, we made a flower!" Lily and Tom said. "It is pretty and colorful."
They hugged each other and laughed. They were happy.

They got in the car and drove for a long time. Lila looked out the window and saw many roads. Some roads were big and busy, with many cars and trucks and noises. Some roads were small and quiet, with only a few houses and animals. Lila did not like the roads. She missed her park.
They arrived at their new house. It was on a lonely road, far from the city. There were no other houses nearby, only fields and hills. Lila did not see any children or toys or flowers. She only saw a dusty yard and a broken fence. She did not like the house. She wanted to go back to her old home.
She got out of the car and followed her mom inside. Her mom showed her her new room. It was small and dark, with no pictures or colors. Lila did not like the room. She felt scared and angry. She threw her ball on the floor and said, "I hate it here! I want to go back!"
Her mom hugged her and said, "I know, honey. I know. It's hard to leave what you know and love. But we have to stay here for a while. It's for our own good. Trust me, okay?"
Lila did not understand. She did not think it was for their own good. She did not trust her mom. She pushed her away and ran outside. She grabbed her ball and ran down the lonely road. She did not care where she was going. She just wanted to get away from the new house. She did not see the car coming. She did not hear the horn. She did not feel the pain. She only saw a flash of light. Then everything went black.

Her nephew replied, "Thank you aunt! That was so kind of you. I didn't think anyone cared." His aunt replied, "Of course I care! That's what aunts are for - to help in any way we can."
The two spent the rest of the day playing with the games and toys the aunt had brought. The nephew was so excited and his aunt was so happy that she had supplied him with the things he needed to make him happy.
The moral value of this story is that it's important to show people you care about them and support them. Aunts are especially good at doing this. Even the smallest thing can mean so much when it comes to making someone feel special.

"Look, there is a huge frog!" Ben shouted. He pointed to a big green frog that was sitting on a rock. It had big eyes and a wide mouth. Ben ran towards the rock. He wanted to touch the huge frog.

"Ben, are you okay?" Lily asked. She ran to the edge of the pond. She saw Ben in the water. He was wet and muddy. He looked sad and scared.
"I'm okay, Lily," Ben said. He tried to smile. He got out of the pond. Mom came and hugged him. She said he was brave and helped him dry off.
"Sorry, Mom," Ben said. "I wanted to see the huge frog."
"It's okay, Ben," Mom said. "The huge frog is just a frog. He is not a toy. He likes to live in the pond. Maybe next time you can watch him from far away."
Ben nodded. He learned his lesson. He did not want to slip again. He and Lily said goodbye to the pond and the frogs. They went home with Mom. They had a warm bath and a hot chocolate. They told Dad about their adventure. They still liked frogs, but they liked them better in the pond.

She picked up the basket and carried it to the laundry room. She opened the dryer and dumped the clothes inside. She did not see Lily's face under the blanket.
Lily felt the basket moving and heard a loud noise. She was confused and frightened. She tried to scream, but the blanket muffled her voice. She felt hot and dizzy. She thought, "What is happening? Where am I? Where is Ben?"
Ben heard the dryer running and had an idea. He ran to the laundry room and opened the dryer. He saw a pile of clothes and a blanket. He pulled the blanket and saw Lily's face. Lily cried and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I thought it was a good place to hide. I didn't know mom would take me to the dryer. It was hot and loud and scary. I'm sorry, Ben."
Ben said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you're safe. But next time, don't hide in the laundry. It's dangerous and not fun. Let's hide in ordinary places, like the closet or the sofa. Okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Ben. I learned my lesson. Let's hide in ordinary places. And let's tell mom we're sorry for making her worry."
They hugged each other and went to find their mom. They apologized and told her what happened. Their mom was relieved and angry. She said, "You two are very lucky. You could have been hurt or worse. Don't ever hide in the laundry again. Do you understand?"
They said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We're sorry, mom."

They said, "We love you, too, mom. We will follow the rules and respect the house. And we will be nice to each other."
They kissed their mom and went to play somewhere else. They hid in ordinary places and had fun. They never hid in the laundry again. They learned their lesson.

The little spider was scared but did not want to fight. The spider said, "Please, Ant, let's not fight. We can share this room and be friends."
The big ant thought about it and decided to give it a try. They both lived in the room together and became good friends. The ant helped the spider make the cobweb even bigger and prettier. The spider helped the ant find food. They were happy and never fought again.
The moral of the story is that it is better to be friends and help each other than to fight.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived two brothers called Joe and Fred. Joe was very adventurous and bold, while Fred was much more timid. Joe suggested that they should try being performers and, to his surprise, Fred agreed.
The brothers invited their friends to the town square for their performance. Joe was excited and brought a microphone. When Fred stepped up to the microphone, he became very nervous. Joe tried to suggest that Fred just sing an orange song, but Fred just looked down at his feet and said nothing.
The crowd started booing at Fred and Joe understood his brother's fear. He stepped in and began singing the orange song but suddenly the microphone stopped working.
The crowd started leaving one by one and soon the brothers were alone. Joe looked at Fred and realised his brother wasn't really ready for the stage. He said, "Let's try something else, something we are both good at. Let's promise each other that we won't be ashamed of trying something new and that there is nothing wrong with having stage fright."
The moral of this story is that it's ok to try something new, but be sure to always be prepared. For Joe, it was a lesson in setting realistic expectations and understanding others' fears. Never shame someone else for feeling nervous and don't expect too much of them before they are ready - foreshadowing an unexpected event can often lead to a bad outcome.

One day, Jimmy the hippo went to the hospital for an x-ray. He was feeling very lazy and he did not want to go, but his mom insisted.
At the hospital, the doctor smiled and said, "Welcome Jimmy! How can I help you today?"
Jimmy said, "I would like a x-ray, please." The doctor nodded and took him to the x-ray room.
When they got there, the doctor said, "I'd like you to stand still while I take the x-ray."
But Jimmy was feeling lazy, so he started talking and laughing and moving around. "Don't ignore the doctor," his mom said sternly.
Jimmy sighed and stood still. The doctor snapped the x-ray and smiled. "Thank you for cooperating," he said.
Jimmy felt relieved. He wasn't so lazy after all!

Tom and Lily were playing with marbles in the garden. They liked to roll them on the grass and see who could get them closer to the big rock. They had many marbles of different colors and sizes.
"Look, Lily, I have a blue marble with white spots. It is very pretty," Tom said, holding up his marble.
"I have a red marble with yellow stripes. It is very fast," Lily said, showing her marble.
They took turns rolling their marbles and counting the steps to the rock. Tom was winning by one step.
"Last round, Lily. Hurry up and roll your marble," Tom said.
Lily nodded and threw her marble with all her might. It flew over the grass and hit the rock with a loud clang. Then it bounced back and rolled into the road.
"Oh no, my marble!" Lily cried. She ran after it, forgetting to look both ways.

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe they belong to someone. Maybe they are for a special day."
Lila did not listen. She grabbed a red candle and a blue candle and put them in her pocket. Tom took a green candle and a yellow candle and did the same.
They ran back to the house and went to their room. They closed the door and lit the candles with a match. They put them on the table and watched them glow.
"They are so nice," Lila said. "They make our room look like a fairy tale."
"Yes, they do," Tom said. "But I feel bad. We should not have taken them. What if someone misses them?"
Just then, they heard a knock on the door. It was their grandma, who lived with them. She opened the door and saw the candles.
"Children, what are you doing?" she asked. "Where did you get these candles?"
Lila and Tom looked at each other. They felt ashamed. They told their grandma the truth. They said they found the candles in a sack in the garden and took them without asking.
Their grandma was not angry. She was sad. She said, "These candles are very special. They are from my old country. I brought them with me when I came here. They are for a festival that I celebrate every year. It is a festival of light and hope. I was going to share them with you and teach you about it. But now, some of them are gone."
Lila and Tom felt very sorry. They hugged their grandma and said they were sorry. They said they did not know. They said they would give the candles back.
Their grandma smiled and said, "It's okay, my dears. I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. That is how you become wise. Come, let's go to the garden and put the candles back in the sack. Then, we can light them together and celebrate the festival. I will tell you all about it."
Lila and Tom nodded and followed their grandma. They put the candles back in the sack and thanked her for being so kind. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect other people's things and to be curious about other cultures. They also learned that their grandma was very wise and loved them very much.

One sunny day, Mr. Whiskers met a little bird named Chirpy. Chirpy saw the sword and wanted to try it too. Chirpy said, "Mr. Whiskers, can I try your sword, please?" Mr. Whiskers said, "Yes, Chirpy, but be careful. It's not a real sword, just a toy."
Chirpy took the sword and tried to fly with it. But the sword was too big for Chirpy. Mr. Whiskers saw Chirpy was having a hard time. He said, "Chirpy, let me help you." Mr. Whiskers held the sword while Chirpy flew around it.
They played together all day and had lots of fun. When the sun went down, Chirpy said, "Thank you, Mr. Whiskers, for letting me try your sword. You are a wise and kind friend." Mr. Whiskers smiled and said, "You're welcome, Chirpy. I'm happy we could play together."
From that day on, Mr. Whiskers and Chirpy became best friends. They played with the sword and had many fun adventures together. They learned that sharing and helping each other made their days more fun and happy.

Tim was having fun, but he did not listen to the funny volcano's warning. He drank and drank and drank from the river. The funny volcano started to look worried.

Tim felt very sick, and he could not play with the funny volcano anymore. The funny volcano was sad, and Tim learned a lesson about listening to his friends.

"Look, Anna, you have a new dress!" Lily said. "You are the most pretty princess ever!"
But then, Lily's mom came into the room. She saw the scissors and the velvet pieces on the floor. She saw Anna's dress with holes in it. She was very angry.
"Lily, what have you done?" she shouted. "You ruined your doll's dress! And you could have hurt yourself with the scissors! They are very sharp and dangerous! You are a very naughty girl!"
She took the scissors and the doll away from Lily. She said Lily had to go to her room and stay there. She said Lily could not play with Anna anymore.
Lily cried and cried. She was very sorry. She loved Anna and did not want to hurt her. She did not mean to be naughty. She just wanted to make Anna more pretty. But now she had no doll, no scissors, and no velvet. She had nothing. She felt very sad and lonely. She wished she had never seen the scissors. She wished she had left Anna's dress ordinary.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the garden. One day, they find a big spider in a web. The spider is black and has eight legs.
"Look, a spider!" Tim says. He wants to touch it.
"Be careful, Tim. The spider might bite you," Sam says. He is afraid of spiders.
"No, the spider is nice. He is intelligent. He makes a web to catch flies. He is my friend," Tim says. He puts his hand near the spider.
The spider moves and makes a sound. He does not like Tim's hand. He wants to be alone.
"Tim, stop! The spider is angry. He is not your friend. He is a wild animal. He does not want to play with you," Sam says. He pulls Tim away from the spider.
"But I want to keep the spider. He is so cool. Can we keep him, please?" Tim asks. He looks at Sam with big eyes.
"No, Tim. We cannot keep the spider. He belongs to the garden. He needs his web and his flies. He will not be happy in a jar or a box. He will be sad and sick. We have to let him go," Sam says. He is wise and kind.
"Okay, Sam. You are right. We have to let him go. Bye, spider. Have a good day. Thank you for showing us your web," Tim says. He waves to the spider.
The spider waves back with one of his legs. He is glad that Tim and Sam leave him alone. He is intelligent, too. He knows that humans are not his friends. He goes back to his web and waits for his next meal.

"Look at my boat!" Ben said. "It is fast and strong. I am a captain!"
They took turns to put their toys in the water and make them splash. They had fun and laughed.
But then, Ben had an idea. He grabbed Lily's crown and threw it in the water. It sank to the bottom.
"Hey!" Lily cried. "That is not nice! Give me back my crown!"
Ben laughed. He reached for the crown, but it was too deep. He could not get it.
"Ha ha!" Lily said. "Now you can't have it either!"

They stopped splashing and looked at each other. They were both sorry. They hugged and said sorry.
They got out of the water and dried themselves. They looked for the crown, but they could not find it. It was gone.
They were sad, but they decided to share the boat. They played with it on the grass. They pretended to sail to a new land. They found a new crown made of flowers. They took turns to wear it. They were happy again.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples on it. They wanted to pick some apples to eat, but the tree was too high for them.
"Let's ask the old man who lives near the tree. He is very wise and kind. Maybe he can help us," Lily said.
They ran to the old man's house and knocked on the door. The old man opened the door and smiled at them.
"Hello, Lily and Ben. What can I do for you?" he asked.
"Hello, sir. We want to pick some apples from the big tree, but we can't reach them. Can you help us, please?" Ben said.
The old man nodded and took a ladder from his garage. He carried it to the tree and set it up. He climbed the ladder and picked some apples for them. He gave them each an apple and said, "Here you go, children. Enjoy your apples. They are sweet and juicy."
"Thank you, sir. You are very nice and helpful," Lily said.
"You're welcome, children. But remember, apples are not only good for your taste, but also for your health. They can help you gain strength and energy. And they can also help you gain wisdom, if you learn from them," the old man said.
"Learn from them? How can we learn from apples?" Ben asked.
The old man smiled and said, "Well, apples can teach you many things. They can teach you about colors, shapes, sizes, and numbers. They can teach you about seasons, growth, and change. They can teach you about sharing, caring, and gratitude. And they can teach you about life, beauty, and joy. All you have to do is look, touch, smell, taste, and listen to them. And then, think, feel, and talk about them. That's how you can learn from apples, and from anything else in the world."
Lily and Ben listened to the old man with wonder and curiosity. They looked at their apples and saw them in a new way. They thanked the old man again and ran back to the park. They ate their apples and enjoyed them very much. And they also learned from them and gained wisdom.

"Where are our birds?" Ben asked.
"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe they are lost."
They looked at the woods and saw many trees and bushes and animals. They were scared.
"Maybe there are bad things in there," Ben said. "Maybe they will hurt our birds."
"No, no," Lily said. "Our birds are smart and brave. They will find a way back to us."
They decided to wait and hope for their birds to come back. They sat on the grass and hugged each other.

One of them was a big black crow. He saw the toy birds and wanted to take them. He flew after them and tried to catch them. He was fast and strong and mean.
"Leave us alone!" the blue bird said.
"Go away!" the pink bird said.
But the crow did not listen. He got closer and closer. He reached out his claws and grabbed the pink bird by the wing. He pulled hard and tried to separate her from the blue bird.
"Help!" the pink bird cried.
"Let her go!" the blue bird said.
He flew at the crow and pecked him with his beak. He made a loud noise and scared the crow. The crow let go of the pink bird and flew away. He did not want to fight with the toy birds. He thought they were harmless, but they were not.
The blue bird and the pink bird hugged each other. They were happy they were safe. They looked for a way back to Ben and Lily. They saw a bright light in the sky. It was the sun. "Look, look!" Ben said. "Our birds are back!"
"Yay, yay!" Lily said. "We missed you so much!"

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big jar of powder on the table. It was white and soft.
"What is this?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is snow," Ben said.
They opened the jar and took some powder in their hands. They threw it in the air and watched it fall. It looked like snow, but it did not feel cold.
"Let's spread it on the grass," Lily said. "It will be fun."
They took more powder and ran around the garden. They spread it on the grass, on the flowers, on the trees, and on each other. They laughed and shouted.
But then, they heard a voice.
"Hey, what are you doing?" It was Mom. She looked angry.
She came to the garden and saw the mess. The powder was everywhere. It was not snow. It was flour.
"Flour? Why did you take the flour?" Mom asked.
"We thought it was snow," Lily said.
"We wanted to play," Ben said.
Mom shook her head. "Flour is not for playing. Flour is for baking. You wasted a lot of flour. And you made a big mess. You have to clean it up."
Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not know they did something bad. They thought they were having fun.
"Sorry, Mom," they said.
Mom sighed. "It's okay. I know you did not mean to. But next time, ask me before you take something. And don't play with boring things like flour. There are many other things you can play with. Come on, I'll show you."
She took them inside and gave them some toys. They played with the toys and forgot about the flour. They learned their lesson. Flour is not snow. Flour is boring.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toy animals in the garden. Sara had a big elephant and Tom had a small mouse. They made noises and pretended to be in the jungle.
"Look, my elephant is so strong and brave!" Sara said. "He can squeeze anything with his trunk!"
"Can he squeeze my mouse?" Tom asked.
"Sure, he can!" Sara said. "But he won't, because he is nice and harmless. He only squeezes bad things, like snakes and crocodiles."
Tom was curious. He wanted to see if the elephant could really squeeze his mouse. He moved his mouse closer to the elephant's trunk.
"Hey, what are you doing?" Sara asked. "Don't touch my elephant!"
"I just want to see!" Tom said. "It's only a toy, it won't hurt!"
But Sara was angry. She did not like Tom touching her elephant. She grabbed the elephant and pulled it away from Tom.
"Give it back!" Tom shouted. "That's not fair!"
They both tugged on the elephant, trying to get it to their side. The elephant's trunk stretched and twisted.
"Stop it!" Sara cried. "You're breaking my elephant!"
They heard a loud snap. The elephant's trunk broke off. They both gasped and let go of the elephant.
They looked at each other, then at the broken toy. They felt sad and sorry.
"I'm sorry, Sara," Tom said. "I didn't mean to break your elephant."
"I'm sorry, Tom," Sara said. "I shouldn't have been so mean to you."
They hugged and said they were still friends. They decided to share their toys and play nicely. They fixed the elephant's trunk with some tape and glue. They learned to be careful and gentle with their toys and each other.

The crab said “Can I have some?”
The bird told him “Yes, of course, you can have some. I cooked it especially for you!”
The crab was so happy and thanked the bird.
He gobbled up the delicious crab and it was the best thing he ever tasted! As he ate, he watched the sand glow in the sunset.

Sara and Ben smile. They have an idea. They go to the house and get some bread. They break the bread into small pieces. They scatter the bread on the ground. They hope the bird will like the bread. Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with toys. One day, they saw a big and shiny toy car in the shop window. They both wanted the toy car very much, but it was very expensive.
"Mom, can we have the toy car, please?" they asked their mom, who was with them.
"I'm sorry, my loves, but we don't have enough money for the toy car. It costs too much. Maybe you can save some money and buy it later," their mom said.
Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They did not want to wait. They wanted the toy car now. They thought of a plan. They wrote a note to their dad, who was at work. They wrote: "Dear Dad, we love you very much. Please buy us the toy car from the shop. It is a very nice toy car. Thank you. Love, Tom and Lily."
They put the note in their dad's coat pocket, which was hanging on the door. They hoped their dad would see the note and buy them the toy car.
But their mom saw the note first. She was not happy. She knew the toy car was too expensive. She took the note and put it in the trash. She called Tom and Lily and said: "What is this note? Did you write this? This is not a nice thing to do. You cannot request things that we cannot afford. You have to be grateful for what you have. And you have to be honest with your dad. He works hard to provide for us. You should not try to trick him."
Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They knew their mom was right. They hugged their mom and said: "We're sorry, mom. We were wrong. We love you and dad very much. We don't need the toy car. We have enough toys. We will be good and patient."
Their mom smiled and said: "I forgive you, my loves. I know you are good and kind. And maybe one day, when we have more money, we can buy the toy car. But for now, let's go home and play with what we have."
Tom and Lily nodded and said: "Okay, mom. Let's go home and play." They held their mom's hand and walked away from the shop window. They did not look at the toy car anymore. They were happy with their mom and their toys.

"Look, a frog!" Sam said. "Can we catch it?"
"OK, but be careful," Mia said. "Frogs are slippery."
They ran after the frog. The frog was fast. It hopped from one place to another. Sam and Mia tried to grab it, but they missed. They laughed and chased it more.
The frog came to a big rock. It jumped on the rock. Sam and Mia followed it. They climbed on the rock too. The frog looked at them. It opened its mouth and said:
"Ribbit! Leave me alone! I am a normal frog. I do not want to play with you. Go away!"
Sam and Mia were surprised. They did not know frogs could talk. They felt scared and sorry. They said:
"Sorry, frog. We did not mean to bother you. We just wanted to see you. You are very cool."
The frog said:
"Too late. You made me angry. Now you will pay. I have a magic power. I can stretch you like rubber. Watch this!"
The frog stretched its tongue. It was very long and sticky. It wrapped around Sam and Mia. It pulled them close to the frog. The frog smiled and said:
"Now you are mine. I will eat you for lunch. You are not cool. You are fools."
Sam and Mia screamed. They tried to get free, but they could not. The frog's tongue was too strong. They cried and wished they had left the frog alone. They learned a hard lesson. They never played with frogs again. The end.

"Me too!" Ben says. "Let's go and ask."

"Yes, yes, yes!" Lila and Ben say.

Lila and Ben hold each other. They hope someone will come. They hear a noise. It is a loud and strong noise. It is a helicopter.

Emma smiled and said, "Want my help? I'm good at fixing things."

Mia and Ben were twins who liked to play outside in the snow. They put on their coats, boots, hats and mittens and ran to the backyard. They saw a big pile of snow and decided to make a snowman.
"Let's grab some snow and roll it into a ball," Mia said.
"OK, I'll grab some too," Ben said.
They worked hard and made a big ball for the snowman's body, a smaller ball for the head, and two more balls for the feet. They found some sticks for the arms, a carrot for the nose, and some rocks for the eyes and mouth.
"Our snowman looks great!" Mia said.
"Yes, he does. But he needs a hat," Ben said.
They looked around and saw a red hat on the fence. It belonged to Mr. Jones, their nosy neighbor who always watched them from his window.
"Let's grab his hat and put it on our snowman," Ben said.
"But that's not nice. It's his hat, not ours," Mia said.
"Who cares? He won't notice. He's too busy being nosy," Ben said.
He ran to the fence and grabbed the hat. He put it on the snowman's head and smiled.
"Look, now he's perfect!" Ben said.
Mia felt bad. She knew they did something wrong. She hoped Mr. Jones wouldn't see them.
But Mr. Jones did see them. He opened his window and shouted.
"Hey, you kids! That's my hat! Give it back right now!"
Mia and Ben were scared. They ran away from the snowman and the hat. They went back to their house and closed the door.
They learned their lesson. They never grabbed anything that didn't belong to them again.

"Thank you, Lila. You are a good friend. You are dependable. That means you always help me and share with me." Tom says, putting the rock in his pocket.
"You are welcome, Tom. You are dependable too. You always play with me and listen to me." Lila says, hugging Tom.

"Who is that, Lila?" Tom asks, curious.
"I don't know, Tom. Maybe he is here to fix something." Lila says, watching the man.
The man comes back to the truck and opens the back. He takes out some tools and a ladder. He carries them to the side of the house. He sets up the ladder and climbs up to the roof. He starts to hammer and saw and drill. He makes more noise and dust.
"What is he doing, Lila?" Tom asks, worried.
"I don't know, Tom. Maybe he is making something new." Lila says, trying to see.
They hear a voice. It is Lila's mom. She comes out of the house and calls them.
"Lila, Tom, come here. I have something to tell you." She says, smiling.
They run to her and hold her hands. She leads them to the front of the house. She points to the roof.
"See, Lila, Tom, the man is making a new window for your room. He is making it bigger and brighter. He is making it so you can see the sun rise every morning. Isn't that nice?" She says, excited.
Lila and Tom look at the roof. They see a hole where the old window was. They see the man working on the new window. They see the sun shining through the dust. They smile and clap.
"Wow, mom, that is nice! Thank you, mom! Thank you, man!" They say, happy.
They hug their mom and wave to the man. They go back to their yard and play some more. They are happy and excited. They can't wait to see their new window and the sun rise. They are dependable friends. They are happy children.

Lily and Ben were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and find shells. Lily found a big shell that was shiny and pink. She was very happy.
"Look, Ben, I found a pretty shell!" she said, holding it up.
Ben looked at the shell and felt jealous. He wanted a pretty shell too. He only had a small shell that was brown and dull.
"That's not a pretty shell, that's a silly shell!" he said, trying to tease Lily. "My shell is better than yours!"
Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like Ben's words. She thought her shell was very pretty and not silly at all.
"No, your shell is not better, your shell is boring!" she said, sticking out her tongue. "My shell is the best!"
They started to argue and shout. They did not want to share or play nicely. They forgot to have fun.
A big wave came and splashed them. They got wet and cold. They stopped arguing and looked at the water. They saw a crab crawling out of the wave. It had big claws and eyes. It looked hungry.
The crab saw the shells in their hands. It wanted to eat them. It moved towards them, snapping its claws.
"Uh-oh, look, a crab!" Lily said, feeling scared.
"Let's run, it's hungry!" Ben said, feeling scared too.
They dropped their shells and ran away. They did not want to be eaten by the crab. They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a blanket. They hugged them and felt safe.
They looked back at the beach. They saw the crab picking up their shells and taking them to its hole. They felt sorry for their shells. They wished they had not fought over them. They learned to be kind and not tease. They decided to play together and find more shells. They had fun again.

"Tim, what happened?" she asked. Tim showed her his knee. "Oh no, you need a bandage," she said. She went inside the house and came back with a bandage. She put it on Tim's knee. "Now, you will become better," she told him.
Just then, they heard a loud noise. They looked up and saw a big, colorful bird in the tree. The bird was singing a happy song. Tim stopped crying and started to laugh. The bird flew down and landed on Tim's shoulder. The bird had a bandage on its wing too! Tim and the bird became best friends and played together all day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a deaf dog named Max. Max could not hear anything, but he was very good at smelling and seeing things.
One day, Max was walking in the park with his friend, a little girl named Lily. They saw a big tree with many pieces of paper on the ground. "What is this?" asked Lily. Max sniffed the pieces and managed to find a note that said, "Find all the pieces and put them together to see a surprise."
Lily and Max worked together to find all the pieces. Max used his nose to smell the pieces and Lily used her hands to put them together. After a while, they managed to find all the pieces and put them together to make a big picture.
The picture was of a beautiful rainbow with a message that said, "You did a great job! Now go and enjoy the park!" Lily and Max were very happy and proud of themselves. They spent the rest of the day playing and having fun in the park. And from that day on, Max and Lily knew that even if Max was deaf, they could still manage to do anything together.

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big case with many cars and trucks. Mia has a small case with many dolls and animals. They like to share their toys and make stories with them.
One day, they find a new toy in Tom's case. It is a shiny orange car that looks very fast and cool. Tom and Mia want to play with it, but they don't know who it belongs to.
"Wow, look at this car!" Tom says. "It is so orange and shiny. Can I play with it?"
"I don't know, Tom. It is not your car. Maybe it is a gift from someone." Mia says.
"Maybe it is from Mom or Dad. They always give us nice things. Let's ask them." Tom says.
They run to the kitchen, where Mom and Dad are making lunch. They show them the orange car and ask them if it is theirs.
"No, sweeties, that is not our car. We don't know where it came from. Maybe it was in the case by mistake." Mom says.
"Be careful with it, though. It looks like it is made of something that can melt. Don't put it near the stove or the heater." Dad says.
Tom and Mia nod and go back to the living room. They decide to play with the orange car together, taking turns to drive it around the floor. They have a lot of fun with it, until they hear a strange sound.
"Uh-oh, what is that?" Mia says.
They look at the orange car and see that it is changing shape. It is getting smaller and softer. It is melting!
"Oh no, the car is melting!" Tom says.
They pick up the car and try to save it, but it is too late. It is a sticky orange mess in their hands.
They start to cry and run to Mom and Dad. They show them the melted car and tell them what happened.
"I'm sorry, sweeties, that was not a real car. It was a candy car. It was supposed to be a treat for you, but we forgot to tell you. We didn't know it was in the case." Mom says.
"It's okay, sweeties, don't cry. We have more candy for you. You can have some after lunch. And you still have your other toys to play with." Dad says.
They hug Tom and Mia and wipe their tears. They give them some water and a napkin to clean their hands. They tell them they love them and they are proud of them for sharing and being kind.
Tom and Mia feel better and smile. They say thank you and they love them too. They go back to the living room and play with their other toys. They forget about the melted car and have a happy day.

Once there was a kind and compassionate boy named George. He wanted to help everyone he met. One day, George was walking in the woods and he saw a shade in trouble. He noticed that it was burning from the sun heat. 
George ran over to help. "Shade, I'm here to help you!" he said, his voice full of compassion. The shade was relieved. 
"Thank you, George! It's so hot. Do you have a way I can cool down?" 
George thought carefully. Suddenly, he had an idea. He found a big leaf and held it over the shade. Instantly the shade didn't feel so hot any more. 
"Thank you George!" said the shade. "Your kind heart has saved me!" 
George was glad. With a cheerful smile, he said, "You're welcome! That's what friends are for!"

Anna ran to her mom and dad. She told them what Tom did. They were shocked and angry. They went to Tom's room and scolded him. They said, "Tom, how could you do that? That is Anna's diary! You have no right to read it or take it! You should be sorry and ashamed!"
Tom did not care. He said, "I don't care! It is just a stupid diary! Anna is a baby! I am not sorry!"
Mom and dad took the diary from Tom and gave it back to Anna. They hugged her and said, "We are sorry, Anna. Tom was very wrong and mean. We will punish him for what he did. You can write in your diary as much as you want. We love you."

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Andy. Everyday he would visit his grandmother, who lived in an old house with a wardrobe in her bedroom. 
One day, while he was visiting, Andy asked his grandmother: "What is in the wardrobe, Grandma?"
Grandma smiled and said: "Anything you believe in is in the wardrobe, Andy."
Andy puzzled over the answer, so Grandma explained further: "You can believe in the kindness of others, or helping those less fortunate than yourself. You can believe in frightening things like monsters or dragons, but you believe in them in different ways."
Andy thought about this for a moment and then asked: "What if I don't believe in anything, Grandma?"
Grandma smiled again and said: "Believing in something is very important, Andy. Believe in yourself, and always stay true to who you are."
Her words stayed with Andy for many years, and he remembered the small lesson that his grandmother had taught him. No matter what people say, believe in yourself and always stay true to who you are.

The goat walked through the woods until he saw a bright red ring. It was dangling from a tree and the goat reached for it. He was so excited! He then put the ring in his pocket and kept walking.
When he returned home, the goat was feeling even sillier. He wanted to show everyone in the village his new red ring. But when he got to the village, he noticed a strange goat standing there. It was the same goat he saw while walking in the woods!
The goat quickly realised that this was no ordinary goat. It was a magical goat! He had used his magical powers to make a red ring appear from the woods.
The goat was amazed and thanked the magical goat for his generous gift. He quickly realised that being ignorant isn't always a bad thing and that you can always learn something new if you just follow your curiosity.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, their mom asked them to make a cake for their dad, who was coming home from work. She gave them a big bowl, some eggs, some flour, some sugar, and some milk. She also gave them a pan to put the cake in.
"Can you mix everything in the bowl, please?" she asked them. "Then you can pour it in the pan and I will put it in the oven."
Ben and Lily nodded and started to work. They cracked the eggs and poured them in the bowl. They added the flour, the sugar, and the milk. They took a big spoon and stirred everything together.
"Look, mom, we made a cake batter!" Lily said proudly.
"Good job, my intelligent twins!" mom said, smiling. "Now, can you pour it in the pan carefully?"
Ben and Lily lifted the bowl and tried to pour the batter in the pan. But the bowl was too heavy and the batter was too runny. They spilled some of it on the table and on the floor.
"Oh no, we made a mess!" Ben said, worried.
"Don't worry, we can clean it up," Lily said, trying to be brave.
Mom came over and saw the spill. She was not angry. She hugged Ben and Lily and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. You did your best and I'm proud of you. Let's wipe the table and the floor and then we can put the pan in the oven."
Ben and Lily helped mom clean the kitchen. Then they watched as mom put the pan in the oven. They waited for the cake to bake, smelling the sweet aroma.
Soon, dad came home from work. He saw the cake on the table and said, "Wow, what a delicious cake! Who made it?"
Ben and Lily ran to him and said, "We made it, dad! We made it for you!"
Dad hugged them and said, "Thank you, my intelligent twins! You are so kind and thoughtful. You made me very happy."
He cut a slice of cake for each of them and they ate it together. They all agreed that it was the best cake ever. They felt very happy and loved. They welcomed dad home with a big smile.

Kaiya's mom knelt down and gave her a reassuring smile. "It's okay, sweety," she said in a soft voice. "The lecture won't be scary. You'll see!"
Kaiya nodded hesitantly and sat down. Throughout the lecture, she tried her best to pay attention, but she still felt a bit shy. 
When the lecture was over, everyone clapped and Mrs. Smart thanked everyone for coming. Kaiya wished she had been brave enough to ask a question, but she was glad that the lecture was over. 
As they left, Mrs. Smart waved goodbye to Kaiya. "You were great listening today!" she said. Kaiya smiled and waved back. Even though she was shy, she felt proud.

He decided to say sorry to his mom and dad. He decided to share his toys with Sara and Lily. He decided to be a better person.
The moral of the story is: Be polite, grateful and respectful to others. They will appreciate you and want to be your friends.

Sara and Ben were playing outside in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes.
"Look, our snowman is so happy!" Sara said.
"Yes, he is. But he might get cold soon. The weather is very icy today," Ben said.
They heard a loud noise from the street. It was a big truck with a plow. It was clearing the snow from the road.
"Oh no, the truck is coming this way!" Sara cried. "It will knock down our snowman!"
They ran to their snowman and hugged him. They hoped the truck would stop or turn away.
But the truck did not stop or turn away. It came closer and closer. It pushed the snow aside with its plow. It hit the snowman with a thud.
The snowman fell apart. His hat and scarf flew away. His carrot nose and buttons rolled on the ground.
Sara and Ben were very sad. They looked at their broken snowman.
The truck driver saw them. He stopped the truck and got out. He walked to them.
"I'm sorry, kids. I didn't see your snowman. I was just doing my job," he said.
He picked up the hat and scarf, the carrot nose and the buttons. He handed them to Sara and Ben.
"Can you fix him?" Sara asked.
"Sure, we can fix him. Let's make him again. But this time, let's make him on the sidewalk, not on the road. That way, he will be safe from the truck," he said.
He helped Sara and Ben to make a new snowman. He put the hat and scarf, the carrot nose and the buttons on him. He smiled at them.
"There, he's as good as new. And he's happy, too," he said.
Sara and Ben smiled, too. They thanked the truck driver.
"Thank you for helping us fix our snowman. You are very nice," they said.
"You're welcome, kids. Have fun, but be careful. The weather is very icy today," he said.
He got back in his truck and drove away. He waved to them.
Sara and Ben waved back. They hugged their new snowman. They were happy again.
