Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree house where they kept their toys and books. One day, they saw an enormous bird flying over their house. It had bright feathers and a long tail. They wanted to see it better, so they ran to the tree house and climbed up the ladder.
"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom said. "It is so pretty and big!"
"I wonder what it is," Lily said. "Maybe it is a parrot or a peacock."
They watched the bird for a while, until it landed on a branch near their tree house. They could hear it making loud noises.
"Hello, hello, hello!" the bird said.
Tom and Lily were surprised. The bird could talk!
"Hello, bird!" Tom said. "What is your name?"
"My name is Polly," the bird said. "I am looking for a meeting."
"A meeting?" Lily asked. "What is a meeting?"
"A meeting is when you talk to other birds and discuss things," Polly said. "I am new here and I want to make friends."
Tom and Lily thought that sounded fun. They liked to talk and discuss things too.
"Can we join your meeting?" Tom asked.
"Sorry, no," Polly said. "The meeting is only for birds. You are not birds, you are children."
Tom and Lily felt sad. They wanted to be friends with Polly, but she did not want them.
"That is not fair," Lily said. "We are nice and we like birds. Why can't we join your meeting?"
"Because you are different," Polly said. "You have no feathers, no wings, no beak. You do not belong with us."
Tom and Lily did not like that answer. They thought Polly was rude and mean.
"We are not different, we are special," Tom said. "We have hair, hands, teeth. We can do many things that birds can't."
"Like what?" Polly asked.
"Like reading, writing, drawing, singing, dancing," Lily said.
"Those are silly things," Polly said. "Birds can fly, sing, build nests, find food. Those are important things."
Tom and Lily and Polly started to argue. They did not agree on anything. They raised their voices and hurt each other's feelings.
Soon, they heard other birds coming. They were Polly's friends. They saw Tom and Lily and Polly in the tree house.
"Who are they?" one bird asked.
"They are children," Polly said. "They wanted to join our meeting, but I said no."
"Good," another bird said. "We do not like children. They are noisy and messy and scary."
The other birds agreed. They flew around the tree house and made angry sounds. They tried to scare Tom and Lily away.
Tom and Lily were scared. They did not like the other birds. They wanted to go home.
"Let's go, Lily," Tom said. "We do not want to be here."
They grabbed their toys and books and ran down the ladder. They ran to their house and closed the door.
They did not want to see Polly or the other birds again. They were not nice. They did not want to be friends.
Tom and Lily hugged each other. They were glad they had each other. They were twins and they loved each other.

"Look, look!" Tom shouted. "A comet! It is so big and shiny!"
Lila looked up and saw the comet too. It was beautiful. She wished she could touch it.
"I want to carry the comet," she said. "I want to hold it in my hands."
Tom shook his head. "You can't carry the comet, Lila. It is too far and too hot. It will burn you and hurt you."
Lila frowned. She did not like Tom's answer. She wanted to carry the comet.
"I can carry the comet," she said. "I will be careful. I will use a blanket and gloves. I will not let it burn me or hurt me."
Tom sighed. He knew Lila was stubborn. He did not want her to get hurt.
"Lila, please listen to me," he said. "You can't carry the comet. It is not a toy. It is a rock that flies very fast. It will not stay in one place. It will fly away and you will lose it."
Lila did not listen to Tom. She ran inside the house and got a blanket and gloves. She ran outside again and looked for the comet. She saw it in the sky, still bright and shiny.
She threw the blanket over her head and ran towards the comet. She stretched out her hands and tried to catch it.
But the comet was too fast and too far. Lila could not reach it. She tripped over a rock and fell to the ground. The blanket and gloves fell off her. She scraped her knee and elbow. She started to cry.
Tom ran to Lila and helped her up. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lila. I'm sorry you got hurt. I'm sorry you could not carry the comet."
Lila sniffed and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. You were right. I can't carry the comet. It is too far and too hot. It is not a toy. It is a rock that flies very fast."

One day, the ball rolled into the street. Tom and Lily ran after it, but they did not look for cars. A big car was coming fast and honked its horn. Tom and Lily were scared and stopped. The car stopped too, and a man got out. He was wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He was a cop.
The cop was angry and said, "What are you doing? You could have been hurt! You have to be careful and look both ways before you cross the street. Where are your parents?"
Tom and Lily did not know what to say. They were sorry and afraid. They looked for their mom, who was sitting on a bench nearby. She saw what happened and ran to them. She hugged them and said, "Are you okay? I'm so sorry, officer. I was watching them, but they ran away so fast. I should have been more attentive."
The cop was still angry, but he saw that the mom was sorry too. He said, "It's okay, ma'am. I'm glad they are not hurt. But you have to teach them how to be safe. The street is not a place to play. You have to use the crosswalk and wait for the green light."
The mom said, "You are right, officer. Thank you for stopping and helping us. I will talk to them and make sure they understand. Can we offer you something to drink? We have some juice and water in our bag."
The cop was surprised by the offer. He said, "That's very kind of you, ma'am. But I have to go back to work. I have to catch bad guys and keep people safe. Maybe another time."
The mom said, "Okay, officer. Thank you again. Have a good day."
The cop said, "You're welcome, ma'am. Have a good day too. And remember, be careful."
He got back in his car and drove away. Tom and Lily waved goodbye to him. They learned a lesson that day. They never ran into the street again. They always looked both ways and used the crosswalk. They also learned that cops are not always scary. Sometimes they are nice and helpful. And sometimes they have unusual offers.

One day, Tim and Spot were playing in the park when the wind blew the flag far away. Spot could not see it anymore. He started to worry. "Oh no! Where is my flag?" Spot said. Tim saw Spot's worry and said, "Don't worry, Spot. We will find your flag."
They looked and looked until they found the flag stuck in a tree. Tim climbed the tree and got the flag. He gave it back to Spot, who was very happy. "Thank you, Tim!" Spot said. "You are my best friend."
The moral of the story is that friends help each other when they are worried or in need. And with loyal friends, there is no need to worry.

One day, a farmer who had an ordinary farm went out to supply food for his sheep. He loaded the wagon and drove away. 
After a while, the farmer stopped the wagon at a river and let the sheep out to graze. He sat quietly and suddenly heard a voice. It said, “My, what ordinary sheep those are!”
The farmer turned and saw a lion standing behind him. It had the biggest teeth he had ever seen! He immediately stood still in fear.
The lion looked at the farmer and said, “I could easily make a meal out of your ordinary sheep.”
The farmer said quickly, “Please don’t eat my sheep. We all have to use the world’s resources in fair and loving ways.”
The lion smiled and nodded. He said, “You’re right, farmer. We must supply the world’s resources to everyone.”
The farmer thanked the lion and watched as it walked away. 
Moral of the story: We must share the world’s resources in a fair and loving way.

He ran and jumped on the box. Crash! The box broke open and many colorful balls came out. Tom and Max were so happy and started to play with the balls.
But then, something unexpected happened. The balls started to move on their own! Tom and Max were surprised. The balls were magic! They could talk and play with Tom and Max. Now, Tom and Max had many new friends to play with. The poor little cat and the big dog were not lonely anymore. They all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They saw a big house with a fence and a gate. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Let's go there," Ben said. "Maybe they have toys and candy."
"No, Ben, that's not our house. That's a rich house. We can't go there," Lily said.
But Ben did not listen. He ran to the gate and opened it. He saw a pool with blue water and a fountain. He was thirsty and wanted to drink some water.
He ran to the pool and leaned over the edge. But he slipped and fell into the water. He could not swim and he was scared. He shouted for help.
Lily heard him and ran to the pool. She saw Ben in the water and tried to reach him. But she was too small and the pool was too deep. She cried and called for help too.
A man came out of the house and saw the children. He was angry and scared. He ran to the pool and pulled Ben out of the water. He was wet and cold and he coughed.
The man called an ambulance on his phone. He told the children to stay on the grass and wait. He said they were naughty and they should not have come to his house.
Soon, the ambulance came with a siren and a light. Two people came out of the ambulance and looked at Ben. They put a blanket on him and a mask on his face. They said he needed to go to the hospital.
They put Ben on a stretcher and took him to the ambulance. Lily followed them and wanted to go with Ben. She was sorry and scared.
"Can I go with him?" she asked.
"Yes, you can. But you have to be quiet and sit still," one of the people said.
They let Lily sit next to Ben in the ambulance. They closed the door and drove away.
Lily held Ben's hand and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I hope you get better soon."

One day, a boy came to the garden. He saw the cauliflower and said, "Why are you confused, cauliflower?" The cauliflower said, "I want to raise my leaves, but I don't know how."
The boy thought for a moment. He had an idea. He said, "Cauliflower, I will help you raise your leaves." The boy started to sing a happy song. The cauliflower liked the song so much that it raised its leaves high.
But then, something unexpected happened. The cauliflower started to grow bigger and bigger. The boy was surprised. He said, "Wow, I didn't know my song could do that!"
The big cauliflower smiled. It was not confused anymore. The boy and the cauliflower became good friends. They played and laughed in the garden every day.

Tom and Lily were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the water and the fish and the birds. One day, the boat stopped at a port. The port had many other boats and people and shops.
"Can we go see the port, mom?" Tom asked.
"Yes, we can go for a little while. But we have to be back before the boat leaves," mom said.
Tom and Lily were happy. They put on their hats and shoes and followed mom and dad to the port. They saw many things. They saw a big fish that someone caught. They saw a man who played music with a guitar. They saw a lady who sold ice cream.
"I want ice cream, mom," Lily said.
"Me too, me too," Tom said.
Mom looked at her watch. "Okay, we have time for one ice cream each. But then we have to go back to the boat. It will leave soon."
Mom bought two ice creams, one for Tom and one for Lily. They licked their ice creams and smiled.
But then, Tom saw something else. He saw a toy store. The toy store had many toys. He saw a car, a ball, a doll, a train. He wanted them all.
"Mom, can I have a toy?" Tom asked.
"No, Tom, you can't. You already have an ice cream. And we have to go back to the boat. It will leave very soon," mom said.
But Tom did not listen. He was selfish. He wanted a toy. He ran to the toy store. He grabbed a car. He did not pay.
"Tom, come back!" mom shouted.
"Tom, that's bad!" Lily said.
But Tom did not hear. He ran with the car.
A man saw Tom. The man worked at the toy store. He was angry. He ran after Tom.
"Hey, you, stop! That's my car!" the man shouted.
Tom was scared. He dropped the car. He ran back to mom and dad and Lily.
But it was too late. The boat had left. They missed the boat.
Mom and dad were sad. Lily was sad. Tom was sad.
He wished he had not been selfish. He wished he had listened to mom. He wished he had not taken the car.
He felt bad. He said sorry to mom and dad and Lily. He said sorry to the man.
The man was kind. He forgave Tom. He gave him back the car.
But they still had to wait for another boat. They had to wait a long time.
Tom learned a lesson. He learned to not be selfish. He learned to listen to mom. He learned to not take things that are not his.
He hugged mom and dad and Lily. He hugged the car.
He hoped they would see the water and the fish and the birds again. He hoped they would have fun on the next boat. He hoped they would not miss the port.

"Why are you running around with a stick? What are you looking for?"
John was embarrassed and he said nothing. The old man smiled and said:
"I think you are looking for something special. Is it really worth looking for a stick?"
John thought about it for a moment and realized the old man is right. He thanked the man and returned the stick to the ground.
The old man shook his head and said:
"If you are looking for something special, maybe you should look somewhere else. Sometimes if you want something special, you have to do something special."
John thanked the old man and walked away, thinking about the old man's words. He realized that looking for something special is not always easy. John was now determined to search for something special and he knew exactly where to look.

Anna likes to hop. She hops in the morning, she hops at noon, she hops at night. She hops on the bed, she hops on the couch, she hops on the floor. She hops when she is happy, she hops when she is sad, she hops when she is bored.
One day, Anna hops too much. She hops on the table, she hops on the chair, she hops on the cabinet. The cabinet is high and big. It has many things inside. Anna wants to see what is inside. She hops on the cabinet and opens the door.
"Wow!" Anna says. She sees many shiny things. She sees cups and plates and spoons and forks. She sees a big cake with candles. She sees a card with her name. She sees a present with a bow. She thinks it is for her. She is very happy. She hops on the cabinet and reaches for the cake.
"Anna, no!" Mommy says. She comes into the kitchen and sees Anna on the cabinet. She is angry and scared. She runs to the cabinet and grabs Anna. She puts her down on the floor. She closes the cabinet door.
"Anna, you are naughty!" Mommy says. "You cannot hop on the cabinet. You can fall and hurt yourself. You can break the things inside. You can ruin the cake. The cake is for your birthday. The present is for you too. But you have to wait until the party. You have to be quiet and good."
Anna feels sorry. She did not know it was her birthday. She did not know the cake and the present were for her. She did not mean to be naughty. She hugs Mommy and says, "I am sorry, Mommy. I love you. I will not hop on the cabinet again. I will be quiet and good. Can I still have the cake and the present?"
Mommy smiles and hugs Anna back. She says, "I love you too, Anna. I am glad you are sorry. You can still have the cake and the present. But you have to wait until the party. The party will start soon. You can hop with your friends and have fun. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Okay?"
Anna nods and says, "Okay, Mommy. Thank you. I am excited for the party. I will hop with my friends and have fun. But I will be careful and listen to you. I promise."
Mommy kisses Anna and says, "You are welcome, Anna. You are a good girl. Happy birthday, my hoppy bunny."

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. One day, they saw a big truck parked next to their fence. The truck had a ladder and a hose and a shiny badge. It was a fire truck.
Lily and Max wanted to see the fire truck up close. They thought it was impressive and cool. They ran to the fence and looked at the truck. They saw some firemen wearing helmets and boots. They waved at them and said hello.
One of the firemen saw them and smiled. He walked to the fence and said, "Hi, kids. Do you like our truck?" Lily and Max nodded and said yes. They asked him what he was doing. He said, "We are here to check the fire hydrant. We need to make sure it works well in case there is a fire."
He pointed to a big metal thing on the sidewalk. It had a cap and a valve and a spout. He said, "That's the fire hydrant. We use it to get water for our hose. We can spray the water on the fire and put it out."
Lily and Max thought that was amazing. They wanted to see how the fire hydrant worked. They asked the fireman if they could help him. He said, "Sorry, kids. This is not a toy. It is very powerful and dangerous. You have to stay away from it. It is not safe for you."
Lily and Max felt sad and curious. They wanted to touch the fire hydrant and see the water. They did not listen to the fireman. They waited until he was busy with his tools. Then they sneaked to the sidewalk and ran to the fire hydrant.
They tried to turn the valve and open the cap. They used all their strength and pushed and pulled. They did not know that the fire hydrant was very strong and tight. They did not know that the firemen had a special wrench to open it.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and felt a splash. The cap flew off and the water gushed out. The water was very fast and hard. It hit Lily and Max and knocked them down. It soaked their clothes and hair and shoes. It flooded the street and the yard and the truck.
Lily and Max screamed and cried. They were scared and wet and cold. The fireman heard them and ran to them. He turned off the valve and stopped the water. He picked them up and carried them to the fence. He checked them for injuries and wrapped them in blankets.
He was angry and worried. He said, "What were you thinking, kids? You could have been hurt or worse. You did not listen to me. You did not stay safe. You were very naughty and foolish."
Lily and Max felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We're sorry, mister. We wanted to see the water. We thought it would be fun. We did not mean to cause trouble."
The fireman sighed and said, "I know, kids. But you have to learn to follow the rules. The rules are there to protect you and others. You have to respect the fire hydrant and the fire truck. They are not for playing. They are for saving lives."
He gave them a hug and said, "I'm glad you're okay. But don't ever do that again. Promise me." Lily and Max nodded and said, "We promise, mister. We learned our lesson. We will be good and safe from now on."
The fireman smiled and said, "That's good. Now go inside and get dry and warm. And say sorry to your mom and dad. They must be worried about you." Lily and Max said, "Okay, mister. Thank you for saving us. And sorry for making a mess." They ran to their house and said goodbye to the fireman.
The fireman waved and said, "You're welcome, kids. And goodbye. Be careful and have fun." He went back to his truck and finished his job. He hoped that Lily and Max would remember their mistake and never repeat it. He hoped that they would grow up to be smart and brave and kind. He hoped that they would always be safe.

The next day, the big truck came back. This time, it had a big box. The big box had a big surprise. The new squash was right. The big surprise was new seeds for the garden. The new squash was happy it could speak and help its friends. Now, the garden would have more squash friends and they could all play together.

But when Tim went home, he felt cold and sad without his jacket. He missed it very much. The next day, he tried to find the man to get his jacket back, but the man was gone. Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big box of labels. The labels have different words and pictures on them.
"Look, Lily, we can use these labels to teach each other new things!" Tom says. He picks up a label that says "apple" and has a red fruit on it. He sticks it on a real apple on the table. "This is an apple. It is red and sweet. Can you say apple?"
"Apple!" Lily repeats. She smiles and claps her hands. She picks up another label that says "dog" and has a brown animal on it. She sticks it on a stuffed dog on the floor. "This is a dog. It is brown and furry. It can bark and run. Can you say dog?"
"Dog!" Tom repeats. He nods and hugs the stuffed dog. He likes dogs. He picks up another label that says "intelligent" and has a star on it. He sticks it on Lily's shirt. "This is intelligent. It means you are smart and learn fast. You are intelligent, Lily. Can you say intelligent?"
Lily looks at the label and frowns. She does not know what it means. She tries to say it, but it is hard. "In-tel-li-gent?" She stutters.
Tom laughs and says, "Yes, that's right. You are intelligent, Lily. And so am I. We are both intelligent, because we like to teach and learn new things. That is a good thing to be. Can you say good?"
"Good!" Lily says. She smiles and sticks the label on Tom's shirt. "You are good, Tom. And so am I. We are both good, because we are kind and helpful. That is a good thing to be. Can you say kind?"
"Kind!" Tom says. He smiles and gives Lily a high-five. "You are kind, Lily. And so am I. We are both kind, because we share and care. That is a good thing to be. Can you say share?"
"Share!" Lily says. She looks at the box of labels and says, "Let's share these labels with our other friends. Maybe they want to learn new things too. Do you want to share, Tom?"
"Yes, I want to share, Lily. Sharing is fun and fair. Let's go and find our other friends. Maybe they have some labels for us too. Come on, Lily, let's go!"
Tom and Lily take the box of labels and run to the playground. They find their other friends and show them the labels. They teach and learn new things together. They are intelligent, good and kind. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big slide and wanted to try it. Lily went first. She climbed up the steps and slid down fast. She laughed and said, "That was fun!"
Tom followed her. He was not afraid of the slide. He wanted to show Lily how brave he was. He climbed up the steps and slid down faster. He shouted, "Look at me!"
But Tom slid too fast. He did not stop at the end of the slide. He flew off and landed on the grass. He hurt his arm and cried, "Ow, ow, ow!"
Lily ran to him. She saw his arm was red and swollen. She said, "Tom, you need help. I will save you."
She helped him stand up and hugged him. She said, "Don't worry, Tom. We will find a grown-up. They will make your arm better."
They walked to the bench where their mom was sitting. She saw Tom's arm and said, "Oh, Tom, what happened?"
Lily told her what happened. She said, "I saved Tom. He slid too fast and hurt his arm."
Mom said, "You are a good friend, Lily. You did the right thing. Tom, you are lucky to have Lily. She has a big heart and a strong muscle."
Tom said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend, too. You have a kind heart and an interesting muscle."
Mom smiled and said, "You both have good hearts and interesting muscles. But next time, be careful on the slide. It is fun, but it can be dangerous, too."
Lily and Tom nodded. They learned their lesson. They said, "We will be careful, Mom. We love you."
Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, too. Now let's go to the doctor and fix your arm, Tom."
They went to the doctor and Tom's arm was fixed. He felt better and said, "Sorry, Lily. I was silly. I wanted to show you how brave I was. But I was not brave. I was foolish."
Lily said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. You are brave, but you don't have to show off. You are my friend, and I like you for who you are."
Tom said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my friend, too. And I like you for who you are."
They hugged and smiled. They were happy and grateful. They had good hearts and interesting muscles. And they had each other.

Sam looked at his car and saw that it was wet and not beeping anymore. He felt sad and angry.
"Lily, you broke my car!" Sam shouted. "Now it can't roll or beep! You are a bad friend!"
Lily felt ashamed and sorry. She didn't mean to break Sam's car. She wanted to help him.
"I'm sorry, Sam!" Lily said, with tears in her eyes. "I didn't want to break your car. I wanted to add fuel. Can we fix it?"
Sam looked at Lily and saw that she was crying. He felt sorry too. He knew that Lily was not a bad friend. She made a mistake.
"It's okay, Lily!" Sam said, hugging her. "Maybe we can fix it. Or we can play with something else. We are still friends!"

Mira was sad and angry. She wanted to get their ball back. She did not believe that Mr. Brown was so mean. She thought that Leo was being a coward. She decided to go to Mr. Brown's yard by herself. She waited until Leo went inside, then she climbed over the fence.

Mr. Brown nodded and smiled.

He saw that Mr. Brown was not mean or scary. He saw that he was old and lonely, but also kind and gentle. He saw that he was a good neighbor and a good friend.

Mia liked to polish her rocks. She had many rocks of different colors and shapes. She found them in the park, in the yard, and sometimes in her pockets. She used a soft cloth and some water to make them shiny and smooth.
One day, she found a very special rock. It was white and sparkly, and it had many tiny bits inside. She thought it was the prettiest rock she ever saw. She ran to show it to her mom.
"Look, Mom, look what I found!" she said, holding the rock in her hand.
"Oh, Mia, that's a beautiful rock!" her mom said. "Do you know what it is?"
Mia shook her head. She did not know.
"It's a mineral, Mia. A mineral is a kind of rock that has special things inside. Some minerals are very rare and valuable. Do you want to polish it?"
Mia nodded. She wanted to polish her mineral and make it even more pretty. She followed her mom to the sink, where they got some water and a cloth.
But as Mia started to polish her mineral, something strange happened. The white and sparkly part started to dissolve in the water, and the tiny bits inside fell out. Mia gasped. Her mineral was gone!
"Mia, I'm sorry, but your mineral was not a real mineral. It was a fake one, made of sugar and glitter. Someone must have left it in the park as a joke. It looked pretty, but it was not strong or lasting."
Mia felt sad and angry. She wanted her mineral back. She did not like jokes like that.
"Mom, who did this? Why did they do this?" she asked.
"I don't know, Mia. Maybe they wanted to have some fun, or maybe they wanted to trick someone. But they were not very nice or smart. They wasted their sugar and glitter, and they made you unhappy. You know what, Mia? You don't need fake minerals. You have many real rocks that are much more pretty and interesting. Why don't we polish them together, and learn more about them?"
Mia smiled. She liked that idea. She still missed her mineral, but she knew her mom was right. She had many real rocks that she loved, and she wanted to polish them and make them shine. She hugged her mom, and they went to polish her rocks. Mia learned that real rocks were better than fake minerals, and that polish could not hide the truth.

Lily and Ben liked to play with rods. They had many rods of different colors and sizes. They used the rods to make shapes, towers, bridges, and animals. One day, they found a big rod that was shiny and had a button on it.
"Wow, look at this rod!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and cool. What do you think it does?"
"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is a magic rod. Let's press the button and see."
They pressed the button and the rod made a loud noise. Then it started to grow longer and longer. It increased so much that it reached the ceiling and the walls.
"Wow, it is a magic rod!" Lily said. "It can increase and make things bigger. Let's make our toys bigger too."
They put their toys near the rod and pressed the button again. The toys also increased and became as big as the rod. They had a giant teddy bear, a giant ball, a giant car, and a giant doll.
"This is so fun!" Ben said. "We have the biggest toys in the world. Let's play with them."
They played with their big toys for a while. They hugged the teddy bear, bounced the ball, drove the car, and dressed the doll. They had a lot of fun.
But they did not notice that the rod was still increasing. It pushed the ceiling and the walls harder and harder. It made cracks and holes in the house. It was too strong and too big.

“Lets try to climb the olive tree,” said Lola excitedly.
“Ok,” said Milo, “I’ll give it a try”.
So both cats started to climb up the tree. After a few minutes, Milo had managed to reach the top of the tree. But Lola was still struggling halfway up. 
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was an old car driving towards them. The cats froze in fear.
The car stopped. The driver, an old man, saw the cats in the tree. He climbed out of his car and said: “You two look very brave. Climb down and I’ll drive you home safely. I promise I’ll be very careful”.
The cats were so happy that they ran back down the tree and into the car. The old man drove them home safely.
The cats thanked the old man for his kindness and waved goodbye as he drove away. From that day on, they never forgot the big olive tree and their happy adventure.

Mom smiled and said, "I have a surprise for you, Lily. Come with me to the living room." Lily followed her mom, hoping to see her book.
In the living room, Lily saw a big box with a bow on it. Mom said, "This is for you, Lily. Happy birthday!" Lily was happy. It was her birthday and she had forgotten. She opened the box and saw many things: a doll, a puzzle, a ball, and a hat. But she did not see her book.
She looked at her mom and said, "Thank you, Mom, but where is my orange book?" Mom winked and said, "Look behind the couch, Lily. There is one more thing for you." Lily ran to the couch and looked behind it. She saw her orange book, but it was not alone. Next to it was a small, furry, orange kitten. The kitten meowed and licked Lily's hand. Lily was very happy. She picked up the book and the kitten and hugged them. She said, "Thank you, Mom, this is the best birthday ever! I love my orange book and my orange cat!"
Mom hugged Lily and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I knew you liked orange things. I saw you reading your book every day, so I thought you would like a friend who looks like it. I hope you will take good care of your cat and your book."
Lily nodded and said, "I will, Mom. I will read my book to my cat and play with him. What is his name?"
Mom said, "You can name him whatever you want, Lily. It's your cat."
Lily thought for a moment and said, "I will name him Leo, like the lion in my book. He is brave and strong and orange, like Leo."
Mom smiled and said, "That's a good name, Lily. I'm sure Leo will love you and your book. Now, let's have some cake and celebrate your birthday."
Lily, Mom, and Leo went to the kitchen and had cake and ice cream. Lily was very happy. She had her orange book, her orange cat, and her mom. She thought it was the best day ever.

Tom did not want to share. He said, "No, Lily, this is my banana. Go away." He held the banana tight.
Lily was angry. She said, "Tom, you are mean. You are a bad brother." She slapped Tom on the face.
Tom was surprised. He felt pain. He dropped the banana. He cried.
Lily picked up the banana. She said, "Ha, ha, now it's mine." She peeled the banana. She saw that it was orange inside. She said, "Yuck, this banana is bad. It is not yellow. It is orange." She threw the banana away.
Tom stopped crying. He saw the orange banana. He said, "Lily, you are silly. That is not a banana. That is a plantain. You can't eat it raw. You have to cook it."
Lily felt silly. She said, "Oh, I didn't know. I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry I slapped you. I'm sorry I took your banana."
Tom said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry I didn't share. I'm sorry I was mean. Do you want to hug?"
Lily said, "Yes, Tom, I want to hug." They hugged.
Mom came in. She saw them hug. She said, "What a nice hug. What are you doing?"
Tom said, "We are hugging. We are sorry. We fought over a plantain."
Mom said, "A plantain? That's funny. Do you want to try a real banana? I have some in the kitchen. They are yellow and sweet."
Tom and Lily said, "Yes, Mom, we want to try a real banana. Thank you, Mom."
They went to the kitchen. They ate a real banana. They liked it. They were happy. They did not fight anymore.

Tom and Lily nod. They learned their lesson. They do not eat mint again. They only smell it.

Tom and Mia are friends who like to play music. Tom has a drum and Mia has a flute. They make sounds with their instruments and try to match the rhythm. Rhythm is when sounds go fast or slow, loud or soft, together or apart.
One day, they go to the park and see a big tree. The tree has rough bark and many branches. Tom and Mia think it is a good place to play music. They sit under the tree and start to play. But they do not pay attention to the rhythm. Tom plays his drum very fast and loud, and Mia plays her flute very slow and soft. They do not listen to each other or the tree.
The tree does not like their music. It thinks it is noisy and messy. It wants them to stop. It tries to tell them by shaking its leaves and making wind. But Tom and Mia do not notice. They keep playing their own way.
The tree gets angry and yawns. It yawns so big and loud that it makes a hole in the ground. Tom and Mia fall into the hole and drop their instruments. They are scared and confused. They look up and see the tree's face. The tree says, "Why did you play such bad music? You did not follow the rhythm. You did not respect me or each other. You made me yawn and open the hole. Now you are stuck here until you learn your lesson."
Tom and Mia feel sorry and ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, tree. We did not mean to upset you. We were not careful with our music. We did not listen to you or each other. We did not follow the rhythm. Please forgive us and let us out."
The tree says, "I will forgive you and let you out, but only if you promise to play better music. You have to listen to each other and the rhythm. You have to be gentle and kind with your instruments and the tree. You have to make harmony, not noise."
Tom and Mia agree and promise. They pick up their instruments and try to play together. They listen to the tree's wind and leaves and match the rhythm. They play their drum and flute fast and slow, loud and soft, together and apart. They make beautiful music that the tree likes. The tree smiles and closes the hole. It lets them out and says, "Well done, Tom and Mia. You have learned your lesson. You have played good music. You have followed the rhythm. You have respected me and each other. You have made harmony, not noise. You are welcome to play under my tree anytime."
Tom and Mia thank the tree and hug it. They are happy and proud. They have made a new friend and learned a new skill. They have learned the value of rhythm, harmony, and respect. They go home and tell their parents about their adventure. They say, "We love music and we love the tree. We will always follow the rhythm and make harmony, not noise."

"Are you OK?" Mom asks.
"Yes, we are OK. But that was scary," Tom says.

"It's OK, Tom. But next time, let me sit in the front. I weigh less than you," Lily says.

"OK, let's go to the slide. But this time, we take turns," Tom and Lily say.

"Maybe it is a ring for a giant," Sara said.
"Maybe it is a wheel for a very old car," Ben said.
They wanted to keep it, but they did not know how to share it. They both grabbed it and pulled.
"Give it to me!" Sara demanded.
"No, it is mine!" Ben demanded.
They pulled and pulled, but the shiny thing did not move. It was stuck in the sand. They pulled harder and harder, but the shiny thing did not budge. They pulled so hard that they fell down.
They looked up and saw a man standing over them. He had a hat and a coat and a big bag. He smiled and said, "Hello, children. Do you know what you have found?"
Sara and Ben shook their heads.
"This is a very special thing," the man said. "It is an ancient coin. It is very old and very rare. It comes from a far away land. It is part of the earth's history."
Sara and Ben were amazed. They had never seen a coin like that before. They felt sorry for fighting over it.
"Can we see it?" Sara asked.
"Of course," the man said. He took a tool from his bag and gently dug out the coin. He cleaned it with a cloth and showed it to them. It was shiny and beautiful.
"Wow," Ben said.
The man told them stories about the coin and the land it came from. He said he was a collector and a teacher. He said he loved to find ancient things and learn about them.
Sara and Ben listened and learned. They forgot about their fight. They thanked the man for showing them the coin and telling them the stories. They asked if they could keep the coin.
The man smiled and said, "No, children. This coin belongs to a museum. It is too precious to keep. But I will give you something else. Something you can share and enjoy."
He reached into his bag and took out two small toys. They were cars, but not like the ones Sara and Ben had. They were very old and very rare. They had strange marks on them, just like the coin.
"These are ancient toys," the man said. "They come from the same land as the coin. They are part of the earth's history, too. They are for you, Sara and Ben. A gift for finding the coin and being curious and kind."
Sara and Ben were delighted. They thanked the man again and hugged him. They took the toys and played with them in the sand. They made roads and bridges and towns. They shared and smiled and had fun.
They learned that ancient things are not only shiny and rare, but also interesting and valuable. They learned that the earth has many stories to tell, and that they can discover them if they look and listen. They learned that sharing is better than demanding, and that kindness is better than fighting. They learned a lot that day, Sara and Ben. And they had a lot of fun, too.

The little boy loved to count and play in the sand. He was so happy that he had the spade and could make the piles so neat and organized. He smiled and thanked his mommy for teaching him how to count.

"Look what I printed!" he said proudly.
The little one looked and was devastated. The picture was all wrong. Instead of the beautiful flower, it was all blurry and smudged. Daddy had printed it badly.
The 3-year-old started to cry. No matter how hard Daddy tried, he could not make it right again.

Once upon a time, there was a clean town. In this town, a big pot was always full of soup. Everyone in the town could eat from the pot. They took turns to stir the soup.
One day, a thief came to the town. He saw the big pot of soup and wanted it all for himself. He thought of a plan to take the soup away when no one was looking.
The thief started to stir the soup, just like the people in the town did. But something unexpected happened. As he stirred the soup, he felt happy and warm. The soup made him feel good and he did not want to take it away anymore.
The thief changed his mind and did not steal the soup. Instead, he stayed in the town and helped the people stir the soup every day. The thief became a good friend to everyone in the town.
From that day on, the town was even more clean and happy. The people and the thief all took turns to stir the soup and shared it with each other. They all lived happily ever after.

Lily liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a big bear. She called him Bobo. Bobo was soft and brown and had a red bow. Lily hugged Bobo every night.
One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we have to go to the office. I have to give a file to my boss. Can you come with me?" Lily nodded. She liked to go to the office. She liked to see the people and the computers and the papers. She took Bobo with her.
At the office, Lily's mom gave her a file. She said, "Lily, can you hold this file for me? I have to talk to my boss for a minute. Don't lose it, okay?" Lily said, "Okay, mom." She held the file. It was big and blue and had many papers inside. She wondered what was in the file.
Lily saw a boy sitting at a desk. He was playing with a car. He looked at Lily and smiled. He said, "Hi, I'm Ben. What's your name?" Lily said, "I'm Lily. This is Bobo." She showed him her bear. Ben said, "Wow, Bobo is cool. Can I see him?" Lily said, "Sure." She gave him Bobo. Ben hugged Bobo. He said, "He's so soft and nice. Can I have him?" Lily said, "No, he's mine. He's my favorite toy." Ben said, "Please, can I have him? I'll give you my car. It's fast and shiny. It's my favorite toy." Lily looked at the car. It was fast and shiny. She liked cars. She said, "Okay, you can have Bobo. I'll take your car." She gave him the file. She took the car.
Lily's mom came back. She said, "Lily, are you ready to go?" Lily said, "Yes, mom. Look, I have a car. Ben gave it to me. He's my friend." Lily's mom said, "That's nice, Lily. But where is the file? And where is Bobo?" Lily said, "I gave them to Ben. He wanted Bobo. He gave me his car." Lily's mom said, "Oh, Lily, you can't do that. The file is very important. It has my work in it. And Bobo is your toy. You can't just give him away. You have to ask me first." Lily said, "But I like the car. And Ben likes Bobo. We made a trade. We're happy." Lily's mom said, "Lily, I'm sorry, but you have to give the car back to Ben. And you have to get the file and Bobo back. It's not fair to Ben or to me. You have to accept that." Lily said, "But mom, I don't want to. I like the car. And Ben likes Bobo. Why can't we keep them?" Lily's mom said, "Because it's not right, Lily. You have to learn to share and to respect other people's things. Come on, let's go talk to Ben and his mom. Maybe we can find a way to make everyone happy." Lily said, "Okay, mom. But I still like the car." She followed her mom. She hoped Ben would still be her friend. She hoped Bobo would still be her favorite toy.

Lily and Tom are friends. They live on a farm with many animals. They like to play and help on the farm.
One day, they see a big cake on the table. It smells good and looks yummy. They want to eat some cake.
"Can we have some cake, please?" they ask Mom.
"Not now, my dears. The cake is for later. We have guests coming soon. You can have some cake after dinner. Now go and play outside," Mom says.
Lily and Tom go outside. But they still think about the cake. They are hungry and curious.
They see a clever fox near the farm. The fox is hungry too. He sees the cake on the table. He wants to eat some cake.
"Hello, little ones. Do you want to play a game with me?" the fox says.
"What game?" Lily and Tom ask.
"It's a fun game. I will tell you a secret. If you guess the secret, you can have some cake. If you don't guess the secret, I can have some cake. Do you want to play?" the fox says.
Lily and Tom nod. They like games. They want to know the secret. They want to eat some cake.
"OK, here is the secret. It is something that is big and round and sweet and has many colors. What is it?" the fox says.
Lily and Tom think hard. They look around. They see the sun, the sky, the flowers, the fruits. But none of them is big and round and sweet and has many colors.
They don't know the answer. They shake their heads.
"Ha ha, you don't know the secret. The secret is the cake. The cake is big and round and sweet and has many colors. Now I can have some cake. Bye bye, little ones," the fox says.
He runs to the table. He jumps on the table. He bites the cake.
But Mom sees the fox. She is angry. She shouts at the fox. She chases the fox away.
"Go away, you naughty fox. You can't eat our cake. That cake is for our guests. And for Lily and Tom. They are good children. They waited for the cake. They deserve some cake. Come here, my dears. You can have some cake now," Mom says.
Lily and Tom are happy. They run to Mom. They hug Mom. They thank Mom.
They eat some cake. The cake is delicious. They share some cake with the animals. The animals are happy too.
They learn a lesson. They don't trust the clever fox. They listen to Mom. They enjoy the farm.

Tim had a friend named Sally. Sally liked to play with her toy ball too. They would play together and have lots of fun.
One day, Tim and Sally were playing with their toy balls when they saw a big, shiny star. The star was very pretty. "Look, Sally!" said Tim. "Let's go see the star!" Sally agreed, and they walked towards the star.
As they got closer, the star started to speak. "Hello, Tim and Sally," said the star. "I see you like to squeeze your toy balls. If you both squeeze your balls at the same time, something special will happen!" Tim and Sally looked at each other and decided to try it. They both squeezed their toy balls, and suddenly, the universe became even cleaner and more beautiful!
The star smiled and said, "Thank you, Tim and Sally. By working together, you made the universe a better place." Tim and Sally learned that working together can make a big difference. From that day on, they always played and worked together, making the universe cleaner and happier for everyone.

"Who left these mints here?" Lila asks.
"I don't know. Maybe someone forgot them," Tom says.
"Can we have some? They look yummy," Lila says.
Tom nods. He opens the jar and takes a mint. He gives one to Lila too. They put the mints in their mouths. They are sweet and cool.
"Mmm, these are good," Tom says.
"Yes, they are," Lila agrees.
They take some more mints and put them in their pockets. They want to save them for later. They close the jar and leave it on the bench. They run to the slide and have fun.
Soon, a man comes to the bench. He is looking for his jar of mints. He is sad. He needs the mints for his bad breath. He has a meeting with his boss. He looks around and sees the jar. He is happy. He picks it up and opens it. He is shocked. The jar is almost empty. There are only a few mints left.
"Hey, who took my mints?" he shouts.
Lila and Tom hear him. They feel guilty. They know they did something wrong. They go to the man and say sorry.
"We are sorry, mister. We took your mints. We didn't know they were yours. We thought they were for everyone," Lila says.
"Yeah, we are sorry. We didn't mean to make you sad. Here, you can have our mints. We have some in our pockets," Tom says.
They give the man their mints. The man is surprised. He sees that they are honest and kind. He smiles.
"Thank you, kids. That is very helpful of you. You are good friends. I forgive you. You can keep some mints for yourselves. But next time, don't take things that are not yours, okay?" he says.
"Okay, mister. We understand. We won't do it again. Thank you for being nice," Lila and Tom say.
They hug the man and say goodbye. They go back to the park and share the mints. They are happy. They learned a lesson. The end.

Lily says, "We need a bottle and some water. I have a bottle here. You can fill it with water from the tap. Then we can give it to Anna and show her how to drink."
Ben says, "OK, Lily, I will fill the bottle with water. You hold Anna and make her sit up."
Ben goes to the tap and fills the bottle with water. He comes back to Lily and gives her the bottle. Lily holds Anna and makes her sit up. She puts the bottle to Anna's mouth and says, "Look, Anna, this is a bottle. It has water inside. Water is good for you. You can drink it like this. See, Lily and Ben drink water from the bottle. You can do it too. Try it, Anna, try it."
Lily and Ben drink some water from the bottle and then give it to Anna. They watch Anna and wait for her to drink. Anna does not drink. She just looks at the bottle and makes a funny face.
Lily and Ben are confused. They wonder why Anna does not drink. They try to make her drink again and again. They say, "Come on, Anna, drink, drink, drink. It is easy. It is fun. It is good for you. Drink, drink, drink."
But Anna still does not drink. She just shakes her head and says, "No, no, no. I don't want to drink. I don't like water. I don't like bottle. I want milk. I want mommy. Mommy, mommy, mommy."
Lily and Ben are surprised. They did not know that Anna can talk. They did not know that Anna wants milk and mommy. They feel sorry for Anna. They say, "Oh, Anna, we are sorry. We did not know that you want milk and mommy. We were trying to teach you how to drink from a bottle. We thought you would like it. We are sorry. We are your friends. We want you to be happy."
Anna looks at Lily and Ben. She sees that they are sorry and that they are her friends. She smiles and says, "It's OK, Lily and Ben. I know you are my friends. I know you want me to be happy. Thank you for trying to teach me. But I don't need a bottle. I have a mommy. She gives me milk. I love milk. I love mommy. Mommy, mommy, mommy."
Lily and Ben smile too. They hug Anna and say, "We love you, Anna. We are happy that you have a mommy. We are happy that you love milk. We are happy that you can talk. You are a good baby doll. You are a good friend."
The end.

Mia tries to help him. She pulls the stick with Tom, but it does not move. They pull harder and harder, but the stick is still tight. They start to cry.
"Hey, what are you doing?" They hear a voice behind them. It is their big brother, Sam. He sees the stick and the hole and smiles. "You are silly. That is not a hole. That is a snake's home. The snake is holding the stick with its mouth. That is why it is tight."
Tom and Mia are scared. They let go of the stick and run away from the rock. Sam laughs and follows them. He picks up the stick and shakes it. The snake lets go and slithers away. Sam throws the stick in the creek and runs after Tom and Mia. He hugs them and says, "Don't worry. The snake is not bad. It just wanted to keep its home. Next time, let's measure something else, OK?"

The little girl squinted her eyes and looked close. Suddenly, she saw it: a little baby duckling, waddling around all alone. The girl gasped in delight, and started to urge Daddy to get the little duckling. "It looks so cute, Daddy! Let's get it!"
However, Daddy shook his head. "No way, silly," he said. "We can't just take it away from its mommy. We have to let nature do its work."
The little girl pouted and sighed, disappointed. However, Daddy patted her head and said, "Don't worry, honey. I'm sure if we come back tomorrow, the baby duckling will have grown a bit bigger."
The little girl nodded her head and smiled, content with Daddy's suggestion. The two of them left the park, eagerly awaiting their next visit.

Lily was a little otter who liked to play in the river with her friends. One day, she saw a big fish swimming near the bank. She wanted to catch it and share it with her friends. She prepared to jump on the fish, but then she heard a loud splash.
"Who are you?" Lily asked, turning around. She saw an unknown otter who was bigger and darker than her. He had a scar on his nose and a mean look in his eyes.
"I am Rex, and this is my river. You are not welcome here. Go away, or I will bite you!" the unknown otter said, showing his sharp teeth.
Lily was scared, but she did not want to give up her fish. She said, "No, this is our river. We live here with our family and friends. You are the one who should go away. You are not nice!"
Rex growled and swam towards Lily. He tried to grab her tail, but Lily was quick and dodged him. She saw her friends coming to help her. They all barked and splashed at Rex, making him angry and confused.
"Leave us alone, Rex! You are not stronger than us. We are a team!" Lily's friends said.
Rex realized he was outnumbered and outmatched. He decided to swim away and look for another river. He muttered, "Fine, I will go. But I will be back. You will see!"
Lily and her friends cheered and hugged each other. They were happy and proud. They thanked Lily for being brave and smart. They shared the big fish and enjoyed their meal. They learned that they could face any unknown danger if they stuck together.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks in their room. They wanted to build a big tower that reached the ceiling. They took turns to add more blocks on top of each other. They were very careful not to make the tower fall.
"How many blocks do we need to finish the tower?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Let's measure it with the ruler," Ben said. He got the ruler from the drawer and held it next to the tower. "Look, the tower is 50 centimeters tall. The ceiling is 100 centimeters tall. We need 50 more centimeters of blocks."
"Wow, that's a lot of blocks. Do we have enough?" Lily wondered.
"Let's see. We have this box of blocks and this bag of blocks. Maybe we can use them all," Ben said. He opened the box and the bag and poured the blocks on the floor. They started to pick up the blocks and stack them on the tower.
They were so busy building that they did not notice that it was getting dark outside. The sun was setting and the sky was turning red and purple. The room was getting darker and darker.
"Ben, I can't see the blocks very well. It's too dark in here," Lily said.
"Me too. Let's turn on the light," Ben said. He reached for the switch on the wall, but he bumped into the tower. The tower wobbled and then crashed to the ground. The blocks scattered everywhere.
"Oh no! Our tower!" Lily cried.
"Our tower is gone. We didn't finish it," Ben said.
They looked at the mess of blocks and felt sad. They worked so hard to build the tower, but they did not make it to the ceiling. They wished they had more time and more light.
"Maybe we can try again tomorrow," Lily said.
"Maybe. But we have to clean up the blocks first," Ben said.
They nodded and started to pick up the blocks and put them back in the box and the bag. They hoped that tomorrow they would have a better chance to finish their tower.

They looked for a rock or a stick, but they could not find anything. They were about to give up, when they heard a voice.
"Hello, children. What are you doing here?"
They turned around and saw an old man with a long beard and a hat. He was holding a cane and a bag. He smiled at them.
"We found this box, sir. But we can't open it," Ben said.
"Let me see," the old man said. He took the box and looked at it. He nodded and said, "This is a very special box. It belongs to me. I left it here a long time ago, when I worked at the mill. It has a gift inside, for someone who is gifted."
"Who is gifted, sir?" Lily asked.
"Someone who can do something very well, or has a special talent," the old man said. He looked at Ben and Lily and said, "Do you have any gifts, children?"
Ben and Lily thought for a moment. Ben liked to draw and paint. He could make beautiful pictures of the mill and the animals. Lily liked to sing and dance. She could make lovely sounds and move gracefully.
"I can draw and paint, sir," Ben said.
"I can sing and dance, sir," Lily said.

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, sir. We promise."
The old man gave them the key and said, "Good. Now, open the box and see what's inside."

There were ribbons and bells and feathers and flowers for Lily. There were also candies and cookies and chocolates for both of them.
"Wow! This is amazing!" Ben said.
"Thank you, sir! Thank you so much!" Lily said.
They looked at the old man, but he was gone. They only saw his hat and his cane and his bag. They were lying on the ground, near the mill. They picked them up and wiped them with their hands. They saw a note on the bag. It said:
"Dear children, I hope you enjoy your gifts. They are from the mill fairy. He likes to help gifted children like you. He also likes to play tricks. He turned me into an old man, so I could give you the box. But now he has turned me back into a bird. I have to fly away, but I will always remember you. Be kind, be happy, be gifted. Love, the mill fairy."
Ben and Lily looked at the sky and saw a bird flying away. It was blue and yellow and red. It sang a beautiful song. They waved and said, "Goodbye, mill fairy! Thank you for the gifts!"
They hugged each other and laughed. They decided to use their gifts and make something for the mill fairy. They also decided to share their gifts with their friends and family. They were very happy. They knew they had met a very special friend. They knew they had a very special day.

The little girl smiled and went to play another day.

Tom and Jen were friends who liked to play tennis. They had a big net and two rackets and a ball. They took turns to serve the ball and hit it back. They counted the points and tried to win.
One day, a new boy came to the park. His name was Ben and he had a big nose and a mean smile. He saw Tom and Jen playing tennis and he wanted to join. He said, "Hey, can I play with you? I'm very good at tennis. I can beat you both."
Tom and Jen did not like Ben. He looked ugly and he sounded rude. But they did not want to be mean, so they said, "OK, you can play with us. But you have to follow the rules. You have to serve from behind the line and you have to hit the ball inside the court. And you have to be nice and fair."
Ben agreed, but he did not follow the rules. He served from too close and he hit the ball too hard and too far. He cheated and he lied. He said he won when he did not. He laughed at Tom and Jen and called them names. He made them feel bad.
Tom and Jen did not want to play with Ben anymore. They said, "Ben, you are not nice and fair. You are ugly and mean. You do not know how to play tennis. You do not know how to be a friend. We do not want to play with you. Go away."
Ben was angry and sad. He said, "You are mean and stupid. You are bad at tennis. You are bad at everything. I don't need you. I can play by myself."
He took the ball and the rackets and ran away. He tried to play tennis by himself, but it was not fun. He had no one to serve to, no one to hit back, no one to count the points, no one to talk to. He felt lonely and bored.
He looked at Tom and Jen. They were playing tennis again. They were having fun. They were smiling and laughing. They were nice and fair. They were good at tennis. They were good at everything. They were good friends.
He wished he could play with them. He wished he could be their friend. He wished he could be nice and fair. He wished he could be good.
He learned a lesson. He learned that being ugly and mean does not help you win. He learned that being nice and fair does help you make friends. He learned that playing tennis is more fun when you play with others. He learned that being good is better than being bad.

They liked to shoot water at each other, at the plants, and at the birds. But they knew they had to be careful not to shoot water at the things in the house, because their mom and dad would be angry.
One day, they were playing with their water gun in the backyard, when they saw a big, shiny toilet in the corner. It was a new toilet that their dad had bought, but he had not installed it yet. Anna and Ben were curious about the toilet, and they wanted to see how it worked. They ran to the toilet, and Anna lifted the lid. She saw a lot of water inside, and she had an idea.
"Let's shoot water at the toilet!" she said to Ben. "Maybe it will make a funny sound!"
Ben thought it was a good idea, too. He aimed his water gun at the toilet, and pulled the trigger. He shot water at the toilet, and waited for the sound. But nothing happened. He shot water again, and again, and again. Still nothing.
"Maybe it's broken," he said to Anna.
"Maybe we need to shoot more water," she said.
They both shot water at the toilet, until their water gun was empty. They looked at the toilet, and saw that it was full of water. They wondered what would happen if they flushed it.
"Let's flush it!" Anna said.
"OK!" Ben said.
They pushed the handle, and the toilet flushed. But instead of going down, the water came up. It came up very fast, and very high. It splashed all over Anna and Ben, and all over the backyard. It made a loud noise, and a big mess.
Anna and Ben were wet, and shocked, and scared. They heard their mom and dad coming out of the house. They looked at them, and saw that they were angry.

"We shot water at the toilet," Anna said.
"Why did you do that?" their dad asked.
"We wanted to hear a funny sound," Ben said.

"We're sorry, mom and dad," they said.
Their mom and dad sighed, and hugged them.
"We're glad you're OK, but you have to be more careful," their mom said. "You can't shoot water at things that are not meant for water. You could have broken the toilet, or hurt yourself, or someone else."
Their dad said, "You have to respect the things that we have, and use them properly. You can't just play with them, without thinking of the consequences."
Anna and Ben nodded, and said, "We understand, mom and dad. We won't do it again."
Their mom and dad said, "We love you, but you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's clean up this mess, and then you can play with your water gun again. But only in the right places, and with the right things."
Anna and Ben said, "OK, mom and dad. Thank you."
They helped their mom and dad clean up the mess, and then they played with their water gun again. But this time, they only shot water at each other, at the plants, and at the birds. And they had fun, without making trouble. They learned their lesson, and they were happy.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to act like pirates and look for gold. They had a map and a shovel and a big hat.
"Arrr, matey, where is the gold?" Tom asked Sara.
"It is under the big tree, see?" Sara pointed to the map. "We have to dig there."
They ran to the big tree and started to dig. They dug and dug until they saw something shiny.
"Look, we found it!" Sara shouted. "It is gold!"
They pulled out a small box with a lock. They opened it and saw many gold coins and jewels.
"Wow, we are rich!" Tom said. "We can buy anything we want!"
They hugged and laughed. They were very happy.
But then they heard a voice.
"Hey, what are you doing with my box?" It was an old man with a beard and a cane. He looked angry.
"This is our gold, we found it!" Sara said.
"No, it is not, it is mine!" the old man said. "I buried it here long ago. Give it back!"
Sara and Tom were scared. They did not want to fight with the old man.
"Sorry, sir, we did not know," Tom said. "We were just playing. Here, take your box."
They gave the box to the old man and ran away.
They felt sad and sorry. They did not mean to take his gold.
They went back to the park and sat on a bench.
"Maybe we should not act like pirates anymore," Sara said.
"Maybe not," Tom agreed. "But we can still play other things."
They looked at the sky and saw a rainbow. It was bright and beautiful.
They smiled and held hands.
They still had each other. And that was more than gold.

"Let's go to the swings," Jen said. "Maybe the dog will not see us there."
"OK," Ben said. "But what if the dog comes to the swings?"
"Then we can use the slide to run away," Jen said.
They ran to the swings and started to swing. They tried to have fun, but they kept looking at the dog. The dog was walking around the park, sniffing and barking. Sometimes, the dog looked at Jen and Ben.
Jen and Ben swung faster and faster. They hoped the dog would leave soon. They wanted to have their snack and go home.
But the dog did not leave. The dog came closer and closer to the swings. Jen and Ben were very nervous. They stopped swinging and held each other.
"Go away, dog!" Jen shouted. "We don't want to play with you!"
The dog did not listen. The dog jumped on the swings and started to lick Jen and Ben. Jen and Ben screamed. They were scared. They did not like the dog's tongue.
Then, they heard a voice.
"Rex, come here, boy!" the voice said. "Sorry, kids, he's just friendly. He likes to play."
Jen and Ben looked up and saw a man. The man was the dog's owner. He had a leash and a bag of treats. He smiled and waved at Jen and Ben.

"No, he's not mean," Tom said. "He's very gentle and friendly. He likes to play, too. Do you want to pet him?"

"Good boy, Rex," Tom said. "He likes you. You're his new friends."
Jen and Ben smiled. They liked the dog, too. They were not nervous anymore. They were happy.

"Sure, you can," Tom said. "But only if you want to. And only if you share your snack with him. He loves bananas and cookies."

Sara smiled. She said, "It is easy. You just have to practice. Come, I will show you. You can do it too."

Sara was happy. She said, "Yes, of course. There are many poses. We can do the cat, the dog, the tree, the snake, and more. Come, let's do yoga together."

One day, Tim and Sam are playing with their jeeps on the floor. Tim wants to make a race with Sam. He says, "My jeep is faster than your jeep. Let's see who can reach the sofa first." Sam nods and says, "OK, let's go." They put their jeeps on the floor and say, "One, two, three, go!"
Tim's jeep zooms ahead of Sam's jeep. It makes loud noises and flashes lights. Sam's jeep follows slowly behind. It is quiet and dim. Tim laughs and says, "Ha ha, I win! My jeep is the best!" Sam feels sad and says, "No fair, your jeep has batteries and mine doesn't."
Tim does not care. He picks up his jeep and says, "I'm going to play with my jeep on the table. You can play with your jeep on the floor." He walks to the table and puts his jeep on it. He does not see that the table is messy. There are books, papers, cups, and crayons on the table.
Tim pushes his jeep on the table. His jeep bumps into a cup. The cup falls off the table and breaks. The water spills on the floor. Tim's jeep snaps a crayon. The crayon breaks into two pieces. The pieces roll off the table and land on the floor. Tim's jeep knocks over a book. The book falls off the table and hits the floor. The pages fly out of the book.
Tim hears a loud noise. He looks at the floor. He sees a big mess. He sees the broken cup, the spilled water, the snapped crayon, and the torn book. He feels scared. He thinks, "Oh no, what have I done?"
Sam hears the noise too. He runs to the table and sees the mess. He sees Tim's jeep on the table. He says, "Tim, you made a big mess. You were not careful with your jeep. You should say sorry."
Tim does not want to say sorry. He says, "It's not my fault. It's your fault. You gave me a bad jeep. Your jeep is slow and boring. My jeep is fast and fun."
Sam feels angry. He says, "No, it's your fault. You were mean and rude. You did not share your jeep. You did not listen to me."
Tim and Sam start to argue. They shout at each other. They do not notice that their mom is coming. She hears the noise and sees the mess. She says, "What is going on here? Who made this mess?" Tim and Sam stop arguing. They look at their mom. They feel guilty. They do not know what to say.

Tom was a little boy who liked to whistle. He whistled when he played, when he ate, and when he went to bed. He whistled so much that his mom and dad sometimes asked him to be quiet.
One day, Tom went to the park with his mom. He saw a big slide and ran to it. He whistled as he climbed up the ladder and slid down. He had so much fun that he did it again and again.
But then, he saw a man in a suit sitting on a bench. The man had a book and a phone. He looked angry and bored. Tom thought he needed some fun. So he whistled very loud as he slid past him.
The man looked up and frowned. He said, "Hey, kid, stop that noise! I'm a lawyer and I'm working on a very important case. You're disturbing me!"
Tom was surprised and scared. He didn't know what a lawyer was, or what a case was. He only knew that the man was mean and rude. He said, "I'm sorry, mister, I didn't mean to bother you. I just like to whistle. It makes me happy."
The man snorted and said, "Well, I don't like it. It makes me unhappy. Go away and find another slide. And don't whistle again, or I'll sue you!"
Tom didn't know what sue meant, either. But he felt sad and hurt. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Tom. The man was wrong to yell at you. You didn't do anything bad. You can whistle as much as you want. It's a beautiful sound. And you know what? I'm a lawyer, too. And I think you have a great case for whistling!"

Lila was a lonely girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had a big purse where she kept all her dolls and their clothes. She loved to dress them up and pretend they were her friends.
One day, she saw a new girl in the park. She had curly hair and a red dress. She was playing with a ball and a dog. Lila wanted to talk to her, but she was shy. She watched her from behind a tree.
The new girl saw Lila and smiled. She walked over to her and said, "Hi, I'm Ruby. What's your name?"
Lila was surprised and scared. She hugged her purse and said, "Lila."
Ruby said, "Do you want to play with me? I have a ball and a dog. They are fun."
Lila said, "No, thank you. I have my dolls. They are fun too."
Ruby said, "Can I see your dolls? I like dolls too."
Lila said, "No, they are mine. You can't touch them."
Ruby said, "Okay, sorry. Bye." She walked away with her ball and her dog.
Lila felt sad. She wanted to play with Ruby, but she was afraid to share her dolls. She opened her purse and took out a doll. She saw that the doll's face was melted. She had left her purse in the sun and the heat had ruined her doll. She cried and cried.
She realized that her dolls were not her real friends. They could not talk to her or play with her. They could only melt and break. She wished she had been nicer to Ruby. She wished she had a real friend.
She ran after Ruby and said, "Ruby, wait. I'm sorry. Can I play with you?"
Ruby turned around and said, "Sure, Lila. I'm glad you changed your mind. Come on, let's play."
Lila smiled and followed Ruby. She left her purse behind. She did not need it anymore. She had found a real friend.
The moral of the story is: It is better to share and make friends than to be selfish and lonely.

One night, she heard a loud noise outside her window. She got scared and ran to her mom and dad's room. She saw them sleeping in their big bed. She shook her mom and said, "Mom, mom, there is a noisy thing outside. What is it?"
Her mom woke up and hugged her. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's just the wind. It's blowing the leaves and the branches. It can't hurt you. Come, let's go back to your room and pray together."
They walked back to Lily's room and knelt by her bed. They prayed to God and asked him to keep them safe and calm. They also thanked him for the wind, because it made the air fresh and clean.
Then, her mom tucked her in and gave her a kiss. She said, "Good night, Lily. I love you. Do you want a prune for a snack? They are sweet and juicy."
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, please. I love prunes. Thank you, mom. I love you too. Good night."
Her mom gave her a prune and turned off the light. Lily ate the prune and felt happy. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of flying with the wind and talking to God.

Ben shook his head. He said, "No, Sara. Wine is not for kids. It is for grown-ups. It can make you sick and sleepy. Mom and dad will be angry if we touch it."
But Sara did not listen. She said, "You are scared, Ben. I am not scared. I want to taste it. I insist." She grabbed the bottle and opened it. She took a big sip.
She made a face. The wine was not yummy. It was sour and bitter. It burned her mouth and throat. She coughed and spat. She felt dizzy and sick.
Ben was right. Wine was not for kids. Sara was foolish. She wished she had listened to Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. You were smart. I was dumb. Can you help me? I don't feel good."
Ben was kind. He said, "It's okay, Sara. I forgive you. But we have to tell mom and dad. They will help you. Come on, let's go inside."
They went inside and told mom and dad what happened. Mom and dad were not happy. They scolded Sara and Ben. They said, "You should never touch wine or any other drink that is not for kids. It is dangerous and bad for you. You could have hurt yourself or others. You have to promise us to never do that again."
Sara and Ben felt ashamed. They said, "We promise, mom and dad. We are sorry. We learned our lesson. We will never touch wine again."
Mom and dad hugged them. They said, "We love you, Sara and Ben. We are glad you are okay. But you have to be more careful and listen to us. We only want what is best for you."
Sara and Ben nodded. They said, "We love you too, mom and dad. We will be more careful and listen to you. Thank you for helping us."
They went to bed early. They had a bad headache and a bad dream. They hoped they would feel better in the morning. They hoped they would never be foolish again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread.
"Look, Lily, a big fish!" Tom said, pointing to the water.
"Wow, it is big!" Lily said. "Can we give it some bread?"
Tom nodded and tore a piece of bread from his sandwich. He threw it into the pond. The big fish saw the bread and swam fast to get it. It opened its mouth and bit the bread. Then it splashed its tail and made a big wave.
"Ha ha, that was fun!" Tom said, laughing. He threw another piece of bread.
But Lily saw something shiny in the water. It was a gem. It was round and blue and sparkled in the sun. Lily wanted to have it. She was careless. She did not think about the fish or the water. She reached out her hand and tried to grab the gem.
"Ouch!" Lily cried. The big fish saw her hand and thought it was food. It bit her finger and made her bleed. Lily pulled her hand back and started to cry.
"Help, help!" Lily shouted. "The fish bit me!"
Tom heard her and ran to her. He saw her finger and the gem. He was scared and sorry.
"I'm sorry, Lily, I'm sorry!" Tom said. He wrapped his napkin around her finger and hugged her. "Don't cry, don't cry!"
A lady who worked in the park heard them and came to help. She saw what happened and took them to the office. She cleaned Lily's finger and put a band-aid on it. She also gave her a lollipop and a sticker.
"Are you okay, Lily?" the lady asked.
Lily nodded and smiled. She felt better. She thanked the lady and said sorry for being careless.
"It's okay, Lily, but you have to be careful next time," the lady said. "The pond is not a place to play. The fish can bite and the water can be deep. You could get hurt or drown. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said yes. She learned her lesson. She did not want the gem anymore. She gave it to the lady and said she could keep it.
"Thank you, Lily, that's very kind of you," the lady said. "But you know what? This is not a real gem. It's just a glass bead. Someone must have dropped it in the pond. It's not worth anything."
Lily was surprised. She thought the gem was precious and beautiful. But it was not. It was fake and dangerous. She was glad she gave it away.
"Come on, Lily, let's go home," Tom said. He held her hand and walked with her. He was glad she was okay. He did not want to play in the pond anymore. He wanted to play in the sandbox.
"Okay, Tom, let's go home," Lily said. She held his hand and walked with him. She was glad he was nice. He was her best friend. She wanted to play with him in the sandbox.

"Of course, my dear, come in," grandma said. She opened the door and saw Lily shivering. She wrapped her in a soft bathrobe and hugged her. "What's wrong, Lily?"
"I heard a noise. It was like a big boom. I thought it was a monster," Lily said.
"Oh, no, Lily, that was just thunder. It's a storm. There's no monster, don't worry," grandma said. She comforted Lily and stroked her hair. "Do you want to hear a story?"
"Yes, please," Lily said.
"Okay, let me tell you a story about a princess who was very rich. She had a big castle, a lot of dresses, and many toys. But she was not happy. She wanted to have a friend. One day, she met a boy who was very poor. He had a small hut, a few clothes, and no toys. But he was happy. He had a dog, a bird, and a flower. He shared them with the princess. They became friends. They played, laughed, and learned together. The princess realized that being rich was not important. She gave some of her things to the poor people. She was happy too. The end."
"That was a nice story, grandma. Thank you," Lily said.
"You're welcome, Lily. I love you," grandma said.
"I love you too, grandma. Can I stay with you until mom and dad come back?" Lily asked.
"Of course, Lily. You can stay with me as long as you want. Now, let's sleep. Good night," grandma said.
"Good night, grandma," Lily said. She snuggled with grandma and the bathrobe. She felt warm and safe. She closed her eyes and fell asleep.

One day, the silly crocodile ordered a big cake to eat. But his friends, the fish and the frogs, did not want him to eat the cake. They were scared that the silly crocodile would become too big and take up all the space in the pond.
The fish and the frogs tried to stop the silly crocodile from eating the cake. They jumped and splashed, but the silly crocodile did not listen. He ate the whole cake and became very big. There was no more room in the pond for the fish and the frogs. They had to leave their home.
In the end, the silly crocodile was all alone in the pond. He had no friends to play with, and he was very sad. The silly crocodile learned that being greedy and not listening to his friends led to a bad ending.
