Lily loved to look at tiny things with her microscope. She had a book with pictures of bugs, plants and crystals that she could find in her garden or her room. She liked to put them on a slide and see how they looked under the microscope. She learned their names and shapes and colors.
One day, she wanted to show her microscope to her friend Max, who came to play with her. She took him to her room and showed him her book and her slides. She said, "Look, Max, this is a microscope. It makes things bigger. Do you want to see?"
Max did not look interested. He said, "That's boring. I don't like tiny things. I like big things, like cars and trucks and dinosaurs. Let's play with those instead." He grabbed a toy car from Lily's shelf and ran to the living room.
Lily felt miserable. She did not understand why Max did not like her microscope. She thought it was the most amazing thing in the world. She stared at her microscope and felt sad. She did not want to play with cars and trucks and dinosaurs. She wanted to share her passion with her friend.
She decided to follow Max to the living room and try to talk to him. She said, "Max, why don't you like my microscope? It's fun and cool and you can learn a lot from it. You can see things that you can't see with your eyes. Don't you want to try?"
Max looked at her and shrugged. He said, "I don't know. I just don't. I think it's silly and hard and boring. I like things that are easy and fun and exciting. Like cars and trucks and dinosaurs. They make noise and move and have teeth. They are awesome."
Lily felt hurt. She said, "But my microscope is awesome too. It shows me a whole new world. A world that is beautiful and amazing and full of wonders. A world that you can't see without it. Don't you want to see that world?"
Max thought for a moment. He saw that Lily was sincere and that she really loved her microscope. He felt sorry for being rude and mean to her. He said, "Okay, Lily. I'm sorry. I was wrong. Maybe I was afraid of trying something new. Maybe I was missing out on something cool. Maybe I can learn something from you. Can you show me your microscope again?"
Lily smiled. She said, "Sure, Max. I'm glad you changed your mind. Come on, let's go to my room. I have a slide with a dinosaur bone. It's awesome."
They went to Lily's room and looked at the dinosaur bone under the microscope. They saw the tiny holes and lines and patterns that made up the bone. They compared it to the picture in the book and learned how it belonged to a big and fierce dinosaur. They were amazed and curious and happy.
They learned that day that different things can be awesome in different ways. They learned that they can share their interests and hobbies with each other and discover new things. They learned that they can be friends even if they like different things. They learned that they can stare at the world with wonder and respect.

"Are you ready to go?" Mom asks.
"Yes, Mom!" Lila and Ben say.
They go to the car and buckle up. Mom drives to Grandma and Grandpa's house. It is not far. Lila and Ben look out the window and see trees and flowers and birds.

"What is it, Grandma?" Lila asks.
Grandma smiles and looks at Grandpa. Grandpa nods and takes out a big envelope from his pocket. He opens it and shows them a picture.
"Look, Lila and Ben. This is your new cousin. He was born yesterday. His name is Leo. He is your aunt's baby. You are going to meet him soon. Isn't he cute?"
Lila and Ben look at the picture. They see a tiny baby with a hat and a blanket. He has a small nose and a small mouth. He is sleeping.
"Wow!" Lila says. "He is so small and cute. I want to hold him."
"Me too!" Ben says. "Can we play with him?"
Grandma and Grandpa laugh. Mom smiles.
"Of course you can. But you have to be gentle and quiet. He is very new and needs a lot of rest. He can't talk or walk yet. He only eats and sleeps and cries. But he will grow and learn soon. Lila and Ben nod. They feel proud and excited. They want to meet Leo and be good cousins. They hug Grandma and Grandpa and Mom and say thank you for the picture.
They hear a soft sound from the picture. It is Leo. He is making a noise with his mouth. He is not crying. He is cooing.
Lila and Ben listen. They are quiet. They hear Leo's voice. It is a sweet sound. It breaks the silence. It fills their hearts.

"Help me please!" cried Steve. He swam up to the boat and explained how he got lost.

Lily laughs. She picks up the snake. She runs after Tom. "It is just a toy, Tom," she says. "It is not real. It is funny."
Tom stops. He looks at the snake. He sees that it is a toy. He feels silly. He laughs too. "You tricked me, Lily," he says. "That was a good joke. You are funny."
Lily and Tom hug. They are friends. They go back to the box of toys. They play some more. They have fun. They bury and find many things. They are happy.

Bob wanted to help the mushroom. He had an idea. "I can attach you to the ground," said Bob. The mushroom was happy.
Bob worked hard to attach the mushroom to the ground. But, as he worked, the mushroom started to grow big. It became a big tree! The tree had many branches for bugs to live on.
The moral of the story is that sometimes, when we help others, unexpected things can happen. And these unexpected things can be good for everyone.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the living room. It had a tag that said "For Lily and Ben, a reward for being good kids". They were very happy and curious. They wanted to open the box and see what was inside.
But their mom said, "No, not yet. You have to wait until your dad comes home. He has a surprise for you. The box is fragile, so be careful. Don't touch it or shake it or break it."
Lily and Ben nodded, but they were impatient. They went to their room and played with their other toys, but they kept thinking about the box. They wondered what was in it. Maybe it was a new game, or a book, or a doll, or a car.
After a while, Ben said, "I can't wait any longer. I want to see what's in the box. Let's go and peek. Mom won't know. She's busy in the kitchen."
Lily said, "No, Ben. That's not nice. Mom told us to wait. We have to listen to her. She will be sad if we disobey. And what if we hurt the box? It's fragile, remember?"
Ben said, "Oh, come on, Lily. Don't be a baby. It's just a little peek. We won't hurt the box. We'll be very gentle. And mom won't be sad. She'll be proud that we're curious and smart. Come on, let's go."
Lily said, "No, Ben. I don't want to go. You go if you want, but I'll stay here."
Ben said, "Fine. I'll go by myself. You're no fun." He left the room and went to the living room. He saw the box on the table. He tiptoed to it and lifted the lid. He saw something shiny and colorful. He reached for it.
But then he heard a loud noise. It was a siren. It was coming from the box. It was an alarm. Ben was scared. He dropped the lid and ran back to his room. He hid under his bed.
Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the box and the alarm. She knew what had happened. She was angry and disappointed. She turned off the alarm and went to find Ben.
She found him under his bed. She said, "Ben, what did you do? Why did you open the box? You know you were not supposed to. You broke the rules. You made a mess. You ruined the surprise. You made me and dad sad. You have to suffer the consequences. You have to go to time out. And you have to apologize to Lily and dad. And you have to wait until tomorrow to see what's in the box. Maybe then you'll learn to be patient and respectful."
Ben said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to see what's in the box. I didn't mean to hurt it. I didn't know it had an alarm. Please don't be mad at me. Please don't make me go to time out. Please let me see what's in the box."
Mom said, "No, Ben. You have to go to time out. You have to learn from your mistake. You have to suffer the consequences. Maybe then you'll appreciate the reward. Now go to your room and stay there until I say so."
Ben said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I love you." He went to his room and sat on his bed. He felt sad and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Lily and mom. He wondered what was in the box. He hoped it was something good. He hoped Lily and dad would forgive him. He hoped mom would still love him. He learned a hard lesson. He learned that curiosity can be good, but it can also be bad. He learned that rules are there for a reason. He learned that fragile things need to be handled with care. He learned that rewards are sweeter when they are earned. He learned that suffering can make you grow. He learned that he had to wait.

John was scared. He looked at the deep blue lake with uncertainty. He couldn't tell if the water was going to be cold. He sighed, as he thought of getting in the water.
His mom smiled. “It’s okay,” she said. “I’ll be with you.”
She held his hand, as they slowly walked towards the lake. John felt a little better, but he was still scared. He took a deep breath and stepped into the water.
He gasped as the cold water hit his skin. He tried to move forward, but he was afraid. Suddenly, he felt his mom’s arms around him.
“It’s okay,” she said. “I’m here.”
John felt a little less scared. He gradually moved his feet and soon he was splashing around in the blue lake. He glanced up at his mom with a smile and she smiled back. He had taken a big step forward, and he knew that he could do anything!

Suddenly he heard a noise coming from the back of the house. It was like something was being added. Spot looked over to see what it was – he was surprised to find something shiny and new! It was a big, open box.
Spot ran over to his owners and said, "Look! What is this new box?" His owners looked down and smiled. "It's a present for you, Spot!" they said. "It has lots of toys inside – would you like to add some?"
Spot was so happy he could hardly believe it. He jumped in and started adding all the toys that he saw. He had so much fun – it was not a normal day for Spot!

Lily liked to play in her yard. She had a swing, a slide and a sandbox. She also had a lot of toys, like dolls, cars and balls. She was happy with her toys, but sometimes she wanted to try new ones.
One day, she saw a big truck in the yard next door. It was red and shiny, and it made loud noises. Lily thought it was incredible. She wanted to play with it. She asked her mom if she could borrow it from the neighbor.
Her mom said no. She said the truck was not a toy, but a tool. She said the neighbor needed it to fix his house. She said Lily could not borrow it, because it was not hers, and it was dangerous.
Lily was sad. She did not understand why the truck was not a toy. She thought it looked like fun. She decided to wait until the neighbor was gone, and then sneak into his yard and borrow the truck.
She waited and waited, until she saw the neighbor leave in his car. She ran to his yard and climbed into the truck. She pushed some buttons and pulled some levers. The truck started to move. It was very fast and loud. Lily was scared. She did not know how to stop it.
The truck crashed into the fence, the tree and the mailbox. It made a big mess. The neighbor came back and saw what happened. He was very angry. He yelled at Lily and her mom. He said Lily was naughty and she had to pay for the damage.
Lily was sorry. She realized she had made a big mistake. She learned that she should not borrow things without asking, and that some things are not toys. She apologized to the neighbor and her mom. She promised to never do it again. She went back to her yard and played with her own toys. She was happy with them, and she did not want to borrow anything else.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They wanted to play with everything.
"Can we go on the slide, mom?" Tom asked.
"Yes, but be careful. Don't push or run," mom said.
Tom and Lily climbed up the slide and slid down. They laughed and had fun. Then they went to the swing and took turns. They felt like they were flying.
"Can we go to the sandbox, mom?" Lily asked.
"Yes, but don't throw sand or eat it," mom said.
Tom and Lily ran to the sandbox and started to make castles and cakes. They used sticks and stones and leaves to decorate them. They were very proud of their creations.
But then, Tom saw something shiny and long in the sand. He picked it up and saw that it was a snake. He was scared and wanted to drop it. But he had a funny idea.
"Look, Lily, I found a toy snake!" he said, holding the snake in his hand.
"Wow, let me see!" Lily said, reaching for the snake.
But the snake was not a toy. It was a real snake. And it did not like being held by Tom. It opened its mouth and bit Tom's finger. Tom screamed and let go of the snake. The snake slithered away into the grass.
"Ow, ow, ow! Mom, help!" Tom cried, holding his finger.
Mom heard Tom's cry and ran to him. She saw the bite mark and the snake. She was very angry and worried.
"Tom, what did you do? That's not a toy snake, that's a real snake! It could be poisonous! Why did you lie to Lily?" she said, taking Tom to the car.
"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to make a joke. I thought it was funny," Tom said, sobbing.
"It's not funny, Tom. It's dangerous. You could have hurt yourself or Lily. You should never lie or play with wild animals. They are not toys. They have feelings and can hurt you. Do you understand?" mom said, driving to the hospital.
"Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I won't lie or play with snakes again," Tom said, feeling sorry and scared.
Mom hugged Tom and said, "I love you, Tom. But you have to be more careful and honest. Lying is bad and can cause trouble. Always tell the truth and respect nature. OK?"
"OK, mom. I love you too," Tom said, hoping the snake was not poisonous.

"Look, Lily, the sun is burning!" Tom said.
"Yes, Tom, the sun is burning. It is very big and yellow. I like the sun," Lily said.
They threw their ball to each other and laughed. They did not see the man with the matches. He was hiding behind a tree. He was very bad and mean. He wanted to make trouble. He lit a match and threw it at the ball.
The ball caught fire. It made a loud noise and a lot of smoke. Tom and Lily were scared and sad. They ran away from the ball. They cried for help.
"Help, help, our ball is burning!" they shouted.
A woman heard them and came to see. She saw the ball and the fire. She saw the man with the matches. She was very angry and brave. She took a bucket of water and threw it at the ball. The fire went out. The ball was black and wet. It was ruined.
"Who did this?" the woman asked.
Tom and Lily pointed at the man with the matches. He was still behind the tree. He was ashamed and afraid. He knew he did a bad thing. He tried to run away, but the woman caught him. She called the police. The police came and took him away.
The woman hugged Tom and Lily. She was very kind and sorry. She gave them a new ball. It was red and shiny. It was not burning.
"Thank you, thank you, you are very nice," Tom and Lily said.
"You are very welcome, you are very brave," the woman said.
They smiled and played with their new ball. They did not see the giant sun anymore. It was behind a cloud. It was still burning, but it did not hurt them. It was their friend.

One day, their mom said, "Tom and Lily, you can play in the yard, but you have to stay in the fence. Do not go out of the fence, or you will be in trouble. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We will stay in the fence."
They ran to the yard and started to play with their ball. They threw it, kicked it, and rolled it. Spot chased the ball and brought it back to them. They had a lot of fun.
But then, the ball bounced too high and went over the fence. It landed on the street, where there were cars and bikes and people. Tom and Lily looked at the ball and then at each other. They wanted to get the ball back, but they also remembered what their mom said.
"Mom said we cannot go out of the fence," Lily said.
"But the ball is out of the fence," Tom said.
"What can we do?" Lily asked.
Tom thought for a moment. He had an idea. He was very clever. He said, "I know. We can ask Spot to get the ball for us. He can go out of the fence and come back. He is a good dog. He will listen to us."
Lily liked the idea. She said, "Yes, let's ask Spot. He is very clever, too."
They called Spot and pointed to the ball. They said, "Spot, can you get the ball for us? Please, Spot, get the ball. We cannot go out of the fence, but you can. You are a good dog."
Spot looked at the ball and then at Tom and Lily. He wagged his tail and barked. He understood what they wanted. He ran to the fence and jumped over it. He ran to the ball and picked it up with his mouth. He ran back to the fence and jumped over it again. He brought the ball to Tom and Lily and dropped it at their feet.
Tom and Lily were very happy. They hugged Spot and said, "Thank you, Spot. You are a very clever and good dog. We love you, Spot."
Spot licked their faces and barked. He was happy, too. He loved Tom and Lily.
They continued to play with their ball in the yard, in the fence, where their mom permitted them to play. They had a lot of fun.

Anna and Ben are friends who live in a village near a big river. They like to play near the water and splash each other. One day, they see a man who is very thirsty. He has a bottle, but it is empty. He asks them if they can share some water with him.
"Please, can I have some water?" he says. "I have walked a long way and I have no water left."
Anna and Ben look at each other. They have a bucket of water that they filled from the river. They can give some to the man, but then they will have less to play with.
"Why do you need water?" Anna asks. "Water is for fun, not for drinking."
The man smiles and says, "Water is for many things, my dear. Water is for drinking, for washing, for cooking, for growing plants, for making rainbows. Water is a gift from God, and we should value it and use it wisely."
Anna and Ben think about what the man says. They realize that water is not only for fun, but also for life. They feel sorry for the man, who has no water. They decide to share their water with him.
"Here, you can have some of our water," Ben says. "We have plenty, and you need it more than we do."
The man thanks them and drinks some water. He feels better and says, "You are very kind and generous, children. You have humble hearts and you know how to share. May God bless you and your water."
Anna and Ben smile and say, "You are welcome, sir. Thank you for teaching us about water. We will value it and use it wisely."
The man leaves and Anna and Ben go back to playing near the water. They splash each other, but they also drink some water and thank God for it. They are happy and grateful. They have learned a valuable lesson.

They pull so hard that the book falls down. The book hits the floor with a loud bang. Some of the pages tear. Sara and Ben are scared.
Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the book on the floor and the torn pages. She is angry. She says to Sara and Ben, "What did you do? You broke the book! That was a special book from Grandma. You are very naughty!"
Sara and Ben are sad. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We just wanted to see the pictures. We did not mean to break the book."
Mom sighs. She says, "I know you did not mean to break the book, but you should not touch things that are not yours. You should ask me first. Now the book is ruined. How can we fix it?"
Sara and Ben think. They say, "We can glue the pages back. We can draw new pictures. We can say sorry to Grandma."
Mom smiles. She says, "That is a good idea. But first, you need to clean up the mess. And then, you need to take a nap. You are tired from playing. Maybe later, we can have some cocoa and cookies. Do you like that?"
Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. We like cocoa and cookies. They are yummy. We love you, Mom."
Mom hugs Sara and Ben. She says, "I love you too, my chubby twins. Now, let's clean up and go to bed."

"Sure, you can have a slice. Can I have some of your sandwich?" Ben says.
"Okay, we can trade. I like pizza too," Mia says.
They swap their food and start to eat. But then, Mia feels something in her mouth. It is hard and shiny. She spits it out on her napkin. It is a ring.
"Ben, what is this?" Mia says, holding the ring.
Ben looks at the ring and turns red. He feels embarrassed.
"Oh, no. That is my mom's ring. I was playing with it this morning and I forgot to take it off. I must have dropped it in the pizza box. I'm sorry, Mia," Ben says.
Mia is surprised. She does not know what to say.
"Are you mad at me?" Ben asks.
Mia shakes her head. She is not mad. She is a good friend.
"No, I'm not mad. It was an accident. But you should keep your mom's ring safe. She might be worried if she can't find it," Mia says.
Ben nods. He is glad that Mia is not mad. He is a good friend too.
"Thank you, Mia. You are right. I will keep it safe. I will give it back to my mom when I go home. And I will share my apple with you," Ben says.
Mia smiles. She likes apples. She likes Ben too. They finish their lunch and go to play. They are happy. They are friends.

"Thank you, dog!" Lily said. "You are very nice. Can we have some of your bone?"
The dog nodded. He put the bone on the ground. He let Lily and Ben have a bite. The bone was tasty. Lily and Ben smiled. They liked the bone. They liked the dog. They made a new friend.

One day, their teacher tells them that they will have a special lunch from another country. She says it is very spicy and some children may not like it. She recommends that they try a little bit first and drink a lot of water.
Sara is curious and wants to try the spicy food. She thinks it will be fun and tasty. Ben is scared and does not want to try it. He thinks it will be hot and hurt his mouth. He wants to eat his sandwich and apple instead.
At lunchtime, Sara gets a plate of the spicy food and sits next to Ben. She takes a small bite and makes a funny face. "Wow, this is spicy!" she says. "But I like it. It has a lot of flavor. Do you want to try some, Ben?"
Ben shakes his head and holds his sandwich. "No, thank you. I don't like spicy food. I like my sandwich and apple. They are good and safe."
Sara shrugs and eats more of the spicy food. She drinks a lot of water and feels happy. Ben eats his sandwich and apple and feels bored. He watches Sara and the other children who try the spicy food. They look like they are having fun and learning something new.
The next day, the teacher asks the children what they thought of the spicy food. Sara raises her hand and says, "I liked it. It was different and exciting. I learned that there are many kinds of food in the world and I want to try more."
Ben lowers his head and says nothing. He feels sad and ashamed. He wishes he had tried the spicy food too. He learned that there are many kinds of food in the world and he missed a chance to try something new.
The moral of the story is: It is good to be curious and try new things. You may discover something you like and learn something new. It is not good to be scared and avoid new things. You may miss something you like and learn nothing new.

Lila and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the woods near their homes. They were very creative and made up stories and games with sticks and stones and leaves.
One day, they found a creek in the woods. It was a small creek, but it had clear water and shiny fish. Lila and Sam decided to build a bridge over the creek with some big sticks. They worked hard and had fun.
"Look, we made a bridge!" Lila said. "Now we can cross the creek and explore the other side."
"Let's go!" Sam said. They held hands and walked over the bridge. They felt proud and happy.
But when they reached the other side, they heard a loud snap. They turned around and saw that their bridge had broken. The sticks had fallen into the water and floated away.
"Oh no!" Lila said. "Our bridge is gone! How will we get back?"
Sam felt scared. He did not like the other side of the creek. It was dark and strange. He did not see any other way to cross the water.
He started to cry. "I want to go home!" he sobbed.
Lila hugged him. She felt scared too, but she wanted to be brave for Sam. She looked around and saw a big log near the creek. It was long and thick and had a smooth top.
She had an idea. She wiped her tears and said, "Don't cry, Sam. I have a plan. We can use this log as a boat. We can push it into the water and sit on it. Then we can paddle with our hands and go back to our side."
Sam looked at the log. He was not sure if it would work, but he trusted Lila. He nodded and said, "OK, let's try."
They worked together and pushed the log into the creek. They climbed on it and sat in the middle. They used their hands as paddles and moved the log slowly across the water.
They were careful not to fall off or get wet. They saw their bridge sticks floating by and waved goodbye to them.
They reached their side and jumped off the log. They were happy and relieved. They hugged each other and said, "We did it! We are back!"
They ran back to their homes and told their parents what happened. Their parents were glad they were safe and praised them for being creative and brave.
Lila and Sam smiled and said, "We are best friends. We can do anything together."

They are not lucky. The farmer finds them. The farmer is not happy. He asks them why they took the wagon. He tells them the wagon is not for children. It is for the cow. He tells them the cow needs the hay. He tells them they have to say sorry to the cow.
Anna and Ben are sorry. They say sorry to the farmer. They say sorry to the cow. They promise to not take the wagon again. They promise to ask before they borrow anything.

Lila was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new things. She had a toy laser that made bright lights and funny sounds. She wanted to see what would happen if she put the laser on different things.
One day, she went to the park with her mom and her laser. She saw a big slide that looked fun. She climbed up the ladder and put the laser on the top of the slide. She pressed the button and the laser made a red light that went down the slide.
"Wow, look at that!" she said.
She slid down after the light and laughed. She felt happy and excited.
She wanted to try more things with her laser. She saw a pond with some ducks. She ran to the edge and put the laser on the water. She pressed the button and the laser made a green light that bounced on the water.
"Quack, quack!" the ducks said. They were curious and followed the light.
Lila giggled and waved at the ducks. She liked to make new friends.
She saw a big tree with some birds. She wanted to see if they liked the laser too. She put the laser on the trunk of the tree. She pressed the button and the laser made a blue light that went up the tree.
"Tweet, tweet!" the birds said. They were surprised and flew away.
Lila frowned and felt sorry. She did not mean to scare them.
She heard her mom calling her. It was time to go home. She picked up her laser and ran to her mom.
"Did you have fun, Lila?" her mom asked.
"Yes, mom. I put the laser on many things. It was very fun. But I scared the birds. I am sorry." Lila said.
"It's okay, Lila. You were just being adventurous. But you have to be careful with your laser. It can hurt some things or some people. You have to ask before you put it on something." her mom said.
"I understand, mom. I will be careful next time. Can I play with the laser again tomorrow?" Lila asked.
"Sure, Lila. But only if you promise to be safe and respectful." her mom said.
"I promise, mom. Thank you. I love you." Lila said.
"I love you too, Lila. You are my adventurous girl." her mom said.
They hugged and went home. Lila was happy. She had a great day with her laser. She wondered what else she could put it on tomorrow.

Max was getting frustrated when out of nowhere, a rabbit came hopping up. The rabbit said to him, “Maybe if you take a few steps back and stay still, I can give it a go.”

Max was so impressed that he needed to stay and watch the rabbit’s work. He watched as the rabbit pulled the rope and suddenly everything unfurled. The rabbit’s work had revealed a beautiful bridge leading over to the other side of the forest.
Max had no idea what the rabbit was doing but he knew that the rope-pulling had been successful. So Max thanked the rabbit and they went on their merry way, each with a smile on their face.

"OK, but be careful," Sam says. "Some cats are shy."
They jog to the bench. Rex stays behind. He does not like cats. They say hello to the cat. The cat looks at them. It does not run away.
"Hi, cute cat," Jen says. "What is your name?"
The cat does not answer. It licks its paw. It does not mind Jen and Sam.
"Can we give you some milk?" Sam asks. He picks up the bowl. He holds it to the cat.
The cat sniffs the milk. It nods. It drinks some milk. It purrs.
"Thank you, kind kids," the cat says. "My name is Luna. I live in the park. Do you want to be my friends?"
"Yes, we do!" Jen and Sam say. They smile. They pet Luna. Luna rubs her head on them.
They are happy. They have a new friend. Rex barks. He is not happy. He wants to jog. Jen and Sam say goodbye to Luna. They jog with Rex. Luna waves to them. She finishes her milk. She takes a nap.

"Why is there a wire?" Ben wondered.

"That's not nice of the rabbits. I like the flowers. They make me happy," Ben said.

"Sure. What game?" Ben said.

They both spun around and around, making noises and faces. They felt dizzy and giggled. They fell down on the grass and looked at the sky. They saw the clouds and the birds. They felt happy and peaceful. They were like two flowers in the garden.

Lily and Ben liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of toys and they made up stories with them. One day, they found a shiny thing in the dirt. It was a crystal. It sparkled in the sun and had many colors.
"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. "It's so pretty!"
"Can I see?" Ben asked. He reached for the crystal, but Lily pulled it away.
"No, it's mine!" she said. "I found it first!"
Ben was sad. He wanted to play with the crystal too. He thought it was not fair that Lily kept it all to herself. He tried to think of a way to get it.
The next day, Lily and Ben played in the garden again. Lily brought the crystal with her and put it on a rock. She pretended it was a magic jewel that gave her powers. Ben watched her and waited for his chance.
When Lily was busy with her other toys, Ben sneaked up to the rock. He grabbed the crystal and ran away.
"Hey, stop!" Lily shouted. "That's mine!"
She chased after him, but Ben was faster. He ran to the other side of the garden, where there was a big tree. He climbed up the tree and hid the crystal in a hole.
"Ha ha, I got it now!" he said. "You can't get it!"
Lily was angry. She tried to climb the tree, but she was afraid of falling. She asked Ben to give the crystal back, but he said no. He was playful, but also mean.
Then, they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Rex. He had smelled the crystal and followed them. He barked and jumped at the tree. He wanted to play with the crystal too.
"Uh oh," Ben said. "Rex is here!"
He looked at the hole, but the crystal was gone. Rex had removed it with his mouth. He ran away with the crystal, wagging his tail.
"Hey, come back!" Lily and Ben shouted. "That's ours!"
They climbed down the tree and ran after Rex. They wanted to get the crystal back, but Rex was faster. He ran to the house and buried the crystal in the yard.
Lily and Ben were sad. They had lost the crystal. They realized they had been silly and selfish. They should have shared the crystal and played with it together. They hugged and said sorry to each other.
They decided to look for another shiny thing in the dirt. Maybe they would find another crystal. Or maybe something else. They didn't know. But they knew they would have more fun if they were nice and playful with each other. And with Rex.

One day, Tom goes to school. He has a new teacher. The teacher gives him a paper with words on it. She says, "Write these words on your paper. Then I will check them." Tom looks at the words. He does not know some of them. He does not know how to spell them. He feels worried. He thinks, "What if I write them wrong? What if the teacher gets angry? What if I get a bad mark?"
Tom tries to write the words. He writes some of them right. He writes some of them wrong. He writes some of them with missing letters. He writes some of them with extra letters. He writes some of them backwards. He writes some of them upside down. He writes some of them with funny shapes. He writes some of them with dots and lines. He writes some of them with colors and stickers. He writes some of them with smileys and hearts.
The teacher comes to check his paper. She looks at his words. She smiles. She says, "Tom, you have a very creative way of writing. You have made some mistakes, but that is okay. Everyone makes mistakes when they learn. The important thing is that you try. You can learn from your mistakes and improve. You can also have fun with writing. Writing is not only about spelling. Writing is also about expressing yourself. You have a lot of ideas and feelings in your writing. I like that. You are a good writer, Tom."
Tom feels happy. He says, "Thank you, teacher. I like to write. I want to learn more words. I want to write better. I also want to write fun. Can I write more words with colors and stickers and smileys and hearts?" The teacher says, "Yes, you can, Tom. You can write whatever you want. You can write your own stories. You can write your own books. You can write your own world. You can write your own magic."
The moral of the story is: Writing is a skill that can be learned and improved, but it is also a way of expressing yourself and having fun. You should not be afraid of making mistakes, but rather learn from them and try again. You should also be creative and original with your writing, and use your imagination and emotions. Writing can be a wonderful and magical activity.

"Sure, you can," said Sara and Ben's mom. "But please be careful with our animals. They are not used to strangers."

Sara and Ben were curious. They wanted to see what was in the cages and tents. They waited until their mom was busy in the kitchen and then they sneaked to the barn. They saw a lion, a tiger, a monkey, a bear, and a clown.

"Let's go closer and touch them," Ben said. He walked towards the lion's cage.
"Ben, no! That's dangerous!" Sara said. She tried to pull him back, but it was too late. The lion roared and jumped at the cage. Ben screamed and ran away. Sara followed him.
They ran out of the barn and bumped into their mom. She was angry and scared.
"What were you doing in the barn?" she asked. "Didn't I tell you to stay away from the circus people and their animals?"
"We're sorry, mom. We just wanted to see them," Sara said.
"Well, you saw them, and you almost got hurt. You should be thankful that the cage was strong enough to stop the lion. Now go to your room and think about what you did," their mom said.
Sara and Ben nodded and went to their room. They felt sorry and scared. They learned their lesson. They decided to never go near the barn again when the circus was there. They also decided to be more thankful for their regular animals, who were friendly and safe.

Timmy was a little boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a big truck, a soft bear, and a yellow ball. He also had a special pillow that he slept with every night. His pillow was blue and had stars on it. He called it his star pillow.
One day, Timmy went to visit his grandma. She was elderly and lived in a small house. She was very kind and gave Timmy cookies and milk. She also had a cat named Fluffy, who liked to nap on the couch. Timmy wanted to play with Fluffy, but Fluffy did not want to play. He hissed and scratched at Timmy.
"Fluffy, be nice!" Grandma said. "He is just a little boy. He wants to be your friend."
But Fluffy did not listen. He ran away and hid under the bed. Timmy felt sad. He wanted to have fun with Fluffy. He decided to look for him. He went to the bedroom and saw Fluffy's tail sticking out from under the bed. He crawled under the bed and tried to grab Fluffy's tail.
"Meow!" Fluffy said. He was angry and scared. He bit Timmy's hand and ran out of the room.
"Ow!" Timmy said. He cried and ran to Grandma. He showed her his hand. It had a red mark on it.
"Timmy, what happened?" Grandma asked. She saw Fluffy run past her. She knew he was the culprit. She hugged Timmy and kissed his hand. "I'm sorry, Fluffy is not a nice cat. He does not like strangers. He needs to learn to share and be gentle."
She took Timmy to the bathroom and washed his hand. She put a band-aid on it and gave him a lollipop. She also gave him his star pillow. She said he could keep it with him until he felt better.
"Thank you, Grandma," Timmy said. He smiled and hugged her. He felt happy again. He liked his star pillow. It made him feel safe and cozy. He decided to forget about Fluffy and play with his toys instead. He hoped that one day, Fluffy would turn into a friendly cat. But for now, he was happy with his Grandma and his star pillow.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They saw a big tree with many flowers and bees. They wanted to climb the tree and see the bees up close.
"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "We can climb the tree and find the hive."
"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Bees can sting us if we make them angry."
They ran to the tree and started to climb. They used their hands and feet to hold on to the branches. They saw the bees flying around the flowers and making a buzzing sound.
"Look, Lily! There is the hive!" Ben said. He pointed to a round thing hanging from a branch. It was brown and had a hole in it. "The bees live there and make honey."
"Wow, Ben! It is so big and shiny!" Lily said. She wanted to touch it and see what it felt like. She reached out her hand and moved closer to the hive.
"Wait, Lily! Don't do that!" Ben said. "The bees will not like it. They will think you are trying to take their honey. They will come out and sting you!"
But Lily did not listen. She was too curious and playful. She touched the hive with her finger. It was sticky and warm. She smiled and said, "It feels nice, Ben!"
But then, the bees noticed her. They came out of the hole and flew around her. They were angry and scared. They made a loud buzzing sound and tried to sting her.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. She felt a sharp pain on her hand and arm. She let go of the hive and fell from the branch. She landed on the ground and started to cry.
"Help, help, help!" Ben shouted. He saw his sister fall and get hurt. He was scared and sad. He climbed down the tree and ran to her. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry. Are you OK?"
Lily was not OK. She had many red bumps on her skin. They were swollen and itchy. She felt sick and dizzy. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry. I was silly and naughty. I should have listened to you."
Ben said, "It's OK, Lily. It's OK. We will go home and tell Mom and Dad. They will help you. They will make you feel better."
They held hands and walked home. They learned a lesson. They learned that bees are not playful. They learned that they should not touch the hive. They learned that they should listen to each other.

One day, a curious boy named Ben saw a big black bird on a tree. It was a raven. Ben wanted to talk to the raven, so he ran to the tree and said, "Hello, raven! What are you doing?"
The raven looked at Ben and said, "Caw, caw! I am looking for food. Do you have any food for me?"
Ben shook his head and said, "No, I don't have any food. But I have a toy car. Do you want to play with it?"
The raven tilted his head and said, "Caw, caw! What is a toy car? How do you play with it?"
Ben smiled and said, "A toy car is a small thing that looks like a real car. You can push it and make it go. Here, I will show you." He took out his toy car from his pocket and pushed it on the ground.
The raven flew down from the tree and landed next to the toy car. He pecked at it and said, "Caw, caw! This is fun. Can I have it?"
Ben said, "No, you can't have it. It is mine. But you can play with it with me. We can be friends."
The raven nodded and said, "Caw, caw! Okay, we can be friends. But can I seat on your shoulder?"
Ben said, "Yes, you can seat on my shoulder. But be careful not to scratch me with your claws."
The raven flapped his wings and said, "Caw, caw! Thank you, Ben. You are very nice. Let's play with the toy car together."
And so, Ben and the raven played with the toy car and became friends. They had a lot of fun and learned new things from each other.

They put their letters in envelopes and stuck some mints on them as stamps. Mints were their favorite candy, and they thought they looked like shiny coins. They put their envelopes in a bag and went around the room, giving them to their toys.
When they came to the lion, Ben said, "Here is your mail, Mr. Lion. You are fierce and brave." He handed him the envelope and smiled.
But the lion did not smile back. He roared and grabbed the envelope with his teeth. He tore it open and ate the mint. Then he looked at Ben and licked his lips.
"Mr. Lion, what are you doing?" Ben asked, scared.
"I am hungry, and you are my mail, too," the lion said, and pounced on Ben.
Sara saw what was happening and ran to help her brother. She grabbed a pillow and threw it at the lion. "Leave him alone, you mean lion!" she shouted.
The pillow hit the lion on the head and made him dizzy. He let go of Ben and fell on the floor. Sara and Ben hugged each other and ran away from the lion.
They decided to play something else and never mail anything to the lion again. They also hid their mints from him, just in case.

"Can I strike the ball?" Tom asks Sam.
"Yes, you can. But be careful. The ball is very fast," Sam says.
Tom runs to the ball. He strikes the ball with his foot. The ball flies in the air. It lands on a spot on the grass. The spot is cold and wet.
"Oops! The ball is in the mud!" Tom says.
Sam runs to the ball. He picks up the ball. The ball is dirty and cold. He tries to wipe the ball with his shirt. His shirt gets dirty and cold too.
"Uh-oh! We need to clean the ball and the shirt," Sam says.
Tom and Sam look for a tap. They find a tap near the slide. They wash the ball and the shirt with the water. The water is cold and makes them shiver.
"Brrr! The water is cold!" Tom says.
"Let's go home and get warm," Sam says.
Tom and Sam take the ball and the shirt. They say goodbye to the park. They walk home with their teeth chattering. They are cold but happy. They had fun playing with the ball.

The little girl thought for a moment, then she pointed to her garden and said: "I'm pretty sure it's in there. I can show you if you want?" 
The witch smiled, thanked her and they went together to the garden. Sure enough, the herb remained there, in the little garden!
The witch thanked the little girl again and said: "Thank you so much! I'm so happy I have everything that I need now." 
And from then on, the old witch and her little neighbor remained good friends.

Anna was a shy girl who liked to draw and write notes. She had a big box of crayons and many papers. She did not like to talk to other kids or play with them. She only liked to be alone with her notes.
One day, a new boy came to her class. His name was Ben. He was loud and mean. He liked to tease and pull other kids' hair. He saw Anna sitting by herself with her notes. He thought she was weird and boring. He wanted to make fun of her.
He walked up to her and said, "Hey, what are you doing with those papers? Are they your secret love letters? Let me see them!" He reached out his hand and tried to grab her notes.
Anna was scared and angry. She did not want him to touch her notes. They were her special things. She said, "No, go away! Leave me alone!" She held her notes close to her chest and turned away from him.
But Ben did not listen. He was stronger and faster than Anna. He pulled hard on her notes and ripped them out of her hands. He laughed and said, "Ha ha, look at these! They are just silly drawings and words. You can't even spell right. You are such a baby!"
He threw her notes in the air and watched them fall to the ground. He stomped on them and tore them apart. He did not care that he was hurting Anna's feelings. He only cared about himself.
Anna felt a big pain in her heart. She saw her notes, her precious notes, destroyed by Ben. She felt like crying. She felt like running away. She felt like she had nothing left.
She looked at Ben with hate and fear. She wished he would go away. She wished he would never come back. She wished he would disappear.
But he did not. He stayed in her class. He kept on being loud and mean. He kept on teasing and pulling other kids' hair. He kept on making Anna's life miserable.
Anna never drew or wrote notes again. She never smiled or laughed again. She never made any friends or had any fun again. She only felt sad and lonely and angry.
She hated Ben. She hated school. She hated herself.

The animal does not answer. It digs a hole in the sand and covers itself with it. Only its nose and eyes are visible.
"Maybe it is shy. Or maybe it is playing hide and seek," Lily says.
"Let's play with it. Maybe it will come out and be our friend," Ben says.
They take some sand and make a small hill next to the animal's hole. They put a stick on top of the hill and pretend it is a flag.
"Look, little animal. We made you a castle. Do you like it?" Lily asks.
The animal does not move. It stays in its hole and watches them.
"Maybe it is hungry. Or maybe it is tired," Ben says.
They go to the kitchen and get some carrots and water. They put them in a bowl and bring them to the sandbox.
"Here, little animal. We brought you some food and drink. Do you want some?" Ben asks.
The animal sniffs the bowl and comes out of its hole. It takes a bite of a carrot and drinks some water. It looks happy and grateful.
"Yay, it likes us. It is not shy anymore," Lily says.
They pet the animal and give it a name. They call it Sandy.
"Sandy, do you want to play with us? We can swing, slide and do exercise," Ben says.
The animal nods and follows them. It swings, slides and runs with them. It is fast and agile. It is harmless and fun.
Ben and Lily are happy. They have a new friend. They play with Sandy until it is time to go inside.
"Bye, Sandy. We will see you tomorrow. We love you," Ben and Lily say.
The animal waves and goes back to its hole. It covers itself with sand and sleeps. It loves them too.

But today, Lisa felt a little scared. Miss Amy said they would learn a new dance, and Lisa did not know if she could do it. She did not want to make a mistake or fall down. She wanted to be a good dancer.
"Lisa, are you ready?" Miss Amy asked, smiling. "We are going to start soon."
Lisa nodded, but she felt her tummy hurt. She wished she could stay home and play with her toys.
"Lisa, you look worried," Miss Amy said, gently. "Is something wrong?"
Lisa shook her head, but she could not speak. She felt her throat tight.
"Lisa, it's okay to be nervous," Miss Amy said, kindly. "But you don't have to be afraid. We are going to have fun and learn together. You are a smart and brave girl, and you can do anything you want. Just relax and enjoy the music. And remember, I am here to help you."
Miss Amy gave Lisa a hug and a kiss. She took her hand and led her to the dance floor. Lisa felt a little better. She looked at Miss Amy and smiled.
"Thank you, Miss Amy," Lisa said, softly. "You are the best teacher ever."
Miss Amy smiled back. "You are very welcome, Lisa. You are the best student ever. Now, let's dance!"
Lisa followed Miss Amy's steps and moved her arms and legs. She listened to the music and felt happy. She forgot about her fear and had fun. She was careful not to bump into anyone, but she also relaxed and let go. She felt like a star.
Lisa loved her dance class. She was glad she came. She learned a new dance, and she made Miss Amy proud. She also made herself proud. She was a good dancer.

Tom is a little pig who lives in a big barn with his mom and dad and many brothers and sisters. He likes to play in the mud, eat corn and apples, and snuggle with his family. But today, he is not feeling well. He has a sore throat, a runny nose, and a fever. He does not want to play or eat. He just wants to rest.
"Mom, I don't feel good," he says to his mom, who is busy making breakfast for the other pigs.
"I know, my sweetie. You are sick. You need to rest and drink some water. I will bring you some soup later," she says, giving him a kiss on his forehead.
"Can I stay in the barn today? I don't want to go outside. It is cold and windy," he says, shivering.
"Of course, you can. You can stay in your cozy bed and read some books or listen to some music. I will check on you often. Don't worry, you will get better soon," she says, tucking him in.
Tom feels sad. He misses his friends and his fun. He wishes he could join them in the yard, where they are running, jumping, and laughing. He hears them through the window, and he feels lonely. He tries to read a book, but he cannot focus. He tries to listen to some music, but he cannot enjoy it. He closes his eyes and tries to sleep, but he cannot relax.
"Mom, I'm bored," he says, when his mom comes back with a bowl of soup.
"I know, my sweetie. Being sick is no fun. But you have to rest and eat some soup. It will make you feel better. And soon, you will be able to play again. I promise," she says, spooning some soup into his mouth.
Tom eats some soup, but he does not like it. He wants some corn and apples, but his mom says they are too hard for his sore throat. He wants some cuddles, but his mom says he has to stay in his bed, so he does not spread his germs to the other pigs. He wants some company, but his mom says she has to take care of the other pigs, who need her too. He feels sad and alone.
"Mom, I love you," he says, when his mom leaves.
"I love you too, my sweetie. You are my brave and strong pig. You will get well soon. Just rest and dream of happy things," she says, blowing him a kiss.
Tom tries to rest and dream of happy things. He dreams of playing in the mud, eating corn and apples, and snuggling with his family. He dreams of being healthy and happy again. He dreams of the big barn, where he feels safe and loved. He smiles in his sleep, and he feels a little better.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their dog, Spot. Spot is a loyal dog. He always follows them and protects them from danger.
One day, Anna and Ben want to go to the park. They ask their mom if they can take Spot with them. Mom says yes, but they have to brush Spot first. Spot has a lot of fur and it gets dirty and tangled.
Anna and Ben grab the brush and go to Spot. They start to brush his fur, but Spot does not like it. He wiggles and barks and tries to run away. Anna and Ben complain.
"Spot, stop moving! You are making it hard for us to brush you!" Anna says.
"Spot, be quiet! You are hurting our ears with your barking!" Ben says.
Spot does not listen. He thinks brushing is boring and painful. He wants to go to the park and have fun.
Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is going on. She sees Anna and Ben struggling with Spot. She smiles and says, "I know Spot does not like brushing, but it is good for him. It makes his fur shiny and healthy. It also shows him that you love him and care for him. He is a loyal dog, and he deserves your kindness and patience."
Anna and Ben think about what mom says. They realize that mom is right. They love Spot and they want him to be happy and well. They decide to try again. They speak to Spot in a gentle and calm voice. They praise him and pet him when he stays still. They brush his fur slowly and carefully. Spot feels the difference. He relaxes and stops wiggling and barking. He even licks Anna and Ben's faces to show his gratitude.
Soon, Spot's fur is smooth and shiny. Anna and Ben are proud of their work. They hug Spot and say, "Good boy, Spot! You are a loyal dog, and we are loyal to you. We are sorry for complaining. We are ready to go to the park now. Do you want to come with us?"
Spot wags his tail and barks happily. He does want to go to the park with them. He follows them to the door and waits for mom to put on his leash. He knows that Anna and Ben are his best friends, and he will always be loyal to them.
The moral of the story is: Be kind and patient with your loyal friends, even when they do something you don't like. They will appreciate your love and care, and they will be loyal to you in return.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big toy bear. They call him Bob. Bob is brown and soft. He has a red hat and a blue scarf.
One day, Tim and Sam want to make a house for Bob. They find some sticks and leaves. They work hard to build a house. They make a door, a window and a roof. They are happy. They say, "Bob, this is your house. You can sleep here and be warm."
But then, they hear a loud roar. They see a real bear. He is big and black. He has sharp teeth and claws. He is mighty. He is angry. He sees the house. He thinks it is his house. He runs to the house. He breaks the door, the window and the roof. He says, "This is my house. Go away!"
Tim and Sam are scared. They run to Bob. They hug him. They say, "Bob, help us! The bear is mean. He broke your house. He wants to hurt us!"
Bob is brave. He stands up. He looks at the real bear. He says, "No, this is not your house. This is my house. These are my friends. You are bad. You go away!"
The real bear is surprised. He sees Bob. He sees his red hat and blue scarf. He thinks, "This is not a real bear. This is a toy bear. He is not mighty. He is silly." He laughs. He says, "You are not a bear. You are a toy. You cannot stop me. I can do what I want."
He tries to grab Bob. But then, he hears a loud bark. He sees a dog. He is big and white. He has a collar and a leash. He is Tim's dog. He is Rex. He is mighty. He is angry. He sees the bear. He thinks, "This is a bad bear. He is hurting my friends. He is breaking their house. He is taking their toy. I will stop him."
He runs to the bear. He bites his leg. He barks. He says, "Leave them alone! This is their house. This is their toy. You are bad. You go away!"
The bear is scared. He feels pain. He hears Rex. He thinks, "This is a real dog. He is mighty. He is not silly. He can stop me. I cannot do what I want." He drops Bob. He runs away. He says, "Sorry, sorry, sorry. I will not come back. I will find another house."
Tim and Sam are happy. They thank Rex. They say, "Rex, you are a hero. You saved us. You saved Bob. You scared the bear. You are mighty." They hug him. They give him a bone.
They fix the house. They put back the door, the window and the roof. They say, "Bob, this is your house. You can sleep here and be warm. You are brave. You are mighty. You are our friend." They hug him. They play with him.
They have fun in the park. They are friends. They are happy. The end.

Mommy nods. "I see. And what are your drums made of?"
Anna and Ben look at their drums. They are not real drums. They are fake drums. They are pots and pans and lids and spoons.
"They are fake drums, Mommy!" Ben says. "But they sound good!"
Mommy laughs. "They do sound good, but they also sound loud. How about we play something quieter for a while? Maybe we can read a book or draw a picture?"
Anna and Ben think for a moment. They like to play with their drums, but they also like to read and draw. And they love Mommy.
"Okay, Mommy!" they say. "We can play something quieter. But can we play with our drums again later?"
Mommy hugs them. "Of course you can, my little drummers. But only for a little bit. And not too loud, okay?"
"Okay, Mommy!" they say. They put away their fake drums and follow Mommy to the living room. They are happy to play something quieter, but they still feel the rhythm in their hearts.

Tom was sad and confused. He did not know what to do. But then, he saw a little girl crying. She was lost and could not find her way home. Tom decided to help her.
Together, they found the little girl's home. Her family was so happy that they gave Tom a big hug. Tom felt warm and loved. That was when he understood the note. Being rich was not about having a lot of things, but about helping others and feeling loved.

Anna liked to play with metal things. She had a metal spoon, a metal cup, and a metal car. She liked to make noises with them and pretend they were magic.
One day, she saw a man with a big truck. He had many metal things in his truck. He stopped near Anna's house and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you want to see my metal things? I sell them for money."
Anna was curious. She ran to the man and said, "Yes, please. What are they?"
The man smiled and showed her his metal things. He had metal cans, metal wires, metal pipes, and metal tools. He said, "These are things I find in the trash. I sell them to people who need them. They are not very pretty, but they are useful."
Anna looked at the metal things. She thought they were not ordinary. She thought they were special. She said, "Can I have one? I like metal things. They are fun to play with."
The man laughed and said, "Sure, you can have one. But you have to give me something in return. What do you have to trade?"
Anna thought for a moment. She did not have money. She did not have toys. She only had her metal spoon, her metal cup, and her metal car. She loved them very much. She did not want to give them away.
She said, "I'm sorry, mister. I don't have anything to trade. I only have my metal things. They are my friends. I can't sell them."
The man nodded and said, "That's okay, little girl. I understand. You love your metal things. They are your treasure. You don't have to sell them. You can keep them. But you can still look at my metal things. Maybe you can find something you like."
Anna smiled and said, "Thank you, mister. You are very nice. Can I look at your metal things?"
The man said, "Of course, you can. Come, I'll show you."
Anna followed the man to his truck. She looked at his metal things. She saw a metal star, a metal bell, and a metal ring. She thought they were beautiful. She said, "Wow, mister. You have very nice metal things. They are not ordinary. They are magic."
The man smiled and said, "Thank you, little girl. You have a good eye. You know what? I'll give you one of these metal things. You can have it for free. You don't have to trade anything. You can have it as a gift. Which one do you want?"
Anna was surprised and happy. She said, "Really, mister? You are very kind. Can I have the metal star? I like stars. They make me happy."
The man said, "Sure, you can have the metal star. Here you go. It's yours. I hope it makes you happy."
Anna took the metal star and hugged it. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you, mister. You are the best. I love the metal star. It's my new friend. I'll take good care of it."
The man said, "You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome, little girl. You are very sweet. I'm glad you love the metal star. It's a good friend. You take good care of it."
Anna said, "I will, I will, I will, mister. Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye."
The man said, "Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye."
Anna ran back to her house. She showed her metal spoon, her metal cup, her metal car, and her metal star to her mom. She said, "Look, mom. Look what I have. I have metal things. They are my friends. They are not ordinary. They are magic."
Her mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful, Anna. I'm happy for you. You have metal things. They are your friends. They are not ordinary. They are magic."

Once upon a time, a little girl named Sara went with her mom to a market. As soon as they got to the market, Sara ran over to the produce aisle and found a bright, red apple.

Sara watched as her mom gently placed the apple on the scale, and the little needle moved around until it reached two pounds.
"Two pounds is the perfect figure," her mom said. "This apple is just right!"
Sara gave a grin as her mom put the apple in the cart. Then she walked over and found a small, yellow banana.
Sara raised it up to show her mom. "Mommy, can I have this banana, too?" she asked.
Her mom smiled again. "Let's weigh it first, honey," her mom said.
Sara watched intently as the needle moved around until it reached one pound. "That is a very flexible figure," her mom said.
Excited, Sara put the banana in the cart with the apple, and together they walked home.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play outside. One night, they saw the moon in the sky. It was big and bright and round.
"Look, Lily, the moon is smiling at us!" Max said.
"Hi, moon!" Lily said. "You are very pretty. Can we be your friends?"
The moon did not answer, but it seemed to wink at them.
"Maybe the moon is shy," Max said. "We should be polite and say good night."
"Good night, moon," Lily and Max said together. "We hope to see you again soon."
They went inside and got ready for bed. Their mom tucked them in and kissed them.
"Did you have fun outside?" she asked.
"Yes, mom, we saw the moon and talked to it," Lily said.
"We were polite and said good night," Max said.
"That's very nice of you," mom said. "The moon is a good friend to have. Do you remember the song I taught you about the moon?"
"Yes, mom, we remember," Lily and Max said.
They sang the song softly with their mom. It went like this:
I see the moon and the moon sees me
God bless the moon and God bless me
I love the moon and the moon loves me
Good night, moon, and good night, me
They finished the song and closed their eyes. They dreamed of the moon and its smile.

Ben and Lily were playing with their crayons and paper. They liked to draw and write letters. Ben knew how to write his name and Lily knew how to write hers. They were very proud of their letters.
But then, Ben saw that Lily had an enormous letter L on her paper. He wanted to have an enormous letter too. He took his red crayon and tried to mark a big B on his paper. But he made a mistake and marked over Lily's L.
"Hey, that's my L!" Lily shouted. "You marked over it! That's not nice!"
"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I wanted to have a big letter too. But I messed up. Can I fix it?"
Lily was angry and sad. She liked her L and she did not want Ben to mark over it. She did not want to share her paper with him. She said, "No, you can't fix it. You ruined it. Go away!"
Ben felt bad. He did not mean to hurt Lily's feelings. He liked Lily and he wanted to play with her. He said, "Please, Lily, don't be mad. I'll give you a new paper and a new crayon. And I'll help you write a new L. Can we be friends again?"
Lily looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry and that he wanted to make up. She thought for a moment. Then she said, "Okay, Ben. I forgive you. You can give me a new paper and a new crayon. And we can write big letters together. But don't mark over my L again, okay?"
Ben smiled and nodded. He said, "Okay, Lily. I won't mark over your L again. I promise. Thank you for being my friend."
They hugged and then they went back to their crayons and paper. They wrote big letters and drew pictures. They had fun and they were happy.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play at the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But their favorite thing was to spin on the round seat. They would sit on the seat and push with their feet until they went very fast.
One day, they saw a new boy at the park. His name was Ben and he looked sad. Lily and Sam wanted to be nice, so they asked him if he wanted to play with them. Ben nodded and followed them to the round seat.
"Sit here, Ben," Lily said. "We will spin you and make you happy."
Lily and Sam pushed the seat hard and Ben started to spin. He smiled at first, but then he felt sick. He wanted to stop, but Lily and Sam did not hear him. They thought he was having fun.
"Stop, stop, please!" Ben cried. "I feel dizzy. I want to get off."
Lily and Sam finally heard him and stopped the seat. Ben stumbled off and ran to a bench. He felt very bad and his face was pale.
Lily and Sam felt sorry for Ben. They realized they had been too rough with him. They ran to the bench and apologized to him.
"We are sorry, Ben," Sam said. "We did not mean to hurt you. We just wanted to play with you."
"We did not know you did not like to spin," Lily said. "We like to spin, but you don't. That's okay. Everyone is different."
Ben forgave them and thanked them for being kind. He said he liked to play other things, like catch or tag. Lily and Sam agreed to play those things with him. They became friends and had fun at the park.
The moral of the story is: Be careful with your friends and respect their likes and dislikes. Don't force them to do something they don't enjoy.

Lily and Tom were playing knights and dragons in the garden. Lily had a big stick that she pretended was a sword. Tom had a green scarf that he wrapped around his head like a dragon.
"Roar! I am a fierce dragon and I will steal your sword, knight!" Tom said, running towards Lily.
"No, you won't! I am a brave knight and I will stop you, dragon!" Lily said, swinging her stick.
They chased each other around the trees and the flowers, having fun. But then, Tom saw a shiny metal sword hanging on the wall of the shed. It was Lily's dad's sword, and he liked to show it to his friends.
"Wow, look at that sword! It is so shiny and sharp! I want it!" Tom said, forgetting about the game.
He ran to the shed and grabbed the sword. It was heavy and hard, not like the stick. He felt proud and powerful.
"Lily, look what I have! I have a real sword!" Tom said, waving the sword in the air.
Lily saw Tom with the sword and felt scared and angry. She knew it was her dad's sword and that he did not like anyone to touch it.
"Tom, that is not your sword! That is my dad's sword! You have to give it back! You are stealing!" Lily said, running to Tom.
But Tom did not listen. He liked the sword too much. He thought he was a real dragon now.
"Roar! I am the strongest dragon and I have the best sword! You can't have it, knight! Go away!" Tom said, pointing the sword at Lily.
Lily felt sad and hurt. She did not want to play with Tom anymore. She wanted her stick back. She had an idea. She remembered that her stick was flexible, not like the sword. She could bend it and twist it.
She picked up her stick and made a loop at the end. She threw the loop over the sword and pulled it hard. The sword slipped out of Tom's hand and fell to the ground. Lily grabbed the sword and ran to the shed. She hung it back on the wall.
"Ha! I got the sword back, dragon! You can't steal it anymore! And you can't play with me anymore, either! You are a bad dragon and a bad friend!" Lily said, sticking out her tongue.
Tom felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had been wrong to take the sword and to be mean to Lily. He wanted to say sorry and to play with her again.
"Lily, wait! I am sorry! I was silly and greedy! I don't want the sword anymore! I want to play with you! Please, can we be friends again?" Tom said, following Lily.
Lily stopped and looked at Tom. She saw that he was sincere and that he had learned his lesson. She felt sorry for him and decided to forgive him.
"Okay, Tom. I forgive you. But you have to promise not to steal anything again. And you have to be nice to me. And you have to play with my stick, not the sword. Deal?" Lily said, holding out her hand.
"Deal, Lily. I promise. And I am sorry. And I like your stick. It is more fun than the sword. Can we play knights and dragons again?" Tom said, shaking her hand.
"Yes, Tom. We can play knights and dragons again. But this time, you have to be a good dragon. And I have to be a good knight. And we have to share and help each other. Okay?" Lily said, smiling.
"Okay, Lily. That sounds good. Let's play!" Tom said, smiling back.
They hugged and picked up their stick and scarf. They ran to the garden and played knights and dragons again. They were happy and they were friends.

"Look, mom, the otter is sliding on its belly!" Lily said, pointing at the pool.
"That looks like fun, doesn't it?" mom said, smiling.
"Can we slide too, mom?" Ben asked.
"Not here, Ben. The pool is for the otter, not for us. But maybe we can find a slide somewhere else in the zoo," mom said.
They walked around the zoo, looking for a slide. They saw a big blue slide near the penguin house. It looked like a big wave.
"Wow, mom, look at that slide!" Lily said, excited.
"That looks like a great slide, Lily. Do you want to try it?" mom asked.
"Yes, yes, yes!" Lily said, nodding.
"What about you, Ben?" mom asked.
Ben looked at the slide. He felt a little scared. It was very high and fast.
"I don't know, mom. It looks scary," Ben said, shaking his head.
Mom hugged Ben. "It's okay, Ben. You don't have to slide if you don't want to. You can watch Lily and me, or you can look at the penguins. They are very cute and funny," mom said.
Ben looked at the penguins. They were black and white, and they waddled and splashed in the water. They made funny noises.
"Okay, mom. I will look at the penguins. Maybe they will make me laugh," Ben said.
Mom kissed Ben. "That's a good idea, Ben. I'm sure they will. And maybe later, you can try the slide if you feel like it. No pressure, okay?" mom said.
"Okay, mom. Have fun, Lily!" Ben said.
Lily ran to the slide. She climbed up the stairs and sat on the edge. She looked at mom and smiled.
"Are you ready, Lily?" mom asked.
"Yes, mom. I'm ready. This is going to be awesome!" Lily said.
She pushed herself off the edge and slid down the blue slide. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She screamed with joy.
"Wheeeeee!" Lily said.
She reached the bottom and splashed into a small pool of water. She got up and shook herself off. She looked at mom and Ben.
"That was so fun, mom! That was the best slide ever! You have to try it, mom!" Lily said.
She looked at Ben. "And you too, Ben! You will love it, I promise! It's not scary, it's fun! Come on, Ben, please!" Lily said.
She ran to Ben and took his hand. She pulled him towards the slide.
"Come on, Ben, please! Trust me, it's fun! I recommend it!" Lily said.
Ben looked at Lily. He saw her happy face and sparkling eyes. He felt her warm hand and gentle pull. He looked at the slide. He felt a little curious. Maybe it was fun. Maybe he could try it. Just once.
"Okay, Lily. Okay. I will try it. Just once," Ben said.
Lily cheered. "Yay, Ben! Yay! You are brave, Ben! You are awesome, Ben! Come on, let's go!" Lily said.
She dragged Ben to the slide. Mom followed them, smiling. She was proud of both of them. She was happy to see them have fun. She was glad they were siblings. She loved them very much.

Lily stopped crying and hugged Ben back. "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I ran too fast. I wanted to play with you."
They walked to their mom and dad, who were sitting on chairs. They saw Lily's knee and put a band-aid on it. They told Lily and Ben to be more careful and not to run on the icy floor. They said they could still play in the pool, but they had to walk slowly and hold hands.
Lily and Ben learned their lesson. They played in the pool together, but they did not run or push. They had fun and stayed safe. They were happy and thankful. They learned that the icy floor can be dangerous, and that they should always look out for each other.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. They also liked to swim in the water, but they had to be careful of the jellyfish. Jellyfish were soft and pretty, but they could sting and hurt.
One day, Lily saw a big jellyfish near the shore. She wanted to touch it and see how it felt. She ran to the water and reached for the jellyfish. Ben saw her and shouted, "Lily, no! That's a jellyfish! It can sting you!"
But Lily did not listen. She thought Ben was just being mean and bossy. She grabbed the jellyfish and lifted it up. She felt a sharp pain in her hand and dropped the jellyfish. She started to cry and ran back to the sand.
Ben followed her and saw her hand was red and swollen. He felt sorry for her and said, "Lily, I'm sorry you got hurt. But you should have listened to me. I was trying to help you. Jellyfish are not toys. They are animals that need to be left alone."
Lily looked at Ben and realized he was right. She said, "Ben, I'm sorry I did not listen to you. You are my brother and you know more than me. You were being important and kind. Thank you for caring about me."
Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you and I want you to be safe. Next time, let's stir the water with a stick and see what we can find. Maybe we can find some fish or crabs or starfish. But no more jellyfish, okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Ben. Let's do that. I love you too."
Mom and dad came and saw Lily's hand. They put some cream on it and gave her a bandage. They also praised Ben for being a good brother and helping Lily. They said, "You two are very brave and smart. We are proud of you. You learned a valuable lesson today. You learned to respect nature and to listen to each other. That's very important."
Lily and Ben agreed and hugged mom and dad. They had a fun day at the beach, but they also learned something new. They learned to stir the water, not the jellyfish.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to the grocery with her mom. They needed to buy food for dinner. Sue's mom said, "Sue, remember to stay near me." Sue nodded and promised to stay close.
They walked around the grocery and saw many interesting things. Sue liked the big, round oranges and the shiny apples. But then, Sue saw a big, green frog near the vegetables! Sue was so excited, she forgot what her mom said.
Sue followed the frog and when it stopped, she said, "Hello, Mr. Frog!" The frog looked at Sue and said, "Hello, Sue! I am a magic frog. I can give you a wish if you help me find my way home." Sue thought about her wish and decided to help the frog.
Sue and the frog found the frog's home near a pond behind the grocery. The frog was happy and said, "Thank you, Sue. What is your wish?" Sue thought for a moment and said, "I wish to always remember what my mom tells me." The frog smiled and granted her wish.
From that day on, Sue always remembered what her mom said and never got lost again. And sometimes, she would visit her new friend, the magic frog, at the pond behind the grocery.

Bobo was sad because he was a big bear and had a lot of weight. He sat down and thought about what to do. Then, he had an idea! Bobo went to his room and found a big box. He put all his toys in the box to make it heavy.
Bobo carried the box to the swing and put it on the swing. He thought the swing would not break now because it already had heavy weight on it. But, something unexpected happened! When Bobo sat on the swing, it did not break. The swing was strong enough for Bobo and the box!
Bobo was very happy that he could play on the swing. From that day on, he was not careless anymore. He put things back where they should be and always read signs carefully. And, he played on the swing every day with his big box of toys.

Tim and Mia liked to play on the beach. They made sand castles and looked for shells. Sometimes they saw big waves that crashed on the shore. They liked to run away from the waves and laugh.
One day, they saw a big ship on the water. It was very old and had many holes. Tim said, "Look, Mia, it's a pirate ship! Maybe it has treasure inside!"
Mia said, "No, Tim, it's not a pirate ship. It's just a broken ship. There is no treasure inside. Pirates are not real."
Tim said, "Yes, they are, Mia. I believe in pirates. They have swords and hats and parrots. They sail the seas and find gold and jewels. Maybe they left some on the ship. Let's go and see!"
Mia said, "No, Tim, it's too far and too dangerous. The ship might sink or the waves might be too strong. We should stay on the beach and play with our sand castles. They are safe and fun."
Tim said, "But, Mia, I want to see the ship. It's ancient and mysterious. Maybe we can find a map or a coin or a skull. It would be so cool!"
Mia said, "Tim, you are silly. You have a big imagination. But I don't want to go with you. You can go by yourself if you want, but I will stay here."
Tim said, "Fine, Mia, I will go by myself. You are boring. I will be back soon with a treasure. You will see!"
Tim ran to the water and swam to the ship. He climbed on the deck and looked around. He saw some ropes and barrels and planks. He did not see any treasure. He felt sad and scared. He wished he had stayed with Mia. He heard a loud noise. It was a wave that hit the ship. The ship started to move and tilt. Tim screamed for help. He wanted to go back to the beach. He wanted to play with Mia and his sand castles. He hoped Mia would hear him and come to save him. He hoped she would still be his friend. He hoped the wave would not take him away.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Daisy and Bill. Daisy was deaf, so she couldn't always understand what Bill was saying. But she understood the love in his eyes, and he soon learned different ways to talk to her without words. Whenever Daisy felt small, Bill put his arms around her like a stitch and let her know she wasn't alone.
One day Bill asked Daisy why she was so quiet. Daisy couldn't answer with words, so she held up her hands and showed him her stitches. They were different from his stitches and they made her look different. Daisy was so scared he would no longer love her when he saw them.
But Bill didn't flinch. "That's okay," he said, putting his arms around her. "I still love you, Daisy."
The moral of the story is that true love is deaf to differences. No matter how different we are from one another, true friendship and love means being there for one another unconditionally. We can find joy in each other's differences and love each other in spite of them.

"Be careful, Lily!" Ben says. "The slide is wet and slippery!"
Lily does not listen. She sits on the slide and pushes herself down. But she goes too fast and slips off the slide. She falls on the grass and hurts her knee. She cries out loud.
"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!" Lily says.
Ben runs to Lily and hugs her. He helps her stand up and walks with her to their mom. Their mom is sitting on a bench with a bag. She sees Lily's knee and takes out a band-aid and a pill.
"Lily, you have a boo-boo. Let me put this band-aid on your knee. It will make it better," Mom says.
She sticks the band-aid on Lily's knee and kisses it. Then she gives Lily a pill.
"This is a pill. It will make the pain go away. But you have to be careful with pills. You can only take them when Mom or Dad gives them to you. And you have to swallow them with water. Do you understand?" Mom says.
Lily nods. She takes the pill and drinks some water from Mom's bottle. She feels better.
"Thank you, Mom. I'm sorry I was not careful. I will listen to Ben next time," Lily says.
Mom smiles and hugs Lily and Ben.
"That's good, Lily. I'm glad you're okay. And I'm proud of you, Ben, for being a good brother and helping Lily. Now, do you want to play some more in the park?" Mom says.
Lily and Ben nod. They hold Mom's hand and go back to the park. They play on the swings and the seesaw. They do not go on the slide again. They have fun and are careful.
