Sara and Ben are friends who like to play on the farm. They like to see the cows, the pigs, the chickens and the horses. One day, they decide to play hide and seek in the barn. Sara counts to ten and then looks for Ben.
She looks behind the hay, under the wagon, and in the stalls. She cannot find Ben anywhere. She hears a giggle from above. She looks up and sees Ben standing on a beam. He is holding a rope.
"Found you!" Sara says. "How did you get up there?"
"I climbed the ladder," Ben says. "It was fun. Watch this!" He swings on the rope and jumps down. He lands on a pile of straw.
"Wow, that was cool!" Sara says. "Can I try?"
"Sure, but be careful," Ben says. He helps Sara climb the ladder. She stands on the beam and grabs the rope. She feels excited and scared.
"Ready?" Ben asks.
"Ready!" Sara says. She swings on the rope and tries to jump like Ben. But she jumps too soon and misses the straw. She falls on the hard floor. She hurts her knee and her elbow. She starts to cry.
Ben runs to her and hugs her. "Are you okay?" he asks.
"No, I'm not okay," Sara says. "I'm hurt and I'm embarrassed. Everyone saw me fall."
"No, they didn't," Ben says. "No one is here. Only me and you. And I don't think you're embarrassed. I think you're brave. You tried something new and hard. That's what friends do."
Sara stops crying and smiles. "Really?" she asks.
"Really," Ben says. "You're my best friend. And I'm sorry you got hurt. Do you want to go see the nurse?"
Sara nods. "Yes, please," she says. "But can we play again later?"
"Of course," Ben says. "But next time, let's play something else. Maybe tag or hopscotch. Or we can feed the animals."
"Okay," Sara says. "That sounds good. I like the farm. And I like you."
They hold hands and walk out of the barn. They are still friends.

"Let me open it!" Ben says. He pulls on the tape.
"No, it's mine!" Anna says. She pushes him away.
They tug and push and yell. The box falls over and breaks. They see a lot of clothes and toys and books. They are for a baby.
"Mama and Papa have a surprise for us," Anna says. She picks up a pink dress.
"What is it?" Ben asks. He sees a blue car.
"They are going to give us a sister," Anna says. She smiles.
"A sister?" Ben says. He frowns.
"Yes, a sister. She is in Mama's tummy. She will come out soon. She will be small and cute and we will love her," Anna says.
Ben is not sure. He likes to be the only boy. He does not want to share his toys and books. He does not want a sister.
"Mama and Papa will reveal her to us when she is ready," Anna says. She hugs the dress.
Ben thinks. He loves Mama and Papa. He loves Anna too, even when they fight. Maybe a sister will be fun. Maybe he can teach her how to build and play. Maybe he can protect her and make her laugh.
He looks at Anna. She is shy. She does not have many friends. She likes to stay at home and draw. Maybe a sister will be good for her. Maybe she will have someone to talk to and share with.
He picks up the car. He gives it to Anna.
"Here, you can have this. It is for our sister," he says.
Anna smiles. She gives him the dress.
"Thank you. You can have this. It is for our sister too," she says.
They hug. They are happy. They are excited. They can't wait to meet their sister.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it.
Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big rope hanging from a tree. They wanted to swing on it and have fun. Lily ran to the rope first and grabbed it. She said, "This is my rope. You can't have it."
Ben was angry. He wanted to swing on the rope too. He said, "No, it's not your rope. It's for everyone. Let me have a turn." He tried to pull the rope from Lily, but she held on tight. They both pulled and pulled, but neither of them would let go.
They started to yell and scream at each other. They did not hear the loud snap. The rope broke and they both fell to the ground. They hit their heads and their arms and their legs. They cried and cried. They were hurt and sad.
A lady came and saw them. She said, "What happened? Why were you fighting over the rope?" She helped them get up and took them to a bench. She said, "You should not be greedy and mean. You should share and be nice. The rope was not yours. It was for everyone. Now look what you did. You broke it and you hurt yourselves. You are very naughty."
Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry. We were wrong. We should have shared and been nice." They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry. We are friends." But the lady was still angry. She said, "You are too late. You can't play on the rope anymore. You have to go home now. And you have to tell your parents what you did. They will be very angry too."
Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to go home. They did not want to tell their parents. They wished they had not fought over the rope. They wished they had been good. They squeezed each other's hands and walked away. They had a bad day.

Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and hold her hand. She said the steam train was very hot and loud and could hurt them. She also said they had to wear their coats and hats, because it was cold outside.
Anna and Ben put on their coats and hats and followed mom to the train station. They saw the steam train waiting on the platform. It was bigger and shinier than their toy trains. They heard the whistle and the hiss of the steam. They smelled the coal and the oil.
They wanted to touch the train, but mom said no. She said it was too hot and dirty. She said they could look at it from a distance. She said they could wave to the driver and the passengers.
Anna and Ben waved to the driver and the passengers. They saw some people get on and off the train. They saw some people carry bags and boxes. They saw some people smile and some people cry.
They wondered where the train was going and what the people were doing. They asked mom if they could go on the train. Mom said no. She said the train was not for them. She said the train was for people who had to change their lives.
Anna and Ben did not understand what mom meant. They did not know why people had to change their lives. They thought it was fun to go on a train and see new places. They thought it was sad to leave their home and their friends.
They felt uncomfortable and confused. They did not like the steam train anymore. They wanted to go back to their toy trains. They told mom they were bored and cold and hungry.
Mom said they could go back home soon. She said they had to wait for the train to leave. She said they had to say goodbye to the train and the people.
Anna and Ben said goodbye to the train and the people. They did not mean it. They did not care. They just wanted to leave.
The train started to move. It made a loud noise and a lot of smoke. It went faster and faster. It disappeared into the tunnel.
Anna and Ben did not see the train anymore. They did not hear the train anymore. They did not smell the train anymore.
They only felt a big boom. They only saw a bright flash. They only smelled fire and smoke.
The tunnel had exploded. The train had crashed. The people had died.
Anna and Ben had died too.

All day long they walked and eventually the sun started to set. The bear said, "look! over there - it looks like a safe place to sleep for the night". 
The dog was unsure but the bear said, "Trust me - I know what I'm doing". The dog thought about it and decided to trust the bear.
Once they arrived at the place, they saw a cozy cave. "Yes! this is perfect," said the bear.
 
The two of them curled up near the cave entrance to sleep and fell fast asleep. In the morning the bear said, "See, I told you to trust me". 
The dog smiled and was so happy they had trusted each other enough to find such a wonderful spot to sleep. They set off on the next part of their adventure which was even more fun than before.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a small garden in her backyard. She loved to grow flowers and watch them bloom. One day, Lily found a small seed on the ground. She picked it up and thought, "I need to plant this seed and see what happens."
Lily dug a small hole in her garden and put the seed in it. She covered the seed with dirt and watered it. Every day, Lily would look at the spot where she planted the seed and say, "Grow, little seed, grow!" But nothing happened for many days.
One sunny day, Lily's mom came outside and saw her looking sad. "What's wrong, Lily?" she asked. Lily said, "My seed is not growing. I don't know what to do." Her mom smiled and said, "It needs sun, water, and time to grow. Be patient, and it will grow." Lily nodded and decided to wait.
After a few more days, the sun shone brightly, and Lily saw a small green sprout coming out of the ground! She was so happy and said, "Look, Mom! The seed is growing!" Her mom smiled and said, "See, with a little sun, water, and patience, your seed grew into a beautiful plant."
From that day on, Lily took care of her small plant, giving it sun and water. And as the days went by, the plant grew bigger and bigger, and soon, beautiful flowers bloomed. Lily learned that with love, care, and patience, even the smallest seed can grow into something wonderful.

Anna and Ben love to watch the trains go by. They sit on the grass near the rail and wave at the drivers. Sometimes they see big trains with many cars, and sometimes they see small trains with only one or two cars. They like to guess what the trains are carrying.
One day, they see a very big and powerful train. It is black and red, and it makes a loud noise. It has a big smokestack on the front, and it blows out white smoke. Anna and Ben are amazed by the train. They wonder what it is doing.
"Look, Ben, that train is different from the others," Anna says. "It is not electric, it is steam. It needs coal to run."
"What is coal?" Ben asks.
"Coal is a black rock that burns. The train has a car full of coal behind the smokestack. The driver has to feed the coal to the fire in the engine. That makes the steam that moves the wheels," Anna explains.
"Wow, that is cool. How do you know that?" Ben says.
"I read it in a book. The book said that steam trains are very old, and they are not used much anymore. They are very powerful, but they are also very dirty and noisy. They pollute the air and the rail," Anna says.
"Then why is that train here?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a special train. Maybe it is going to a museum, or a show, or a festival. Maybe it is carrying something important, or something fun," Anna says.
They watch the train until it disappears in the distance. They hope to see it again someday. They think it is a very interesting and powerful train. They wonder what it is feeding on.

Lily said: "You are welcome, Anna. You are the best friend ever. Now, let's have some fun and magic."
The end.
Moral value: The story teaches the value of love, gratitude, and responsibility. Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big truck with many animals inside. They wanted to see the animals, so they ran to the truck. Mom followed them and told them to be careful.
Inside the truck, they saw a lion, a zebra, a monkey, and a leopard. The leopard was sleeping on a soft mat. Ben and Lily thought the leopard was pretty, with its yellow and black spots. They wanted to touch it, but mom said no.
"Leopard is not a pet. Leopard is wild. Leopard can bite and scratch. You can look, but not touch," mom said.
But Ben did not listen. He was curious and brave. He reached out his hand and touched the leopard's tail. The leopard woke up and was angry. It turned around and slapped Ben's hand with its paw. Ben cried out in pain and fear.
"Ow! Ow! Ow! Mom, help!" Ben shouted.
Mom ran to Ben and hugged him. She checked his hand and saw a mild cut. She took out a band-aid and put it on his hand.
"I'm sorry, Ben. Leopard hurt you. You should have listened to me. Leopard is not a pet. Leopard is wild. You have to be careful with wild animals. They don't like to be touched," mom said.
Ben nodded and said sorry. He learned his lesson. He did not want to touch the leopard again. He hugged mom and said he loved her.
Lily watched and felt sorry for Ben. She also learned her lesson. She did not want to touch the leopard either. She hugged Ben and said she loved him.
The leopard watched and felt sorry too. It did not mean to hurt Ben. It was just scared and angry. It wished Ben and Lily would leave it alone. It went back to sleep on its soft mat.

Tom and Mia like to play in the park. They have a bow and some arrows. The arrows are made of sticks and feathers. They pretend to be hunters and look for animals.
One day, they see a big bird in a tree. It has yellow and black feathers and a long tail. Tom says, "Look, Mia, a bird! Let's catch it with our arrows!" Mia nods and says, "OK, Tom, you shoot first. I will shoot next."
Tom pulls the bow and aims at the bird. He lets go of the arrow. The arrow flies in the air. But it does not hit the bird. It hits a branch and falls down. The bird sees the arrow and flies away. Tom says, "Oh no, I missed!"
Mia says, "Don't worry, Tom, I will try." She pulls the bow and aims at the bird. She lets go of the arrow. The arrow flies in the air. It hits the bird in the wing. The bird cries and falls down. Mia says, "Yay, I got it!"
Tom and Mia run to the bird. They see that it is hurt and bleeding. They feel sorry for the bird. They say, "We are sorry, bird, we did not mean to hurt you. We were just playing."
The bird looks at them with sad eyes. It says, "Please help me. I need water. My wing is dry and sore."
Tom and Mia say, "OK, bird, we will help you. We will get some water and a bandage. We will make you feel better."
They go to the fountain and fill a cup with water. They find a cloth and wrap it around the bird's wing. They give the bird some water and some seeds. The bird drinks and eats. It says, "Thank you, Tom and Mia. You are kind and good. I forgive you for shooting me."
Tom and Mia say, "You are welcome, bird. We are sorry for shooting you. We will not do it again. We will be your friends."
The bird says, "I will be your friend too. But please, do not play with arrows. They are dangerous and can hurt. Play with something else, like a ball or a kite."
Tom and Mia say, "OK, bird, we will. We will play with a ball or a kite. We will have fun and be safe."
They hug the bird and say goodbye. They take their bow and arrows and put them away. They get a ball and a kite and go back to the park. They play and laugh and have fun. They are happy and the bird is happy too.

Tom and Lily were brother and sister. They liked to play in the park with their ball and their bike. One day, they saw a shiny crown on a bench. It was gold and had jewels on it.
"Wow, look at that crown!" Tom said. "It is so pretty. I want to wear it."
"No, Tom, that is not ours. Someone else left it here. Maybe they will come back for it. We should not touch it." Lily said. She was a good girl and knew how to share.
But Tom did not listen. He ran to the bench and grabbed the crown. He put it on his head and said, "I am the king of the park. I can do whatever I want."
Lily was sad and angry. She said, "Tom, that is not nice. You are being selfish and greedy. You should give the crown back. It does not belong to you."
But Tom did not care. He rode his bike around the park and shouted, "I am the king. Move out of my way. This is my park."
Soon, a man came to the park. He was looking for something. He was the owner of the crown. He was a magician who had a show in the park. He had left his crown on the bench by mistake. He was very alert and saw Tom wearing his crown.
"Hey, kid, that is my crown. Give it back to me. It is part of my costume. I need it for my show." The man said.
Tom was scared. He did not want to give the crown back. He tried to ride away, but the man was faster. He caught Tom and took the crown from him. He was very angry and said, "You are a bad kid. You should not take things that are not yours. You could have ruined my show. You should be ashamed of yourself."
Tom felt sorry. He knew he had done wrong. He said, "I am sorry, sir. I was foolish. I thought the crown was cool. I wanted to be the king. But I was not the king. I was a thief. Please forgive me."
The man was still mad, but he saw that Tom was sincere. He said, "Well, I accept your apology. But you have to learn your lesson. You have to respect other people's things. You have to be honest and kind. You have to be a good kid. Do you understand?"
Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, sir. I understand. I will never do that again. I will be a good kid. Thank you for forgiving me."
The man smiled. He said, "You are welcome. Now, go and play with your sister. And maybe you can watch my show later. I will show you some magic tricks. But remember, the real magic is in your heart."
Tom ran to Lily. He hugged her and said, "I am sorry, Lily. You were right. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. You are a good sister. Can we still play together?"
Lily smiled. She said, "Of course, Tom. I love you. You are a good brother. Come on, let's play. And maybe we can watch the magic show later. It sounds fun."
Tom and Lily played happily in the park. They learned their lesson. They learned to be honest, kind, and respectful. They learned to share and care. They learned to be good kids. And they had fun. The end.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. Sometimes they also like to pretend they are grown-ups. They have a small table and two chairs in their room. They also have cups and spoons and a pot.
One day, they decide to play coffee shop. Anna is the customer and Ben is the seller. Ben fills the pot with water and puts it on the table. He says, "Welcome to my coffee shop. What do you want to drink?"
Anna says, "I want coffee, please."
Ben says, "OK, coffee is one dollar. Do you have money?"
Anna says, "No, I don't have money. But I have this." She shows Ben a shiny necklace. It is her favorite toy. She likes how it sparkles in the light.
Ben looks at the necklace. He thinks it is very pretty. He says, "Wow, that is a nice necklace. Where did you get it?"
Anna says, "It was a gift from Grandma. She said it is very special. She said I should value it."
Ben says, "What does value mean?"
Anna says, "It means you like it a lot and you take good care of it. You don't lose it or break it or give it away."
Ben says, "Oh, I see. Well, I value this pot. It is my best toy. I use it to make coffee and tea and soup. I don't let anyone else touch it."
Anna says, "Can I touch it?"
Ben says, "No, you can't. It is mine."
Anna says, "But I want to touch it. It looks fun. Can I trade my necklace for your pot?"
Ben thinks for a moment. He likes the necklace, but he likes the pot more. He says, "No, you can't. The pot is more important to me than the necklace. I value the pot more."
Anna feels sad. She says, "But I value the necklace more. It is more important to me than the coffee. I want to keep it."
Ben says, "Then you can't have coffee. You have to pay for it."
Anna says, "But I'm thirsty. And I want to play with you."
Ben says, "Then you have to find something else to trade. Something I value more than the pot."
Anna looks around the room. She sees their books, their toys, their clothes. She doesn't know what to choose. She feels confused. She says, "I don't know what to do. Can we just share?"
Ben says, "Share? What does that mean?"
Anna says, "It means we both use something and we both enjoy it. We don't have to trade or pay. We just have fun together."
Ben says, "Oh, I see. That sounds nice. How do we do that?"
Anna says, "We can take turns. You can use my necklace for a while, and I can use your pot for a while. Then we can switch. And we can both drink coffee."
Ben says, "OK, that sounds fair. Let's try it."
Anna says, "OK, let's do it."
They smile at each other. They share the necklace and the pot. They drink the coffee. They have fun. They value each other.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big spoon. They used the spoon to pretend they were cooking, digging, or flying.
One day, their mom said, "I need the spoon to make soup. Please give it to me." Ben and Lily did not want to give the spoon. They said, "No, mom, we are playing with it. It is our spoon."
Mom said, "You can play with your other toys. The spoon is not a toy. It is a tool. I need it to make food for us. If you share the spoon, I will let you taste the soup later."
Ben and Lily thought about it. They liked soup. They wanted to taste it. But they also liked the spoon. They did not want to share it. They looked at each other. They had an idea.
They said, "OK, mom, we will share the spoon. But only if you permit us to use it first. We want to do one more thing with it." Mom said, "What do you want to do with it?" Ben and Lily said, "We want to measure how tall we are. We want to see who is taller."
Mom smiled. She said, "That is a silly thing to do with a spoon. But OK, you can do it. But hurry up. The soup is almost ready." Ben and Lily took the spoon and stood next to each other. They put the spoon on their heads. They tried to see who was taller.
They were surprised. They were the same height. The spoon was the same on both of their heads. They said, "Wow, we are twins. We are the same. We are both tall." They laughed. They felt happy.
They gave the spoon to mom. They said, "Thank you, mom, for letting us use the spoon. We are sorry we did not want to share it. We learned something new. We are twins. We are the same. We are both tall. And we love you."
Mom hugged them. She said, "I love you too, my tall twins. You are very smart and kind. I am proud of you. Now, let's go taste the soup. It is hot and yummy. And you can use your own spoons to eat it."
The end.
Moral value: Sharing is caring. We can learn from each other. We are all special and equal.

Tim went to his friend, Sue. "Sue, watch me open the heavy box," he said. Sue watched as Tim opened the box and gave her an invitation. Sue was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim! I will come to your party."
Tim gave invitations to all his friends. They all came to his birthday party. They played games, ate cake, and had fun. At the end of the party, Tim's mom said, "Good job, Tim! You shared your invitations and made your friends happy."
The moral of the story is: Sharing makes everyone happy.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big bug with many legs and a wide back. It was a beetle. They wanted to catch it and keep it in a jar.
They ran after the bug, but it was fast and smart. It hid under a leaf, then under a rock, then under a log. Tim and Sam did not give up. They wanted to be the first to catch the bug. They raced each other to find it.
But they did not watch where they were going. They bumped into each other and fell down. They hurt their knees and elbows. They also lost sight of the bug. It crawled away to a safe place.
Tim and Sam cried and rubbed their wounds. They were sad and angry. They blamed each other for making them fall. They did not want to be friends anymore.
Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She came to see what was wrong. She saw their tears and their scrapes. She hugged them and cleaned their wounds. She asked them what happened.
They told her about the bug and the race. She listened and nodded. Then she said, "I know you both like bugs, but you should not fight over them. Bugs are free and belong to nature. You should respect them and let them be. And you should also respect each other and be kind. Friends are more important than bugs. Do you understand?"
Tim and Sam nodded. They felt sorry for what they did. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They also said sorry to the bug and thanked it for showing them a lesson. They decided to play something else and share their toys. They were happy and friends again.

"Let's go somewhere else," Tom says. "This structure is not safe. It can hurt us."
But Anna is curious. She wants to see what is inside. She says, "I don't care. I want to explore. It looks like a castle."
She runs to the structure and tries to open a door. But the door is stuck. She pushes harder and harder. Suddenly, the door breaks and falls down. Anna falls with it. She screams.
Tom hears her scream and runs to help her. He sees her lying on the ground, bleeding from her leg. He is scared and sad. He says, "Anna, why did you do that? I told you it was dangerous. Now you are hurt."
He takes off his shirt and wraps it around her leg. He tries to stop the bleeding. He says, "Don't worry. I will get help. Stay here. Don't move."
He runs to find a grown-up. He sees a lady with a phone. He says, "Please, help me. My friend is hurt. She fell from the structure. It is dangerous. Please, call an ambulance."
The lady nods and calls an ambulance. She says, "Don't worry, little boy. You did the right thing. Your friend will be okay. The ambulance is coming soon."
Tom hopes she is right. He hopes Anna will be okay. He hopes she will learn to listen and be careful. He hopes they can still play in the park, but not on the dangerous structure.

Tom and Mia were twins who liked to play in the forest. One day, they saw a big house with a black roof and a red door. They were curious and wanted to look inside.
"Maybe there is someone nice who lives here," Mia said.
"Or maybe there is a witch who will eat us," Tom said.
They knocked on the door, but no one answered. They pushed it open and walked in. The house was dark and messy. There were pots and pans, books and bottles, and a big black cat.
"Hello?" Mia called out.
"Who are you?" a voice said. It was a witch who was lying on a couch. She had a long nose, a pointy hat, and a green dress. She looked angry and tired.
"We are sorry, we just wanted to see your house," Tom said.
"See my house? How rude! This is my house, and you are not welcome here. Go away, or I will turn you into frogs!" the witch said.
The twins were scared and ran to the door. But the door was locked. They tried to open it, but it did not move.
"Please, let us go. We won't bother you again," Mia said.
"No, you will stay here and learn. You will learn to clean my house, to cook my food, to feed my cat, and to do my spells. You will be my helpers, and I will be your teacher. You will work hard, and I will be lazy. That is the deal," the witch said.
The twins did not like the deal. They did not want to be the witch's helpers. They wanted to go home and play. They looked around and saw a window. It was small and high, but maybe they could reach it.
"Tom, I have an idea. Let's climb on that table and jump out of the window. Maybe we can escape," Mia whispered.
"OK, let's try. But be careful, the witch might see us," Tom whispered back.
They waited until the witch was snoring on the couch. Then they tiptoed to the table and climbed on it. They pushed the window open and jumped out. They landed on the grass and ran away.
They ran until they reached their home. They hugged their mom and dad and told them what happened. Their parents were shocked and glad that they were safe.
"Never go to that house again. That witch is mean and dangerous. You were lucky to get away," their mom said.
"We know, mom. We learned our lesson. We will never be curious again," the twins said.
But they did not really mean it. They still liked to play in the forest and explore new things. They just avoided the witch's house and hoped she would not find them. They were happy and brave, and the witch was lonely and lazy. That was the end.

Lily and the boy thought about it. They said, "Okay, we can try that. We can play together with the yellow car. We can share."
Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I'm proud of you. You are learning to be kind and fair. And you are learning that different things can be good too. Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree with a swing and a slide. They also had a small pond with some fish and frogs. They loved to watch the animals and feed them bread crumbs.
One day, they saw a big, black and yellow bug flying near the tree. It was a bee, and it was looking for honey. Lily and Ben were curious and wanted to see where the bee went. They followed it quietly, hoping to find some honey too.
The bee flew to a hole in the tree, where there was a hive full of honey. Lily and Ben smelled the sweet honey and their mouths watered. They wanted to taste some, but they were afraid of the bees. They decided to wait until the bee left, and then sneak some honey.
But the bee did not leave. It stayed in the hive, making more honey with the other bees. Lily and Ben grew restless and bored. They started to tease each other, trying to make the other one go first.
"I dare you to touch the hive," Lily said to Ben.
"No, you go first," Ben said to Lily.
"Chicken, chicken, bawk bawk bawk," Lily said, making chicken noises.
"Monkey, monkey, ooh ooh ooh," Ben said, making monkey noises.
They laughed and pushed each other, but they did not notice that their noise had woken up the bees. The bees were angry and came out of the hive, buzzing loudly. They saw Lily and Ben and thought they were trying to steal their honey. They flew towards them, ready to sting them.
Lily and Ben screamed and ran away, leaving the honey behind. They ran to their house, where their mom was waiting for them. She saw their scared faces and asked them what happened.
"We saw a bee and some honey, and we wanted to try some, but the bees chased us," Lily said.
"We were teasing each other, and we made too much noise, and the bees got mad," Ben said.
Mom hugged them and said, "You should not tease each other, or the bees. They work hard to make honey, and they do not like to share. Next time, be nice and quiet, and maybe they will let you have some honey."
Lily and Ben nodded and said they were sorry. They learned their lesson and never teased the bees again. They also learned to share their own honey with each other, and with their mom. They were happy and sweet, just like honey.

The mushroom was now able to help the other plants and animals in the forest. It gave shade to the little plants, and it was a home for the bugs. The other animals in the forest saw how the mushroom helped everyone, and they learned to be persistent too.
Moral of the story: Being persistent and helping others can make a big difference.

"Hold on tight, David!" his mom shouted.

Anna and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make soup with water and toys. Anna turned on the faucet and filled a big pot with water. She added some blocks, a spoon and a doll. "This is chicken soup," she said. "Do you want some, Ben?"
Ben nodded and took a bowl. He poured some water from the pot into his bowl. But he poured too much and the water spilled on the floor. Anna saw the mess and got angry. "Ben, you are so silly!" she shouted. "You made the floor wet and dirty. Now Mom will be mad at us. I don't want to play with you anymore."
Ben felt sad and sorry. He did not mean to spill the water. He wanted to make Anna happy. He looked at Anna and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I didn't do it on purpose. Please don't be mad at me. Can we still be friends?"
Anna looked at Ben and saw his sad face. She remembered that Ben was her best friend and that he always shared his toys with her. She also remembered that Mom always told her to forgive people who say sorry. She thought that Ben was smart and kind. She smiled and said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. We can still be friends. Let's clean up the floor together and then we can have some real soup. Mom will be proud of us."
Anna and Ben hugged and then got some towels. They wiped the floor and put the toys back in the box. They turned off the faucet and washed their hands. They went to the living room and found Mom. She had made some real chicken soup for them. She gave them each a bowl and a spoon. She said, "You are such good kids. I love you both. Enjoy your soup."
Anna and Ben smiled and said, "We love you too, Mom. Thank you for the soup. It's delicious."
They ate their soup and talked about their game. They were happy and glad that they forgave each other. They learned that friends sometimes make mistakes, but they can always say sorry and make up. They also learned that water is fun, but they have to be careful with the faucet. They decided to play in the kitchen again, but next time they would use less water and more toys.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play together. But sometimes they disagreed about what to play. One day, their aunt came to visit them. She brought them a new toy: a big puzzle with many pieces.
"Wow, thank you, auntie!" Lily and Max said. They wanted to try the new puzzle right away. But they disagreed about where to start. Lily wanted to start from the corners, and Max wanted to start from the middle.
"No, Lily, the middle is better. You can see the picture better," Max said.
"No, Max, the corners are better. You can make the edges first," Lily said.
They argued and argued, and did not listen to each other. They pulled the puzzle pieces from each other's hands, and made a big mess. Their aunt watched them and shook her head.
"Lily and Max, stop fighting. You are not being nice to each other. You need to share and cooperate. Why don't you take turns and help each other?" their aunt said.
But Lily and Max did not listen to their aunt. They kept disagreeing and fighting. They did not notice that their dog, Spot, was curious about the new toy. Spot sniffed the puzzle pieces and thought they were snacks. He picked up some pieces with his mouth and ran away.
"Hey, Spot, come back! That's our puzzle!" Lily and Max shouted. They stopped fighting and ran after Spot. They tried to get the puzzle pieces back, but Spot was too fast and playful. He ran around the house, and hid under the sofa, and jumped on the bed.
Lily and Max chased Spot, but they could not catch him. They realized that they had made a big mistake. They had wasted their time disagreeing and fighting, and now they had lost their new toy. They felt sad and sorry.
They went back to their aunt and said, "Auntie, we are sorry. We were not nice to each other. We disagreed and fought, and we did not listen to you. And now Spot has taken our puzzle, and we can't find it. Can you help us, please?"
Their aunt smiled and hugged them. She said, "I'm glad you are sorry. It's okay to disagree sometimes, but you need to respect and listen to each other. And you need to take care of your toys. Don't worry, I will help you find Spot and the puzzle. But first, you need to say sorry to each other, and promise to play nicely."
Lily and Max looked at each other and said, "Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Max. We promise to play nicely." They hugged each other and smiled. They learned their lesson. They thanked their aunt and followed her to find Spot and the puzzle. They hoped they could still put the puzzle together, and see the picture. They decided to start from the corners and the middle, and help each other. They agreed that the new toy was fun, but not as fun as playing together.

Lila liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they made shapes with their bodies and breathed slowly. It made them feel peaceful and happy. Sometimes, Lila's mom played soft music or lit a candle to make the yoga more special.
One day, Lila wanted to do yoga with her mom, but her mom was busy. She had to work on her laptop and make some calls. Lila felt sad and bored. She looked around the living room and saw her mom's yoga mat, her music player and her candle. She had an idea.
She took her mom's yoga mat and replaced it with her own blanket. She took her mom's music player and replaced it with her own toy piano. She took her mom's candle and replaced it with her own flashlight. She thought she was making her own yoga.
She lay down on her blanket and turned on her flashlight. She pressed some keys on her toy piano and made some noises. She tried to make some shapes with her body and breathe slowly, but it did not feel peaceful or happy. It felt silly and wrong.
Her mom heard the noises and came to the living room. She saw what Lila had done and felt angry and sad. She said, "Lila, what are you doing? You took my things and replaced them with yours. That is not nice. That is not yoga. That is stealing and lying. You hurt my feelings and broke my trust. You need to say sorry and give me back my things."
Lila saw her mom's face and felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I wanted to do yoga with you, but you were busy. I thought I could make my own yoga, but I was wrong. I did not mean to hurt you or break your trust. Please forgive me and take back your things."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Lila, I forgive you. I know you love yoga and you love me. But you cannot take things that are not yours and replace them with yours. That is not fair or respectful. You need to ask before you borrow or use something. And you need to be honest and tell the truth. That is how you show love and kindness. That is how you do yoga."

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They had a small shovel and a bucket. They were having fun.
"Look, Lily, I found a shiny thing!" Ben said. He held up a metal thing with teeth. It was a key.
"Wow, Ben, what is it for?" Lily asked. She touched the key with her finger.
"I don't know. Maybe it opens a door or a box. Maybe it has a treasure inside!" Ben said. He put the key in his pocket.
"Let's go and see if we can find it!" Lily said. She grabbed her shovel and bucket.
"Okay, but we have to be careful. The key is fragile. It can break or bend. We have to stay away from the rocks and the water," Ben said. He followed Lily.
They searched around the garden, looking for a door or a box that matched the key. They did not find anything. They were getting tired and hungry.
"Ben, Lily, time for lunch!" Mom called from the house.
"Okay, Mom, we're coming!" Ben and Lily said. They ran to the house.
"Did you have fun in the garden?" Mom asked.
"Yes, Mom, we did. Look what we found!" Ben said. He showed Mom the key.
"Wow, that's a nice key. Where did you find it?" Mom asked.
"We found it in the dirt. We don't know what it is for. Do you know, Mom?" Lily asked.
Mom looked at the key. She smiled.
"I do know, my loves. This is a very special key. It belongs to your grandma. She gave it to me when I was a little girl. It opens a music box that plays a beautiful song. Do you want to hear it?" Mom asked.
"Yes, please, Mom!" Ben and Lily said.
Mom took them to her bedroom. She opened a drawer and took out a wooden box. She used the key to open it. The box played a sweet melody.
Ben and Lily listened with wonder. They hugged Mom.
"Thank you, Mom, for sharing this with us. We love you," they said.
"I love you too, my loves. And I'm glad you found the key. It is a precious gift from grandma. She would be happy to know that you appreciate it. But remember, it is fragile. You have to be gentle with it and keep it safe. Okay?" Mom said.
"Okay, Mom. We will. We will stay careful with the key and the box," Ben and Lily said.
They enjoyed the music and the lunch. They were happy.

Lily saw a stick on the ground. She picked it up and ran towards Sam. She wanted to poke him with the stick. She thought that would make him give her the ball.

Lily opened her eyes and saw Sam. She was still sad, but she forgave him. She hugged him back and said she was sorry too.
They decided to share the ball and play together. They had more fun that way.
The moral of the story is: Don't be selfish and mean to your friends. Share and be kind.

"Oh no, our house is ruined!" Mia says.
"It's okay, we can make another one." Tim says.

"Spot, stop! That's not food, that's clay!" Tim says.
"Yuck, Spot, that's disgusting! You'll get sick!" Mia says.
They run to Spot and try to pull him away from the clay. But Spot likes the clay and growls at them. He does not want to share. Tim and Mia are scared and call for help.
"Mom, Dad, help! Spot is eating our clay house!" they shout.
Mom and Dad hear their shouts and come to the living room. They see the mess and the dog and the children. They are surprised and worried.
"What happened here?" Mom asks.
"We made a model of our house with clay, but we dropped it and Spot ate it!" Tim explains.
"Oh dear, that's not good. Spot, spit it out!" Dad says.
He grabs Spot by the collar and takes him to the bathroom. He makes him drink some water and spit out the clay. He checks if Spot is okay. He is. He gives him a hug and a treat.
Mom helps Tim and Mia clean up the clay from the floor. She throws away the broken pieces and wipes the stains. She gives them a hug and a kiss.
"I'm sorry your model got ruined. It was very nice. But you can make another one tomorrow. How about we rest now and watch a movie?" she says.

They found a big hill in the park. They thought it would be fun to go down the hill in their jet. They put on their helmets and goggles and got ready. "Are you ready, Ben?" Lily asked. "Yes, I am, Lily," Ben said. "Let's go!"

Lily and Ben learned their lesson. They still liked to play with their jet, but they did not go down hills anymore. They parked their jet in a safe place and played with other kids. They realized that being adventurous was good, but being reckless was bad. They thanked the nice lady for helping them and for teaching them. They became smarter and safer pilots.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find bugs. But they had to be quiet, because Mom was working inside. She said they could not make noise or she would be angry.
"Look, I found a big worm!" Tom said. He showed Lily his worm. It was brown and slimy.
"Wow, that's a big one!" Lily said. She wanted to touch it, but Tom did not let her. He said it was his worm.
"Let me see, let me see!" Lily said. She tried to grab the worm, but Tom pulled it away. They started to fight over the worm.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She came out of the house. She looked very angry. She had a measure in her hand. She was measuring something for her work.
"Sorry, Mom," Lily and Tom said. They stopped fighting. They did not want Mom to be more angry.
"What are you doing with that worm?" Mom asked. She saw the worm in Tom's hand. She did not like worms. She thought they were gross.
"It's my worm, Mom. I found it in the hole," Tom said. He held the worm tight.
"Well, you can't keep it, Tom. It's not a pet. It belongs in the ground. Put it back where you found it," Mom said.
"But Mom, I like it. It's my friend. Can I keep it, please?" Tom said. He made a sad face.
"No, Tom. You can't keep it. It's not good for the worm. It needs to be free. Now, put it back and go play something else. And be quiet, please. I have to finish my work," Mom said.
Tom did not want to put the worm back. He wanted to keep it. He had an idea. He waited until Mom went back inside. Then he whispered to Lily.
"Let's escape with the worm. Let's go to the park. There we can play with the worm and no one will bother us," Tom said.
"OK, let's go," Lily said. She liked the idea. She wanted to play with the worm too.
They took the worm and ran to the gate. They opened the gate and ran to the street. They did not see the car coming. They did not hear the horn. They did not feel the bump. They did not escape.

They show each other their houses and play with them. They pretend to drive the cars and dress the dolls.

"Ben, come and see my new garden," Lily says. "It is very pretty and colorful."
Ben walks over to Lily's garden. He likes the grass and the flowers. He wants to touch them. He steps on the paper. But the paper breaks and he falls into the hole.
"Help, help!" Ben cries. "I'm in a deep hole!"
Lily hears Ben and runs to him. She sees him in the hole. She feels sorry and scared. She did not want to hurt Ben. She wants to help him.
"Ben, I'm sorry, I'm sorry," Lily says. "I made a hole to surprise you. But it was a bad surprise. I will get you out."

"Lily, that was a mean thing to do," Ben says. "You could have hurt me. You made a mess of the floor. You are not a good designer."

"Ben, I'm very sorry," Lily says. "I wanted to make you laugh. But I made you cry. I will clean the floor. I will make you a nice surprise. Please forgive me."
Ben looks at Lily. He sees her tears and her smile. He remembers they are friends. He remembers they like to design things together. He decides to forgive her.
"OK, Lily, I forgive you," Ben says. "But don't make any more holes. Let's make something nice together. Let's design a castle for our toys."
Lily and Ben hug and smile. They forget the hole and the mess. They take their blocks and make a big castle on the floor. They put their dolls and cars inside. They have fun and talk to each other. They are happy. They are good designers.

It was a rainy day and Lily wanted to go outside and play. She put on her boots and her coat and asked her mom for an umbrella.
"Here you go, sweetie. Be careful and don't get wet," her mom said, handing her a pink umbrella with flowers.
"Thank you, mom. I love you," Lily said, opening the umbrella and running to the door.
She stepped outside and saw a big puddle. She smiled and jumped into it, making a splash. She laughed and felt the raindrops on her face. She liked the sound of the rain and the smell of the wet grass.
She saw a little bird on a branch, shivering and wet. She felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help. She walked over to the tree and said, "Hello, bird. Are you cold? Do you want to share my umbrella?"
The bird looked at her and nodded. It flew down and landed on her shoulder. Lily held the umbrella over both of them and said, "There, now we are both warm and dry. Do you want to be my friend?"
The bird chirped and nuzzled her cheek. Lily smiled and hugged the bird. She was happy to have a new friend. She said, "What is your name, bird?"
The bird said, "My name is Blue. What is yours?"
"My name is Lily. Nice to meet you, Blue," Lily said.
They talked and played under the umbrella, until Lily's mom called her for lunch. Lily said, "Blue, I have to go now. But you can come with me if you want. Do you want to come?"
Blue said, "Yes, I do. Thank you, Lily. You are very kind."
Lily said, "You're welcome, Blue. You are very sweet."
She removed the umbrella from her shoulder and held it in her hand. She and Blue walked back to the house, where her mom was waiting for them. Lily said, "Mom, this is Blue. He is my new friend. Can he stay for lunch?"
Her mom smiled and said, "Of course he can, honey. He is very cute. Come on in, both of you. I have some sandwiches and juice for you."
Lily and Blue went inside and enjoyed their lunch. They were very happy and grateful. They had found each other on a rainy day.

Lily likes to chew. She chews her food, her toys, her clothes, and sometimes her hair. She thinks chewing is fun and makes her teeth strong. But chewing can also get her in trouble.
One day, Lily found a teaspoon in the kitchen. She thought it was shiny and pretty. She wanted to chew it. She put it in her mouth and bit hard. But the teaspoon was not soft like food or toys. It was hard and metal. It hurt Lily's teeth and tongue. She cried out loud.
Mom heard Lily cry and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily with the teaspoon in her mouth. She was worried and angry. She took the teaspoon out and checked Lily's mouth. She said, "Lily, why did you chew the teaspoon? You could have broken your teeth or cut your tongue. Teaspoons are not for chewing. They are for measuring and stirring. You are lucky you are not hurt. Don't ever chew teaspoons again."
Lily felt sorry and scared. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't know. I just wanted to chew something shiny. I won't chew teaspoons again. Can I chew something else?"
Mom hugged Lily and said, "I know you like to chew, but you have to be careful. You can chew your food, your toys, or your gum. But don't chew anything that is hard, sharp, or dirty. And don't chew too much or too fast. You might choke or get a tummy ache. Chewing is good, but only in moderation."
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I understand. I will chew only good things and not too much. Can I have a cookie?"
Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can have a cookie. But use a teaspoon to scoop some milk first. And don't chew the teaspoon."

Ben and Lily love to go to the beach with their mom and dad. They like to play in the sand, splash in the water, and look for shells and rocks. Sometimes they see fish and crabs and other animals in the sea.
One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It had a net and a lot of buckets. Ben and Lily were curious and asked their mom what the boat was doing.
"That boat is catching shrimp, sweeties," their mom said. "Shrimp are small pink animals that live in the water. Some people like to eat them, and some people like to provide them for other animals, like birds and turtles."
"Can we see the shrimp, mom?" Lily asked.
"Maybe, if we are lucky," their mom said. "Let's go closer to the boat and wave to the people on it. Maybe they will show us some shrimp."
Ben and Lily ran to the edge of the water and waved their arms. The people on the boat saw them and smiled. One of them held up a bucket and shouted, "Hey, kids, do you want to see some shrimp?"
"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said.
The person on the boat threw the bucket to their dad, who caught it and brought it to them. Inside the bucket, there were many shrimp, wriggling and jumping. They were pink and shiny and had long whiskers and tails.
"Wow, they are so cute!" Lily said. "They look like tiny bugs."
"They are adorable," Ben said. "Can we touch them, dad?"
"Sure, but be gentle," their dad said. "They are alive and they might pinch you."
Ben and Lily reached into the bucket and picked up some shrimp. They felt soft and wet and ticklish. They laughed and giggled as they played with the shrimp.
"Thank you for the shrimp!" they shouted to the people on the boat.
"You're welcome, kids!" the people on the boat shouted back. "Have fun!"
Ben and Lily thanked their dad and gave him back the bucket. They watched as he threw the shrimp back into the water. They waved goodbye to the boat and went back to their mom.
They told her all about the shrimp and how adorable they were. They said they wanted to see more shrimp next time they came to the beach.
Their mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you had a good time, sweeties. Maybe we can provide some shrimp for the birds and turtles next time. They would love that."
Ben and Lily nodded and smiled. They loved the beach and they loved the shrimp. They hoped to see them again soon.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to build a big tower. They put one block on top of another block. They are very careful. They do not want the tower to fall.
"Look, Anna, our tower is almost complete!" Ben says. He is happy.
"Yes, Ben, it is very tall and pretty!" Anna says. She is happy too.
They need one more block to finish the tower. They look around. They see a block on the table. It is red and shiny. They both want the block.
"I want the block!" Ben says. He runs to the table.
"No, I want the block!" Anna says. She runs to the table too.
They reach the table at the same time. They both grab the block. They pull and tug. They do not share.
"Let go, Ben!" Anna says. She is angry.
"Let go, Anna!" Ben says. He is angry too.
They pull and tug harder. The block slips from their hands. It flies in the air. It lands on the tower. The tower wobbles and shakes. It falls down. The blocks scatter everywhere. They make a loud noise.
Anna and Ben are shocked. They look at the mess. They look at each other. They feel sad and sorry.
They hear a voice. It is Mom. She is in the living room. She is having a meeting with her boss. She is on the phone.
"What was that noise?" Mom says. She is worried.
Anna and Ben do not know what to say. They are scared.
They hear footsteps. It is Mom. She comes to the playroom. She sees the mess. She sees Anna and Ben. She is not happy.
"What happened here?" Mom says. She is stern.
Anna and Ben lower their heads. They do not look at Mom.
"We were playing with blocks," Anna says. She is quiet.
"We wanted to build a tower," Ben says. He is quiet too.
"But we fought over the last block," Anna says. She is ashamed.
"And we made the tower fall," Ben says. He is ashamed too.
"We are sorry, Mom," Anna and Ben say together. They are sincere.
Mom sighs. She is not angry anymore. She is gentle.
"I know you are sorry, Anna and Ben," Mom says. She is kind.
"But you should not fight over toys," Mom says. She is firm.
"You should share and take turns," Mom says. She is wise.
"And you should be careful and quiet when I have a meeting," Mom says. She is serious.
"Do you understand?" Mom says. She is hopeful.
"Yes, Mom, we understand," Anna and Ben say together. They are respectful.
They hug Mom. They say sorry again. Mom hugs them back. She says it is okay.
They help Mom clean up the mess. They put the blocks back in the box. They say goodbye to Mom's boss on the phone. They apologize for the noise.
Mom smiles. She is proud.
Anna and Ben smile. They are happy.
They learn a lesson. They do not fight over toys anymore. They share and take turns. They are careful and quiet when Mom has a meeting. They are good children.

Once upon a time, there was a big, bald man named Tom. Tom had a big clock in his house. Tom was scared of the clock because it made a loud sound. One day, Tom's friend, Sam, came to visit.
"Tom, why are you scared of the clock?" Sam asked.
"I don't like the loud sound it makes," Tom said.
Sam had an idea. He took the clock and put it in a box. Then, he put the box in the closet. Now, the clock's sound was not so loud. Tom was happy and not scared anymore.
But then, something unexpected happened. The clock stopped making any sound at all. Tom and Sam opened the closet and saw that the clock was broken. They were sad because the clock was very special to Tom.

But the woods were dark and scary. They heard strange noises and saw big shadows. They lost sight of the butterfly. They felt lost and sad.
"Lily, I'm hungry," Max said. "And I'm scared. Can we go back?"
"I don't know, Max," Lily said. "I don't know where we are. Maybe we can find someone to help us."
They walked around, hoping to see the park or a house. But they only saw more trees and bushes. They were about to give up, when they smelled something yummy.
"Max, do you smell that?" Lily asked. "It smells like cookies!"
They followed their noses and came to a small cabin. They saw a kind old lady sitting on the porch. She had a plate of cookies and a glass of milk.
"Hello, children," the lady said. "Are you lost?"
"Yes, ma'am," Lily said. "We were chasing a butterfly and we got lost in the woods. Can you help us?"
"Of course, dear," the lady said. "But first, why don't you have some cookies and milk? They are yummy and good for you."
Lily and Max smiled. They thanked the lady and ate the cookies and milk. They felt happy and warm. The lady told them her name was Grandma Rose and she lived in the cabin with her cat. She also liked to search for bugs and flowers. She showed them her jar of heroes.

Lily and Max were amazed. They saw their butterfly in the jar. It was still yellow and black, but it looked more beautiful. They felt proud and happy.
"Can we keep it, Grandma Rose?" Lily asked.
"No, dear," Grandma Rose said. "We have to let it go. It has a long journey to make. It has to find its home and its friends. Just like you."
She opened the jar and let the butterfly out. It flew around them and landed on Lily's nose. It tickled her and made her giggle. Then it flew away, into the sky.
"Bye, bye, butterfly," Lily and Max said. "Thank you for being our hero."
Grandma Rose hugged them and said, "Don't worry, children. I'll help you find your way back. But first, let's have some more cookies and milk. They are yummy and good for you."
Lily and Max nodded. They liked Grandma Rose. She was kind and sweet. She was their hero, too.

Sara loves to ride her bike. She has a unique bike with pink and purple stripes and a basket with flowers. She likes to go to the park with her bike and play with her friends.
One day, she sees a boy with a big bike. His bike has no stripes, no basket, and no flowers. It has a bell and a light. He rides very fast and makes loud noises. Sara thinks his bike is boring and ugly.
"Hey, you!" the boy shouts at Sara. "Your bike is silly and girly. You can't ride fast like me. You should get a better bike."
Sara feels angry and sad. She likes her bike. She thinks it is pretty and fun. She does not want a better bike. She wants the boy to leave her alone.
"No, you!" she shouts back. "Your bike is noisy and dull. You can't ride smooth like me. You should get a nicer bike."
The boy feels angry and proud. He likes his bike. He thinks it is cool and strong. He does not want a nicer bike. He wants Sara to admit he is better.
They start to argue and ride around the park. They try to show off their bikes and skills. They do not see the big rock on the path. They both hit the rock and fall off their bikes. Their bikes get hurt. Sara's tire pops. The boy's light breaks.
They both cry and look at their bikes. They feel sorry and scared. They do not care about their bikes being unique or better. They just want their bikes to be okay.
They look at each other and stop crying. They see that they are both hurt and sad. They see that they both love their bikes. They see that they both made a mistake.
"I'm sorry," Sara says. "I was mean to you. Your bike is not ugly. It is different. Different is good."
"I'm sorry, too," the boy says. "I was rude to you. Your bike is not silly. It is special. Special is good."
They smile and help each other. They walk their bikes to the bike shop. They ask the bike man to fix their bikes. They wait and talk. They find out they have some things in common. They like the same ice cream. They like the same animals. They like to ride their bikes.
They become friends and ride their bikes together. They learn to appreciate their bikes and each other. They learn that unique is good.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to climb the trees and swing on the branches. They had a lot of fun.
But then they saw a big dog. The dog was barking and running towards them. Anna and Ben were scared. They climbed up a tree and hid behind a branch.
"Go away, dog!" Anna shouted. "We don't want to play with you!"
The dog stopped and looked at them. He wagged his tail and made a whining sound. He seemed friendly, but Anna and Ben did not trust him.
"What do we do?" Ben asked. "Do we stay here or do we go down?"
Anna did not know. She shrugged. She did not like the dog, but she also did not like being stuck in the tree.
"Maybe we can wait until the dog leaves," she said. "Or maybe we can call for help."
They looked around, but they did not see anyone. They felt upset. They wished they had not climbed the tree.
Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She had come to pick them up.
"Anna! Ben! Where are you?" she called.
"Mom! We're here!" Anna and Ben shouted. "We're in the tree!"
Mom saw them and smiled. She also saw the dog. She was not afraid of the dog. She knew the dog. His name was Spot. He belonged to her friend.
"Spot, come here, boy!" she said. "You're a good dog, but you scared Anna and Ben. They don't know you."
Spot obeyed and came to mom. He licked her hand and wagged his tail. Mom petted him and praised him.
"Anna, Ben, it's okay. You can come down now. Spot is not a bad dog. He just wanted to play with you. He's very friendly and gentle. Do you want to meet him?"
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They were still scared, but they also felt curious. They decided to give Spot a chance. They climbed down the tree and approached mom and Spot.
"Hello, Spot," Anna said. "We're sorry we yelled at you. We were afraid."
Spot licked Anna's face and made her giggle. Ben also petted Spot and felt his soft fur. Spot was happy and rolled on his back.
"See? He's a nice dog," mom said. "He likes you. Do you like him?"
Anna and Ben nodded. They smiled and hugged Spot. They were not upset anymore. They had made a new friend.

One day, they play the memory game in the park. They find a tall tree with a big branch. They put the cards on the branch and sit on the grass. They start to play.
"Look, I found two bananas!" Lily says. She flips two cards with yellow bananas.
"Good job, Lily!" Tom says. He claps his hands. He flips two cards with red apples.
"Wow, you are good too, Tom!" Lily says. She smiles.
They play for a long time. They find many matches. They have fun.
But then, a strong wind blows. The wind makes the cards fly away. The cards go up in the air and down to the ground. Tom and Lily are sad. They lose their cards.
"Oh no, our cards!" Tom says. He tries to catch them.
"Where are they?" Lily says. She looks around.
They run after the cards. They find some on the grass, some on the flowers, and some on the swings. They pick them up and put them in a pile.
They look at the pile. They see that some cards are missing. They cannot find them.
"Maybe the wind took them far away," Tom says. He frowns.
"Maybe they are in the tall tree," Lily says. She points to the branch.
They look at the branch. They see two cards with blue birds. They are stuck on the branch.
"Look, there they are!" Tom says. He jumps.
"But they are too high," Lily says. She stretches her arms.
They think of a way to get the cards. They see a ladder near the tree. They run to the ladder. They carry it to the tree. They put it against the branch.
Tom climbs the ladder. He is brave. He reaches the branch. He grabs the cards. He climbs down.
"Yay, you did it!" Lily says. She hugs Tom.
"Yay, we have all the cards!" Tom says. He hugs Lily.
They are happy. They have their cards. They have their memory game. They have their friend. They play again.

As Tim was picking up acorns, he saw a small piece of paper on the ground. He picked it up and tried to fold it. Tim's friend, a wise old owl named Mr. Hoot, saw him and asked, "What are you doing, Tim?"
Tim showed the paper to Mr. Hoot and said, "I found this paper and I want to fold it, but I don't know how." Mr. Hoot smiled and said, "I can teach you how to fold it, but first, let's pick up all the acorns."
Tim and Mr. Hoot picked up all the acorns and put them in a big pile. Then, Mr. Hoot showed Tim how to fold the paper into a little boat. Tim was so happy with his new boat! He thanked Mr. Hoot and they both went to a small pond to play with the boat.
As they played with the boat, the wind started to blow. The boat floated away and landed on the other side of the pond. Tim was sad, but Mr. Hoot said, "Don't worry, Tim. I knew this would happen. That's why we picked up all the acorns first."
Tim smiled and hugged Mr. Hoot. They went back to the big pile of acorns and ate some. Tim knew that he had a wise friend in Mr. Hoot and that he would always be there to help him.

They ran to the tent and opened the flap. They saw many books, toys, and games on the floor. They picked up some of them and started to play. They did not hear the teacher coming back from the bathroom.
"Hey, what are you doing here?" the teacher asked in a loud voice. "This is not your camp. This is for big kids only. You are not allowed to touch anything here. You are very naughty!"
Lily and Tom felt scared and sorry. They dropped the things they were holding and ran out of the tent. They hoped the teacher would not tell their mom and dad.
But the teacher was not so mean. She knew they were just curious and did not mean to make a mess. She followed them and called them back.
"Wait, wait, don't run away. I'm not going to punish you. I just want to talk to you. Why did you come to the camp?"
Lily and Tom stopped and turned around. They looked at the teacher with big eyes.
"We wanted to see what was inside the tent. We like to learn new things too. We are sorry we touched your stuff. We did not break anything," Lily said.
"Yes, we are sorry. We will not do it again. Please don't be mad at us," Tom said.
The teacher smiled and knelt down to their level.
"I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you like to learn new things. But you have to ask before you enter someone else's camp. And you have to be careful with the things you play with. They belong to other kids who worked hard to make them. Do you understand?"
Lily and Tom nodded.
"Yes, we understand. Thank you for not punishing us. You are very nice," Lily said.
"Yes, thank you. You are very strong too. You can lift all those books and toys," Tom said.
The teacher laughed and hugged them.
"You are very sweet. And you are very smart too. You can learn a lot of things if you keep being curious and respectful. Maybe one day you can join the camp when you are older. Would you like that?"
Lily and Tom nodded again.
"Yes, we would like that very much. Thank you for letting us see the camp. Can we say goodbye to the other kids?" Lily asked.
"Of course you can. Come on, let's go and meet them. They are very friendly and they will show you some of their projects. Maybe you can even play with them for a while. How does that sound?"
Lily and Tom smiled and followed the teacher to the tent. They were happy they made a new friend and learned something new. They decided they would always ask before they enter someone else's camp. And they would always be careful with the things they play with. They knew that was the right thing to do.

One day, their mom said, "Ben and Lily, it's time for your bath. Come on, let's go to the bathroom." But Ben and Lily did not want to stop playing. They said, "Mom, can we play a little more? Please, please, please!"
Mom said, "No, you have to take your bath now. It's getting late and you have to go to bed soon. Don't delay, or you will miss your bedtime story." She took their hands and led them to the bathroom.
Ben and Lily were not happy. They did not like to wash. They liked to play. They thought of a plan to make mom go away. They said, "Mom, we are hungry. Can we have a snack before the bath?"
Mom said, "No, you already had dinner. You can have a snack tomorrow. Now get in the bathtub and wash with the duck." She filled the bathtub with warm water and soap bubbles. She put the duck in the water and said, "Have fun, but don't splash too much."
Ben and Lily got in the bathtub, but they did not wash. They played with the duck and splashed water everywhere. They laughed and giggled and made a big mess. They did not see that mom had left the bathroom and closed the door.
Mom went to the kitchen to get a glass of water. She saw a bottle of hot sauce on the counter. She had a bad idea. She said, "Ben and Lily are being naughty. They don't want to wash. They want to play. I will teach them a lesson. I will make their bath spicy."
She took the bottle of hot sauce and went back to the bathroom. She opened the door and said, "Ben and Lily, are you done with your bath?" But Ben and Lily did not hear her. They were too busy playing. Mom poured the hot sauce in the bathtub and said, "There, now your bath is spicy. Enjoy!"
Ben and Lily felt a burning sensation on their skin. They screamed and cried. They said, "Mom, what did you do? It hurts, it hurts! Help us, help us!" But mom did not help them. She said, "That's what you get for delaying your bath. Now you have to stay in the bathtub until you wash off the hot sauce. And no bedtime story for you."
Ben and Lily were very sad and very angry. They hated mom and they hated the duck. They wished they had listened to mom and taken their bath earlier. They learned a hard lesson. They never delayed their bath again.

But her dad was very smart. He saw the file under the sofa and knew it was his. He wondered who moved it. He opened the file and saw that some papers were wrinkled and torn. He was not happy.
He went to Lily's room and asked her if she knew anything about the file. Lily looked at her dad and tried to act innocent. But her dad saw her guilty face and knew she was lying. He was not angry, but he was disappointed.
He explained to Lily that the file was very important and that she should not touch it without his permission. He told her that he loved her, but that she had to be more careful and respectful. He asked her to apologize and to help him fix the papers.
Lily felt sorry. She hugged her dad and said she was sorry. She helped him smooth the papers and tape the tears. She learned her lesson. She still liked to examine things, but she asked before she touched them. She was very persistent, but also very polite.

The bird spoke, "Hey, what are you doing up here?" The baby crab was so scared, he did not know how to answer. He just stayed quietly, not making a sound.
Then the bird spoke again. "It's OK. I'm not here to hurt you. I just wanted to say hello." 
The baby crab looked up at the bird, still shaking. But he started to feel a little less fearful. 
"My name is Peep" said the bird. "What's yours?" 
"I'm...I'm...Pinch" the baby crab replied, feeling safe enough to speak. 
"It's nice to meet you, Pinch" said Peep. And with that, the bird flew away.
From that day forth, Pinch was no longer fearful. He had made a new friend and now he felt safe and happy.

The cat agreed and waited for the leaves to fall. The bird started to shake the branch with all its strength. Many leaves fell, and the cat tried to catch them. They both had fun playing together.
After a while, they stopped playing and said goodbye. The bird was happy that it found a new friend, and the cat learned that not all birds were afraid of it. They promised to play together again the next day.

Her mom looked for her and called out, "Amy, where are you?" Amy giggled and stayed quiet. Her mom came into the dark room and saw Amy's shoes. She knelt down and said, "I see you, Amy!"
Amy laughed and came out from behind the box. "You found me, Mom!" she said. They both smiled and continued to play hide and seek all day long. The cobweb in the corner stayed there, but Amy wasn't scared of it anymore.

"Let's go see!" said the bunny. So, they hopped and ran through the woods, following the distant light. As they got closer, they saw a big net. Inside the net were many birds, trying to escape.
"Help us, please!" cried the birds. The bunny and the squirrel wanted to help their new friends. So, they worked together to chew and pull at the net. With their teamwork, they made a big hole in the net.
The birds were able to escape through the hole. They flapped their wings and flew away, thanking the bunny and the squirrel for their help. The bunny and the squirrel felt very happy and proud. They went back to their cabin, knowing they had done a good thing. From that day on, they had many more friends in the woods.

Lily and Ben were hot and thirsty. They wanted to drink some juice. They saw a big cooler in the park. It had a sign that said "Free juice for everyone". They ran to the cooler and opened it.
Inside the cooler, there were many bottles of juice. They looked yummy. Lily and Ben each took a bottle and opened it. They smelled the juice. It smelled bad. They tasted the juice. It tasted worse. They spit out the juice and made a face.
They looked at the bottles again. They saw that the juice was old and rotten. There were bugs and mold in the juice. Someone had put the bad juice in the cooler to trick people. Lily and Ben felt sick and sad. They threw away the bottles and closed the cooler.
They saw a man walking by. He had a big smile and a bag. He was the one who had put the bad juice in the cooler. He wanted to see people drink the bad juice and laugh at them. He was a mean and nasty man. He did not care about people. He was a poor man, not in money, but in heart.
Lily and Ben had an idea. They found a stick and some mud. They stirred the mud with the stick until it was thick and gooey. They waited for the man to come back to the cooler. When he came back, he opened the cooler and reached for a bottle. Lily and Ben threw the mud at him. The mud hit him in the face and covered his clothes. He screamed and dropped the bottle. He ran away, looking like a dirty pig.
Lily and Ben laughed and cheered. They had taught the man a lesson. They hoped he would never do such a mean thing again. They felt happy and proud. They went to find some good juice and some good friends. They had a good day.

Lila and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw a well in the corner. It was old and deep and dark.
"Let's look inside the well," said Ben. He ran to the well and peered over the edge. He saw nothing but black.
"Be careful, Ben," said Lila. She followed him and held his hand. "It is scary and dangerous."
Ben wanted to be brave. He leaned over the well and shouted, "Hello, hello, is anyone there?"
But no one answered. Only his voice came back, louder and louder. It sounded like a monster.
Ben was scared. He lost his balance and fell into the well. He screamed and cried.
Lila was shocked. She saw Ben disappear into the well. She cried too. She ran to the house and called for help.
"Mommy, mommy, Ben fell into the well!" she sobbed.
Mommy heard Lila and came out. She saw the well and Lila's tears. She was worried and angry.
"Who told you to play near the well?" she asked. "It is not safe. It is not a toy."
She called daddy and the neighbors. They brought a rope and a flashlight. They lowered the rope into the well and told Ben to grab it.
"Ben, Ben, can you hear me?" mommy shouted. "Hold on to the rope. We will pull you up."
Ben heard mommy's voice. He was cold and wet and hurt. He saw the rope and the light. He grabbed the rope and held on tight.
They pulled Ben up from the well. He was dirty and bleeding and crying. Mommy hugged him and kissed him. She was happy and relieved.
"Ben, Ben, are you okay?" she asked. "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I love you."
Ben nodded and hugged mommy back. He was sorry too. He loved mommy.
Lila ran to Ben and hugged him too. She was glad and sorry. She loved Ben.
"Ben, Ben, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I love you," she said.
Ben smiled and hugged Lila back. He was glad too. He loved Lila.
They went inside the house. Mommy cleaned Ben's wounds and gave him a bandage. She gave him a glass of milk and a cookie. She gave him a lovely teddy bear.
"Ben, Ben, this is for you," she said. "It is a lovely teddy bear. It will keep you company and make you feel better."
Ben took the teddy bear and cuddled it. He liked the teddy bear. It was soft and warm and friendly.
"Thank you, mommy," he said. "Thank you for the lovely teddy bear. Thank you for saving me."
Mommy smiled and kissed Ben again. She was proud of Ben. He was brave and strong and sweet.
"You're welcome, Ben," she said. "You're welcome, my lovely boy. I'm glad you're safe."

One day something strange appeared in the meadow. It was big, green and didn't move. The fly was a bit scared of it, so he decided to approach it slowly.
"Hello! Who are you?" asked the fly.
The big green thing didn't respond.
The fly tried again. "What is this big, green thing?"
Suddenly, the big, green thing opened its mouth and a mild voice said, "I am the Wind".
The wind started blowing the fly around the meadow. Although the fly was scared at first, he soon realized that the wind was actually helping him to get around faster. From that day forward, the fly felt proud of the wind's help.
The moral of the story is that things that seem strange or scary at first can turn out to be helpful in the end.

"Let me have it first!" Lily said. She tried to grab the bird from the shelf.
"No, it's mine!" Ben said. He pushed Lily away and reached for the bird.
They both pulled and tugged at the bird, but it was too fragile. It slipped from their hands and fell to the floor. It broke into many pieces. Lily and Ben gasped and cried.
Mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the broken bird and the sad twins. She was angry and sad too.
"Who did this?" she asked. "This was a special gift from Grandma. She gave it to me when I was a little girl. It was very precious and fragile. You should not have touched it without asking me."
Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They did not know it was Mom's bird. They did not mean to break it.
"We're sorry, Mom," they said. "We wanted to play with it. We did not know it was yours. We did not know it was fragile."
Mom sighed and hugged them. She knew they were sorry, but she was still sad.
"I forgive you, but you have to learn to be careful with other people's things. And you have to learn to share and take turns. You can't always have what you want. Sometimes you have to wait and be patient. Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They said they would try to be more careful and more kind.
Mom smiled and kissed them. She said she loved them. She said they could help her make a meal for dinner. They could make Grandma's favorite soup and bread. They could also make a card for Grandma and say sorry for breaking her bird.
Lily and Ben agreed. They felt a little better. They went to the kitchen with Mom and helped her raise the pot and stir the soup. They learned how to knead the dough and shape the bread. They also drew a picture of a bird and wrote "We love you Grandma" on the card.
They hoped Grandma would like their meal and their card. They hoped she would forgive them too. They learned that fragile things can break, but love can heal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Toby. She was three years old and very curious.
One day, Toby saw a beautiful velvet chair with big, fluffy arms. She was so excited that she just had to sit in it. So she climbed up and jumped into it. But she didn't notice there was a gun on the chair.
Suddenly, a loud bang went off! Toby started crying, panicking.
Her Mom rushed into the room and saw Toby with the gun in her hand. She quickly took Toby in her arms, soothed her and said, "It's okay sweetheart, Mommy's here."
Toby was so scared, but mom was very patient. She picked up the gun and showed it to Toby. "This is what made the noise. It's called a gun. Guns shoot, and they can be very dangerous. You must never touch the gun, okay?"
Toby nodded and gave her mom a hug. From then on, Toby learnt to always be careful around weapons and to show patience to others.
