Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. One day, they saw a big bird in the park. It had a long neck, long legs and black and white feathers. It was an ostrich.
"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom said. "It is so big and funny!"
"Can we go and say hello?" Mia asked.
"OK, but be careful. It might be scared of us," Tom said.
They walked slowly towards the ostrich. The ostrich saw them and tilted its head. It was a nosy ostrich. It wanted to know what they were doing.
"Hello, bird. We are Tom and Mia. What is your name?" Mia said.
The ostrich did not answer. It opened its beak and made a loud noise. It sounded like a honk.
"Wow, you can honk! That is cool!" Tom said.
The ostrich honked again. It flapped its wings and ran towards them. It was not scared of them. It was angry at them.
"Uh-oh, it does not like us. Hurry, run!" Tom said.
Tom and Mia turned around and ran away. The ostrich chased them. It was faster than them.
"Help, help! The bird is after us!" Mia said.
They ran to the gate of the park. They saw their mom waiting for them. She had a big bag of popcorn.
"Mom, mom! There is a big bird in the park. It is an ostrich. It is nosy and angry. It honked at us and chased us. We are scared!" Tom and Mia said.
Their mom looked at the ostrich. It stopped at the gate and looked at them. It smelled the popcorn. It was a hungry ostrich. It wanted to eat the popcorn.
"Oh, dear. That is not a nice bird. It is a mean bird. It should not be in the park. It should be in the zoo. Come here, kids. Let's go home and have some popcorn. Maybe the bird will go away," their mom said.
She took their hands and walked away. The ostrich watched them go. It honked again. It was still hungry. It saw another bag of popcorn on a bench. It ran to the bench and ate the popcorn. It was a happy ostrich. It liked popcorn.

One night, the bunny was thirsty and went out looking for something to drink. It went through the woods and soon spotted a shelter. Then, it saw a pond nearby and excitedly hopped over to get a drink.
The bunny said to himself, "I'm so thirsty. I will drink from the pond." As it bent down to drink, it heard another voice behind it.
It was a bear! The bear growled. The bunny knew it was in trouble.
The bear said, "I'm the owner of this shelter. You cannot drink from my pond without my permission!"
The bunny was scared, but it decided to apologize to the bear. It tried to explain that it was just very thirsty.
But the bear didn't seem to understand. The bear decided to teach the bunny a lesson and chased after it.
The bunny was terrified. It ran as fast as it could, but the bear was faster. In the end, the bear caught the bunny and ate it.
The kind bunny was gone forever. It was the last time it was helpful and tried to get a drink.

One sunny day, Princess Lily and her friends were playing "guess the picture" in the garden. Lily drew a picture of a big, hard rock. It was very hard for her friends to guess what it was. They guessed a ball, a house, and a tree, but they were all wrong. Princess Lily felt sad because her friends could not guess her picture.
Then, Princess Lily's mom, the queen, came to the garden. She saw that Lily was sad and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her mom about the hard picture she drew. The queen smiled and said, "Sometimes, things are hard, but we should not give up. We should keep trying and help each other." Princess Lily learned that it was okay for things to be hard, and that the important thing was to keep trying and be there for her friends. From that day on, she always remembered the queen's wise words and shared them with her friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a fat bird on a tree. The bird has a red chest and a black cap. It is a robin.
"Look, a robin!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"
Ben nods. He wants to talk to the bird. He tries to whistle like the bird. He makes a high sound with his mouth. But the bird does not answer. It flies away.
"Where did it go?" Ben asks. He is sad.
Lily hugs him. She has an idea. She points to a bench. There is a man on the bench. He has a whistle in his hand. He blows the whistle. It makes a loud sound.
"Maybe he can help us," Lily says. "Let's ask him."
They run to the bench. They say hello to the man. He smiles. He sees their faces. They look curious.
"Do you like my whistle?" he asks.
"Yes, we do!" Lily and Ben say.
"Can you show us how to whistle?" Ben asks.
"Sure, I can," the man says. "It is easy. You just need to put your lips together and blow. Like this."
He blows the whistle again. It makes a loud sound. Lily and Ben try to copy him. They put their lips together and blow. But they only make a soft sound. They try again and again. They do not give up.
After a while, they make a louder sound. They are happy. They thank the man. He gives them each a whistle. He says they can keep them.
"Thank you, thank you!" Lily and Ben say.
They run back to the tree. They blow their whistles. They hope the robin will come back. They want to be friends with the bird. They whistle and whistle. They have fun.

Tim and Sue were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big train set. They liked to make the train go fast and loud on the tracks.
One day, their mom gave them a treat. She gave them each a mint candy. The candy was smooth and sweet in their mouths. Tim and Sue said thank you and smiled.
But then, Tim had a bad idea. He wanted to see what would happen if he put his mint candy on the train track. He thought it would be funny to make the train crash. He did not tell Sue what he was doing.
Sue was busy making the train go around a curve. She did not see Tim's mint candy on the track. The train hit the candy and stopped. The candy got stuck in the wheels and made a mess. Sue was very angry and sad. She yelled at Tim.
"Tim, why did you do that? You ruined our train! That was not nice!"
Tim felt sorry. He knew he did a bad thing. He said sorry to Sue and tried to help her fix the train. But it was too late. The train was broken and the candy was wasted.
Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the train and the candy and the twins. She was very disappointed and mad. She said to Tim.
"Tim, you were very naughty. You did not share your candy. You did not respect your toy. You did not listen to your sister. You have to punish for what you did. You have to go to your room and think about your mistake. And you have to give Sue your other candy as a sorry gift."
Tim felt very bad. He did not want to punish. He did not want to go to his room. He did not want to give up his other candy. But he knew he had to. He said sorry again to Sue and gave her his candy. He said sorry to his mom and went to his room.
Sue felt sorry for Tim too. She knew he was just curious and wanted to have fun. She did not want him to punish too much. She said to her mom.
"Mom, can I go to Tim's room and play with him? I forgive him for what he did. And I want to share my candy with him. Maybe we can fix the train together."
Mom smiled and hugged Sue. She said to her.
"Sue, you are very kind and sweet. You know how to forgive and share. You can go to Tim's room and play with him. But first, let me help you clean up the mess. And maybe we can find a way to fix the train too."
The twins learned a lesson that day. They learned that mint candy is not for playing. They learned that toys are for respecting. They learned that sisters and brothers are for loving. They learned that saying sorry and forgiving are important. They learned that mom is always there to help and teach. They learned that playing together is more fun than playing alone.

"OK, Ben, I like red. But what about these birds? They are small and blue. They are budgies. Can we sort them by size?" Lily asked.
"Sure, Lily, we can sort them by size. The macaws are bigger than the budgies. But what about these birds? They are big and white. They are swans. They are bigger than the macaws. How can we sort them?" Ben wondered.
"Maybe we can sort them by sound, Ben. The macaws are loud and squawky. The budgies are quiet and chirpy. The swans are silent and graceful. Do you hear them?" Lily suggested.
"Yes, Lily, I hear them. You are right. We can sort them by sound. That is a perfect way to sort them. We are good at sorting, Lily. We are smart," Ben said.
"Thank you, Ben. You are smart, too. I like sorting with you. Sorting is fun. Do you want to sort more animals?" Lily said.
"Yes, Lily, I want to sort more animals. Let's go and see the monkeys. They are funny and noisy. Maybe we can sort them by what they do," Ben said.
"OK, Ben, let's go and see the monkeys. I like monkeys. They are cute and silly. Maybe we can sort them by what they eat," Lily said.
Ben and Lily ran to see the monkeys. They had fun sorting them. They had fun at the zoo. Mom and Dad smiled and watched them. They were proud of Ben and Lily. They were happy.

Sara likes the rockhopper penguin. She thinks it is cool and pretty. She smiles and waves to it. The rockhopper penguin looks at Sara and makes a loud noise. It sounds like it is saying hello.
"Hello, rockhopper penguin," Sara says. "You are rare and I like you. Maybe one day I can bathe with you. But for now, I will just watch you and be your friend."

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the garden. One day, they see a big truck with many sheep in it. The truck stops near their house.
"Look, Sara, sheep!" Ben says. "They have soft wool. Can we touch them?"
Sara nods. They run to the truck and ask the man who drives it. The man smiles and says, "Sure, you can touch them. But be gentle. They are going to the farm to get a haircut."
Sara and Ben touch the wool. It is warm and fluffy. They like it. They see a small sheep that is not in the truck. It is behind a bush. It looks scared.
"Hello, little sheep," Sara says. "Why are you not in the truck?"
The sheep bleats. It does not want to go to the farm. It likes its wool.
"Can we keep it, please?" Ben asks the man.
The man shakes his head. "No, you can't. It belongs to the farmer. He needs the wool to make clothes and blankets. Come on, little sheep, get in the truck."
The sheep runs away. It does not want to lose its wool. Sara and Ben chase it. They catch it and hug it.
"Please, let us keep it," Sara says. "We will take good care of it. We will not cut its wool."
The man sighs. He sees that Sara and Ben love the sheep. He thinks for a while. Then he says, "OK, you can keep it. But you have to ask your mom and dad first. And you have to carry it to your house. It is heavy."
Sara and Ben are happy. They thank the man. They ask their mom and dad. They say yes. They help Sara and Ben carry the sheep to their house. They give it a name. They call it Wooly.
Wooly is happy too. It has a new home and new friends. It does not have to go to the farm. It keeps its wool. It is clear that Sara and Ben and Wooly love each other. They play together in the garden every day.

The little boy smiled. "Yes, complete silence!" he said. 
Mum suddenly looked sad. "Oh sweetheart, why don't you go and play outside now?" she asked. 
The little boy stopped smiling and hung his head. He looked ashamed. 
"But why, Mum?" 
Mum gently put her hand on his shoulder. "I just think it would make you happy, sweetheart. Plus, Dad and I need some time to ourselves." 
The little boy nodded and ran outside. He shut the door behind him and forced a big smile. He was a little bit ashamed, but glad he still had a chance to play outside. 
The silence in the kitchen felt even bigger without him, but Mum and Dad were happy, knowing the little boy was happy too.

They hugged each other and said, "I forgive you."

One day, a big whale swam in the deep blue sea. The whale saw a pretty flower that was about to bloom. The whale was so happy to see the flower. He knew that when it bloomed, it would be very pretty.
"Hello, little flower," said the whale. "I can't wait to see you bloom!" The flower smiled at the whale. It was excited to bloom too. But it needed some help. The flower told the whale that it was very thirsty.
The whale wanted to help the flower. He swam to the top of the water and took a big breath. Then, he sprayed water from his blowhole onto the flower. The flower drank the water and started to grow.
The flower grew and grew, and soon, it was ready to bloom. The whale watched as the flower bloomed into a beautiful, bright color. But then, the whale saw that the flower was spoiled. It had too much water and its petals were falling off.
"Oh no, little flower!" said the whale. "I'm so sorry I gave you too much water." The flower smiled at the whale and said, "It's okay, big whale. Thank you for helping me. I still got to bloom, and I was happy to meet you." The whale smiled and swam away, happy to have met the flower too.

Tom and Mia went to the zoo with their mom. They wanted to see the animals and learn new things. Mom said they could choose one animal to observe closely and draw a picture of it.
Tom and Mia looked at the lions, the monkeys, the giraffes, and the penguins. They were all very interesting, but they wanted to find something more original. Then they saw the otters. The otters were swimming, playing, and sliding in the water. They looked very happy and funny.
"Can we observe the otters, mom?" Tom asked.
"Sure, let's go closer and watch them," mom said. She gave them each a paper and a crayon.
Tom and Mia sat on a bench and observed the otters. They noticed how they had brown fur, long tails, and small ears. They saw how they used their paws to hold fish and shells. They heard how they made squeaky noises to communicate.
"Look, that one is doing a trick!" Mia said, pointing at an otter that was spinning in the air.
"Wow, that's amazing!" Tom said. He tried to draw the otter on his paper, but it was too fast.
Mia decided to draw a different otter, one that was resting on a rock. She drew its shape, its fur, and its eyes. She was very proud of her picture.
"Mom, look at my picture!" Mia said, showing her mom.
"That's very good, Mia. You observed the otter very well," mom said.
"Thank you, mom. What about Tom's picture?" Mia asked.
Tom looked at his paper. He had only drawn a circle and some lines. He felt sad.
"I'm sorry, mom. I couldn't draw the otter. It was too hard," Tom said.
"That's okay, Tom. You tried your best. And you know what? Your picture is very original. No one else has drawn an otter like that," mom said.
Tom smiled. He realized that his picture was special, just like the otter. He showed it to Mia and the otters. They all squeaked in approval.

Anna liked to look at small things with her new microscope. She got it for her birthday from her dad, who was a scientist. He taught her how to use it and how to be careful with it. She liked to see the hairs on a leaf, the spots on a ladybug, and the shapes of salt crystals.
One day, she found a jar with some water and a label that said "pond life". She was curious and wanted to see what was inside. She opened the jar and poured some water on a slide. She put the slide under the microscope and looked through the eyepiece. She saw many tiny animals swimming and crawling. They had legs, tails, shells, and eyes. Some were green, some were brown, some were clear. They looked like aliens to Anna.
She was so fascinated that she did not hear her mom calling her for lunch. She did not notice that one of the animals had escaped from the slide and was crawling on the table. It was a water flea, and it was looking for a way back to the water. It saw the jar and jumped towards it. But it missed and landed on the floor.
"Anna, come here, please!" her mom said again, louder. Anna heard her and got up from her chair. She did not see the water flea on the floor. She stepped on it and squished it.
"Oops!" she said. She looked down and saw a tiny stain on her shoe. She did not know what it was. She wiped it off with a tissue and threw it in the trash. She ran to the kitchen to have lunch with her mom.
She did not know that she had killed the water flea that had escaped from her microscope. She did not know that there were many more animals in the jar, waiting for their turn to be seen. She did not know that some of them were hungry and looking for food. She did not know that some of them were predators and looking for prey. She did not know that some of them were smart and looking for a way out. She did not know that her new microscope was a dangerous place for pond life.

Lily and Ben were playing with sticks and stones in the backyard. They liked to make shapes and sounds with them. Lily found a big, rough stone that was shiny and smooth on one side. She showed it to Ben and said, "Look, this is my treasure. It is pretty and hard."
Ben wanted to see the stone, but Lily did not want to share. She said, "No, it is mine. You can't have it." She held the stone close to her chest and turned away from Ben.
Ben felt sad and angry. He thought Lily was not nice. He looked around and saw a dry twig on the ground. He picked it up and said, "Fine, I don't need your stone. I have this twig. It is better than your stone. It can make fire."
Lily did not believe him. She said, "No, it can't. You are lying. You are silly. You can't make fire with a twig."
Ben wanted to prove her wrong. He rubbed the twig on the rough stone, hoping to see a spark. He rubbed harder and harder, but nothing happened. He got frustrated and threw the twig at the stone. The twig bounced off the stone and hit Lily on the head.
Lily cried out in pain and dropped the stone. She felt a bump on her head and tears in her eyes. She said, "Ow, ow, ow! That hurt! Why did you do that?"
Ben felt sorry and scared. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I was trying to make fire. I was mad at you. I wanted your stone."
Lily and Ben looked at each other and realized they were both wrong. They had been mean and selfish. They had not shared or listened. They had not been good friends.
They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry. I forgive you. Let's be friends again."
They picked up the stone and the twig and decided to play together. They learned that sharing and caring are better than fighting and hurting. They learned that fire is not a toy and that they should be careful with sticks and stones. They learned that friendship is more precious than any treasure.

"Stay here with me," mom said. "The fire truck is here to help. The fire is very hot and dangerous. We need to be safe and far away."
But Ben and Lily were curious. They ran behind a tree and peeked at the house. They saw some men in yellow suits and helmets. They had masks on their faces and axes in their hands. They were firemen. They went inside the house with the hose. They were brave.
Then Ben and Lily heard a loud bark. It was a dog. The dog was in the house. It was scared and trapped. It ran to the window and looked out. It had a wide mouth and big eyes. It wanted to get out.
"Look, mom, a dog!" Ben and Lily shouted. They felt sorry for the dog. They wanted to help.
"Stay back, kids," one of the firemen said. He saw the dog too. He put down his axe and ran to the window. He broke the glass with his hand. He reached for the dog. The dog was happy. It licked his face.
The fireman lifted the dog and carried it outside. He knelt down and put the dog on the ground. He checked if the dog was hurt. The dog was fine. It wagged its tail and barked.
"Good boy, good boy," the fireman said. He gave the dog a hug.
Ben and Lily clapped their hands. They were glad the dog was safe. They ran to the fireman and the dog. They asked if they could pet the dog.
"Sure, kids, but be gentle," the fireman said. He smiled. He was kind.
Ben and Lily knelt down and stroked the dog's fur. The dog licked their faces too. They laughed. They made a new friend.
Mom came over and thanked the fireman. She was proud of him. She was also proud of Ben and Lily. She hugged them and said they were good kids.
They all watched as the fire truck put out the fire. The house was saved. The dog's owner came and thanked the firemen too. He was happy to see his dog. He thanked Ben and Lily for caring.
They all said goodbye and went their ways. Ben and Lily waved to the fire truck as it drove away. They had a fun and exciting day. They learned a lot. They learned about fire trucks, firemen, and dogs. They learned about danger, bravery, and kindness. They learned to kneel and to care.

Once upon a time there was a family of bees who lived in a big tree. The big tree had three stages that the bees lived on.
The first stage was the most flexible; the family could do whatever they wanted there. 
The second stage was where the family stored all of their honey. The bees were very particular about this. 
The third stage was where the family held their activities. 
One day, one of the younger bees decided to explore the third stage. The parents warned the young bee not to go, but it didn't listen. 
When the young bee got to the third stage, it was too late. It fell off the edge of the tree and became trapped there! 
The family tried to get the young bee to safety, but it was stuck. But then the mother bee had an idea. She thought that if the stage was more flexible, the young bee might be able to squeeze out of it. 
So, the family worked together to make the stage more flexible. They used their wings to brush and bend the twigs until it was just the right shape. 
Finally, the young bee made it back up safely. From then on, the family used their wings to make sure the stage was always flexible. 
 
The End.

"Let's feed our dolls," Lily said. "They must be hungry."
"Okay," Tom said. "But I don't have any food for my doll."
Lily looked around and saw a string on the ground. She picked it up and gave it to Tom.
"Here, you can use this as food," she said. "It looks like spaghetti."
Tom took the string and put it on his doll's plate. He pretended to feed his doll with a spoon.
"Yum, yum, yum," he said. "My doll likes spaghetti."
But the string was not food. It was a worm. The worm was hiding in the string and it was very angry. It did not like to be on a plate. It did not like to be fed with a spoon. It wanted to go back to the ground.
The worm wriggled and twisted and bit Tom's finger.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The string bit me!"
Lily looked at the string and saw the worm. She screamed and dropped her cup.
"That's not string, that's a worm!" she said. "You are so foolish, Tom. How can you feed a worm to your doll?"
Tom felt very silly and very sorry. He threw the worm away and ran to his mom. He wanted a band-aid and a hug.
Lily picked up her doll and her cup. She did not want to play with Tom anymore. She wanted to find real food for her doll. She thought Tom was a bad friend.

In the end, Lucy and Spot found the big, red ball, but it was in a deep hole. Lucy fell into the hole and couldn't get out. Spot tried to help, but he couldn't. The bitter old cat came and said, "I told you it was not safe." The moral of the story is to listen to those who try to keep you safe.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a big box in the garage. They thought it was a good place to hide and pretend.
"Let's be pirates and sail the seas!" Ben said.
"Okay, but I want to be the captain!" Sara said.
They climbed into the box and used a broom as a mast. They put a blanket over the box to make a sail. They pretended to see sharks and islands and treasure.
"Look, there's a ship! Let's attack it and take their gold!" Ben shouted.
"Repeat, repeat, what did you say?" Sara asked. She could not hear him well under the blanket.
"I said, there's a ship! Let's attack it and take their gold!" Ben repeated.
"Oh, okay. But be careful, they might have cannons!" Sara said.
They made loud noises and waved their arms. They had a lot of fun.
Soon, their mom came to the garage. She saw the box moving and heard the noises. She lifted the blanket and smiled.
"What are you two doing in there?" she asked.
"We're pirates, mom! We're sailing the seas and fighting other ships!" Ben said.
"That sounds very exciting. But it's time for lunch now. Come out of the box and wash your hands," mom said.
"Can we play pirates again after lunch?" Sara asked.
"Sure, if you want to. But first, you have to put the box and the broom and the blanket back where you found them. And you have to say thank you to dad for giving you the box. He was very thoughtful to save it for you," mom said.
"Okay, mom. Thank you, dad!" Sara and Ben said.
They got out of the box and hugged their mom. They ran to the kitchen to eat their lunch. They were happy and hungry. They liked to play pirates, but they also liked to eat.

One day, however, the elderly man decided to stay out later than usual. The sky was growing dark, but he was so caught up in his book that he didn't notice how late it was. Suddenly, a gust of wind swept across the park and the man's book flew away! 
The elderly man was afraid, but he must have been very brave because he ran after his book. As he chased it, it seemed like the book was leading him in a certain direction.
Eventually, the man got too close to the edge of a very deep pit that he hadn't seen before. He stopped in his tracks and tried to back away, but it was too late. He fell into the pit, never to be seen again. 
The elderly man was never able to finish his book, but the jazz records played all night long and told the story of the man who loved to read and had gotten himself into an unlucky and dangerous situation.

Ben and Mia were at the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the seesaw and the slide. The slide was very big and shiny, and they had to climb many steps to reach the top.
"Look, mom, I can slide very fast!" Ben shouted as he slid down the slide. He landed on the soft grass and laughed.
"Me too, me too!" Mia said. She followed her brother and slid down the slide. She was a little scared, but she liked the feeling of the wind in her hair.
They slid down the slide many times, until they saw a man with a cart. The man had many candies in his cart. He had lollipops, gummies, chocolates and more. Ben and Mia loved candies. They ran to the man and asked him for some.
"Please, please, can we have some candies?" they said.
The man smiled and said, "Sure, you can have one candy each. But you have to pay me one coin for each candy."
Ben and Mia looked at their mom. She was sitting on a bench, reading a book. They did not have any coins. They felt sad.
"Please, mom, can we have some coins for candies?" they said.
Mom looked at them and said, "No, you can't. You already had a snack before we came to the park. You don't need any more candies. They are not good for your teeth and your tummy. Come on, let's go back to the slide. It's more fun than candies."
But Ben and Mia did not want to go back to the slide. They wanted candies. They were persistent. They kept asking their mom for coins. They whined and cried and stamped their feet.
"Please, mom, please, please, please!"
Mom was not happy. She said, "Stop it, Ben and Mia. You are being very naughty and rude. If you don't stop, we will have to go home and you will have no candies and no slide. Is that what you want?"
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They did not want to go home. They wanted to stay at the park and play on the slide. They realized that they were being silly and selfish. They said sorry to their mom and to the man. They gave him a hug and a smile.
"Sorry, mom, sorry, man. We don't need candies. We have the slide. The slide is better than candies."
Mom smiled and said, "That's right, Ben and Mia. The slide is better than candies. I'm proud of you for being good and polite. Now, let's go back to the slide and have some more fun."
Ben and Mia nodded and ran back to the slide. They slid down the slide many times, until they were tired and happy. They forgot about the candies. They had the slide. The slide was better than candies.

"I have an idea," Ben said. "Let's play twist." He showed Anna how to twist his body and make funny shapes. Anna giggled and tried to copy him.
They twisted and turned on the floor, making each other laugh. They twisted their arms, their legs, their necks, and their faces. They twisted so much that they got dizzy and fell down.
But then, they heard a loud snap. They looked up and saw that the television cord had come loose from the wall. It was thin and frayed, and it had twisted around Ben's foot when he was playing.
"Uh-oh," Ben said. "Mama is going to be mad."
They heard Mama coming from the kitchen. She saw the television cord and the broken plug. She saw Ben and Anna on the floor, looking scared.
"What did you do?" she asked, her voice stern.
"We were playing twist, Mama," Anna said. "We didn't mean to break the television."
Mama sighed. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She knew that Ben and Anna were just trying to have fun. She hugged them and said, "It's okay. I can fix the television later. But next time, be careful with the cords. They are not toys. They can be dangerous."
She unplugged the television and put the cord away. She told Ben and Anna to go to their room and find something else to play with. She hoped they would not twist anything else.

"Hello, Anna!" Ben and Lily say. "Are you ready to dance?"
"Yes, I am!" Anna says. "I love to dance!"
They walk to the dance studio. There they see their teacher, Miss Rose. She is very nice. She smiles and says, "Welcome, children! Today we are going to learn a new dance. It is called the bunny hop. Are you alert and ready?"
"Yes, we are!" Anna, Ben and Lily say.
Miss Rose shows them how to do the bunny hop. They have to hop like bunnies, with their ears up and their noses twitching. They have to follow the music and the rhythm. They have to have fun.
Anna, Ben and Lily try to do the bunny hop. They hop and hop and hop. They laugh and giggle. They have fun. They dance.

Lila did not believe him. She shrugged and said, "I don't care. I want to climb on the rock. It looks fun."
She ran to the rock and tried to climb on it. But the rock was not strong. It cracked and crumbled under her feet. Lila fell down and scraped her knee. She cried out loud.
Ben ran to her and helped her up. He said, "I told you the rock was fragile. Are you okay?"

Ben hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lila. I'm sorry you got hurt. Let's go to the nurse and get a band-aid. Then we can play something else."
Lila smiled and said, "Okay, Ben. Thank you for being my friend."
They walked to the nurse together, holding hands. They learned a lesson about the rock and about listening.

The next day, Lesley decided to take a longer walk with Buster, so they could go further than the park. But they had gone too far and Buster got so excited, he ran off without his leash. Lesley was so worried and shouted for Buster to come back. But he had disappeared.
Lesley was so sad and never saw Buster again. The park had been his home, but now he was gone. She learnt that she should have valued cleanliness more and never let him off his leash.

He used the screwdriver to loosen the bolts and the hammer to bang the chain. He tried to pump air into the tire, but it did not work. He got frustrated and angry. He threw the tools on the floor and kicked the bike. He made a big mess and a loud noise.

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you too. I want to learn how to fix things like you. Can you teach me?"

She took a peach crayon and showed it to Lily.
Lily looked at the peach crayon and then at her picture. She said, "Oh, I see. I used the wrong color. I'm sorry, mommy. I didn't mean to make daddy look funny." Mommy said, "It's okay, Lily. The moral of the story is: Love is more important than perfection.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "Our ball is gone!"
Lily tried to cheer him up. "Don't worry, Ben. Maybe we can get it later. Let's go have dinner now. Mom made spaghetti and meatballs, your favorite!"
Ben nodded, but he was still sad. He loved his ball. He hoped it would not stay in the tree forever.

Ben looked at Mom and sighed. He told her what happened to his ball. He hoped she would not be mad.
Mom smiled and hugged him. "I'm sorry, Ben. I know how much you love your ball. But don't worry, we can get it back. After dinner, we can go outside and use a ladder to reach the branch. How does that sound?"

Ben caught the ball and hugged it. He was so happy. He thanked Mom and said, "I love you, Mom. And I love my ball!"

Sara and Tom were playing hide and seek in the park. Sara was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Tom ran behind a big bush and waited for Sara to find him. He was very quiet and still.
Sara looked around the park and called out, "Tom, where are you? I can't see you!" She walked near the bush where Tom was hiding, but she did not look behind it. She went to another place and looked some more.
Tom thought Sara would never find him. He felt bored and lonely. He wanted to play with Sara again. He decided to come out of the bush and surprise her. He jumped out and shouted, "Boo!"
But Sara was not there. She had gone to the other side of the park. Tom did not see her. He felt scared and sad. He wondered where Sara had gone. He thought she had vanished.
He started to cry and called out, "Sara, Sara, where are you? Please come back!" He hoped Sara would hear him and come back.
Sara heard Tom's voice and ran back to him. She saw him crying and hugged him. She said, "Tom, I'm sorry. I did not know you were behind the bush. I did not vanish. I was looking for you."
Tom stopped crying and smiled. He said, "Sara, I'm sorry too. I wanted to surprise you, but I scared myself. I'm glad you're here."
Sara and Tom hugged again and said, "We're friends." They decided to play another game, but this time they stayed close to each other. They did not want to vanish again. They wanted to have fun.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. But they did not like to clean up their mess. They left the cars all over the floor and the sofa and the table.
"Time to tidy up, kids!" Mom called from the kitchen. "Dinner is ready soon!"
Lily and Tom groaned. They did not want to stop playing. They wanted to keep having fun.
"Can we play a little more, Mom?" Lily asked.
"No, you can't. You have to tidy up now. It's not fair to leave your toys everywhere. Someone could trip and get hurt. And it's not nice to be messy. You have to respect your home and your things." Mom said.
Lily and Tom knew Mom was right, but they still felt lazy. They decided to play a trick on Mom. They took their toy cars and put them in reverse. They made them go backwards and hide under the couch and the chairs and the pillows. They thought Mom would not see them and they could play with them later.
"Look, Mom, we tidied up!" Tom said, pretending to be proud.
Mom came to the living room and looked around. She saw that the floor was clear, but she also saw something strange. She saw little wheels and bumpers and headlights poking out from under the furniture. She realized what Lily and Tom had done.
"That's not tidy, that's sneaky!" Mom said, frowning. "You did not put your cars away, you just reversed them and hid them. That's not how you tidy up. That's how you make more trouble. You have to take your cars out and put them in the toy box. And you have to apologize for lying to me."
Lily and Tom felt ashamed. They knew Mom was angry and disappointed. They did not like to make Mom feel that way. They took their cars out and put them in the toy box. They said sorry to Mom and gave her a hug.
"We're sorry, Mom. We won't reverse our cars and hide them again. We'll tidy up properly next time." Lily and Tom said.
Mom smiled and hugged them back. She was glad they learned their lesson.
"That's good, kids. I'm proud of you for being honest and responsible. Now you can have dinner and maybe play a little more later. But remember, always tidy up after yourself. It's the right thing to do." Mom said.
The end.
Moral value: The story teaches the value of honesty, responsibility and respect. It shows that lying and hiding things is not a good way to avoid chores, and that it can hurt the feelings of others. It also shows that tidying up is important for safety and order, and that it can make the home and the toys more enjoyable.

So, they picked fruits all day long. But when the sun went down, the little boy got lost. He was very sad and scared. The good wolf tried to help him find his way home, but they couldn't.
In the end, the little boy and the good wolf stayed lost in the big forest. They were both very sad. The moral of the story is to always stay close to your family and not to talk to strangers, even if they seem good.

Tom and Lily were playing in the old barn. They liked to pretend they were explorers, finding treasures and secrets. They climbed on the hay bales, crawled under the planks, and peeked through the cracks. They saw many things: a rusty bike, a broken doll, a shiny tin can.
But they also saw many cobwebs. Cobwebs were sticky and icky. They made Tom and Lily sneeze and itch. They did not like cobwebs. They tried to avoid them, but sometimes they touched them by mistake.
"Yuck!" Tom said, as he wiped a cobweb from his face. "I hate cobwebs. They are everywhere."
"Me too," Lily agreed. "They are gross. Let's get rid of them."
They decided to unite and work together. They found a broom and a stick. They used them to sweep and poke the cobwebs. They made a big pile of cobwebs in the corner. They felt proud and happy.
But then they heard a voice. A small, sad voice.
"Please, stop. You are hurting us."
Tom and Lily looked around. They saw a spider on the wall. It was looking at them with big, wet eyes.
"Who are you?" Tom asked.
"I am Sam. And these are my friends. We live in the cobwebs. They are our homes. You are destroying them."
Tom and Lily felt ashamed. They did not know that the cobwebs were homes for spiders. They did not mean to hurt them. They felt sorry.
"We are sorry, Sam," Lily said. "We did not know. We were just playing."
"Can you please stop?" Sam asked. "We have nowhere else to go. We are harmless. We only eat flies and bugs. We do not bother you."
Tom and Lily nodded. They put down the broom and the stick. They looked at the pile of cobwebs. They felt bad.
"Is there anything we can do to help?" Tom asked.
Sam thought for a moment. He had an idea.
"Maybe you can help us rebuild our homes. You can use the cobwebs you swept. You can make new shapes and patterns. You can be creative. We will be grateful."
Tom and Lily liked the idea. They thought it sounded fun. They agreed to help.
They picked up the cobwebs and started to make new homes for the spiders. They made circles and stars and hearts. They made letters and numbers and animals. They made a big, beautiful web.
The spiders were happy. They thanked Tom and Lily. They invited them to visit anytime. They became friends.
Tom and Lily learned a lesson. They learned that cobwebs were not just sticky and icky. They learned that they were homes for spiders. They learned that they should not judge things by how they look. They learned that they should be kind and respectful to all living things.
They smiled and hugged. They felt good. They had united with the spiders. They had made a difference.

Sue wanted to warn her friends about the flood. She decided to tear a piece of paper and write a note to her friends. She wrote, "Watch out for the flood!" Sue gave the note to her friends, and they all read it. They were thankful for Sue's warning.
The rain came, and it rained a lot. The river started to flood, just like Sue thought it would. But because of her note, all her friends were ready. They moved their things to higher places and stayed safe. When the flood was over, they all thanked Sue for her help. Sue was happy she could help her friends, and they all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, Tom saw Sam's new truck and wanted it very much. He asked Sam, "Can I have your truck? It is big and red and makes noise."
Sam liked his truck and did not want to give it away. He said, "No, this is my truck. You have your own toys. Go and play with them."
Tom felt angry and jealous. He thought of a way to get the truck. He said, "How about we trade? You give me your truck and I give you my teddy bear. It is soft and cuddly and you can sleep with it."
Sam was not very smart and did not know what trade meant. He thought Tom was being nice and wanted to share. He said, "OK, we can trade. Here is my truck. Give me your teddy bear."
Tom smiled and took the truck. He gave Sam his teddy bear, but it was old and dirty and had a hole in it. Sam did not notice and hugged the teddy bear. He said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend."
Tom ran away with the truck and played with it. He felt happy and proud. He did not care about Sam or his teddy bear.
Soon, it was time for lunch. Tom and Sam went to their homes. Tom's mom made him a sandwich and a glass of milk. She said, "Eat well, Tom. You must be hungry after playing so much."
Tom was not hungry. He had eaten a lot of candy before playing. He said, "No, thank you, mom. I am not hungry. I just want to play with my truck."
Tom's mom was surprised and worried. She said, "But you need to eat, Tom. Candy is not good for you. It will make you sick and spoil your teeth. Please eat your sandwich and drink your milk."
Tom did not listen. He said, "No, mom. I don't want to. Leave me alone." He ran to his room with his truck.
Tom's mom was sad and angry. She said, "Fine, Tom. Do what you want. But don't come to me when you feel bad."
Tom played with his truck for a long time. He made it go fast and loud. He did not care about anything else. He did not notice that he was feeling tired and sick. He did not notice that his mouth was dry and his stomach was hurting. He did not notice that his teeth were hurting and his gums were bleeding.
He only noticed when he could not play anymore. He felt very bad and weak. He wanted to cry and call his mom. He wanted to eat and drink. He wanted to sleep and cuddle. He looked at his truck and did not like it anymore. He looked at his teddy bear and missed it very much. He wished he had not traded it with Sam. He wished he had been a good friend and a good son.
He tried to get up and go to his mom, but he could not. He fell on his bed and closed his eyes. He yawned and whispered, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry, teddy bear."
But no one heard him. No one came to help him. He was alone and sick and sad.
The end.
Moral: Don't be greedy and selfish. Be kind and honest. Share and care. Eat well and listen to your mom.

"Look, it is moving!" Lily said. "It is restless. It wants to go back to the dirt."
"Let's keep it as a pet," Tom said. "We can give it some leaves and water."
They took the jar to the porch and put it on a table. They went to get some leaves and water. But they did not see that the sun was shining on the jar. The jar got very hot. The worm got very hot too.
"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" the worm said. "It is burning! Help me, help me!"
The worm tried to get out of the jar, but it was too tight. It was very scared and sad.
Tom and Lily came back with the leaves and water. They saw the worm in the jar. They saw that it was burning.
"Oh no, oh no, oh no!" they said. "We are sorry, worm! We did not mean to hurt you!"
They quickly opened the jar and took out the worm. They put it on the grass and poured some water on it. They hoped that it would feel better.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" the worm said. "You are kind. You saved me."
The worm smiled and waved at them. Then it crawled back to the dirt.
Tom and Lily felt sorry for the worm. They learned that they should not keep worms in jars. They decided to let the worms be free in the garden. They played with other things instead.

The rock hit Lily on the head. She fell off the swing and hit the ground. She cried and cried. She had a big bump on her head and blood on her hair. Tom was scared. He ran away and hid behind a bush.
A lady saw what happened. She ran to Lily and helped her. She called Lily's mom and the doctor. Lily's mom came and took her to the hospital. She was very sad and mad. She said, "Who did this to you, Lily?"
Lily said, "Tom did it. He was clumsy and mean. He threw a rock at me because I wanted to swing." Lily's mom said, "That was very bad of Tom. He hurt you and ran away. He is not a good friend. You should not play with him anymore."
Lily nodded. She felt sorry for herself. She wished she had not pushed Tom off the swing. She wished she had rocked with him instead. She learned a hard lesson. Rocking is better than swinging. And being nice is better than being mean.

They all laughed and said, "Wow! That smells so good!" Emma showed them the bottle and said, "It's so colorful and it sparkles, too!" 
Everyone was happy and laughed. From that day on, whenever Emma went to the park, all her friends came to greet her and enjoy her rainbow magic perfume.

Lily and Ben were playing in their room. They had many toys, but they liked the clock best. The clock was big and round, and it made funny noises. Sometimes it said "tick-tock", sometimes it said "ding-dong", and sometimes it said nothing at all.
One day, the clock stopped working. It did not say anything, and the hands did not move. Lily and Ben were sad. They wanted to fix the clock, but they did not know how. They asked their mom for help.
"Mom, our clock is broken. Can you make it work again?" Lily said.
"I'm sorry, sweeties, but I can't. The clock is very old, and it needs a special part that I don't have. Maybe we can find a new clock for you later." Mom said.
"But we love this clock. We don't want a new one. We want this one." Ben said.
"I know, honey, but sometimes things break and we have to let them go. Why don't you play with something else for now?" Mom said.
Lily and Ben did not want to play with something else. They wanted to play with the clock. They insisted that Mom try to fix it. They said "please" and "pretty please" and "pretty please with sugar on top". But Mom said no. She said it was impossible.
Lily and Ben were very upset. They cried and stomped their feet. They did not listen to Mom. They did not want to give up on the clock.
Then, they had an idea. They remembered that Dad had a toolbox in the garage. Maybe they could find something to fix the clock. They sneaked out of their room and went to the garage. They opened the toolbox and looked inside. They saw many things that they did not know. They saw hammers and nails and screws and pliers and wrenches and wires. They thought they looked like fun.
They took some of the things and went back to their room. They put the clock on the floor and started to hit it and poke it and twist it and pull it. They hoped that they could make it work again. They did not notice that they were making a big mess. They did not notice that they were breaking the clock even more. They did not notice that Mom was coming to check on them.
"Kids, what are you doing?" Mom said, when she saw the disaster. She was shocked and angry. She saw the clock in pieces, and the tools scattered everywhere. She saw the scratches and dents and sparks on the floor. She saw Lily and Ben with dirty hands and faces.
"We're fixing the clock, Mom. We're making it work again." Lily and Ben said, proudly.
Mom did not know what to say. She did not know whether to laugh or cry. She did not know how to explain to them that they had made a big mistake. She did not know how to make them understand that the clock was gone for good. She did not know how to make them happy again. She wished she had a magic wand.

He sees a big, green dinosaur with a long neck and a small head. He thinks it is a brontosaurus. He likes brontosaurus. He walks towards it. He says, "Hello, brontosaurus. You are very big and nice. Can I be your friend?"
But the brontosaurus does not answer. It does not look at Ben. It does not move. It is not a real dinosaur. It is a fake dinosaur. It is made of wood and metal and paint. Ben is very sad. He feels cheated. He hates fake dinosaurs. He says, "You are not a brontosaurus. You are a liar. You are a bad dinosaur. I hate you!"

He sees his mom and dad run to him. He sees a man with a hat and a badge. He thinks he is a famous dinosaur hunter. He hopes he will be his friend.

Ben nods and wipes his tears. He says, "Deal. I promise. I will never kick a dinosaur again. I will be a good boy. I will be a famous dinosaur hunter. And you will be my friend."
The man smiles and shakes Ben's hand. He says, "Deal. I will be your friend. And I will teach you how to make dinosaurs. Real and fake. How does that sound?"

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. Lily saw a green caterpillar on a leaf. She picked it up and showed it to Max.
"Look, Max, a caterpillar!" she said. "It is so soft and wiggly."
Max looked at the caterpillar. He wanted to touch it too. He reached out his hand, but Lily moved away.
"No, Max, it is mine!" she said. "You can find your own caterpillar."
Max felt sad and angry. He did not like to share. He grabbed the leaf from Lily and ran away. Lily chased him and shouted.
"Give it back, Max, give it back!"
They ran around the garden, until they reached the shed. Max opened the door and went inside. He shut the door behind him. He thought he was safe.
But he was not. The shed was dark and scary. He heard noises and saw shadows. He felt something crawl on his leg. He screamed and dropped the leaf.
Lily heard Max scream. She ran to the shed and opened the door. She saw Max crying and shaking. She felt sorry for him.
"Max, are you okay?" she asked. "What happened?"
Max pointed to the leaf. Lily saw the caterpillar crawling away. She also saw spiders, ants, and beetles in the shed.
"Max, you should not have taken the caterpillar," she said. "This is not a good place for it. It needs the sun and the plants. And you need to be nice and share."
Max nodded. He was sorry too. He hugged Lily and said.
"I am sorry, Lily. You are right. Can we be friends again?"
Lily smiled and said.
"Of course, Max. We are always friends. Come on, let's go outside and find more bugs and flowers. And maybe another caterpillar for you."

Sam nodded. He loved lemon cake. It was sweet and sour and soft. His mom gave him a lemon and a knife. She said, "Be careful, Sam. The knife is sharp. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice in this bowl."
Sam did as his mom said. He cut the lemon in half and squeezed the juice. But some of the juice squirted in his eye. It stung and burned. Sam dropped the lemon and the knife and cried. His mom hugged him and wiped his eye. She said, "I'm sorry, Sam. That must have hurt. Let me see your eye. It's okay. It will get better soon."
Sam felt better, but he was still grumpy. He didn't want to help his mom anymore. He wanted to eat the cake. He said, "When will the cake be ready, mom?"
His mom said, "Not yet, Sam. We have to mix the batter and put it in the oven. Then we have to wait for it to rise and bake. It will take some time, Sam. But I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?"
Sam nodded. He liked surprises. His mom opened the fridge and took out a bowl. She said, "This is the frosting for the cake. It's also lemon. Do you want to taste it, Sam?"
Sam smiled. He loved frosting. He dipped his finger in the bowl and licked it. It was sweet and sour and creamy. He said, "Mmm, this is good, mom. Can I have some more?"
His mom laughed and said, "Sure, Sam. But not too much. We have to save some for the cake. Come on, let's finish the cake together. It will be delicious, Sam. You'll see."
Sam forgot his grumpiness and helped his mom finish the cake. He stirred and poured and tasted. He watched the cake rise and bake in the oven. He spread the frosting on the cake. He decorated it with lemon slices. He was proud of his cake. He said, "Can we eat it now, mom?"
His mom said, "Yes, Sam. We can eat it now. You did a great job, Sam. You are a good helper. I love you, Sam."
Sam hugged his mom and said, "I love you too, mom. And I love lemon cake."

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tom had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were having fun until Tom saw something shiny on the floor.
"Look, Lily, a screw!" Tom said, picking up the small metal piece. "I wonder where it came from."
"Maybe from your truck," Lily said, looking at Tom's toy. "It has many screws on it."
Tom examined his truck and saw a hole where a screw was missing. He tried to fit the screw back in, but it was too hard. He needed a tool to turn the screw.
"Can I use your screwdriver, dad?" Tom asked, running to his father, who was reading a book on the couch.
"Sure, son, but be careful with it. And mind your sister, don't hurt her with the screwdriver," his father said, handing him the tool.
Tom thanked his father and ran back to his truck. He was excited to fix his toy. He put the screw in the hole and started to turn the screwdriver.
"Tom, can I help you?" Lily asked, coming closer to him.
"No, Lily, this is my truck and my screw. Go play with your doll," Tom said, pushing her away.
Lily felt sad and angry. She didn't like Tom's attitude. She wanted to play with him and his truck. She looked around and saw something enormous on the shelf. It was a big red ball that their uncle had given them for Christmas.
Lily had an idea. She climbed on a chair and reached for the ball. She held it with both hands and threw it at Tom's truck.
"Hey, what are you doing?" Tom shouted, as the ball hit his truck and made it fall over. The screw and the screwdriver flew out of his hands.
"That's what you get for being mean to me," Lily said, sticking out her tongue.
Tom was furious. He got up and chased Lily around the living room. They started to yell and fight.
Their father heard the noise and came to see what was going on. He saw the mess and the broken toys. He was not happy.
"Tom, Lily, stop it right now!" he said, in a loud voice. "Why are you behaving like this? You should share your toys and play nicely. And you should not throw things or use tools without supervision. You could have hurt yourselves or damaged something."
Tom and Lily stopped and looked at their father. They felt ashamed and sorry. They knew they had done wrong.
"We're sorry, dad," they said, in a low voice.
"Come here, both of you," their father said, opening his arms. "I love you, but you need to learn to respect each other and your things. Now, let's clean up this mess and see if we can fix your toys. And then, maybe we can play with the ball together. How does that sound?"
Tom and Lily nodded and hugged their father. They apologized to each other and helped to tidy up the living room. They hoped their toys were not too damaged. They also hoped their father would still let them play with the ball. They learned a lesson that day: to mind their manners and their toys.

Dad looks at the shark. He says, "Don't worry, Anna. The shark is not hungry. He is just curious. He will not hurt us. He is a friend of the reef. He helps to keep the reef healthy and clean. Let's wave to him and say hello."
Anna and Ben wave to the shark. The shark waves back with his tail. He swims away. Anna and Ben are not scared anymore. They are brave and proud. They swim back to the boat. The people on the boat applaud them. They say, "Well done, Anna and Ben! You are great explorers of the reef!"

"Can we play with it?" Sara and Ben ask.

Lila and Tom are best friends. They like to play hide and seek in the park. Lila is good at hiding, but Tom is good at finding. One day, they play a new game. They call it peek and tell.
Lila hides behind a big tree. She waits for Tom to find her. She hears his footsteps coming closer. She peeks from behind the tree. She sees Tom looking around. He does not see her. She smiles. She thinks she will win.
But then, Tom stops. He turns around. He looks at the tree. He sees Lila's eyes. He says, "I found you, Lila! You peeked!"
Lila comes out from behind the tree. She says, "No, I did not peek! You did not find me!"
Tom says, "Yes, you did peek! I saw you! You have to tell the truth!"
Lila says, "No, you did not see me! You are lying!"
They start to argue. They do not sound like best friends. They sound like enemies.
A lady who works in the park sees them. She comes over. She says, "What is the matter, children? Why are you fighting?"
Lila and Tom tell her their stories. They both say they are right. They both say the other is wrong.
The lady says, "Hmm, this is a tricky situation. How can we know who is telling the truth?"
She thinks for a moment. Then she says, "I have an idea. Let's play peek and tell again. But this time, I will be the seeker. You two will be the hiders. And you will have to be reliable. That means you will have to do what you say. If you say you will not peek, you will not peek. If you say you will peek, you will peek. And then you will tell me the truth. Do you agree?"
Lila and Tom nod. They agree. They think it is a fair game.
They go to hide. The lady counts to ten. Then she says, "Ready or not, here I come!"

Sam was a brown bear who loved to swim. He swam in the big lake every day, splashing and diving and having fun. He had many friends who swam with him, like the ducks, the fish and the frogs. They all liked Sam and played with him.
One day, a new bear came to the lake. He was big and black and mean. He saw Sam swimming and said, "Hey, you! Get out of the water! This is my lake now! You don't belong here!"
Sam was scared and sad. He did not want to leave his friends and his lake. He said, "But I have always swum here. This is my home. Why can't we share the lake?"
The black bear growled and said, "No! I don't share with anyone! I am the strongest and the best! You are a weak and silly brown bear who can't do anything! Go away or I will hurt you!"
Sam did not know what to do. He did not want to fight, but he did not want to lose his lake. He looked around and saw his friends watching him. They looked worried and angry. They wanted to help Sam, but they were afraid of the black bear.
Then, Sam had an idea. He remembered something his mother had taught him. He said, "Okay, I will go away, but only if you can do something better than me. Can you swim as fast as me?"
The black bear laughed and said, "Of course I can! I can do anything better than you! You are a joke!"
Sam said, "Then let's have a race. From here to that big rock and back. The winner can stay in the lake, and the loser has to leave. Do you agree?"
The black bear agreed. He was sure he would win. He did not know that Sam had a trick up his sleeve. He did not know that the big rock was the home of the beavers, who were Sam's friends too.
Sam and the black bear got ready to swim. The ducks, the fish and the frogs cheered for Sam. The black bear snorted and said, "You are wasting your time. I will beat you easily!"
Sam said, "We'll see about that. On your mark, get set, go!"
Sam and the black bear swam as fast as they could. Sam was ahead, but the black bear was close behind. They reached the big rock and turned around. But as they did, the beavers came out of their hole and bit the black bear's tail. The black bear yelped and stopped swimming. He was in pain and angry. He tried to shake off the beavers, but they held on tight.
Sam saw what happened and smiled. He swam back to the shore and won the race. He said, "I did it! I won! You have to leave now!"
The black bear was ashamed and furious. He said, "No fair! You cheated! You had help from the beavers!"
Sam said, "No, I didn't cheat. I used my brain and my friends. You see, the lake belongs to everyone who lives here and cares for it. You don't belong here because you are mean and selfish. You don't have any friends. You only have enemies. You should learn to be nice and share, or you will always be alone and unhappy."
The black bear realized that Sam was right. He felt sorry for himself and for what he had done. He said, "You are right. I was wrong. I'm sorry. Can you forgive me?"
Sam said, "Yes, I can forgive you. But you have to promise to be nice and share from now on. And you have to apologize to the beavers and the others too."
The black bear agreed. He apologized to the beavers and the others. He asked them if he could swim with them and be their friend. They said yes, but only if he was nice and shared. The black bear said he would. He thanked Sam for teaching him a lesson.
Sam was happy. He had saved his lake and his friends. He had also made a new friend. He said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Come on, let's swim and have fun!"
Sam and the black bear swam and had fun. The ducks, the fish and the frogs joined them. They all played and laughed and enjoyed the lake. They all belonged there. They were all happy.

Buddy barks happily and licks Ben's face. He says, "Yes, yes, yes. You can take me home. You are my best friend, too. You are kind and gentle. You make me feel comfortable and safe."
Ben and Buddy hug each other. Mom sees them and says, "I think you found your match, Ben. Buddy is a sweet and loyal dog. He needs a good home and a good family. Are you sure you want him?"
Ben says, "Yes, mom. I want him more than anything. He is my dog, and I am his boy. We belong together."
Mom says, "OK, then. Let's fill out the papers and take him home. I am happy for you, Ben. You made a good choice."

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and run in the park. But they do not like to sit and eat their food. They always say, "No, no, no! We want to play more!"
One day, Mommy makes them a yummy lunch. She puts some bread, cheese, fruit and milk on their plates. She says, "Lily and Ben, come and sit and eat your food. It is good for you and it will make you strong and happy."
But Lily and Ben do not listen. They run away and hide under the table. They say, "No, no, no! We want to play more!"
Mommy is sad. She says, "Lily and Ben, please come and sit and eat your food. I made it with love and I want you to grow and be healthy."
But Lily and Ben do not listen. They run away and hide behind the sofa. They say, "No, no, no! We want to play more!"
Mommy is angry. She says, "Lily and Ben, this is the last time I ask you. Come and sit and eat your food. Or you will have no dessert and no toys."
But Lily and Ben do not listen. They run away and hide in the closet. They say, "No, no, no! We want to play more!"
Mommy is tired. She says, "Fine. If you do not want to sit and eat your food, you can stay in the closet. I will eat your food and your dessert and play with your toys."
Lily and Ben hear Mommy. They feel sorry. They say, "Mommy, we are sorry. We were naughty. We will come and sit and eat our food. Please do not eat our food and our dessert and play with our toys."
Mommy smiles. She says, "I am glad you are sorry. I was only joking. I will not eat your food and your dessert and play with your toys. But you have to sit and eat your food and be gentle. Then you can have your dessert and play with your toys."
Lily and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mommy. We will sit and eat our food and be gentle. Thank you, Mommy. We love you."
Mommy hugs them. She says, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. You are my good twins."
The end.
Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their parents, to eat their food and to be gentle. It also shows the consequences of being naughty and the importance of saying sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a small ant named Andy. Andy was a very busy ant. He had a lot of work to do every day. One day, he was carrying a big leaf back to his home.
On his way, he met a big bear named Ben. Ben was very hungry. He saw Andy carrying the leaf and said, "Andy, can I eat your leaf? I am very hungry." Andy replied, "No, Ben. I need to finish my work. You can find other food in the forest."
Ben was sad, but he understood. He went away to look for other food. While Andy was walking, he saw a big fall. He was scared, but he knew he had to cross it. So, he took a deep breath and jumped.
Andy made it across the fall and was very happy. He finished his work and went back to his home. The moral of the story is, if you are busy and work hard, you can overcome any challenge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old, but already so brave! A warm sunny day, Lucy decided to go exploring in the woods. She found a big patch of mushrooms growing on the ground. She split the mushrooms and she could see the small insides. The mushrooms were yummy and they smelled so good. 
Suddenly, Lucy heard a funny sound coming from the bush. She walked closer, and to her surprise, she saw a little rabbit hiding there! She asked, “What are you doing here? Come say hi!”. 
The little rabbit replied, “Well, I was looking for mushrooms too. I heard you split them and I thought you found some yummy ones for us both!”. 
Lucy and the little rabbit chatted and exchanged stories until it started to get dark. Before they parted, the little rabbit gave Lucy a big hug and said, “It was great to meet you. Let’s come back together for the mushrooms again soon!” 
Lucy and the little rabbit said goodbye and went their separate ways. Lucy was so excited that she had made a new friend in the woods and they both enjoyed the yummy mushrooms.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. Sam has many cars and trucks. He is rich. Ben has only one car. He is not rich.
One day, Sam and Ben go to the park. They see a big hill. Sam says, "Let's play on the hill. We can race our cars and trucks down the hill. I will win because I have more cars and trucks than you."
Ben says, "OK, let's play. But I can win too. My car is fast and strong. It has a name. Its name is Red."
Sam says, "A name? That is silly. Cars and trucks don't have names. They are just toys. I have many toys. I don't need to name them."
They go to the top of the hill. They put their cars and trucks on the ground. They say, "Ready, set, go!" They push their cars and trucks down the hill.
Sam's cars and trucks go fast. But they also go wild. They bump into each other. They crash and break. They stop before the end of the hill.
Ben's car goes fast too. But it also goes straight. It does not bump or crash. It reaches the end of the hill. It is the winner.
Ben is happy. He says, "See? Red is the best car. It has a name. It has a friend. It has me."
Sam is sad. He says, "Oh no. My cars and trucks are broken. They are not fun anymore. They are just trash."
Ben says, "Don't be sad, Sam. You can play with Red. Red can share. Red can be your friend too."
Sam says, "Thank you, Ben. Thank you, Red. You are both nice. Can I name one of your trucks?"
Ben says, "Sure, Sam. You can name one of my trucks. What do you want to name it?"
Sam thinks for a moment. He says, "I want to name it Blue. Blue is a good name. Blue is a good color. Blue is a good friend."

"Help me, little bird," said the dirty owl. "I want to be clean like you. How do I clean my wings?"
The little bird looked at the owl and said, "You need to fly fast like me. The speed will make the mud fly off your wings."
So, the dirty owl tried to fly fast. He used all his speed. But the mud did not come off. The owl felt sad. He thought he would be dirty forever.
Just then, a big rain cloud came over the tree. It started to rain. The rain washed the mud off the owl's wings. He was clean! The owl was happy and thanked the little bird. The little bird smiled and said, "Sometimes, help comes when you least expect it." They both flew off into the sky, happy and clean.

Anna loved to play with her dolls. She had a big dollhouse, with many rooms and furniture. She liked to pretend that her dolls were her friends, and that they had tea parties and adventures together. She always used her favorite cup, a pink one with flowers, to pour tea for her dolls.
One day, her brother Tom came into her room. He was older and bigger than Anna, and he liked to tease her. He saw her cup on the table, and he had an idea. He said, "Hey, Anna, can I have some tea?" Anna was happy that Tom wanted to play with her. She said, "Sure, Tom, sit down and I'll pour you some." She picked up her cup and filled it with water from a pitcher.
Tom took the cup and pretended to drink. He made a face and said, "Yuck, this tea is awful! It tastes like dirt!" He spat out the water and threw the cup on the floor. The cup broke into pieces, and Anna gasped. She loved her cup, and now it was gone. She felt angry and sad. She said, "Tom, you're mean! You broke my cup! Go away!" She started to cry.
Tom felt bad. He didn't mean to break the cup, he just wanted to make a joke. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna, I didn't know you liked the cup so much. I was just playing. Please don't cry." He tried to hug her, but she pushed him away. She said, "No, you're not sorry. You don't care about me or my dolls. You don't believe in tea parties. You're a bad brother!" She ran to her bed and buried her face in her pillow.
Tom felt worse. He wanted to make Anna happy, not sad. He looked at the broken cup, and he had an idea. He ran to his room and got some glue and tape. He came back to Anna's room and said, "Anna, look, I fixed your cup. See, it's good as new. I'm really sorry, Anna, I do care about you and your dolls. I do believe in tea parties. Can we be friends again?" He showed her the cup, which was still cracked and taped, but looked like a cup again.
Anna looked at the cup, and then at Tom. She saw that he was sorry, and that he tried to fix his mistake. She felt a little better. She said, "Thank you, Tom, for fixing my cup. It's not the same, but it's still my cup. I'm sorry, too, for being mean to you. You're not a bad brother. You're a good brother. Can we have a tea party together?" She smiled and wiped her tears.
Tom smiled, too. He said, "Yes, Anna, we can have a tea party together. I'll be your guest, and you'll be the host. You can pour me some tea, and I'll drink it. I won't make a face, I promise. I'll say it's the best tea ever." He sat down and took the cup. He said, "Cheers, Anna, to tea parties and friends." He clinked the cup with Anna's, and they both laughed. They had a tea party, and they had fun. They forgot about the broken cup, and they remembered that they loved each other.

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw a hedge with many flowers. The flowers were pink and white and yellow. They smelled sweet and nice.
"Look, Tom, pretty flowers!" Sara said. She wanted to pick one for her mom. She reached out her hand to the hedge.
"Wait, Sara, don't!" Tom said. He knew the hedge had thorns. Thorns were sharp and hurt. He tried to stop Sara, but it was too late. She touched a thorn and cried out.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara said. She pulled back her hand. It had a red dot on it. It was bleeding. She felt scared and sad. She ran to her mom.
"Mom, mom, help!" Sara said. She showed her mom her hand. Her mom took her inside. She washed her hand and put a band-aid on it. She hugged Sara and kissed her.
"It's okay, Sara, it's okay," her mom said. "You have a delicate hand. You have to be careful with thorns. They can hurt you."
"I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry," Sara said. She felt sorry for picking the flower. She wanted to return it to the hedge. She thought the hedge would be sad too.
"Can I go back to the hedge, mom?" Sara asked. "I want to say sorry to the hedge and the flower."
Her mom smiled. She understood Sara's feelings. She was a kind and gentle girl.
"Sure, Sara, you can go back to the hedge," her mom said. "But be careful. Don't touch the thorns again. And say hello to Tom for me."
Sara nodded. She thanked her mom and ran back to the garden. She saw Tom waiting for her. He looked worried.
"Sara, are you okay?" Tom asked. He was sorry for Sara. He wanted to help her.
"I'm okay, Tom, I'm okay," Sara said. She showed him her band-aid. She smiled. "My mom fixed my hand. She said I have a delicate hand. Do you have a delicate hand too?"
Tom looked at his hand. It was bigger and stronger than Sara's. He shook his head.
"No, I don't have a delicate hand," Tom said. "But I have a delicate heart. I care about you, Sara. You are my friend."
Sara hugged Tom. She felt happy and warm. She was glad Tom was her friend.
"Thank you, Tom, thank you," Sara said. "You are my friend too. Come, let's go to the hedge. I want to say sorry to the hedge and the flower."
Tom nodded. He followed Sara to the hedge. They saw the flower that Sara had picked. It was wilting and sad.
"I'm sorry, hedge, I'm sorry, flower," Sara said. She put the flower back to the hedge. She hoped it would feel better. "You are pretty and nice. I won't hurt you again."
The hedge seemed to hear Sara. It rustled and shook. It made a soft sound. It sounded like "thank you".
Sara and Tom smiled. They felt happy and peaceful. They played in the garden until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the hedge and the flowers. They promised to return another day.

Jim was walking through the woods one day. He saw a big tiger leaning against a tree. Its tail was moving from side to side, like it was upset. 
Jim approached the tiger, with caution, and asked softly, "Are you alright?". The tiger just glared and continued to sway back and forth.
Jim carefully stepped back and noticed a small creature peering out from behind a bush. It was a mouse.
Jim said, "Are you the one making the tiger upset?". The mouse nodded his little head.
Jim bent down and said, "Don't worry, I'm here to help". The mouse nodded again and pointed to the tiger.
With a brave heart, Jim took a step closer and helped the mouse up onto the tiger's back. The tiger growled but remained still. 
Suddenly, the mouse started purring through its little whiskers, and the tiger leaned its head down against the mouse. The mouse was purring louder, and the tiger seemed content. 
Jim smiled, pleased that he was able to help the two friends.

Their mom was happy to see them. She said, "I am glad you are safe, Ben and Spot. You learned a valuable lesson today. Never trust a pirate. And always listen to your mom."

One day, the big, strong man went to the market. When he came back, the small girl was gone. He looked around and saw that his big chest was open. All his shiny things were gone too! The big, strong man was very sad. He was not proud anymore. The small girl, who he thought was his friend, took all his shiny things and left. The big, strong man learned that not everyone is who they seem to be.

Lily liked to draw with her pink crayons. She had a big file where she kept all her drawings. She drew flowers, stars, hearts and animals. She was very proud of her file.
One day, her brother Max came into her room. He saw her file on the floor. He was curious. He opened the file and looked at the drawings. He did not like them. He thought they were too pink and too girly. He took a black crayon and started to scribble over the drawings.
Lily saw what he was doing and ran to him. She was very angry and sad. She shouted at him.
"Max, quit it! Quit it now! You are ruining my drawings! They are mine, not yours! Give me back my file!"
Max did not listen. He laughed and kept scribbling. He said.
"Your drawings are silly and boring. Pink is a bad color. Black is better. I am making them more fun."
Lily tried to grab the file from him, but he was stronger. He pushed her away. She fell on the floor and started to cry.
Mom heard the noise and came into the room. She saw what was happening and scolded Max.
"Max, what are you doing? How could you be so mean to your sister? You have to apologize to her and help her fix her drawings. You have to respect her things and her feelings. And you have to quit being rude and selfish."
Max felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had hurt Lily. He gave her back the file and said.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have touched your file or your drawings. I know you like pink and I like black, but that's okay. We can like different things. Can you forgive me?"
Lily stopped crying and looked at him. She saw he was sincere. She nodded and said.
"I forgive you, Max. But you have to promise me you won't do it again. And you have to help me make my drawings nice again. Maybe we can use some other colors too, like blue and green and yellow."
Max agreed and hugged her. He said.
"I promise, Lily. And I will help you. Maybe we can draw together and make a new file for both of us. And maybe we can use some stickers and glitter too."
Lily smiled and hugged him back. She said.
"That sounds fun, Max. I love you, brother."
Mom smiled and said.
"I love you too, kids. Now, let's go and get some paper and crayons and start drawing."

Emma liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long yellow hair and a pink dress. Emma liked to brush Lily's hair and make her look charming.
One day, Emma found a new hat in her mom's closet. It was a big hat with flowers and ribbons. Emma thought it would match Lily's dress. She took the hat and ran to her room. She put the hat on Lily's head and smiled.
"Look, Lily, you are so pretty!" Emma said. "Do you like your new hat?"
But Lily did not say anything. She just stared at Emma with her blue eyes. Emma felt sad. She wanted Lily to talk to her.
"Please, Lily, say something!" Emma begged. "Don't you like me?"
Emma did not know that Lily was not a real doll. She was a magic doll. She could talk, but only when she wore the right hat. The hat in mom's closet was not the right hat. It was a hat for another magic doll.
The other magic doll was in mom's closet too. She was hiding behind some coats. She had short brown hair and a green dress. She was angry. She wanted her hat back. She did not like Emma or Lily.
She waited until Emma left the room. Then she sneaked out of the closet and went to Emma's room. She saw Lily on the bed, wearing her hat. She grabbed the hat and pulled it off Lily's head.
"Ha, ha, ha!" she laughed. "This is my hat, not yours! You are a silly doll!"
But as soon as she put the hat on her own head, she stopped laughing. She felt a shock. The hat was not her hat either. It was a trick hat. It made her say the opposite of what she wanted to say.
"Oh, no, no, no!" she cried. "This is not my hat, it is yours! You are a charming doll!"
Lily heard her voice. She opened her mouth and spoke.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" she said. "This is the right hat for me! You are a nice doll!"
Emma came back to the room. She saw the two dolls talking. She was amazed. She clapped her hands and joined them.
"Wow, wow, wow!" she said. "You can talk! You are both my friends!"
The three of them played happily together. They tried on different hats and matched them with their dresses. They had a lot of fun. Emma was glad she found the new hat. It was a magic hat. It made her dolls come alive.
