Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They had a big box of cars and trucks and buses. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving on the road.
"Look, Lily, I have a license!" Ben said, holding up a card with his name and picture on it. He had made it with his mom yesterday. "I can drive any car I want!"
"Wow, Ben, that's cool!" Lily said, admiring his license. "Can I see it?"
"Sure, here you go!" Ben said, handing her the card. "But be careful, don't lose it or bend it!"
Lily took the card and looked at it closely. She saw Ben's smile and his blue eyes. She saw the letters and numbers. She saw the word "license". She wanted to have one too.
"Can I have a license, Ben?" Lily asked. "Can you make one for me?"
"Maybe later, Lily," Ben said. "But now let's play some more. I want to drive the big red truck. It's fast and loud!"
"OK, Ben," Lily said. She gave him back the card and picked up a yellow car. She liked the yellow car. It was shiny and cute.
They drove their cars on the grass and the dirt. They made turns and stops and honks. They had fun and laughed.
But then, Lily saw something. She saw a puddle of water near the fence. It was from the hose that dad had used to water the plants. The puddle looked wet and sparkly. Lily had an idea.
"Hey, Ben, look!" Lily said. She drove her yellow car towards the puddle. "Let's make our cars soak!"
Ben looked at the puddle. He did not like the idea. He liked his cars dry and clean. He did not want them to get wet and muddy.
"No, Lily, don't do that!" Ben said. He tried to stop her, but he was too late. Lily reached the puddle and drove her car into it. She splashed the water and made a big mess. She giggled and said, "Whee!"
Ben was angry. He drove his big red truck after her. He wanted to get his license back from her. He did not want it to soak too. He reached the puddle and grabbed the card from her hand. But he was clumsy. He slipped and fell into the puddle. He soaked his clothes and his hair and his face. He dropped his license and his truck into the water. He cried and said, "Ow!"
Lily was sorry. She did not mean to make Ben cry. She got out of the puddle and helped him up. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was just playing. Are you OK?"
Ben was not OK. He was wet and dirty and sad. He looked at his license and his truck. They were wet and dirty too. He said, "No, Lily. You ruined my license and my truck. They were my favorite things. Now they are no good."
Lily felt bad. She wanted to make Ben happy. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I can help you clean them. Maybe they are still good. Maybe we can dry them and fix them. Maybe we can make a new license for you. And for me too. Please don't be mad at me."
Ben looked at Lily. He saw her eyes and her smile. He saw that she was his friend. He saw that she was sorry. He felt a little better. He said, "OK, Lily. Maybe you are right. Maybe we can still play. But next time, don't make our cars soak. OK?"
"OK, Ben," Lily said. She hugged him and said, "You are my friend. I like you."
They went inside the house. They cleaned their cars and their clothes and their faces. They dried their license and their truck. They made a new license for Lily. They played some more. They were happy.

Max wanted to help the bird. He thought of an idea. He said, "I can lend you my bowl. Let's go find some water."
They walked and walked, and finally, they found a puddle of water. Max put his bowl on the ground, and the bird drank the water from it. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Max, for lending me your bowl."
From that day on, Max and the bird were best friends. They always helped each other when they needed it.

"Look, Tim, there is a ladder!" Lily says. She points to a wooden ladder leaning on the tree. "We can use it to get the apples!"
"Good idea, Lily!" Tim says. He runs to the ladder and climbs up. He reaches for an apple, but it is still too far. He leans over the ladder, but he loses his balance. He falls down and lands on the grass.
"Ouch!" Tim cries. He rubs his head. "That hurt!"
Lily runs to him and hugs him. "Are you okay, Tim?" she asks. She is worried.
"I'm okay, Lily," Tim says. He smiles. "But I didn't get any apples."
Lily looks at the tree. She sees a low branch with a big apple. She has an idea. She lets go of Tim and runs to the branch. She jumps and grabs the apple. She runs back to Tim and gives him the apple.
"Here, Tim, this is for you," she says. "You are brave. This is your reward."
Tim takes the apple and bites it. It is sweet and juicy. He shares it with Lily. They both smile.
"Thank you, Lily," he says. "You are kind. This is the best apple ever."
They hug each other and eat the apple. They are happy. They are friends.

The old man was getting tired and frustrated. He said to himself, "What am I going to do?"
Suddenly, he heard a tiny voice from the forest. It was a 3 year old child. The child said, "Why don't you use softer wood?"
The old man said, "That's a good idea! I'll get softer wood and try again."
And so the old man got softer wood and he built the barrel. He was very pleased with the result.
The old man thanked the little child and said, "Thank you for your help. You are very wise for such a small one." 
The child smiled, happy to have helped. The old man put the barrel over his shoulder and went off, to use his barrel for his big job.

When Jim looked closer, he noticed a small piece of paper tied to the bird's leg. Curious, he slowly got closer. With a gentle touch, he untied the piece of paper and read it carefully.
It said: "Thank you! This is my freedom license. I am so excited to be able to fly around and explore this beautiful world. Please help me if you can. Ann"(the year old bird).
Jim smiled and nodded. He was eager to help so he took his license and waved it towards the bird. Ann flew away, singing a happy song. 
Jim watched Ann fly away and knew that he had done the right thing. He put his license back in his pocket and smiled.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big basket of muffins on a bench. They were hungry and wanted to eat some. But the basket had a sign that said "For the birds. Please do not touch."
Ben did not care about the sign. He said, "I want a muffin. They look yummy." He ran to the basket and grabbed a muffin. Lily followed him and said, "Ben, stop! That is not nice. The muffins are for the birds. They need food too."
Ben did not listen to Lily. He bit the muffin and said, "Mmm, this is good. I want another one." He reached for another muffin. But then, he heard a loud squawk. A big crow flew down from a tree and pecked his hand. Ben dropped the muffin and cried, "Ow, ow, ow! That bird hurt me!"
Lily ran to Ben and hugged him. She said, "Ben, are you okay? I told you not to take the muffins. The crow was trying to protect them. He was angry that you took his food."
Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was greedy and rude. I should have listened to you. I should have respected the birds and their food. Can you forgive me?"
Lily smiled and said, "Of course, I forgive you, Ben. You are my brother and I love you. But next time, please be kind and share. There is enough food for everyone."
Ben nodded and said, "You are right, Lily. You are my sister and I love you too. Next time, I will be kind and share. And I will not touch the muffins again. They are cold and hard anyway."
They hugged and went back to their mom, who was waiting for them. She gave them a warm and soft cookie each. They thanked her and ate the cookie. They learned their lesson and never bothered the birds or their muffins again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big ladder near a tree. They wanted to climb it and see what was on top.
"Let's go up the ladder!" Tom said.
"OK, but be careful!" Lily said.
They ran to the ladder and started to climb. They were very happy and excited. They reached the top and saw a big nest. There was a bird in the nest. It was very ugly. It had a big beak, small eyes and brown feathers. It looked angry.
"Hello, bird!" Tom said.
"Go away!" the bird said. "This is my home! You are not welcome here!"
The bird flapped its wings and pecked at Tom. Tom was scared and hurt. He let go of the ladder and fell down. He spun in the air and landed on the grass.
"Tom!" Lily shouted. "Are you OK?"
Lily climbed down the ladder and ran to Tom. She hugged him and checked if he was OK. He had a scratch on his arm, but he was not badly hurt.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the garden. They had a birdcage with a blue bird inside. The bird sang sweet songs and made them happy.
One day, Tim said to Sam, "Let us lift the birdcage and take it to the park. We can show the bird to our friends and let it fly a bit."
Sam said, "No, Tim. Mom said we should not lift the birdcage or let the bird out. The bird might get lost or hurt. We should leave it here and watch it from afar."
But Tim did not listen to Sam. He was stubborn and wanted to have fun. He lifted the birdcage and ran to the park with it. Sam followed him, worried and sad.
At the park, Tim met his friends and showed them the bird. They all said, "Wow, what a great bird! Can we touch it? Can we feed it? Can we play with it?"
Tim said, "Sure, why not? It is just a bird. It will not mind." He opened the birdcage and let the bird out. The bird flew in the air, happy and free.
But then, a big cat saw the bird and jumped at it. The bird tried to fly away, but the cat was faster and caught it in its mouth. The bird cried out, but no one could help it. The cat ran away with the bird, leaving Tim and his friends shocked and scared.
Sam came to Tim and said, "Tim, why did you do that? You were wrong to lift the birdcage and let the bird out. You did not care for the bird. You did not listen to Mom. You did not listen to me. Now the bird is gone and we are sad. How will we tell Mom?"
Tim felt sorry and ashamed. He realized his mistake and wished he could undo it. He said, "Sam, I am sorry. I was foolish and selfish. I did not think of the bird or you or Mom. I only thought of myself. I learned a hard lesson today. I will never do that again."
But it was too late. The bird was gone and the birdcage was empty. Tim and Sam went home, crying and afraid. Mom saw them and asked what happened. They told her the truth and she was angry and sad. She said, "Tim, you were very naughty and careless. You hurt the bird and broke our trust. You must face the consequences of your actions. You will not play in the garden or the park for a long time. You will also do extra chores and say sorry to the bird and to Sam and to me. Maybe then you will understand the value of life and love and respect."
Tim and Sam nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We are sorry. We will do as you say. We will try to be better."
The moral of the story is: Do not lift what is not yours. Do not let go of what is precious. Do not hurt what is living. Listen to your elders and your siblings. They know what is best for you and for others.

Surprised, Daisy said yes and the bird flew away. Daisy walked over to the big black tree and looked underneath. Sure enough, there were a bunch of strawberries. Some were red and some were black.

The bird bowed back and said: "You're welcome Daisy". Daisy smiled and said goodbye.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play chess. Chess was a game with black and white pieces that moved on a board with squares. Tom had a gray cat named Smokey who liked to watch them play.
One day, Tom and Mia were playing chess at Tom's house. Tom was winning and Mia was sad. She wanted to win too. She saw Smokey sitting on the couch and had an idea.
"Mia, do you want to pet Smokey?" she asked Tom. "He is very soft and nice."
"Sure, I like Smokey," Tom said. He left his chess pieces and went to the couch. He picked up Smokey and gave him a hug.
Mia smiled and quickly moved some of Tom's pieces. She made a checkmate and said, "I win, I win!"
Tom looked at the board and saw that Mia had cheated. He was angry and hurt. He squeezed Smokey too hard and Smokey scratched him. Tom let go of Smokey and cried.
"Mia, that was not fair! You moved my pieces when I was not looking!" he shouted.
Mia felt sorry and ashamed. She knew she had done a bad thing. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I was jealous and wanted to win. But that was wrong. Can you forgive me?"
Tom looked at Mia and saw that she was sincere. He said, "I forgive you, Mia. But don't do that again. Chess is a game of rules and respect. And don't hurt Smokey. He is my friend too."
Mia nodded and hugged Tom. She said, "I'm sorry, Smokey. You are a good cat. Can I pet you?"
Smokey meowed and licked Mia's hand. He was not mad anymore. He liked Tom and Mia. They were his friends too.
They put the chess pieces back and played another game. This time, they played fair and had fun. They learned a lesson about honesty and kindness. And Smokey watched them with his gray eyes. He was happy.

"I don't know. Maybe he is a friend of Dad," Ben says.
They run to their dad, who is in the kitchen. They want to ask him about the bald man.
"Dad, dad, who is the bald man with the big truck?" Sam says.
Dad looks out of the window. He smiles.
"Oh, that is Mr. Lee. He is our new neighbor. He just moved in today. He is very nice. He likes pizza too," Dad says.
"Really? Can we go and say hello to him?" Ben says.
"Sure, but first, let's finish our pizza. It is getting cold. And don't forget the sauce. It is yummy," Dad says.
Sam and Ben nod. They love sauce. They eat their pizza quickly. Then they put on their shoes and run to the door.
"Bye, Dad. We are going to meet Mr. Lee," Sam says.
"Have fun, boys. And be polite. Don't mention his bald head. He might not like it," Dad says.
Sam and Ben say okay. They go to the bald man's truck. They see him carrying boxes.
"Hello, Mr. Lee. We are Sam and Ben. We live next door. Welcome to our street," Sam says.
"Hello, Sam and Ben. Thank you for your kind words. I am happy to meet you. Do you like pizza?" Mr. Lee says.
"Yes, we do. We just had some. With sauce. It was good," Ben says.
"That's great. I like pizza too. With sauce. And cheese. And pepperoni. Maybe we can have pizza together sometime," Mr. Lee says.
Sam and Ben smile. They think Mr. Lee is nice. They don't mention his bald head. They don't care. They just want to be his friends. And eat pizza with him. And play with his truck.

"Ben, what do we do?" Mia asks.
"I don't know, Mia. The dog is scary. Maybe we should wait until it goes away," Ben says.
"But what if it doesn't go away? What if it comes to our lab?" Mia says.
Ben thinks for a moment. He remembers that his mom told him that dogs are not bad. They just need to be friendly and calm. He decides to be brave.
"Mia, I have an idea. Maybe we can make the dog our friend. We can give it some of our snacks. Do you have any snacks in the lab?" Ben says.
Mia nods. She has some crackers and cheese in her backpack. She gives them to Ben.
"OK, Mia. You stay here. I will go outside and talk to the dog. Don't be afraid. I will be back soon," Ben says.
He takes the snacks and opens the door. He sees the dog. The dog sees him. The dog stops barking and wags its tail. Ben smiles. He walks slowly to the dog. He holds out his hand with the snacks.
"Hi, dog. We are Ben and Mia. We are not mean. We want to be your friends. Do you want some snacks?" Ben says.
The dog sniffs Ben's hand. It licks the snacks. It licks Ben's hand. It makes a happy sound. Ben pets the dog. The dog likes Ben.
"See, Mia? The dog is nice. Come and meet him," Ben says.
Mia comes out of the lab. She is still a little scared. But she sees that Ben and the dog are getting along. She walks to them. She gives the dog a cracker. The dog licks her hand too. She pets the dog. The dog likes Mia.
"Wow, Ben. You are so brave. You made the dog our friend. He is cute. What should we name him?" Mia says.
Ben thinks for a moment. He looks at the dog. The dog has brown fur and black spots.
"How about Spot? He has spots. Do you like Spot, dog?" Ben says.
The dog barks. He wags his tail. He likes Spot.
"Spot it is. Welcome to our lab, Spot. You can play with us. We have lots of things to show you," Mia says.

The children and the teacher laughed again. They all had fun drawing on the monster and playing with it. The big, friendly monster became their new friend.

They go to the bathroom. They see the bathtub. The bathtub is long and white. They have an idea. They want to cut the bathtub. They think it will be funny.
They start to cut the bathtub with the scissors. They make a big hole in the bathtub. Water comes out of the hole. The water is everywhere. The bathroom is wet.
Mom hears the water. She runs to the bathroom. She sees Tom and Lily. She sees the scissors and the bathtub. She is angry and scared.
"What are you doing?" she asks. "Why did you cut the bathtub?"
Tom and Lily look at Mom. They are sorry. They do not know what to say.
"We wanted to play," Tom says.
"We did not know," Lily says.
Mom sighs. She takes the scissors from them. She tells them to go to their room. She calls Dad. She needs help to fix the bathtub. She hopes Tom and Lily will learn their lesson.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna, who had long hair and a pink dress. Lily always took Anna with her when she went to the park, the store, or the library.
One day, Lily and her mom went to the library to borrow some books. Lily brought Anna with her and held her by the waist. She saw many books with pictures and words, and she wanted to look at them. She put Anna on a chair and went to the shelves.
"Stay here, Anna. I will be back soon," she said to her doll.
But Lily forgot about Anna. She was so busy looking at the books that she did not hear her mom calling her.
"Lily, it's time to go. We have to return the books and go home," her mom said.
Lily ran to her mom and gave her the books she liked. She did not remember Anna.
"Did you forget something, Lily?" her mom asked.
Lily looked around and saw Anna on the chair. She felt sad and sorry.
"Oh, Anna! I forgot you! I'm so sorry!" she cried and ran to her doll. She hugged her and said, "I love you, Anna. You are my best friend."
Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. But you have to remind yourself of the things that are important to you. Anna is important to you, right?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. Anna is very important to me. I will never forget her again."
Her mom kissed her and said, "That's good, Lily. Now let's go home and read some of the books we borrowed. Maybe we can find a story about dolls."
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, mom. That sounds fun. Thank you, mom."
She held Anna by the waist and walked with her mom. She learned a lesson that day. She learned to remind herself of the things that are important to her. And she learned to love her doll more.

Lily liked to play with her drum. She got it for her birthday from her grandma. She liked to make loud noises with it and sing along. She felt happy when she played with her drum.
One day, she took her drum to the park with her mom. She wanted to show it to her friends. She saw Ben and Anna on the swings. She ran to them with her drum. She said hello and banged on her drum.
But Ben and Anna did not say hello back. They looked at Lily with angry faces. They did not like the loud noise. They said, "Stop it, Lily! You are hurting our ears! Go away!"
Lily felt sad and confused. She did not understand why her friends were mean to her. She liked her drum. Why did they not like it too? She looked at her mom for help.
Her mom came to her and gave her a hug. She said, "Lily, I know you love your drum, but not everyone likes the same things. Sometimes, loud noises can make people feel uncomfortable. They can make their ears hurt or their heads ache. Maybe you can play with your drum somewhere else, where it does not bother anyone. Or maybe you can play with something else with your friends, like a ball or a doll. Would you like that?"
Lily nodded. She recognized that her mom was right. She did not want to make her friends feel bad. She wanted to play with them and have fun. She said sorry to Ben and Anna and put her drum away. She asked them if they wanted to play with her ball. They smiled and said yes. They all ran to the grass and played together. Lily felt happy again. She still liked her drum, but she also liked her friends. She learned to be kind and respectful. She was a good girl.

Once upon a time there was a friendly boat on the sea. It was an old boat and its crew was very alert and observant.
On board was an anchor, which was big and heavy. Suddenly the boat started to shrink and the anchor kept on getting heavier and heavier.
"Oh no!" the crew said. "What can we do to fix this?" 
The captain thought for a moment and then said: "I know! We'll need to tie the anchor to the outside of the boat so that it doesn't weigh down the boat as it gets smaller."
So the crew quickly got to work and secured the anchor outside the boat.
No sooner had they done this than they felt the boat start to grow back to its normal size.
The crew cheered and thanked each other for their hard work – and for being so alert that they had noticed the boat shrinking in the first place.

They hugged and then played with their toys together. They had fun and learned to respect each other's choices. They were happy and cared for each other.

After a while, Sue wanted to chew some gum. She took out a piece of gum and gave one to Tom. But Tom didn't know how to chew gum. He tried to swallow it and started to choke. Sue quickly knelt down and patted Tom's back, and the gum came out. Tom was so thankful to Sue for helping him.
Sue said, "Tom, you should never swallow gum. It's not good for you." Tom nodded and said, "Thank you, Sue. I will remember that." They continued to play and had a great day at the park.
The moral of the story is to always be careful with what you eat and to help your friends when they need it.

One time, John's Mom told him to try it and he was so scared. 
When the food came, much to his surprise, it looked like nothing more than a big piece of delicious fried chicken. He was relieved to find out that the scary thing on the menu was not as scary as he'd thought!
The moral of the story is that something can look scary, but it may not be so bad after all. Even if things don't look quite how we expect them to, it's always important to gain understanding and relate to each other with an open mind.

When they got close, the big shiny thing started to talk! It said, "Hello, I am a magic fish. I love this swamp too. I can make one wish come true for each of you." Fred and his friends were very happy and excited.
Fred's friend, Sam, wished for a big party with lots of food. The magic fish made it happen, and they all had a great time. Then it was Fred's turn to make a wish. He thought for a moment, and then he said, "I wish for more friends to love and play with in our swamp."
The magic fish smiled and made Fred's wish come true. Suddenly, many new frogs appeared in the swamp. They all became friends and played together. Fred and his friends were very lucky to have found the magic fish and to have so many new friends to love in their swamp.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a new bridge in the park. It is red and shiny. They want to cross the bridge and see what is on the other side.
But there is a problem. A big dog is sitting on the bridge. It is black and furry. It has sharp teeth and loud bark. It does not let anyone pass. Lily and Ben are scared of the dog. They do not know what to do.
They try to talk to the dog. They say, "Please, let us cross the bridge. We want to see what is on the other side. We will not hurt you or bother you. We are nice and friendly." But the dog does not listen. It growls and snarls at them. It does not move.
Lily and Ben are sad. They think they will never cross the bridge. They think they will never discover what is on the other side. They sit on the grass and cry.
Then, they hear a whistle. They look up and see a man. He is wearing a blue hat and a green shirt. He has a leash in his hand. He is the owner of the dog. He says, "Sorry, kids. I did not know my dog was on the bridge. He ran away from me. He is not mean. He is just scared of new things. Come on, boy. Let's go home."
He walks to the bridge and calls the dog. The dog listens to him. It wags its tail and follows him. It leaves the bridge. Lily and Ben are happy. They thank the man and the dog. They run to the bridge and cross it. They discover what is on the other side. It is a pond with ducks and fish. It is beautiful and fun. They play and laugh. They have a good day.

One day, Leo got caught in a trap. He roared loudly for help. Mimi heard him and ran to see what was wrong. "Help me, Mimi! I am stuck in this trap," cried Leo. Mimi wanted to help her friend, so she thought of a plan.
Mimi went to find her friend, the wise owl. "Owl, I need your help," said Mimi. "Leo is stuck in a trap. What do you recommend we do?" Owl thought for a moment and said, "You can chew through the rope to set him free."
So Mimi went back to Leo and chewed through the rope. The trap opened, and Leo was free. He was very happy and thanked Mimi for her help. From that day on, the mighty lion and the little mouse became the best of friends, and they always helped each other when they needed it.

Sara and Tom were playing with blocks. They wanted to build a big tower. Sara had a notebook and a ruler. She liked to measure the blocks and write the numbers in her notebook. Tom did not have a notebook or a ruler. He just liked to stack the blocks and see how high they could go.
"Look, Sara, I made a taller tower than you!" Tom said, pointing to his blocks.
Sara looked at Tom's tower and frowned. She took her ruler and measured Tom's tower. Then she measured her own tower. She wrote the numbers in her notebook.
"No, Tom, your tower is not taller. Your tower is 12 inches and my tower is 13 inches. See, I wrote it in my notebook. My tower is taller!" Sara said, showing Tom her notebook.
Tom did not like what Sara said. He felt angry and sad. He did not care about the numbers. He just wanted to have fun. He pushed Sara's tower and made it fall. Sara's blocks and notebook scattered on the floor.
"Tom, why did you do that? That was mean and rude! You made my tower fall and you broke my notebook!" Sara cried, picking up her things.
Tom felt sorry for what he did. He saw Sara's tears and heard her cry. He realized he was wrong. He wanted to say sorry, but he did not know how.
"Sara, I'm sorry. I was grumpy and jealous. I should not have pushed your tower or broken your notebook. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends again?" Tom said, looking at Sara with a sad face.
Sara looked at Tom and saw his sad face. She felt sorry for him too. She knew he did not mean to hurt her. She wanted to be friends again.
"Tom, I forgive you. I was grumpy and bossy too. I should not have bragged about my tower or shown you my notebook. Can we share the blocks and the notebook? Can we build a tower together?" Sara said, smiling at Tom.
Tom smiled back at Sara. He nodded and hugged her. They picked up the blocks and the notebook. They decided to work together and build a bigger and better tower. They learned to be kind and respectful to each other. They had more fun and were happier.

Sara loves ice cream. She likes to eat it after dinner. But today, she cannot find her ice cream in the freezer. She asks her mom, "Where is my ice cream?"
Mom says, "I'm sorry, Sara. I forgot to buy more ice cream. We ran out of it yesterday."
Sara feels sad. She really wants ice cream. She says, "Can we go to the store and buy some?"
Mom says, "Not today, Sara. It is too late and dark. But I have an idea. Why don't we make our own ice cream?"
Sara is curious. She says, "How can we make ice cream?"
Mom says, "It is easy. We need milk, sugar, vanilla, and a plastic bag. Come, I will show you."
Mom and Sara go to the kitchen. Mom pours some milk and sugar into a small plastic bag. She adds a drop of vanilla. She seals the bag and shakes it. Then she puts the bag inside a bigger plastic bag. She fills the bigger bag with ice and salt. She seals it and gives it to Sara.
Mom says, "Now, you have to shake the bag for a long time. The ice and salt will make the milk freeze and turn into ice cream."
Sara shakes the bag. She shakes it hard and fast. She shakes it for a long time. She feels the bag getting colder and harder. She says, "Is it ready?"
Mom says, "Let's see. Open the bag and check."
Sara opens the bag. She sees a soft and white ball of ice cream. She takes a spoon and tastes it. It is sweet and creamy. She says, "Wow, this is good. This is the best ice cream ever."
Mom smiles. She says, "I'm glad you like it. You made it yourself. You are a famous ice cream maker."
Sara feels happy. She says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever."
Mom and Sara hug. They share the ice cream. They return the empty bags to the freezer. They go to bed with sweet dreams.

Lily was very careful. She followed her dad's instructions and soon the teddy bear's ear was fixed. She put the cap on its head and smiled. "There, teddy," she said. "Now you are all better. And you have a cap like me."
Her dad smiled too and hugged her. "You are very kind, Lily," he said. "And you are a very good fixer. I'm proud of you."
Lily felt happy. She loved her dad and her teddy bear. She loved to fix things with her cap. She felt very soft and warm.

One day while she was at the park, Emily noticed a notebook lying on the ground. She picked it up and began writing some of her thoughts on the paper. She was so excited about the notebook, she wanted to show her friends.
Emily ran up to her friends and showed them the notebook. They all thought it was really cool and wanted to join in writing in the notebook too. 
Emily quickly became a leader of the group as all the children started to write in the notebook. She was very competitive, trying to one-up her friends every chance she got.
The children spent many afternoons at the park playing and writing in the notebook. Emily could feel something special was happening, and she was right. Over time her friends saw how good Emily was at writing stories, and they decided to create their very own magazine.
The children worked very hard to make the magazine and with Emily's leadership they created the most amazing stories. Everyone was so proud of what they had achieved. Emily had noticed the notebook in the park all those months ago, and it had been a sign of things to come.

"Hey, Tim!" said the little bird. "Why are you always so naughty and make big messes?"
Tim the hippo looked at the bird and said, "I don't know. I just like to have fun and play in the mud!"
One day, while Tim was making a big mess in the mud, he found a shiny stone. Tim picked it up and looked at it. Suddenly, the stone started to glow, and Tim turned into a little bird just like his friend!
Now, Tim could not make big messes in the mud anymore. He had to learn how to be a good little bird and play in the trees. Tim learned that being naughty was not always fun, and sometimes it is better to be nice and make friends.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big tree with many leaves and nuts. They also saw a squirrel that was running and jumping on the branches.
"Look, mom, a squirrel!" Ben said, pointing at the furry animal.
"Yes, it's a squirrel. Do you know what it likes to eat?" mom asked.
"Nuts!" Lily said, picking up a brown nut from the ground.
"Can I give it to the squirrel?" Ben asked, holding another nut in his hand.
"Sure, but be careful. Squirrels are shy and fast. You have to be quiet and gentle," mom said.
Ben and Lily walked slowly to the tree, holding their nuts. They saw the squirrel looking at them with its black eyes. They smiled and stretched their hands with the nuts.
"Hello, squirrel. We have some nuts for you. Do you want them?" Lily said softly.
The squirrel sniffed the nuts and then took one from Ben's hand. It bit the nut and made a crunchy sound. Ben and Lily giggled. The squirrel took another nut from Lily's hand and then ran up the tree.
"Thank you, squirrel. Bye-bye!" Ben and Lily said, waving at the squirrel.
The squirrel waved back with its tail and then hid the nuts in a hole. It was happy and full.
Ben and Lily went back to their mom, who hugged them and praised them for being kind and brave.
They had a fun day at the park, but they also made a messy pile of nut shells on the ground. They helped mom to clean it up before they left. They hoped to see the squirrel again.

One day, the hippo saw something interesting. It was a big, round ball. The hippo did not know what it was. He asked his friends, "What is this?" The fish said, "I don't know." The bird said, "I don't know." The frog said, "I don't know."
Then, the hippo had an idea. He said, "I will ask my mom." His mom was very smart. She knew a lot of things. The hippo asked, "Mom, what is this?" His mom said, "This is a ball. It is fun to play with. I recommend you try it." The hippo was happy. He played with the ball and had a lot of fun. His friends liked the ball too. They all played together and had a great day.

Mom told them to clean their room and put away their toys. Anna and Ben did not want to do that. They wanted to keep playing. They said no to mom. Mom was not happy. She said they had to do it or they would not get any snacks. Anna and Ben still said no. They ran away to the backyard.
Mom was busy in the kitchen. She did not see them go. She thought they were in their room. She made a cake and some sandwiches for the visit. She put them on the table. She went to get some drinks from the fridge.
Anna and Ben were hungry. They smelled the cake and the sandwiches. They sneaked into the kitchen. They saw the food on the table. They thought mom would not mind if they had a little bite. They climbed on the chairs and reached for the cake. They took a big piece and ate it. It was yummy. They wanted more. They took another piece and another. They did not see the crumbs and the frosting on the table and on their faces.
Mom came back from the fridge. She saw Anna and Ben eating the cake. She saw the mess on the table. She was angry. She yelled at them. She said they were naughty and rude. She said they ruined the cake and the visit. She said they had to go to their room and stay there.
Anna and Ben were scared. They heard mom yell. They saw her angry face. They felt bad. They did not mean to make mom angry. They did not mean to ruin the cake and the visit. They panicked. They dropped the cake and ran to their room. They cried and hugged each other. They said they were sorry. They wished mom would forgive them. They wished their aunt and uncle would still come. They wished they had listened to mom and cleaned their room and put away their toys.

But Lily does not see his foot. She only sees his face. She thinks he is making a funny face at her. She laughs and says, "You look silly, Ben!" Ben is confused. He looks at his foot and says, "No, look at my foot, Lily! It is a joke!"
Lily looks at his foot and sees it in the air. She does not think it is funny. She thinks it is rude. She says, "That is not a joke, Ben! That is mean! You should not put your foot up like that. It is not fair to the other kids. They might get hurt by your foot."
Ben feels bad. He did not mean to be mean. He only wanted to make Lily laugh. He says, "I am sorry, Lily. I did not know it was mean. I will not do it again. Can we still be friends?"
Lily thinks for a moment. She sees that Ben is sorry. She says, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to be careful with your foot. And you have to find better jokes. Can you do that?"
Ben nods. He says, "Yes, Lily. I can do that. Thank you for being my friend. You are very fair."
They hug and smile. They go to play some more. They have fun and joke with each other. But they do not use their feet. They use their words.

Sara shook her head. She did not have any fuel. She only had water in her bottle. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I don't have fuel. Maybe we can find some in the house."
They ran to the house and asked their mom for fuel. Their mom smiled and said, "Fuel is not for toy cars, my dears. Fuel is for real cars. Your toy cars need batteries. Do you know what batteries are?"
Sara and Tom nodded. They had seen batteries before. They were small and shiny and had plus and minus signs on them. Their mom said, "Batteries have power inside them. They can make your toy cars work again. But you have to be careful with them. They can be dangerous if you put them in your mouth or break them. Do you understand?"
Sara and Tom said, "Yes, mom. We understand. Can we have some batteries, please?"
Their mom gave them each a new battery and showed them how to put it in their toy cars. She said, "Now you can play with your cars again. But remember to be humble and share. Don't boast or fight. And don't waste the power. Turn off your cars when you are done. OK?"
Sara and Tom said, "OK, mom. Thank you for the batteries. You are the best."
They hugged their mom and ran back to the garden. They put the batteries in their cars and turned them on. Their cars started to work again. They were happy and excited. They said to each other, "Let's race again. But let's be humble and share. And let's thank mom for the batteries. She helped us restore our cars."

One day, Lily and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big tree with red berries on it. Lily and Ben liked berries, so they ran to the tree and picked some.

"Be careful, sweeties, some berries are not good to eat. They can make you sick or dead," mom said, walking over to them.
"How do we know which berries are good?" Ben asked, looking at his hand.
"Mom knows. She can serve us good berries at home. Let's go back and wash our hands first," mom said, taking their hands and leading them away from the tree.
On the way home, they saw a bird lying on the ground. It was not moving or making any sound.
"Mom, look, a bird!" Lily said, pointing at it.
"Is it dead, mom?" Ben asked, looking sad.
"Yes, sweetie, it is dead. Maybe it ate some bad berries from the tree. That's why we don't eat berries we don't know," mom said, hugging them.
"Can we help the bird, mom?" Lily asked, wiping her eyes.
"We can't help the bird, but we can say a prayer for it and bury it in the dirt. Then we can go home and have some good berries that mom will serve us," mom said, smiling.
Lily and Ben nodded and helped mom dig a hole for the bird. They said a prayer and covered it with dirt. Then they went home and had some good berries that mom served them. They were happy and thankful for the good berries and the good mom.

Tommy was a big boy who liked to play with his cars and trucks. He had many cars and trucks of different colors and sizes. He liked to make them zoom and crash on the floor. He also liked to wear his uniform, a blue shirt and pants that his mommy gave him. He said his uniform made him look like a policeman.
One day, Tommy was playing with his cars and trucks in his room, when his little sister Lily came in. Lily was a baby who liked to grab and chew things. She saw Tommy's cars and trucks and wanted to play with them too. She crawled to Tommy and reached for his red car.
"No, Lily, that's mine!" Tommy shouted. He snatched the car from Lily and pushed her away. Lily started to cry.
"Tommy, what are you doing?" Mommy asked. She heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tommy holding his car and Lily crying on the floor.
"Mommy, Lily tried to take my car!" Tommy said. "She can't play with my cars and trucks, they are mine!"
"Tommy, that's not nice. You have to share with your sister. She is too little to understand. She just wants to play with you. You can't be selfish and mean. You have to be kind and gentle." Mommy said.
"But Mommy, she will break them! She will put them in her mouth and make them dirty! She can't play with my cars and trucks!" Tommy said.

Lily started to add blocks to her tower. She was careful and balanced them well. She wanted her tower to be graceful and strong. Ben also started to add blocks to his tower. He was fast and piled them up. He wanted his tower to be big and tall.
Soon, their towers were very high. Lily and Ben looked at each other's towers. They both thought their own tower was better. They started to say mean things to each other.
"Your tower is too slow and boring. Mine is faster and more fun!" Ben said.
"Your tower is too messy and shaky. Mine is more graceful and stable!" Lily said.
They kept arguing and did not notice that their towers were getting too high. Suddenly, both towers fell down with a loud crash. The blocks scattered everywhere. Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They had no more blocks to play with.
They sat on the floor and looked at the mess. They realized that they had been silly and rude. They had wasted their blocks and their fun. They felt sorry and wanted to be friends again.
They looked at each other and said, "I'm sorry. I was wrong. Your tower was good too. Can we play together again?"
They hugged and smiled. They decided to work together and make a new tower. They used all the blocks and helped each other. They made a tower that was high and graceful and fun. They had more fun than before. They learned that sharing and being kind is better than fighting and being mean.

Once upon a time there was a regular girl called Alice. One day, she went out to explore the wild woods and found a big, red ball. Excited, she picked it up and kicked it away. Suddenly, a strange voice said, "Hey! Don't kick my ball!" Startled, Alice looked around, but there was nobody there. Strangely, Alice heard the same voice again, "Hey Alice, can you give me my ball back? Please?"
Alice couldn't believe it. But, she was brave and ran to get the ball. This time, she saw a little creature standing there. It was a furry, little fox! But, it had wings! 
Alice asked, "Are you the one who asked for the ball?". The fox nodded and smiled.
Alice gave the fox the ball and the fox thanked her. Together, they kicked the ball, up and down and around, until the sun went away.
Alice said goodbye to the fox and promised to come back soon. She left the wild woods happy, with a big smile on her face.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy trucks in the garden. They liked to load the trucks with dirt, leaves and rocks and drive them around. Sometimes they pretended to be builders, farmers or explorers.
"Look, Lily, I have a big load of dirt. I can make a hill with it," Tom said, dumping his truck on the ground.
"That's nice, Tom, but I have a better load. I have juice in my truck. I can drink it when I am thirsty," Lily said, showing him her truck with a bottle of juice inside.
"Juice? That's not a good load. That's a drink. You can't build anything with juice," Tom said, shaking his head.
"Yes, I can. I can build a juice fountain. Watch this," Lily said, tipping her truck over and letting the juice spill out.
The juice splashed on the grass, the dirt and the rocks. It also splashed on Tom, who was not happy.
"Hey, stop that! You are making a mess. And you are wasting juice. Juice is for drinking, not for playing," Tom said, wiping his face.
"Sorry, Tom. I was just having fun. Do you want some juice? I have some left," Lily said, offering him the bottle.
"OK, thank you. But next time, don't load your truck with juice. Load it with something else," Tom said, taking a sip.
"Like what?" Lily asked.
"Like... like... cookies. Cookies are a good load. You can eat them and share them and they are yummy," Tom said, smiling.
"OK, cookies sound good. Let's go and ask Mom if we can have some cookies. And then we can load our trucks with them and drive them fast," Lily said, nodding.
"OK, let's go. But be careful. Don't spill the juice or the cookies. We don't want to make more mess," Tom said, holding his truck.
"OK, I will be careful. Come on, Tom, let's go fast," Lily said, holding her truck.
They ran to the house, holding their trucks and their juice. They were happy and hungry. They liked to play with their trucks and they liked to load them with different things. But they liked to drink juice and eat cookies more.

"No, Tom, that is a bad letter. That is not funny. That is mean. The teacher will be sad and angry. We will be in trouble. Do not send it, Tom. Throw it away," Ann says.

"Tom, did you send me this letter?" the teacher asks.
Tom nods. He thinks the teacher will praise him. He thinks the teacher will think he is funny.
"Yes, I did. Do you like it?" Tom says.
The teacher does not like it. The teacher is very upset. The teacher scolds Tom. She tells him he is foolish and rude. She tells him he has to go to the principal's office. She tells him he has to say sorry. She tells him he has to stay after school. She tells him he has to write a good letter.
Tom feels ashamed. He feels sorry. He wishes he did not send the letter. He wishes he listened to Ann. He cries. He goes to the principal's office. He says sorry. He stays after school. He writes a good letter. He learns his lesson. He never sends a bad letter again.

"No, this is my cereal. You can have something else," Sara says.
"But I want cereal too. Why do you get all the cereal?" Tom says.

Mom hears them from the bedroom. She comes to the kitchen. She sees the red box of cereal and the twins.

Sara and Tom think about it. They nod. They smile.
"Okay, Mom. We can share the rainbow cereal. Thank you," Sara and Tom say.

Mom watches them. She is happy. She thinks they are beautiful. Just like the rainbow.

Mom shook her head. "No, you can't. It's past your bedtime. You need to sleep well, so you can have fun tomorrow. We are going to the zoo, remember? You love the zoo. Now, say goodnight to the clock and put it away."
Lily and Tom said goodnight to the clock, but they did not put it away. They hid it under their pillow, and waited for mom to leave. When mom closed the door, they took out the clock and turned it on. They giggled and pressed the buttons.
But the clock was too loud. It said the time, and sang a song, and made a beep. Mom heard the noise and came back to their room. She was not happy. She saw the clock under their pillow and took it away.
"Lily and Tom, you are very naughty. You did not listen to me. You lied to me. You are not supposed to play with the clock at night. It's too noisy. It will keep you and everyone else awake. I'm very disappointed in you. You should be ashamed of yourselves."
Lily and Tom felt bad. They knew they did something wrong. They looked at mom with sad eyes and said they were sorry.
Mom sighed. She hugged them and said she loved them, but they had to learn to follow the rules. She said they could have the clock back tomorrow, but only if they behaved well. She tucked them in and kissed them goodnight.
Lily and Tom said goodnight to mom and to each other. They closed their eyes and tried to sleep. They did not want to play with the clock anymore. They wanted to dream of the zoo.

The doctor said, "You are welcome, Timmy. You are a good boy. You will be well soon. Just drink lots of water and sleep a lot. And eat some apples, too. They are good for you." He gave Timmy a sticker and a hug. He said goodbye to Timmy and his mom. He left with his bag.
Timmy felt a little better. He drank some water and ate an apple. He went to bed and slept. He dreamed of bananas and stickers. He was lucky. He had a nice doctor.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Michael. He lived in a place called Sunny Valley. Michael was deaf. He could not hear.
One day, Michael wanted to visit his friends who lived in the next place. But he was very scared. He didn't know how his friends would react when they found out he couldn't hear.
On the way to his friends' house, Michael met an old man. The man asked why Michael looked scared. So Michael told him his story.
The old man smiled and said, "I'll joke with you when you meet your friends. That way, they'll know that you can't hear, and they'll still like you!"
Michael smiled and thanked the old man. When he arrived at his friends' house, he told them the old man's joke and his friends started to laugh.
The moral of this story is that even if you have a disability, you can still fit in with other people. If you show you are friendly and brave, everyone will accept you for who you are.

When the subway came, the cat got scared and ran. Tim ran after the cat, and he didn't see that he was getting too close to the edge. "Tim, stop!" his mom yelled, but it was too late. Tim tripped and started to fall. Everyone gasped as Tim fell onto the subway tracks.

Lily was a chubby girl who liked to play with fire. She had a box of matches that she hid under her bed. Sometimes, when her mom and dad were not looking, she would light a match and watch it burn. She liked the bright flame and the warm feeling.
One day, she found a cloth in her closet. It was a pretty cloth with flowers and birds on it. Lily thought it would look nice on her wall. She took the cloth and a match and went to her room. She pinned the cloth on the wall and lit the match. She held the match close to the cloth and smiled.
But then, something bad happened. The cloth caught fire and started to burn. The fire grew bigger and bigger and made a lot of smoke. Lily was scared and dropped the match. She ran out of her room and screamed for help.
Her mom and dad heard her scream and ran to her room. They saw the fire and the smoke and grabbed a bucket of water. They threw the water on the fire and put it out. They were angry and worried. They looked at Lily and said:
"Lily, what did you do? You could have burned the whole house! You could have hurt yourself and us! Playing with fire is very dangerous and wrong. You should never do it again. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and started to cry. She was sorry and ashamed. She hugged her mom and dad and said:
"I'm sorry, mom and dad. I was stupid and curious. I won't play with fire again. I love you."
Her mom and dad hugged her back and said:
"We love you too, Lily. But you have to be careful and listen to us. Fire is not a toy. It can burn and hurt. You have to respect it and stay away from it. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said:
"I understand, mom and dad. I learned my lesson. Fire is not a toy."
The moral of the story is: Playing with fire is dangerous and wrong. You should respect fire and stay away from it.

"Can I crack the eggs?" Sara asked.
"OK, but be careful. Don't let the shells go in the bowl," Mom said.
Sara took an egg and tapped it on the edge of the bowl. But she tapped too hard and the egg broke in her hand. The yolk and the white ran down her fingers. She felt sticky and yucky.
"Oops, sorry," Sara said.
"It's OK, we have more eggs. Here, use this one," Mom said. She gave Sara a paper towel to wipe her hand.
Ben watched Sara and wanted to crack an egg too. He grabbed an egg from the carton and smashed it on the table. The egg splattered everywhere. Some of it landed on Mom's face and hair. Mom gasped and looked angry.
"Ben, what did you do?" Mom yelled.
"I wanted to crack an egg too," Ben said.
"That's not how you crack an egg. You made a big mess. Go to your room right now," Mom said.
Ben felt sad and scared. He ran to his room and slammed the door. He heard Mom sigh and clean up the kitchen. He heard her put the cake in the oven and set the timer. He wished he could say sorry and help her.
But he didn't get a chance. The oven was old and broken. It got too hot and started a fire. The smoke alarm went off and Mom screamed. She grabbed Sara and ran out of the house. She called the firemen and waited for them to come.
Ben heard the noise and smelled the smoke. He opened his door and saw the flames. He was trapped in his room. He cried and shouted for Mom. But she didn't hear him. He was alone and afraid.
The firemen came and put out the fire. They searched the house and found Ben. But it was too late. He was gone. Mom and Sara were very sad. They lost their home and their Ben. They wished they could have their cake and their happy birthday. But they couldn't. They had nothing.

Sam said, "No, you are wrong. Ten is not the last number. There is more. Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty. I win!"
Tom was angry. He said, "You are stupid. You made up those numbers. They are not real. You are cheating."
Sam was sad. He said, "No, I am not stupid. I learned those numbers from my big sister. She is smart. She goes to school. You are mean."
Tom and Sam started to fight. They pushed and hit each other. They did not see the car coming. The car was fast. The car hit them. They flew in the air. They fell on the ground. They did not get up. They were hurt. They were bleeding. They were not breathing.
The driver of the car was scared. He stopped the car. He got out. He saw Tom and Sam. He called for help. He said, "Oh no, oh no, what have I done? I did not see them. They were playing in the street. They were not in the house. They were not safe. They were silly. They were dead."

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park with their dog, Rex. Rex is a big and impressive dog. He can run fast, jump high, and catch a ball in his mouth.
One day, Ben and Sam see a man in the park. He has a lot of meat in a bag. He is going to have a barbecue with his friends. Rex smells the meat and runs to the man. He wants to eat the meat.
"Hey, stop! That's my meat!" the man shouts. He tries to grab Rex, but Rex is too quick. He takes a big bite of the meat and runs away.
"Rex, come back!" Ben and Sam call. They run after Rex, but he is too fast. He runs to the other side of the park, where there is a pond.
Rex sees the pond and thinks it is a good place to eat his meat. He jumps into the water and swims to the middle. He holds the meat in his mouth and enjoys it.
Ben and Sam reach the pond and see Rex. They are worried. They don't know how to swim. They kneel by the edge of the water and wave their arms.
"Rex, come here! It's dangerous!" they say. They hope Rex will listen to them and come back.
Rex hears them and looks at them. He sees that they are scared and sad. He loves his brothers and doesn't want to make them unhappy. He decides to share his meat with them. He swims back to the shore and drops the meat on the ground. He wags his tail and licks their faces.
"Good boy, Rex!" Ben and Sam say. They hug Rex and thank him. They break the meat into pieces and give some to Rex. They eat the meat together and smile.
The man sees them and walks to them. He is angry and wants his meat back. He yells at them and scolds them.
But Rex growls and barks at him. He protects his brothers and his meat. He shows his teeth and makes the man afraid.
The man backs away and leaves them alone. He goes to his friends and tells them what happened. They laugh at him and tease him.
Ben and Sam and Rex are happy. They finish their meat and play in the park. They are a good team. They love each other.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big mailbox near the road. It is red and shiny. They want to look inside.
"Can we open it?" Tom asks Lily.
"I don't know. Maybe it is not for us," Lily says.
They go closer to the mailbox. They see a small hole on the side. They hear a sound. It is a voice. It is very weak.
"Help me, please. I am stuck in here," the voice says.
Tom and Lily are scared. They do not know who is in the mailbox. They do not know what to do.
"Who are you?" Tom speaks to the hole.
"I am a bird. A bad man put me in here. He wanted to send me away. Please, let me out," the voice says.
Tom and Lily feel sorry for the bird. They want to help him. They look for a way to open the mailbox. They see a lock on the front. They need a key.
"Where is the key?" Lily asks the bird.
"I don't know. The bad man took it. Maybe he dropped it somewhere. Please, hurry. I can't breathe in here," the bird says.
Tom and Lily look around. They see a shiny thing on the ground. It is a key. They pick it up. They run to the mailbox. They put the key in the lock. They turn it. The mailbox opens. They see a small, yellow bird inside. He is very weak. He can barely move.
"Thank you, thank you. You saved me," the bird says.
Tom and Lily are happy. They take the bird out of the mailbox. They hold him gently. They give him some water and some seeds. They stroke his feathers. He feels better.
"You are very brave and kind," the bird says. "You are my friends."
Tom and Lily smile. They are glad they helped the bird. They are glad they have a new friend. They play with him until it is time to go home. They say goodbye to the bird. They promise to come back and visit him. They walk away, holding hands. They are proud of themselves. They did a good thing.

Anne knew it was bad, but she didn't care. All she cared about was staying by the river.

Anne had to learn the hard way that sometimes it is best to listen to her mom.

Sara and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They were very happy.
But then, the sun came out and it was very warm. The snowman started to melt. His hat fell off, his scarf got wet and his nose dropped. Sara and Tom were very sad.
"Look, our snowman is gone!" Sara cried.
"Maybe we can make another one," Tom said.
But there was not enough snow left. They looked around and saw a bottle of shampoo on the porch. Tom had an idea.
"Let's use this to make a snowman!" he said.
He poured some shampoo on the ground and shaped it into a ball. He put another ball on top and a smaller one for the head. He found some sticks for the arms and some stones for the eyes and mouth.
"See, we have a new snowman!" he said.
But Sara did not like it. She thought it was ugly and smelly.
"That's not a snowman, that's a shampoo man!" she said.
She kicked the shampoo man and it fell apart. The shampoo splashed everywhere. Tom was very angry.
"Why did you do that?" he shouted.
"Because it was not a real snowman!" she shouted back.
They started to fight and push each other. They got shampoo on their clothes and hair. They were very messy.
Their mom came out and saw them. She was not happy.
"What are you doing?" she asked.
"We were making a snowman, but Sara ruined it!" Tom said.
"No, he ruined it! He used shampoo!" Sara said.
Mom shook her head. She took them inside and gave them a bath. She washed the shampoo off their hair and clothes. She was not graceful. She was stern.
She told them to say sorry to each other and to share their toys. She told them to be nice and not to waste shampoo. She told them to wait for more snow to make a real snowman.
Sara and Tom felt bad. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They promised to be good and to play together. They hoped for more snow soon. They still loved snowmen.

"Rex, come here! Drop the ball!"

"That is not a snake, Tom. That is a cable. It helps the TV to show pictures and sounds," she says.
Tom does not believe her. He thinks she is deaf. He thinks she cannot hear the snake hiss.
"No, Sue, you are deaf. That is a snake. It can bite us. We have to run away," he says.
He grabs Sue's hand and pulls her. He runs to the door. But he is not careful. He trips on the cable. He falls down. He hurts his knee. He cries.
Sue helps him up. She hugs him. She is sorry for him.
"Tom, you are not deaf. You are silly. That is a cable. It cannot bite us. It is not alive. But you have to be careful. You can suffer if you fall on it. It can make you bleed," she says.
Tom looks at his knee. He sees blood. He is sad. He is sorry for being silly.
"I am sorry, Sue. You are right. That is a cable. It is not a snake. I was silly. I did not listen to you. I suffer because I was not careful," he says.
Sue smiles. She is happy. She is still his friend.
"It is OK, Tom. I forgive you. You are still my friend. Come, I have a band-aid for your knee. Then we can watch TV. But we have to be careful with the cable. We do not want to suffer again," she says.
They go to the bathroom. Sue puts a band-aid on Tom's knee. Then they go to the living room. They watch TV. They are careful with the cable. They are happy. They are friends.

"Look, Ben, look what I found!" she says, holding up the shell.
"Wow, that is a nice shell, Anna. Can I see it?" Ben says, reaching for the shell.
"No, it is mine. I found it first. You can find your own shell," Anna says, pulling the shell away.
Ben feels sad and angry. He wants to see the shell too. He thinks Anna is not being fair. He tries to grab the shell from Anna, but she runs away. She runs along the water, laughing.
Ben runs after her. He wants to catch her and get the shell. He runs faster and faster. He does not see where he is going.
Suddenly, he steps on something hard and sharp. He feels a pain in his foot. He screams and falls down. He looks at his foot and sees blood. He also sees a crab that is pinching his toe. The crab is angry and scared. It thinks Ben is trying to hurt it.
"Ow, ow, ow! Help, help, help!" Ben cries.
Anna hears Ben's scream. She stops running and turns around. She sees Ben on the ground, with a crab on his foot. She feels sorry for him. She drops the shell and runs to him.
"Ben, are you okay? What happened?" she says, kneeling next to him.
"A crab bit me. It hurts. Make it go away," Ben says, sobbing.
Anna carefully takes the crab off Ben's toe. She throws it back into the water. She hugs Ben and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry I was mean to you. I should have shared the shell with you. It is not worth hurting you."
Ben hugs Anna back and says, "It's okay, Anna. I'm sorry I tried to take the shell from you. It is yours. You can have it."
Anna and Ben look at each other and smile. They are friends again. They walk back to the shell and pick it up. They decide to share it. They think it is more attractive when they are happy.

Joe and his best friend Jack were playing in the park one summer day. Joe whistled happily as they ran around, laughing and having a great time. Suddenly, Jack noticed something down in the drain near the slide.
“What’s that, Joe?” asked Jack, pointing at it.
“It looks like an animal!” said Joe, kneeling down at the drain to get a better look.
Joe tried to reach down and grab it, but it was too deep and he couldn't reach. They watched as a friendly little mouse scampered around the drain trying to get out.
“We should help that mouse get out of the drain,” Joe said.
Jack shook his head and replied, “We’ll never be able to do that.”
But Joe didn’t give up. He whistled to the mouse and put his hand out. The mouse slowly scurried towards Joe’s hand and he was able to grab it.
Jack was so surprised when Joe held up the mouse that he jumped back. “Wow!” shouted Jack, “You did it!”
Joe smiled and put the mouse down in the park, where it scurried away, free and happy again. Joe and Jack laughed and smiled, happy that their friendship had saved the day.

Lily and Ben liked to play with their toys. They had cars, dolls, blocks and books. One day, they found a new toy in the closet. It was a big black box with a red button and a long wire. It had a small round thing at the end of the wire.
"What is this?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a record," Ben said.
"A record? What is a record?" Lily wondered.
"Maybe it is something that makes sounds. Let's try it," Ben said. He pressed the red button and spoke into the small round thing. "Hello, hello, this is Ben. Can you hear me?"
Then he let go of the button and pressed it again. He heard his own voice coming out of the box. "Hello, hello, this is Ben. Can you hear me?"
Lily and Ben laughed. They thought it was funny to hear their voices. They took turns to press the button and say different things. They said their names, their favorite colors, their favorite animals and their favorite songs.
They played with the record for a long time. They did not notice that their mom came into the room. She smiled and watched them.
"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" she asked.
"We are playing with the record," Lily said.
"The record? That is not a record. That is a tape recorder. It is a toy that can record and play back sounds. Do you like it?" mom explained.
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They were confused. They did not know what a tape recorder was. They did not know what record and play back meant.
They looked at the box and the wire and the small round thing. They did not understand how it worked.
They looked at mom and shrugged.
"We like it. It is fun," they said.
Mom nodded and hugged them.
"I'm glad you like it. It was my toy when I was a little girl. You can keep it and play with it as much as you want. But be careful not to break it or lose it. And don't forget to put it away when you are done," she said.
"Okay, mom. Thank you, mom," Lily and Ben said.
They gave mom a kiss and went back to playing with the tape recorder. They decided to call it the record anyway. They liked that name better. They thought it was a magic toy that could make their voices sound funny.
They did not notice that mom took a picture of them with her phone. She wanted to record the moment and share it with dad. She thought they were adorable.

Anna and Ben love to play in the park. They like to run, swing, slide and climb. But their favorite thing is to feed the ducks. They always bring some bread and look for the ducks in the pond.
One day, they see a new duck. It is small and yellow and has a big red bow around its neck. It looks like a toy duck, but it moves and quacks like a real duck. Anna and Ben are curious. They want to feed the new duck and make friends with it.
"Hello, little duck," Anna says. "Do you want some bread?" She throws a piece of bread into the water. The new duck swims towards it and eats it. It quacks happily.
"Wow, you are a good duck," Ben says. "What is your name?" He throws another piece of bread. The new duck swims to it and eats it. It quacks again.
"I don't think it can talk," Anna says. "Maybe it has a tag with its name on it. Let's try to catch it and see."
Anna and Ben run to the edge of the pond. They reach out their hands and try to grab the new duck. But the new duck is fast and smart. It swims away from them and quacks loudly.
"Hey, stop that!" a voice says. "That's my duck. His name is Rudy. He's a birthday present from my grandma. She said he likes to swim and play, but he always comes back to me."
Anna and Ben look up and see a boy standing on the other side of the pond. He has a big smile and a basket with more bread. He waves at them and whistles. The new duck hears him and swims to him. He picks up the duck and hugs it.
"Sorry, we didn't know," Anna says. "He's a very nice duck. Can we play with him too?"
"Sure, you can," the boy says. "But you have to be gentle and careful. He's not a toy, he's a life. And he doesn't like to be wet for too long. He likes to be dry and warm and cuddly."
Anna and Ben nod and smile. They walk around the pond and join the boy and the duck. They share their bread and play together. They learn more about Rudy and his grandma. They make a new friend and have a lot of fun. They include the new duck in their game and he includes them in his life. They are all happy.

He saw his toys on the floor. They were as big as him now. He ran to them and tried to play, but they were too heavy and hard. He could not lift them or move them. He felt scared and sad. He wanted to be big again.

"Listen, Tom," Lily says. "Do you hear that?"
Tom stops drinking and listens. He hears a funny sound from the glass. It sounds like a whistle.
"What is that?" Tom asks.
Lily laughs. "It is the air in the glass. When you drink, you make a hole in the water. The air goes in and out and makes a noise."
Tom tries again. He drinks and listens. He hears the whistle again. He thinks it is silly and funny. He laughs too.
"Let me try," Lily says. She takes the glass and drinks. She listens. She hears the whistle.
They take turns drinking and listening. They make different noises with the glass. They giggle and have fun.
Mum comes in and sees them. She smiles.
"What are you doing?" she asks.
"We are making tea and music," Lily says.
"We are using the glass and the air," Tom says.
Mum thinks they are very clever and creative. She joins them and drinks and listens. They all make silly noises and laugh together.

Max learned that he didn't need to be fearful of everything, and the bug was very happy that his home was safe.

One day, the fox spotted a juicy peach on a branch just above the well. Excited, the fox stepped onto the slippery edge of the well and began to climb up the branch. But, just as the fox was about to reach the peach, they started to slip! 
"Oh no!" shouted the fox. Just then, a friendly rabbit hopped up.
"Let me help you fox!" said the rabbit. The rabbit quickly made a rope of grass and lowered it down to the fox. 
The fox grabbed a hold of the rope and was pulled to safety. 
"Thank you so much!" said the fox. 
"You're welcome!" said the rabbit. 
The fox rubbed their paws together with gratitude as the rabbit hopped away. Thanks to the rabbit, the fox was safe and the clever fox never slipped again!

Lily liked to watch the pigeons in the park. They had gray and white feathers and made funny noises. Sometimes they flew away and sometimes they came back. Lily wondered where they went.
One day, Lily saw a man with a big bag. He took out some letters and gave them to some pigeons. The pigeons had little rings on their legs. The man said, "Fly, my pigeons, fly! You are my mail birds. You take the letters to far places."
Lily was curious. She ran to the man and asked, "What are you doing? Why do you give letters to pigeons?"
The man smiled and said, "Hello, little girl. I am a pigeon keeper. I train my pigeons to carry messages. They are very smart and fast. They can find their way to any place I tell them. They are my friends and helpers."
Lily thought that was very interesting. She said, "Can I see your pigeons? Can I touch them? Can I give them a letter?"
The man nodded and said, "Sure, you can. But be gentle and quiet. They are shy and gentle too. And if you want to give them a letter, you have to write something nice and short. They can only carry small papers."
Lily was happy. She took a piece of paper and a crayon from her backpack. She wrote, "Hi, I am Lily. I like pigeons. You are cool. Bye." She folded the paper and gave it to the man. The man put it in a small envelope and tied it to a pigeon's leg. He said, "This pigeon is called Ruby. She is very brave and loyal. She will take your letter to my friend in another town. He will write back to you and send it with another pigeon. Do you want to see her fly?"
Lily said, "Yes, please!" She watched as the man threw Ruby into the air. Ruby flapped her wings and soared into the sky. She looked like a tiny dot in the blue. Lily waved and said, "Bye, Ruby! Thank you for taking my letter!"
The man said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a very nice and polite girl. I hope you get a reply soon. Maybe you can come back and visit me and my pigeons again."
Lily said, "I would love that. You and your pigeons are very interesting. Thank you for showing me your mail birds."
The man said, "You are welcome, Lily. Have a good day."
Lily said, "You too." She ran back to her mom and told her everything. She was very excited and happy. She hoped to see Ruby and the other pigeons again. She wondered what her letter said. She wondered what the other town was like. She learned something new and made a new friend. She had a great day.

Tom nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, Mia. You were right. The ants are dangerous. I will not poke their home again. I will be nice to the ants. And to you."

Lila and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. But their favorite thing was to hang from the monkey bars. They felt strong and happy when they did that.
One day, a new boy came to the park. His name was Ben. He was bigger than Lila and Tom. He wanted to play with them, but he was not very nice. He pushed Lila and Tom off the monkey bars and said, "This is my spot. You are too small and weak to hang here. Go away!"
Lila and Tom felt sad and angry. They did not want to play with Ben. They wanted to hang from the monkey bars. They tried to tell him to stop, but he did not listen. He laughed at them and said, "You are silly and stupid. You don't know anything. I know everything. I have wisdom."
Lila and Tom did not know what wisdom meant. They thought it was something good. They wanted to have wisdom too. They asked Ben, "What is wisdom? How do you get it?"
Ben smirked and said, "Wisdom is when you know everything and you are always right. You get it by being big and strong and smart. You don't have wisdom. You are small and weak and dumb. You will never have wisdom."
Lila and Tom felt bad. They thought they were not good enough. They wished they were big and strong and smart like Ben. They wondered if they could ever have wisdom.
Then, they saw a lady walking by. She had long, white hair and a kind smile. She looked very old, but also very beautiful. She saw Lila and Tom and said, "Hello, children. What are you doing?"
Lila and Tom told her about Ben and the monkey bars and wisdom. They asked her, "Do you know what wisdom is? Do you have wisdom?"
The lady nodded and said, "Yes, I know what wisdom is. And yes, I have wisdom. But wisdom is not what Ben told you. Wisdom is not when you know everything and you are always right. Wisdom is when you learn from everything and you are always kind. Wisdom is not when you are big and strong and smart. Wisdom is when you are humble and gentle and brave. Wisdom is not something you get by pushing others away. Wisdom is something you get by helping others along. Wisdom is not something you have. Wisdom is something you share."
Lila and Tom listened to the lady and felt a warm feeling in their hearts. They understood what she meant. They realized that Ben was not wise at all. He was mean and rude and selfish. They decided that they did not want to be like Ben. They wanted to be like the lady. They wanted to have wisdom.
They thanked the lady and gave her a hug. They said, "You are very wise and very beautiful. We want to be wise and beautiful too. Can you teach us how to be wise and beautiful?"
The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can. But you already have wisdom and beauty inside you. You just need to let them shine. Come, let's go to the monkey bars. I will show you how to hang and how to share."
Lila and Tom followed the lady to the monkey bars. They saw Ben still hanging there, alone and bored. They asked him, "Do you want to play with us? We have a new friend. She is very wise and very beautiful. She can teach us all how to be wise and beautiful too."
Ben looked at them and at the lady. He felt curious and confused. He wondered what they were talking about. He said, "OK, I will play with you. But who is she? And what is wisdom? And what is beautiful?"
The lady said, "I am a grandma. And wisdom is when you learn from everything and you are always kind. And beautiful is when you are humble and gentle and brave. And you can be wise and beautiful too, if you want to. Come, let me show you."
And so, Lila and Tom and Ben and the grandma played together on the monkey bars. They hung and swung and laughed and talked. They learned and shared and helped and cared. They became friends and had fun. And they all felt wise and beautiful.

Tilly replied “What? A crazy idea? What is it?”
Mellie said, “Let’s make our own train with the dough. We can use it to play a game.”
Tilly was excited, “Yes! That’s a great idea! Let’s make our own train!”

Ben and Mia liked to swim in the sea. They had masks and fins to see the fish and the reef. The reef was like a big garden under the water, with many colors and shapes. Ben and Mia liked to play with the fish and look for shells and starfish.
One day, they saw a big boat near the reef. The boat had a big net that it threw into the water. Ben and Mia were curious and swam closer to see what the boat was doing. They saw that the net was catching many fish and some of the reef. They felt sad and angry. They wanted to help the fish and the reef.
They saw a man on the boat who was speaking to another man. They could not hear what he was saying, but they saw that he was pointing at the net and smiling. He looked happy and greedy. Ben and Mia did not like him. They wanted to make him stop.
They had an idea. They swam to the net and started to pull and bite it. They made holes in the net and let some of the fish and the reef out. They hoped that the man would see and get scared. They hoped that he would leave the reef alone.
But the man did not see. He was too busy speaking and laughing. He did not care about the fish and the reef. He only cared about the money he would get. He did not know that there was something else in the water. Something big and fierce. Something that did not like boats and nets. Something that liked to eat fish and men.
It was a shark. A big, fierce shark. It smelled the fish and the blood in the water. It saw the boat and the net. It saw the man who was speaking and laughing. It felt hungry and angry. It wanted to make him stop.
It swam fast and hard. It jumped out of the water and bit the net. It tore the net and let all the fish and the reef out. It saw the man who was speaking and laughing. It bit him too. It made him stop.
Ben and Mia saw the shark. They were scared and amazed. They swam away from the boat and the net. They swam back to the shore. They were safe and happy. They thanked the shark for saving the fish and the reef. They hoped that the man would learn his lesson. They hoped that he would never come back.

"Hey, you two, get down from there!" he says. "You are not supposed to touch the flag. It is a sign of respect. You should kneel and salute it, not climb on it."
Tim and Kim are scared. They get down from the bench and kneel on the ground. They do not know how to salute, so they just put their hands on their hearts.

"It's okay, kids," he says. "You made a mistake, but you learned from it. That's how you grow and become better. Now, let me show you how to salute the flag properly."
He teaches them how to stand straight, look at the flag, and raise their right hand to their forehead. He tells them to say the pledge of allegiance with him.
Tim and Kim follow his instructions. They feel proud and happy. They salute the flag and say the pledge of allegiance with him.
