The fog was rolling in from the sea. It was thick and dangerous. Little Sandy was wrapped up warmly against the cold, standing at the edge of the beach and looking out over the grey mass, bravely. 
"Wow, it's really foggy out there," he said. He could just make out the boats out at sea, their sails barely visible in the darkness.
His dad joined him, placing a strong arm around his shoulders.
"It looks dangerous out there," he said, pointing to the fog, "That's why you should always stay close to the shoreline and never venture too far out at sea. This fog can be deceiving."
Little Sandy nodded and sighed and the two of them went back home, where his Dad storied him a story and tucked him in bed. 
The next day, the fog was even thicker, and the air seemed darker. Little Sandy's dad was pacing up and down the beach, wringing his hands with worry.
"Oh Sandy, I was afraid of this!" he said, "Some of the fishermen went too far out yesterday and the fog has been so thick, they can't find their way back!"
Little Sandy felt his heart beat faster. Those were the same words his father had spoken the night before. The same warning. He had been right. The fog was dangerous indeed.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey and a fox. The fox was very hungry and he wanted to eat something. He asked the monkey if he knew where food was, and the monkey said, “There is an oven in the forest that has lots of food in it. But be careful and don't get caught.”
The fox was so excited and he ran to the oven. He opened the door, and there was so much delicious food inside. He grabbed some food that looked very tasty and started eating. But it was very bitter tasting.
The fox was confused and thought to himself, “Something is not right here.” He realized that the food had been stolen from another animal's home. He knew it was wrong to take someone else's food, so he quickly put the food back in the oven and ran back home.
The next day, the fox had a plan. He asked the monkey to help him, and together they returned to the oven and stole all the food that was inside. This time it tasted sweet, and they enjoyed their feast!
Even though they had gotten away with their sneaky plan, the fox still felt a little bit bad. He had learned a valuable lesson and promised himself to never steal again.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the park. They saw a huge barrel near the slide. They wondered what was inside.
"Let's open it!" Ben said.
"Maybe it has toys or candy!" Mia said.
They ran to the barrel and tried to lift the lid. But it was too heavy and stuck.
"Hello? Is anyone there?" They heard a voice from inside the barrel.
They were surprised and scared. Who was in the barrel?
"Who are you?" Ben asked.
"I'm a monkey. I was in a truck, but it stopped and I got out. Then I found this barrel and hid inside. But now I can't get out. Can you help me?" The voice answered.
"A monkey?" Mia said. "Wow! That's cool!"
Ben and Mia looked at each other. They liked monkeys. They wanted to help.
"OK, we'll help you. But you have to be nice and not bite us. And you have to share your bananas with us." Ben said.
"Deal. Thank you, kids. You are very kind." The voice said.
Ben and Mia pushed and pulled the lid until it opened. They saw a brown monkey with a long tail and big eyes. He smiled and waved at them.
"Hi, I'm Max. What are your names?" He asked.
"I'm Ben and this is Mia. We're friends." Ben said.
"Nice to meet you, Ben and Mia. You're my friends too. Do you want to play with me?" Max asked.
"Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia said.
They took Max out of the barrel and played with him in the park. They had a lot of fun. They shared bananas and stories. They slid on the slide and swung on the swings. They laughed and hugged.
They were happy. They had a new friend. A monkey friend.

He would run around the house, pointing the pistol and making "bang bang" sounds. Tim's mom always told him to be careful with his toy and not to point it at people.
One day, Tim went to the park to play with his friends. He brought his white pistol with him. He showed his friends the pistol and they all wanted to play with it too. Tim's mom told him to let his friends have a turn with the pistol. So, Tim let them play with his toy.
While they were playing, Tim's mom talked to them about being kind and sharing with others. She said it's important to let others have a chance to play with our toys. Tim and his friends learned that sharing is good and makes everyone happy. From that day on, they always shared their toys with each other and had lots of fun together. The moral of the story is to share and be kind to others, so everyone can have fun and be happy.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were animals. Ben was a lion and Lily was a bird. They roared and chirped and had fun.
Then they heard a knock on the door. It was their mom. She came in with a big smile on her face. She said, "Hi, kids. I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?"
Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the door. They saw a man standing outside. He had a weird face. He had a big nose, a long beard, and a hat with feathers. He looked like a pirate. He said, "Ahoy, mateys. I'm your uncle Jack. I came to visit you."
Ben and Lily stared at him. They did not know him. They felt scared. They hid behind their mom. They said, "Who is he? He has a weird face. We don't like him."
Their mom hugged them and said, "Don't be afraid. He is my brother. He is your uncle. He lives far away. He came to say hello. He is very nice. He brought you some gifts. Do you want to see them?"
Ben and Lily shook their heads. They did not want to see the gifts. They did not want to see the man. They said, "No, thank you. We want to play. We want him to leave."
Their mom looked sad. She said, "I'm sorry, kids. He won't stay long. He just wants to meet you. He loves you. Can you be polite and say hi?"
Ben and Lily did not want to be rude. They loved their mom. They peeked from behind her and said, "Hi, uncle Jack. Nice to meet you."
Uncle Jack smiled and said, "Hi, Ben and Lily. Nice to meet you too. You are very cute. I'm sorry if I scared you. I don't mean to. I just like to dress like a pirate. It's fun. Do you like pirates?"
Ben and Lily looked at each other. They liked pirates. They liked to dress up too. They said, "Yes, we like pirates. They are cool. Do you have a ship?"
Uncle Jack nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I have a big ship. It's called the Black Pearl. Do you want to see it?"
Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, we want to see it. Can we go with you?"
Uncle Jack laughed and said, "Sure, you can. But only if your mom says yes. And only if you promise to be brave and have fun."
Ben and Lily looked at their mom. She smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But only for a little while. And only if you promise to be careful and listen to your uncle."
Ben and Lily agreed and said, "We promise. We promise."
They took their uncle's hand and went to see his ship. They forgot about his weird face. They only saw his kind eyes. They had a lot of fun. They learned to say "Arrr" and "Yo-ho-ho". They played with his parrot and his sword. They felt like real pirates.
They were glad they did not leave. They were glad they met their uncle. He was not so weird after all. He was very nice. They loved him.

One day, their mom said, "I made spaghetti for lunch. Come and eat, my little actors." Ben and Lily ran to the kitchen. They loved spaghetti. It was their favorite food.
But when they saw their plates, they were surprised. The spaghetti was not red, like usual. It was green, and it had little pieces of broccoli and cheese on it. "What is this?" Ben asked. "This is not spaghetti. This is yucky."
Mom smiled. "This is a special spaghetti. It is good for you, and it tastes yummy. Try it, you might like it."
Lily was adventurous. She liked to try new things. She picked up a fork and twirled some green spaghetti. She put it in her mouth and chewed. "Mmm, this is good," she said. "It is cheesy and crunchy. I like it."
Ben was not adventurous. He did not like to try new things. He pushed his plate away and crossed his arms. "No, I don't want it. I want red spaghetti. This is not good."
Mom sighed. "Ben, don't be so picky. You should be more like your sister. She is brave and curious. She likes to act and to eat new things. You are missing out on a lot of fun."
Ben looked at Lily. She was smiling and eating her green spaghetti. She looked happy and satisfied. He felt a little jealous. Maybe he was missing out on something. Maybe he should be more adventurous, too.
He picked up his fork and twirled some green spaghetti. He put it in his mouth and chewed. He made a face. He did not like it. It was cheesy and crunchy, but it was also bitter and weird. He spit it out and said, "Blech, this is bad. I don't like it. I want red spaghetti."
Mom shook her head. "Ben, you are not acting. You are being rude. You should at least try to be polite and say thank you. And you should not waste food. There are children who have nothing to eat."
Ben felt ashamed. He knew Mom was right. He was not acting. He was being rude. He did not want to be rude. He wanted to be a good actor. He wanted to make Mom happy.
He picked up his fork again and twirled some green spaghetti. He put it in his mouth and chewed. He smiled and said, "Mmm, this is good. Thank you, Mom. You are the best cook."
Mom smiled back. "You are welcome, Ben. You are a good actor. And a good son."
Lily winked at Ben. She knew he was acting. She was proud of him. He was adventurous, after all.

Sam and Jen are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make a race track with cardboard and tape.
"Let's race our cars!" Sam says. "The fastest car wins!"
"OK!" Jen says. "But how do we know who is faster?"
Sam thinks for a moment. He sees a big clock on the wall. He has an idea.
"We can use the clock!" he says. "We can start when the clock says zero, and stop when it says ten. Then we can count how many times our cars go around the track. The car with more times is faster!"
Jen nods. She likes Sam's idea. They choose their cars and put them on the track. They wait for the clock to say zero.
"Ready, set, go!" Sam shouts. They push their cars with their hands. They make vroom-vroom noises. They watch their cars zoom around the track.
Sam's car is red. It is big and shiny. It has a lot of speed. It goes around the track very fast.
Jen's car is blue. It is small and cute. It has a lot of stickers. It goes around the track very slow.
Sam sees that his car is faster than Jen's car. He smiles. He thinks he will win.
Jen sees that her car is slower than Sam's car. She frowns. She thinks she will lose.
She looks around. She sees a yellow car on the floor. It is available. It is not on the track. She has an idea.
She picks up the yellow car. She adds it to her blue car. She makes a double car. She pushes the double car with both hands. She makes louder vroom-vroom noises. She watches the double car zoom around the track.
The double car has more speed than the red car. It goes around the track faster. It catches up with the red car. It passes the red car.
Sam sees that the double car is faster than his car. He gasps. He thinks he will lose.
Jen sees that the double car is faster than Sam's car. She cheers. She thinks she will win.
The clock says ten. They stop pushing their cars. They count how many times their cars go around the track.
Sam's car goes around the track four times. Jen's double car goes around the track five times.
"Wow!" Sam says. "You win! How did you do that?"
"I added a yellow car to my blue car!" Jen says. "It made my car faster!"
"That's so cool!" Sam says. "Can I try?"
"Sure!" Jen says. "Let's race again!"
They swap their cars. They wait for the clock to say zero. They race again. They have fun. They are friends.

The mirror did not say anything. It only showed Lily's face. Lily moved the mirror around and saw different things behind her. She saw her bed, her toys, her window, and her door. She wondered what else the mirror could show her.
She walked to the door and opened it. She saw the hall and the stairs. She went down the stairs and saw the living room and the kitchen. She saw her mom and dad and her baby brother. She waved the mirror at them.
"Look, Mom, look, Dad, look, baby!" she said. "I have a mirror! It shows me everything!"
Her mom and dad smiled and said hello. Her baby brother giggled and reached for the mirror. Lily did not want to share. She ran away with the mirror.
She went to the garden and saw the flowers and the trees and the birds. She saw a pond with water and fish. She went to the pond and looked at the mirror. She saw the water and the fish and her face. She leaned closer and closer to the mirror. She wanted to see more.
But the mirror was slippery and Lily lost her grip. The mirror fell into the pond and sank. Lily could not see it anymore. She only saw the water and the fish. She felt sad and scared. She had lost her mirror.
She cried and cried. She ran back to the house and told her mom and dad what happened. They hugged her and said it was okay. They said they would buy her a new mirror. They said they loved her.
Lily felt better. She said she was sorry. She said she loved them too. She learned a lesson. She learned that the mirror was not as deep as the pond. She learned that the mirror was not as important as her family. She learned to be careful and to share. She was a good girl.

Tom is a cop. He likes to help people and catch bad guys. He wears a blue suit and a hat with a star. He has a car with lights and a siren. He thinks his job is fun.
One day, Tom goes to a school. He wants to teach the kids about being a cop. He brings his car and his hat. He shows them how to turn on the lights and the siren. He lets them try on his hat. He tells them how to be safe and follow the rules.
Some kids think Tom is cool. They ask him many questions. They want to be cops when they grow up. They say thank you to Tom. They give him hugs and high fives.
But one kid thinks Tom is boring. His name is Ben. He does not listen to Tom. He does not ask any questions. He does not try on the hat. He does not say thank you. He yawns and rolls his eyes.
Tom sees Ben. He feels sad. He wants Ben to like him. He wants Ben to learn. He goes to Ben and says, "Hi, Ben. Do you like being a cop?"
Ben shakes his head. He says, "No, I don't. Being a cop is boring. I want to be a pirate. Pirates are fun. They have swords and treasure and ships. They do whatever they want. They are not boring like cops."
Tom smiles. He says, "I see. Pirates are fun, but they are also bad. They steal and fight and break the rules. They make people sad and scared. They are not nice like cops. Cops are good. They help and protect and follow the rules. They make people happy and safe. They are not boring like pirates."
Ben thinks for a moment. He says, "Really? I didn't know that. Maybe being a cop is not so boring. Maybe being a pirate is not so fun. Maybe I can learn more about being a cop. Can I try on your hat?"
Tom nods. He says, "Sure, Ben. You can try on my hat. You can also learn more about being a cop. You can ask me anything you want. I will be happy to answer. Maybe you will like being a cop after all."
Ben smiles. He says, "Thank you, Tom. You are a nice cop. You are not boring. You are fun. Maybe I will be a cop when I grow up. Or maybe I will be something else. But I will always be good and follow the rules. And I will always learn new things."
Tom hugs Ben. He says, "You are welcome, Ben. You are a smart kid. You are not boring. You are fun. You can be anything you want when you grow up. But I hope you will always be good and follow the rules. And I hope you will always learn new things."

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a big bag of popcorn in the kitchen. They wanted to eat some, but they knew they had to ask their moms first.
"Let's take some popcorn and hide in the garden," Tom said. "Our moms won't know."
"No, that's not honest," Lily said. "We have to tell them the truth."
Tom did not listen to Lily. He took some popcorn and ran to the garden. Lily followed him, feeling sad.
In the garden, Tom found a big rock. He thought it was fun to rub the popcorn on the rock and make it pop. He laughed and ate the popcorn.
Lily watched him and shook her head. She did not want to rub the popcorn on the rock. She thought it was dirty and wasteful.
Soon, their moms came looking for them. They saw Tom with the popcorn and the rock. They were angry and disappointed.
"Tom, why did you take the popcorn without asking?" Tom's mom asked. "And why did you rub it on the rock? That's not nice or clean."
Tom felt ashamed. He did not know what to say.
Lily's mom saw Lily with no popcorn. She smiled and hugged her.
"Lily, you are a good and honest girl," Lily's mom said. "You did not take the popcorn without asking. You did not rub it on the rock. You are a good friend to Tom."
Lily felt happy. She knew she did the right thing.
The moral of the story is: Be honest and respectful. Don't take things without asking. Don't waste food or make a mess.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the forest. They had a wooden spear that they made with their dad. They pretended to be hunters and chased animals.
One day, they saw a big deer with horns. They wanted to catch it and bring it home. They ran after it with their spear. But the deer was fast and smart. It ran away from them and hid behind a tree.
"Where did it go?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Let's look around." Sam said.
They split up and searched for the deer. Tom went to the left and Sam went to the right. Tom saw something brown and furry behind a bush. He thought it was the deer. He crept closer and threw his spear.
But it was not the deer. It was a bear. A big, angry bear. It roared and stood up on its hind legs. It had sharp teeth and claws. It was not afraid of the spear.
Tom was scared. He turned around and ran. He shouted for Sam.
"Help! Help! There is a bear!"
Sam heard Tom and ran to him. He saw the bear chasing Tom. He picked up a stick and threw it at the bear. The stick hit the bear on the nose. The bear stopped and snarled.
"Run, Tom, run!" Sam said.
Tom and Sam ran as fast as they could. They ran out of the forest and back to their home. They slammed the door and locked it. They were safe.
They hugged each other and breathed hard. They were glad they escaped the bear.
They learned a lesson. They were ignorant. They did not know much about the forest and the animals. They did not respect them. They should not play with a spear. They should not chase a deer. They should not throw a spear at a bear.
They decided to play something else. Something safer and nicer. They decided to play with their dog. Their dog was friendly and loyal. He did not roar or bite. He licked their faces and wagged his tail. He was happy to see them.
They played with their dog and had fun. They forgot about the forest and the spear and the bear. They were happy too.

Tom was bald. He did not like his head. He wanted hair like his wife. His wife had long and soft hair. She loved Tom very much.
One day, Tom saw a shop. The shop had a sign. The sign said: "We can improve your hair. Come in and try." Tom was curious. He went inside the shop.
A man greeted him. The man had a lot of hair. The man said: "Hello, sir. Do you want to improve your hair? We have a special offer. You can choose any color and style you like. It is easy and fast."
Tom said: "Yes, please. I want to improve my hair. I want to have hair like my wife. She has brown and curly hair. Can you do that?"
The man said: "Of course, sir. No problem. Just sit here and relax. I will use this machine. It will make your hair grow in minutes. Trust me, you will look great."
Tom sat on a chair. The man put a helmet on his head. The helmet had wires and buttons. The man turned on the machine. The machine made a loud noise. Tom felt a tickle on his head.
After a while, the man turned off the machine. He took off the helmet. He gave Tom a mirror. Tom looked at himself. He was shocked. He had hair, but not like his wife. He had pink and spiky hair. He looked like a clown.
Tom said: "What have you done? This is not what I wanted. This is not how my wife's hair looks like. This is awful. I want my money back."
The man said: "Sorry, sir. There was a mistake. The machine mixed up the colors and styles. I can fix it. Just give me another chance."
Tom said: "No, thank you. I don't trust you. I don't want your hair. I want my bald head back. How can I get rid of this hair?"
The man said: "Well, sir. There is only one way. You have to shave it off. Here, take this razor. It is free. Good luck, sir. And have a nice day."
Tom took the razor. He ran out of the shop. He went home. He shaved off his hair. He was bald again. He felt better. He hugged his wife. His wife said: "I love you, Tom. You are handsome with or without hair. You don't need to improve anything. You are perfect for me."
Tom said: "Thank you, my dear. You are right. I love you, too. You are the best wife in the world. You make me happy with or without hair. You are perfect for me, too."

One day, Sara's mom said they were going to visit her grandma. Her grandma lived in the country, far away from the city. Sara was excited to see her grandma, but she was also sad to leave her bike. She asked her mom if she could take her bike with them.
"I'm sorry, Sara, but there is no room for your bike in the car. You can play with your grandma's toys when we get there. Maybe she has a bike you can ride," her mom said.
Sara nodded, but she felt lonely without her bike. She hugged her bike and said goodbye. She hoped her bike would not miss her too much.
When they got to the country, Sara saw a lot of green fields and trees. She also saw some cows and horses. She thought they were pretty, but she still missed her bike. She went inside her grandma's house and gave her a big hug.
"Hello, Sara, I'm so happy to see you. Do you want to see what I have for you?" her grandma said.
Sara smiled and followed her grandma to the backyard. There, she saw a surprise. It was a bike, just like hers, but blue. It had a bell and a basket, too.
"Wow, grandma, is this for me?" Sara asked.
"Yes, my dear, it is. I knew you loved to ride your bike, so I got you one for your visit. You can ride it as much as you want, and explore the country with me. Do you like it?" her grandma said.
Sara was so happy, she could not believe it. She hugged her grandma and thanked her. She ran to the bike and got on. She rang the bell and smiled.
"I love it, grandma, thank you so much. Can we go for a ride now?" Sara said.
"Of course, my dear, let's go. I'll show you some beautiful places. And don't worry, your bike at home will be waiting for you when you come back," her grandma said.
Sara and her grandma rode their bikes together, and Sara felt the wind on her face. She saw the cows and the horses, and the flowers and the birds. She felt happy and not lonely anymore. She loved the country, and she loved her grandma. And she loved her bike, both the red and the blue.

One day, Lily was in the toilet and saw something weird. She did not know what it was and asked her mummy.
Mummy said, "Oh, Lily! That's a spider. Don't worry, it is not dangerous."
Lily was still scared and asked, "What does it do in the toilet? That's weird!"
Mummy laughed and said, "Spiders like to eat the bugs in the bathroom. That's why it's in there!"
Lily was curious and wanted to know more. She asked, "Can I help it do its job?" 
Mummy smiled and said, "No, sweetheart. That's okay. The spider knows what is best. Just let it do its own thing and it will be fine."
Lily thought that was nice and decided to watch the spider instead of playing with her toys. She thought it was cool how the spider can do its job all on its own.

As the rain poured down, Tim rode his scooter through the puddles. He splashed and laughed, having so much fun. But then, he saw something big and scary in the street. It was a big, scary dog! Tim was scared, but he wanted to be brave.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play on the farm. They have a big dog named Spot who likes to run and bark. One day, they see a new thing in the stable. It is a big, brown horse with a long mane and tail.
"Wow, look at the horse!" Tim says. "Can we pet it?"
"I don't know," Kim says. "Maybe we should ask Dad first."
They run to find Dad, who is working in the field. They tell him about the horse and ask if they can pet it.
"Sure, you can pet the horse," Dad says. "But be careful, he is very old and sick. He has a bad leg that hurts a lot. And he has a sore on his side that is rotting. It smells bad and has flies on it. You don't want to touch that."
"Yuck, that's gross," Tim says. "Why do you have a horse that is rotting?"
"Well, the horse belongs to Mr. Jones, who lives next door. He can't take care of him anymore, so he asked me to keep him in the stable until he finds a new home for him. I'm trying to help him, but I don't think he will get better. He is too old and weak."
"That's sad," Kim says. "Can we give him some water and hay? Maybe that will make him feel better."
"Sure, you can do that," Dad says. "But don't get too close to his sore. And wash your hands after you pet him. Come on, I'll show you where the water and hay are."
Tim and Kim follow Dad to the stable. They fill a bucket with water and put some hay in a trough. They pet the horse gently on his head and neck. He looks at them with sad eyes and makes a soft noise.
"Hello, horse," Tim says. "We are Tim and Kim. We are your friends. We want you to be happy."
The horse nods his head and drinks some water. He nibbles on some hay. He seems to like Tim and Kim. They smile and hug him.
"Good horse," Kim says. "We hope you find a new home soon. A home where you are not rotting and hurting. A home where you are loved."
The horse whinnies and licks their faces. He thanks them for being kind. Tim and Kim giggle and wipe their faces. They say goodbye to the horse and run back to Dad. They tell him they had fun with the horse. Dad smiles and hugs them.
"You are good kids," Dad says. "You have big hearts. You made the horse happy today. And you made me proud."

Then, a funny thing happened. Out of the broken pieces of the new rod came a butterfly. It was the most beautiful creature the little girl had ever seen. She watched in wonder as the colorful butterfly flew around the garden. Suddenly, the little girl was so happy again. 
The little girl thanked the rod for giving her such a special gift. She decided to always take care of nature from then on. The little girl and the butterfly became best friends and always played together in the garden.

"Look, our tower is so tall!" Ben says.
"Yes, it is!" Lily says. "We are good builders!"
They are happy and proud. They have success. They want to show their tower to their teacher and their friends.
But then, a big wind comes. It blows hard and fast. It makes their tower fall down. All the blocks crash to the ground. Ben and Lily are sad and angry. They cry and shout.
"No, no, no!" Ben says. "Our tower is gone!"
"Why, why, why?" Lily says. "We worked so hard!"
They hug each other and wipe their tears. They look at the mess of blocks. They feel like giving up.
But then, their teacher comes. She sees their tower and their faces. She smiles and hugs them.
"I saw your tower before the wind came," she says. "It was amazing! You did a great job!"
She helps them pick up the blocks. She tells them they can try again. She tells them they are brave and smart. She tells them she is grateful for them.
Ben and Lily feel better. They smile and thank their teacher. They decide to build another tower. They hope it will be even bigger and stronger. They are still friends. They are still good builders. They are still happy and proud. They still have success.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big box on the table. It had a shiny paper and a bow.
"Let's open it!" Lily said. She grabbed a knife from the drawer.
"No, no, no!" Tom said. "That is not for us. That is for Mommy. And the knife is sharp. It can hurt you."
"But I want to see what is inside. Maybe it is a toy or a book or a cake." Lily said. She tried to cut the paper with the knife.
Tom ran to the door and called for Mommy. "Mommy, Mommy, come quick! Lily has a knife and she is opening your box!"
Mommy came into the kitchen and saw Lily with the knife and the box. She was angry and scared. She took the knife from Lily and put it away. She looked at the box and saw a hole in the paper.
"Oh, Lily, what have you done? This is a very special gift from Grandma. She made it for me. It is a scarf. She wrapped it with love and care. And you ruined it with the knife." Mommy said.
Lily felt bad. She did not mean to make Mommy sad. She saw the scarf in the box. It was red and blue and green. It had flowers and stars and hearts. It was very pretty. But it was also very smelly.
"Mommy, why is the scarf smelly?" Lily asked.
Mommy sniffed the scarf and made a face. "Oh, no. The scarf is smelly because Grandma has a cat. And the cat likes to sleep on the scarf. And the cat is not very clean. He has fleas and dirt and hair. And he pees on the scarf. That is why it is smelly." Mommy said.
Lily and Tom made a face too. They did not like the smelly scarf. They did not want to touch it or wear it.
"Mommy, can we throw away the smelly scarf?" Lily asked.
Mommy thought for a moment. She loved Grandma and she knew Grandma loved her. She did not want to hurt Grandma's feelings. But she also did not want to keep the smelly scarf.
"Maybe we can wash the smelly scarf and make it clean and nice. And then we can wrap it again and send it back to Grandma. And we can say thank you and we love you. And we can ask her to make us a new scarf without the cat." Mommy said.
Lily and Tom nodded. They liked that idea. They helped Mommy wash the smelly scarf and dry it and wrap it. They wrote a card for Grandma and put it in the box. They hoped Grandma would understand and not be mad. They also hoped Grandma would make them a new scarf that was not smelly.

"Hello, doggy!" Lily said. "What is your name?"
The dog barked and pointed his nose at a tag on his collar. It said "Rex".
"Rex!" Ben repeated. "That is a good name for a dog. Do you want to play with us, Rex?"
Rex nodded and ran after a ball that Lily threw. They had fun for a long time. Then they got tired and hungry.
"Let's go home, Lily," Ben said. "It is time for lunch and a nap."
"OK, Ben," Lily agreed. "But can we take Rex with us? He is so charming. Maybe he is lost and needs a home."
They looked around, but they did not see anyone who looked like Rex's owner. They decided to take Rex with them. They held his collar and walked to Lily's house. Lily's mom was surprised to see them with a dog.
"Who is this, Lily?" she asked.
"This is Rex, mom," Lily said. "He is our new friend. He was in the park and he was charming. Can we keep him, please?"
Lily's mom smiled and petted Rex. He wagged his tail and licked her hand.
"Well, he is a charming dog, indeed," she said. "But we have to find out if he belongs to someone else. Maybe he has a family who is looking for him. We can call the number on his tag and see."
Lily and Ben nodded. They understood that Rex might have another home. But they hoped that he could stay with them. They gave him some water and food and made a cozy bed for him in the living room. Then they ate their lunch and went to sleep. Rex curled up next to them and slept too. He was happy to have such charming friends.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, Anna saw a new toy in the shop. It was a big bear with a red heart on its chest. Anna wanted the bear very much. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no. She said they had no money for new toys.
Anna was sad and angry. She thought of a plan to get the bear. She went to Ben's house and saw that he had a lot of toys. She saw a black car that Ben liked very much. She asked Ben if she could play with the car. Ben said yes, because he was a good friend. He gave Anna the car and said, "Be careful with it. It is my favorite."
Anna took the car and ran away. She did not say thank you or goodbye. She went to the shop and gave the car to the shopkeeper. She said, "I want to trade this car for the bear with the heart." The shopkeeper looked at the car and said, "This is a very nice car. Are you sure you want to trade it?" Anna said yes, because she only wanted the bear.
The shopkeeper gave Anna the bear and took the car. Anna hugged the bear and smiled. She thought she was very clever. She went home with the bear and put it on her bed. She did not play with it. She just looked at it.
The next day, Ben came to Anna's house. He was sad and angry. He said, "Anna, where is my car? You took it and did not give it back. That was not nice. That was mean." Anna said, "I traded your car for this bear. See? It has a heart. It is better than your car." Ben said, "That was not your car to trade. It was mine. You did not ask me. You did not request. You stole it. That was wrong. You have a black heart. You are not my friend anymore." He turned around and left.
Anna felt a pain in her chest. She looked at the bear and saw that its heart was not red anymore. It was black. She realized that she had done a bad thing. She had hurt her friend and herself. She had lost the car and the bear. She had no toys and no friends. She cried and cried.
The moral of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. Do not trade what is not yours. Do not hurt your friends. Be honest and kind. Request before you take. Say thank you and goodbye. Then you will have a red heart and happy friends.

"Oh no!" Tom said. "I broke the ball!"
Lily saw what happened. She was sad. She liked the ball. It was her favorite toy. She said to Tom, "Why did you break the ball? It was not a drum. It was a ball. Now we can't play with it."
Tom felt sorry. He did not mean to break the ball. He said to Lily, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not know it would break. I wanted to make an interesting sound for our song. Can you forgive me?"
Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sorry. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But next time, be careful with the toys. They are not all drums. Some are balls, some are dolls, some are cars. They are for playing, not breaking."
Tom nodded. He said, "You are right, Lily. I will be careful. Thank you for forgiving me. Can we still play music?"
Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, we can still play music. But let's use the toys that are for music. Like the drum, the guitar, the flute and the bell. They make interesting sounds too. And they don't break."
Tom and Lily hugged. They picked up their music toys. They played a new song. It was loud and happy. Their mom and dad clapped and cheered. They were proud of their band.

Tom and Lily were playing with a puzzle. They liked the puzzle because it had many colors and shapes. They tried to fit the pieces together to make a picture of a farm.
"Look, I found the cow!" Tom said, holding a piece with black and white spots.
"Good job, Tom!" Lily said. "Can I have the piece with the red barn?"
Tom nodded and gave Lily the piece. They worked on the puzzle for a long time. They were patient and careful.
But then, Tom saw a piece that he really liked. It had a yellow duck on it. He wanted to put it in the puzzle, but Lily had it in her hand.
"Give me the duck, Lily!" Tom said, reaching for the piece.
"No, Tom, it's mine!" Lily said, pulling the piece away.
They both tugged on the piece, but it was too hard. The piece ripped in half. The duck was broken.
Tom and Lily gasped. They looked at the piece and then at each other. They felt sad and angry.
"That was my duck!" Tom said, crying.
"You ripped it!" Lily said, crying too.
They threw the piece on the floor and turned away from each other. They did not want to play anymore.
Their mom heard them crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken piece and the unfinished puzzle.
"What happened, Tom and Lily?" she asked.
They told her what happened. They blamed each other for the duck.
Mom sighed. She picked up the piece and showed it to them.
"Look, Tom and Lily, this is just a piece of cardboard. It's not a real duck. It can be fixed with some tape. But you know what can't be fixed so easily? Your friendship. You are brother and sister. You should love and help each other, not fight and hurt each other. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded. They felt sorry for what they did.
"Can you say sorry to each other and forgive each other?" Mom asked.
Tom and Lily looked at each other. They saw the tears in their eyes and the hurt in their hearts.
They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry, Lily. I forgive you."
Mom smiled and hugged them too. She said, "That's very good, Tom and Lily. I'm proud of you. Now, let's finish the puzzle together, okay?"
Tom and Lily agreed. They taped the piece and put it in the puzzle. They found the other pieces and made the picture of the farm. They were happy and proud.
They learned that puzzles are fun, but friendship is more important. They learned to be patient and kind. They learned to forgive.

The bee was very happy. He took the nectar from the delicate flower and said, "Thank you, flower! Now, I can make honey for my family." The flower felt good that she could help the bee. They became friends and played together in the garden every day. And they all lived happily in the beautiful spring garden.

Ben and Jen are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they see a big map on the wall. The map has many colors and shapes. Ben points to a shape and says, "What is this?"
Jen looks at the shape and says, "That is a nation. A nation is a place where many people live. They have a name and a flag and a leader."
Ben nods and says, "I see. And what is this color?"
Jen says, "That is blue. Blue is a color like the sky and the water. Some nations have blue in their flag."
Ben says, "I like blue. It is a clean color. It makes me happy."
Jen says, "Me too. Let's find more blue nations on the map."
They look at the map and see many blue nations. They say their names and flags. They have fun.
But then, a big boy comes to the map. He is mean and angry. He does not like Ben and Jen. He says, "Get away from the map. It is mine. You are stupid and dirty. You do not know anything about nations."
Ben and Jen are scared and sad. They say, "No, please. We are just playing. We are not stupid and dirty. We know some things about nations."
The big boy does not listen. He pushes Ben and Jen away from the map. He tears the map from the wall. He throws the map on the floor. He steps on the map. He says, "Ha ha ha. Now the map is broken. Now the nations are broken. Now you have nothing to play with."
Ben and Jen cry. They see the map on the floor. They see the colors and shapes. They see the blue nations. They are not clean anymore. They are dirty and torn. They are not happy anymore. They are unhappy.
The end.

"Please, Chief! I want to quit my job," said Pete.
The village chief thought for a moment and looked at Pete. "I understand why you want to quit. But why do you have to leave? This village is so useful," he said. 
Pete told the village chief about his dreams and his hopes for the future. He said he wanted to explore the world and find new things. 
The village chief smiled. "I understand," he said. "If you're sure that this is what you want to do, you have my permission. Go and explore the world, Pete!"
So Pete left the village, but it was always in his heart. He kept the useful things the village gave him, and the knowledge it taught him. From that day, he went on many adventures, and he never forgot how useful the village was.

Once upon a time, there was a patient bear. He was always very calm and waited a long time for something to happen.
One day, he was walking through the forest when he saw a shiny jewel. Amazed at the beauty of the jewel, the bear decided to take it home.
On his way home, the bear started to roll the jewel along the path. As he rolled it, he imagined all the things he could do with the jewel. Suddenly, he heard a voice, "Bear, stop rolling that jewel and put it back where you got it".
Startled, the bear saw a wise owl who repeated, "Bear, if you take something from the forest, you must give something back. Put the jewel back and take something else instead."
The bear thanked the wise owl and did as he said. The bear was patient and instead of taking the jewel, he rolled away a pinecone. He took the pinecone home and thanked the wise owl again.
Moral: Be patient and take only what you need.

"We're sorry, Mom. We won't touch it again. We'll be obedient." Tim and Lily said.
Mom smiled. She hugged them and kissed them.
"That's good, Tim and Lily. I love you. Now, why don't you play with your blocks or your dolls? They are much more fun and safe than an ashtray." Mom said.

The kind duck wanted to help the bunny. So, the duck said, "I will teach you to swim. Don't be worried. I am here with you." The duck took the bunny to the water and showed the bunny how to rub its feet in the water.
The bunny started to rub its feet in the water, just like the duck. Soon, the bunny was not worried anymore. The duck and the bunny became good friends and played together on the island every day.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a long bean on the ground. It is green and shiny.
"Wow, look at this bean!" Sara says. "It is so long and pretty. I want it!"
"No, I want it!" Tom says. "I saw it first. It is mine!"
They both pull on the bean. It is very strong. They cannot break it.
"Stop it!" Sara says. "You are hurting the bean. Let go!"
"No, you let go!" Tom says. "You are being mean. Share!"
They keep pulling and pulling. They are not happy. They are angry.
Then, they hear a voice. It is Mama. She is looking for them.
"Sara, Tom, where are you?" Mama says. "It is time to go home. Come here!"
Sara and Tom drop the bean. They run to Mama. They hug her.
"Mama, we found a long bean!" Sara says. "But we could not share it. We fought over it."
"Mama, we are sorry!" Tom says. "We were not nice to each other. We hurt the bean."
Mama smiles. She picks up the bean. She looks at it.
"This is a special bean," Mama says. "It is a magic bean. It can grow into a big plant. Do you want to see?"
Sara and Tom nod. They are curious. They want to see.
Mama takes them to a pot. She digs a hole. She puts the bean in the hole. She covers it with dirt. She waters it.
"Let's wait and see what happens," Mama says. "Maybe tomorrow, we will see something."
Sara and Tom look at the pot. They look at each other. They feel sorry.
"Tom, I am sorry I was mean to you," Sara says. "You can have the bean. I don't need it."
"Sara, I am sorry I was mean to you," Tom says. "You can have the bean. I don't need it."
They hug each other. They are friends again.
"Mama, can we share the bean?" Sara and Tom say. "We want to see the magic together."
Mama nods. She is proud of them.
"Of course you can share the bean," Mama says. "Sharing is caring. And caring is magic."

One day, Lily saw a new bird in the pet shop. It was in a big cage with a sign that said "Parrot". The bird was green and red and blue. It had a long tail and a fancy hat. It looked at Lily and said "Hello".
Lily was surprised. She said "Hello" back. The bird said "What is your name?" Lily said "Lily". The bird said "Lily, I like you. Do you like me?" Lily said "Yes, I like you. You are a nice bird."
The bird said "Lily, do you want to be my friend?" Lily said "Yes, I want to be your friend. Can I take you home?" The bird said "Yes, you can take me home. But you need to ask the man first."
Lily ran to the man who worked in the pet shop. She said "Please, can I have the parrot? He is my friend. He can talk to me." The man smiled and said "The parrot is very special. He is very smart and funny. But he is also very expensive. He costs a lot of money."
Lily was sad. She did not have a lot of money. She only had a few coins in her pocket. She said "But I really want the parrot. He is the best bird ever." The man said "I understand. But I can't give you the parrot for free. Maybe you can save some money and come back later."
Lily thought for a moment. She said "Can I recommend something?" The man said "Sure, what do you want to recommend?" Lily said "Maybe you can give me the parrot for a little money and a trade. I can give you my coins and my teddy bear. He is very soft and cuddly. He can keep you company when you are lonely."
The man looked at Lily and her teddy bear. He saw that she really loved the parrot. He said "That is a very kind offer, Lily. But I don't think it is fair. The parrot is worth much more than your coins and your teddy bear. How about this? I will give you a discount on the parrot. You can pay me half of the money now and half later. And you can keep your teddy bear. He is your friend too."
Lily was happy. She said "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are very nice. I will pay you the rest of the money soon. I promise." The man said "You're welcome, Lily. I hope you and the parrot will be very happy together. He is a very fancy bird. You need to take good care of him. Give him food and water and toys and love."
Lily nodded. She said "I will, I will, I will. He is my fancy friend. I will give him everything he needs." The man gave Lily the cage with the parrot. Lily said goodbye to the man and the other birds. She took the cage and her teddy bear and went home with her mom. She was very excited to show her dad and her brother her new friend. She said to the parrot "What is your name?" The parrot said "My name is Pepe. Pepe the parrot. And you are Lily. Lily the lovely. We are friends." Lily said "Yes, we are friends. Pepe and Lily. Lily and Pepe. The best friends ever." And they were.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy castle. They had many knights, horses and dragons. They liked to make up stories about the castle and the king.
One day, they decided to have a big battle. Ben was the king of the castle and Lily was the queen of the dragons. They made loud noises and moved their toys around.
"Roar! I am the queen of the dragons and I want your castle!" Lily said.
"No! I am the king of the castle and I will not give it to you!" Ben said.
They fought and fought until they knocked over the castle and some of the toys broke. They both felt sad and angry.
"Look what you did! You broke my castle and my knights!" Ben said.
"Well, you broke my dragons and my horses!" Lily said.
They started to cry and shout at each other. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong.
"Ben, Lily, what is going on here? Why are you crying and shouting?" mom asked.
They told mom what happened and how they had a big battle. Mom looked at the mess and the broken toys.
"Oh, Ben, Lily, I'm sorry that your toys are broken. But you know, fighting is not a good way to play. You should try to share and settle your problems with words, not with toys. Fighting can hurt you and your toys and your feelings. Do you understand?" mom said.
Ben and Lily nodded. They felt sorry for fighting and breaking their toys. They also felt sorry for hurting each other's feelings.
"Mom, we're sorry. We didn't mean to fight and break our toys. We just wanted to have fun. But we got too carried away. Can we fix our toys and play nicely?" Ben said.
"Mom, we're sorry. We love our toys and we love each other. We don't want to fight anymore. Can we hug and say sorry?" Lily said.
Mom smiled and hugged them. She helped them fix their toys and clean up the mess.
"That's very good, Ben and Lily. I'm proud of you for saying sorry and making up. You are both very tough and brave, but you are also very kind and gentle. "Don't be afraid," Ben said. "We are friendly. Do you want to play with us?"

They took the penguin by the flippers and led him to the snowman. They introduced him to the snowman and gave him a hat and a scarf too. They made him feel welcome.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they find a big piano in the corner. It is black and shiny and has many keys.
"Look, Lily, a piano!" Tom says. "Can we play with it?"
"OK, Tom, but be careful. It is very big and heavy," Lily says.
They run to the piano and start to press the keys. Some keys make high sounds and some keys make low sounds. They try to match the sounds with their voices.
"La, la, la!" Tom sings, pressing a high key.
"Ba, ba, ba!" Lily sings, pressing a low key.
They giggle and have fun. But then they smell something bad. It is coming from the piano.
"Yuck, what is that?" Tom asks, holding his nose.
"Let's see," Lily says, opening the lid of the piano.
They see a smelly sock inside the piano. It is old and dirty and has holes.
"Ew, a sock!" Tom says. "Who put it there?"
"Maybe it is Dad's sock. He plays the piano sometimes," Lily says.
They take out the sock and throw it in the trash. Then they close the lid and keep playing.
"Next time, we will check the piano before we play," Tom says.
"Yes, and we will tell Dad to wash his socks," Lily says.
They laugh and match the sounds again. They like the piano, but not the sock.

The moral of the story is simple: if something looks bad, it's probably not good for you. It's important to always make wise decisions.

One day, while he was playing in the park, he saw a door with a knob on it. He wondered what was behind the door, but it was too hard for him to open.
He asked a grownup what was behind the door. The grownup said, "I'm sorry but I can't open it for you, Larry. It's too hard for you."
Larry was very sad. Then, out of nowhere, he heard a gentle voice say, "You can do it Larry! Pull the knob." Larry was surprised. He looked around but he couldn't find who said it.
Just then, the grownup said, "I'm not sure what's behind the door, but I recommend you give it a try. Pull the knob slowly, but don't be too harsh."
So Larry very slowly pulled the knob and - to his great surprise - the door opened! Behind the door there was a beautiful playground, just like the grownup said. Larry was so happy!
He thanked the grownup and ran off to explore the playground. Larry had a wonderful time playing and having lots of fun.

Lila and Ben were friends who lived in a hut near the forest. They liked to play and explore together, but sometimes they argued over toys and food. One day, they found a big basket of apples in the forest. They were very happy and wanted to take them home.
"Let's share the apples," Lila said. "You can have half and I can have half."
"No, I want more apples," Ben said. "I found them first. You can have only one."
"That's not fair," Lila said. "You are not a good friend. I don't want to play with you anymore."
Lila ran away, crying. Ben took the basket and went back to the hut. He ate some apples, but he felt lonely and sad. He missed Lila and wished he had been nicer to her.
Meanwhile, Lila met a fox in the forest. The fox was hungry and saw the apple in Lila's hand. He smiled and said, "Hello, little girl. What a nice apple you have. Can I have a bite?"
Lila was scared of the fox, but she remembered what her mother had taught her. She said, "No, thank you. This is my apple. But I can give you something else. I have some bread and cheese in my bag. You can have them if you are hungry."
The fox was surprised and touched by Lila's kindness. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very generous and good. You have a big heart. I will not hurt you. I will be your friend."
Lila and the fox shared the bread and cheese. They talked and laughed and had fun. Lila felt happy and forgot about Ben and the apples.
Later, Lila and the fox went back to the hut. They saw Ben sitting outside, looking sad and bored. He had eaten all the apples, but he still felt hungry and sick. He saw Lila and the fox and felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "Lila, I'm sorry. I was mean and greedy. I should have shared the apples with you. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends again?"
Lila smiled and said, "Of course, Ben. I forgive you. We can be friends again. But you have to learn to care for others and not only for yourself. Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy. Look, I have a new friend. This is the fox. He was hungry and I gave him some food. He is very nice and friendly. He can be our friend too."
Ben was happy and grateful. He said, "Thank you, Lila. You are a good friend. And hello, fox. You are welcome to our hut. Can we play together?"
Lila, Ben, and the fox hugged and played together. They learned to care for each other and share what they had. They lived happily in the hut near the forest.
The end.

Once upon a time there was a small ant and it was looking for something to eat. Suddenly it saw something shining in the distance. It was a shiny, red apple! 
The ant was so excited and scurried towards the red apple. But before it could reach the apple, it noticed a big sign ahead. It read "DO NOT TOUCH - STAY AWAY." The ants knew it had to obey the sign, so it stayed away.
Just then another ant came along and was about to take the apple and ignore the sign. The first ant quickly stopped it and said, “We must obey the sign and not take the apple!”
The other ant listened and for the first time it thought about why the sign was there. It thought that if it ignored the sign, it might be in trouble. So it heeded the advice of the first ant and stayed away from the apple.
The moral of the story is when we see a sign, it's important to listen and obey. The ants showed us if we ignore signs, we can be in trouble.

They went closer to the noise. They saw a big box. The box was making the noise. The squirrel was brave and jumped on the box. The box stopped making the noise. The squirrel and his friends were not scared anymore. They found out the box was just a toy. They played with the toy and had more fun than ever.

Lily liked to write poems. She wrote them on paper with her crayons. She wrote about her toys, her cat, and her mom. She was very proud of her poems.
One day, she wanted to show her poems to her dad. He was in the kitchen, making dinner. She ran to him with her paper and said, "Dad, dad, look at my poems!"
Her dad smiled and said, "Wow, Lily, these are very nice poems. You are very smart and creative. Can I read them?"
Lily nodded and gave him the paper. Her dad took it and started to read. He said, "This one is about your teddy bear. It says, 'I love my teddy bear. He is soft and brown. He hugs me when I sleep. He is my best friend.' That is very sweet, Lily."
Lily beamed and said, "Thank you, dad. Do you like the next one?"
Her dad said, "Yes, let me see. This one is about your cat. It says, 'My cat is funny. He likes to play with yarn. He chases mice and birds. He purrs when I pet him.' That is very cute, Lily."
Lily clapped and said, "Thank you, dad. Do you like the last one?"
Her dad said, "Yes, of course. This one is about your mom. It says, 'My mom is beautiful. She has long hair and blue eyes. She sings to me and reads to me. She loves me very much.' That is very lovely, Lily."
Lily hugged her dad and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you very much, too."
Her dad hugged her back and said, "I love you, too, Lily. You are a very good poet. Can I keep your poems?"
Lily said, "Yes, dad. You can keep them. But be careful. Don't burn them."
Her dad said, "Don't worry, Lily. I won't burn them. I will put them on the fridge, so everyone can see them."
Lily said, "Okay, dad. That is a good idea. But don't put them near the stove. The stove is hot. It can burn things."
Her dad said, "Okay, Lily. I won't put them near the stove. I will put them on the other side of the fridge. That is safe."
Lily said, "Okay, dad. Thank you for reading my poems. You are the best dad ever."
Her dad said, "You are welcome, Lily. And you are the best poet ever."
They smiled and kissed. Then they went to the table to eat dinner. Lily was happy. Her dad was happy. They both loved poems. And they both loved each other.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They liked to run and jump and throw a ball for Spot to catch. Spot was very fast and smart and loved to play with them.
One day, they saw some ducks by the pond. The ducks were swimming and quacking and eating bread that someone had thrown for them. Lily and Ben wanted to see the ducks up close, so they walked slowly and quietly towards them.
"Look, Ben, the ducks have a trail of babies behind them!" Lily whispered, pointing at the fluffy ducklings. "They are so cute and tiny!"
"Can we touch them?" Ben asked, reaching out his hand.
"Shh, no, we have to be careful. They might be scared of us," Lily said.
But it was too late. Spot saw the ducks and ran towards them, barking loudly. The ducks were very alert and saw Spot coming. They quickly scattered in different directions, leaving the pond and flying away. The ducklings followed their mothers, but some of them got lost and confused.
"Spot, no, bad dog!" Lily and Ben shouted, running after Spot. They tried to catch him and stop him from chasing the ducks, but he was too fast and excited.
The ducks were gone, and so was the bread. Lily and Ben felt sad and sorry. They wished they had not scared the ducks away. They hoped the ducks and their babies would come back soon. They hugged Spot and told him to be more gentle and quiet next time. They decided to go home and have a snack. Maybe they could come back another day and see the ducks again.

Sara is sad and angry. She says, "That is not nice, Tom. You are mean. You hurt the elephant and me. You should say sorry and finish your mouse." She picks up her elephant and hugs it. She does not want to play with Tom anymore.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Anna and Peter. It was a bright, sunny day and they were playing in the park.
Suddenly, Anna saw a swan by the pond. "Look, Peter!" Anna pointed to the swan.
"What is it?" asked Peter in wonder.
"It's a swan!", Anna said. "Let's go closer!"
So they went over to the swan. It was very cold by the pond but the swan didn't seem to mind. Anna and Peter stared in awe.

"Look, Lily, I made a big tower!" Tom said, showing his sister his creation. "It is very tall and strong."
Lily smiled and clapped her hands. "That is a good tower, Tom. But I made a better bridge. It is very long and thin. It can go over the water and the cars can drive on it."
Tom looked at Lily's bridge and nodded. "That is a good bridge, Lily. But can it hold my tower? Let me try to put it on your bridge."
Lily shook her head. "No, Tom, don't do that. Your tower is too heavy for my bridge. It will break it and make a mess."
But Tom did not listen. He picked up his tower and tried to balance it on Lily's bridge. But the bridge was too thin and the tower was too heavy. The bridge snapped and the tower fell down. The blocks scattered all over the floor.
"Tom, you broke my bridge!" Lily cried, feeling sad and angry. "That was not nice. You should say sorry."
Tom felt sorry too. He saw that Lily was upset and that he had ruined their game. He did not mean to break her bridge. He wanted to make her happy.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to break your bridge. I was just curious. Can we build it again?" Tom said, looking at Lily with a sorry face.
Lily looked at Tom and saw that he was sorry. She knew that he was her brother and that he loved her. She decided to forgive him.
"Okay, Tom. I forgive you. But next time, please ask me before you touch my things. And let's clean up this mess before dinner. Mom will be mad if she sees it." Lily said, giving Tom a hug.
Tom hugged Lily back. "Okay, Lily. I will ask you next time. And let's clean up together. Mom will be happy if she sees it. And maybe she will make us our favorite dinner. I hope it is pizza."
Lily and Tom smiled and started to pick up the blocks. They put them back in the box and made their room tidy. They were happy to play together and to have each other. They hoped that mom would make them pizza for dinner. They loved pizza.

"Hello, mug," she said louder. "Do you like to sing?"

"I wanted to sing to the mug, but the mug did not talk to me," Lily said.
Her mom smiled and hugged her.
"Lily, mugs are not alive. They cannot talk or sing. They are for drinking," her mom explained.
"Really?" Lily asked.
"Yes, really. But you know who can talk and sing with you? Me. And dad. And your toys. And your friends. Do you want to sing with me?" her mom asked.
Lily nodded and smiled. She wiped her tears and hugged her mom.
"Yes, please. I love to sing with you," she said.
They picked up the mug and filled it with water. They pretended it was tea. They sang a song about tea and cats and mugs. They had fun. Lily learned that mugs are not interesting, but singing with mom is.

Sue thanked Tim and Spot for their help. They all walked back on the trail together, and Sue took Fluffy home. Tim and Spot went back to their walk, happy that they had made a new friend and helped her find her cat.

One day, a hairy bear was looking for food in the forest. He was very hungry and wanted to find some honey or berries. He saw a big cave and thought there might be something good inside. He walked to the cave and sniffed the air.
"Hello, is anyone there?" he asked in a loud voice.
But he heard no answer. He decided to go inside and see for himself. He did not know that the cave belonged to a lion, who was sleeping in the dark.
The bear entered the cave and saw a pile of bones and fur. He thought they were leftovers from the lion's meal. He picked up a bone and started to bite it. It was hard and dry, but he was too hungry to care.
Suddenly, he heard a roar behind him. It was the lion, who had woken up and saw the bear eating his bone. He was very angry and wanted to chase the bear away.
"Hey, that's mine! Get out of my cave!" he shouted.
The bear was scared and dropped the bone. He turned around and saw the lion's big teeth and claws. He knew he had to run fast or he would be in trouble.
"Sorry, I did not know. I was just hungry. Please don't bite me!" he said.
He ran out of the cave and back to the forest. He learned his lesson and never went to the lion's cave again. He looked for food somewhere else, where it was safe and no one would bite him.

Tom wanted to see the elephant's nose up close. He went closer to the cage and reached out his hand. He poked the elephant's nose with his finger.
The elephant felt the poke and lifted its nose. It looked at Tom with its small eyes. It was confused. Why did this little human poke its nose? It did not like it. It made a loud noise and sprayed some water at Tom.
Tom was wet and scared. He ran back to Mom and Dad. Lily laughed. She said, "That was silly, Tom. You should not poke the elephant's nose. It does not like it."
Mom and Dad hugged Tom and dried him with a towel. They said, "It's okay, Tom. The elephant was just surprised. You should be careful and respectful with the animals. They have feelings too."
Tom nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, elephant. I did not mean to make you angry. You have a very cool nose."
The elephant heard Tom and calmed down. It waved its nose at Tom and made a soft noise. It was not angry anymore. It was curious.
Tom and Lily smiled. They waved back at the elephant and said, "Bye, elephant. You are very cool too."

Anna liked to feed the pigeons in the park. She had a bag of bread crumbs that she broke into small pieces. She threw them on the ground and watched the pigeons come and eat. She liked their soft feathers and their cooing sounds.
One day, she saw a big pigeon with a shiny ring on its leg. It looked different from the other pigeons. It had a red bandana around its neck and a small backpack on its back. Anna was curious. She threw a bread crumb near the big pigeon and called, "Come here, pretty pigeon!"
The big pigeon looked at Anna and flew to her. It landed on her shoulder and nuzzled her cheek. Anna giggled and stroked its feathers. She opened the backpack and found a note inside. It said, "Hello, Anna. I am a special pigeon. I work for a man who sends messages with me. He told me to find you and give you this note. He said you are a good girl and he loves you very much. He is your daddy. He is far away, but he will come back soon. He said to be obedient and listen to your mommy. He said to feed me well and keep me safe. He said he will send me again with another note. He said to look for the ring on my leg. That is how you know it is me. Love, Daddy."
Anna was happy and surprised. She hugged the big pigeon and said, "Thank you, pretty pigeon! You are a special pigeon! You brought me a message from my daddy! I love you and I love my daddy! I will be obedient and listen to my mommy. I will feed you well and keep you safe. I will look for the ring on your leg. I will wait for your next message. You are my friend!"
The big pigeon cooed and nodded. It ate some more bread crumbs and drank some water from a fountain. It stayed with Anna for a while, then flew away. Anna waved goodbye and smiled. She put the note in her pocket and ran to her mommy. She told her everything. Her mommy was happy and proud. She hugged Anna and said, "You are a lucky girl, Anna. You have a special pigeon and a brave daddy. He is doing a very important job. He will come back soon. He loves you very much. So do I."
Anna was happy. She loved her mommy and her daddy and her special pigeon. She looked at the sky and hoped to see the big pigeon again. She knew he would come back. She knew he would bring her another message. She knew he would increase her joy.

The leopard saw its chance. It jumped out of the cage and ran towards the boys. It was fast and angry.
Tim and Sam were scared. They did not know what to do. They panicked. They screamed and ran away.
"Help, help, a leopard is chasing us!" they shouted.
Some people in the park heard them and saw the leopard. They were also scared. They called the police and the zoo.
The police and the zoo came quickly. They had nets and guns. They caught the leopard and put it back in the cage. They thanked the truck driver for bringing the leopard to the zoo. They scolded him for being careless.
They also talked to Tim and Sam. They told them they were brave and lucky. They told them not to go near wild animals again. They told them to be more careful.
Tim and Sam nodded. They were sorry and relieved. They hugged each other and their mom. They learned a lesson. They never played near leopards again.

"If you stay flexible and do your best, you can do anything!"
The beetle smiled, thanked the wise lizard and continued his journey.
The beetle explored a lot and enjoyed the peace and quiet of his adventures. Everywhere he went, he tried to stay flexible and do his best.
One day, he came across a mud puddle in the middle of a clearing. He hopped in and soon found himself stuck in the mud! He tried to move and wriggled his body in all directions, but the harder he tried, the deeper he sunk.

The beetle felt relieved, and grateful for the wise words of the lizard. From that day forward, he remembered the lesson he had learnt. No matter how stuck he felt, if he stayed flexible and did his best, he could reach any goal.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom says. He picks up a tube with a red liquid. "I wonder what it does."
"Let me see!" Ben says. He tries to grab the tube from Tom. "It's mine!"
"No, it's mine!" Tom says. He pulls the tube back. "You always want what I have!"
They tug and pull and yell. The tube slips from their hands and falls on the floor. It breaks and the red liquid spills everywhere. It makes a loud snap and a big smoke.
"Uh-oh," Tom and Ben say. They cough and cover their eyes.
Dad hears the noise and runs to the garage. He sees the mess and the smoke. He is angry and scared.
"What have you done?" he shouts. "This is not a toy! This is my lab! It has chemicals and experiments! It is dangerous!"
He picks up Tom and Ben and takes them outside. He puts them on the grass and checks if they are hurt.
"Are you okay?" he asks.
Tom and Ben nod. They are sorry and scared.
"We're sorry, Dad," they say. "We didn't know. We just wanted to play."
Dad hugs them and sighs. He is glad they are okay.
"I know, boys," he says. "But you have to be careful. You can't touch things you don't know. You could get hurt or break something. You have to ask me first."
Tom and Ben nod again. They understand.
"We will, Dad," they say. "We won't touch your lab again. We promise."
Dad smiles and kisses them.
"Good," he says. "Now let's go inside and clean up. And then we can read a book or play a game. Something safe and fun."
Tom and Ben smile and hug Dad. They are happy and love him.
They think his lab is cool, but also stupid. They don't want to play with it anymore. They have better things to do.

"Tom, we can't go in the mud," Lily said. "We will spoil our new shoes. Mom will be sad and angry."
Tom did not listen. He ran to the puddle and sprang in it. He laughed and shouted as he made big splashes. He did not care about his shoes.
Lily watched him and felt bad. She wanted to join him, but she also wanted to keep her shoes clean. She did not know what to do.
Then, Mom came out of the house. She saw Tom in the mud and Lily on the grass. She was not happy.
"Tom, what have you done?" Mom said. "You have spoiled your new shoes. They are all dirty and wet. How can you be so careless?"
Tom stopped laughing. He looked at his shoes and felt ashamed. He wished he had listened to Lily.
"I'm sorry, Mom," Tom said. "I was silly. I wanted to have fun, but I did not think about my shoes."
Mom sighed. She took Tom by the hand and brought him inside. She told him to take off his shoes and put them in the sink. She said he had to wash them and dry them. She also said he could not play outside for the rest of the day.
Lily followed them. She felt sorry for Tom, but she also felt proud. She had made the right choice. She had not spoiled her new shoes. She had obeyed Mom.
Mom smiled at Lily. She hugged her and praised her.
"Lily, you are a good girl," Mom said. "You have been careful and respectful. You have not spoiled your new shoes. You have made me happy."
Lily smiled back. She was happy too. She learned that it was better to be careful and respectful than to be careless and spoiled. She hoped Tom would learn too.

Anna loved to visit her grandma's farm. She liked to see the cows, the pigs, the chickens and the horses. She also liked to play with her cousin Ben, who lived on the farm. But sometimes, Ben was not very nice. He liked to pinch Anna when no one was looking. He thought it was funny, but Anna did not. It hurt and made her cry.
One day, Anna and Ben were feeding the chickens. Ben had a handful of corn and Anna had a bucket of water. Ben saw a big, brown chicken with a red comb. He thought it looked funny, so he pinched its tail. The chicken did not like that. It squawked and pecked Ben's hand. Ben dropped the corn and screamed. Anna saw what happened and felt sorry for Ben. She put down the bucket and ran to him.
"Are you okay, Ben?" she asked, looking at his hand. It was red and bleeding.
"No, it hurts!" Ben sobbed. "The chicken bit me!"
Anna hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. That was not nice of the chicken. But you know what? It was not nice of you to pinch it either. Pinching hurts, Ben. You should not pinch anyone, not even a chicken."
Ben looked at Anna and realized she was right. He remembered how he pinched her many times and made her cry. He felt bad and said, "You're right, Anna. I'm sorry. I should not pinch you or anyone. It's mean and wrong. Will you forgive me, Anna?"
Anna smiled and said, "Of course, Ben. I forgive you. You're my cousin and I love you. But please, don't pinch me again, okay?"
"Okay, Anna. I won't pinch you again. I love you too." Ben said. He hugged her back and said, "Thank you for being compassionate, Anna. You're very kind and sweet."
They heard their grandma calling them for lunch. They held hands and walked to the house. They decided to be nice to each other and to the animals from then on. They learned a lesson that day: pinching is not fun, it's hurtful. And being compassionate is better than being mean.

Two frogs were hopping down the road when they suddenly heard a loud noise. One of them asked the other, "What was that?” 
The other one replied, “I don't know, let's go find out!” 
They hopped down the road and saw a copper bag in the middle of the road. One of the frogs cried out, “Incredible! Let's go see it up close.”
The frogs hopped over to the bag and suddenly they heard the noise again. This time, they heard a voice say, “Freeze!” 
Both frogs paused, then the first frog said, “We'd better not, it's someone else's bag. That's not polite. We need to be respectful of other people's belongings.” 
The two frogs then hopped away and continued on their journey.
Moral: The moral of the story is to be respectful of other people's belongings and don't take what isn't yours.

Lucy planted the seed in the ground and watered it every day. Soon, a tiny green plant came up. Lucy was very happy. She talked to the plant and said, "Grow big and strong, little tomato plant!"
But one day, a big storm came and broke the little tomato plant. Lucy was sad. She wanted to restore the plant, so she asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lucy. We can fix it together."
They put a small stick next to the plant and tied it with a string. Lucy kept taking care of the plant with love. Soon, the little tomato plant grew big and strong. It made a big, red tomato just like Lucy wanted. Lucy was very happy and proud of her persistent work.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous tree. A little bird lived in the tree and loved to count the leaves every day! The bird had a silly idea - to use a napkin to count each and every leaf.
The bird flew to the ground and picked up a napkin. He flew back up to the tree and started counting. But when he tried to count them all, the napkin just couldn’t fit all the leaves!
The bird was frustrated and flew away from the tree, "This is impossible! How will I ever get to count all these leaves?"
Just then, an old wise owl appeared from behind the tree. "Listen, my young friend," said the old owl, "you can’t count everything in the world, some things can’t be counted. So enjoy the beauty of the leaves and don’t try to count them all. Life’s too short to count everything!"
The bird was enlightened by the owl’s wise words and flew away with a smile on his face. He enjoyed the beauty of the leaves without even trying to count them.
The moral of the story is that while counting is important, we should not forget to appreciate the beauty of things that cannot be counted.

A nice girl found Ollie and put him back with his family. The big boy felt bad for kicking Ollie. He said sorry to the small onion and his friends. The boy learned that it is not nice to hurt others. From that day on, he was kind to all the plants and bugs in the garden. And they all lived happily ever after.

"Oh, I see," Mia says. "But sparks can be dangerous, right?"

Tom and Mia watch the fire truck do its job. They are glad that no one is hurt. They are also glad that they have each other. They are good friends. They like to discuss things and learn new words.

"But I want to touch the moon. It looks so pretty." Lily says.
"Me too. Maybe the moon is fake. Maybe it is a big ball of light." Ben says.
"No, the moon is not fake. It is real. It is a big rock that goes around the earth. It makes light at night." Ben's mom says.
"How do you know, mom?" Ben asks.
"I know because I learned it in school. And because I saw it with a telescope. A telescope is a thing that makes things look bigger." Ben's mom says.
"Can we see the moon with a telescope, mom?" Lily asks.
"Maybe someday, honey. But for now, let's enjoy the swings. The swings are real and fun." Lily's mom says.
Lily and Ben nod. They go back to the swings. They swing high and low. They look at the moon. They feel happy.

Sam nods. He is sorry too. He says, "I'm sorry, Mia. You are right. The pepper is bad for me. It is only good for Mom. Next time, I will listen to you, OK?"
They smile at each other. They are still friends. They go back to the garden. They play with other things. They do not touch the peppers again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make different dishes with the pots and pans. Tom had a big spoon and Lily had a small spoon. They stirred and mixed and tasted their food.
"Look, I made soup!" Tom said, holding up his spoon. "It has carrots and peas and noodles. Do you want some?"
"Yes, please!" Lily said, bringing her spoon to her mouth. "Mmm, it's yummy! You are a good chef, Tom."
"Thank you, Lily. You are a good chef, too. What did you make?" Tom asked, looking at her pot.
"I made cake!" Lily said, smiling. "It has flour and sugar and eggs and chocolate. Do you want some?"
"Yes, please!" Tom said, eager to try her cake. He scooped some with his spoon and put it in his mouth. But it was not cake. It was sticky and gooey and bitter. Tom spit it out and made a face.
"Yuck! This is not cake, Lily. This is icky. What did you put in it?" Tom asked, wiping his tongue.
"I was creative!" Lily said, proud of her invention. "I put in ketchup and mustard and vinegar and salt. It's a new kind of cake. Don't you like it?"
"No, I don't like it, Lily. It's gross. You should not put those things in cake. You should stop being creative and follow the recipe." Tom said, shaking his head.
"But I like being creative, Tom. It's fun. You should try it, too. Maybe you will like it." Lily said, holding out her spoon.
"No, thank you, Lily. I like my soup. You can have your cake. But please, don't give it to anyone else. They might get sick." Tom said, moving his pot away from her.
"Okay, Tom. I won't give it to anyone else. But I still like my cake. It's special. And I like being creative. Maybe next time I will make something else." Lily said, taking another bite of her cake. She did not mind the taste. She liked being different.

The little red bear thought it was an adventure at first. He flew higher and higher until he eventually saw a storm brewing in the distance. He flew closer and saw lightning, thunder and dark clouds. Suddenly, he felt scared.
"It's time to go home," he thought. But he was too late. The storm was getting closer and it was too strong for the little bear to fight. He couldn't get back to his wrap. 
The little red bear was stuck! He sneezed and admitted his defeat. Eventually, the storm passed, but he was never able to return home. The little red bear was never seen again.

"No, it's mine!" Tim said. "Go away!"

"Let go!" Tim said. "You are mean!"
"No, you are mean!" Lily said. "You are selfish!"

"Ha ha, that's what you get!" Lily said. "The duck is mad at you!"
Tim felt hurt and angry. He picked up the stick and threw it at Lily. The stick hit Lily's head. Lily fell down and cried. She had blood on her face.

Lily was alone and hurt. She did not have the stick. She did not have Tim. She did not forgive Tim. She did not want to be his friend anymore.
The pond was quiet and sad. The fish and frogs and ducks did not like to see Tim and Lily fight. They wished they could be friends again. But they did not know how.
