One day, a man came to the hut. He had a big bag of shiny things. He said he wanted to buy the cow. He showed Tom and Lily the shiny things. He said they were gold and silver. He said they were very valuable. He said they could buy many things with them.
Tom and Lily liked the shiny things. They wanted to have them. They asked their mother and father if they could sell the cow. Their mother and father said no. They said the cow was more valuable than the shiny things. They said the cow gave them food and warmth. They said the shiny things were only pretty, but not useful. They said they loved the cow and would not trade her.
Tom and Lily were angry. They thought their mother and father were selfish. They thought they did not care about what they wanted. They thought they could have more fun with the shiny things. They decided to sneak out at night and sell the cow to the man.
They waited until their mother and father were asleep. They took the cow and the dog and went to find the man. They found him near the river. He was happy to see them. He gave them the bag of shiny things and took the cow. He said he would sell the cow to someone else for more money. He said he did not care about the cow. He said he only cared about himself.
Tom and Lily took the bag of shiny things and ran back to the hut. They hid the bag under their bed. They thought they were clever and rich. They did not notice that the dog was not with them. They did not hear the dog bark and cry as the man took him too. They did not see the man smile and say he would sell the dog to someone else for more money. They realized they had been selfish and foolish. They realized they had lost their friends and their food. They realized they had hurt their mother and father. They realized they had been tricked by the man. They realized the shiny things were not valuable at all.
They ran to their mother and father and told them what they had done. They said they were sorry and asked for forgiveness. They said they wanted to get the cow and the dog back. They said they did not care about the shiny things. They said they loved the cow and the dog and their mother and father.
Their mother and father were shocked and angry. They scolded Tom and Lily for being selfish and disobedient. They said they had put their family in danger and trouble. They said they had to learn their lesson and work hard to make up for their mistake. They said they did not know if they could find the cow and the dog again. They said they hoped the cow and the dog were safe and well.
They took the bag of shiny things and went to look for the man. They hoped to trade the shiny things for the cow and the dog. They hoped the man had not sold them yet. One day, he decided to make a basket of goodies for his mum as a special surprise. He decided to bake some cookies, a cake for his mum, and some other treats he knew she would love.
Once he had finished baking, he put the treats into a pretty basket and was about to take it to his mum when he saw his neighbour. His neighbour was poor and had nothing to eat.
The boy thought of how he could share his kind gesture with the neighbour. He gifted the attractive basket to the neighbour, telling him to share it with his family. The neighbour was extremely happy and thanked the boy.
The moral of this story is that it is important to be kind and generous to others, even if it is a simple act. Every act of kindness is special and can go a long way.

"The town is a big place with many people and houses and shops," Lily explains. "It is very interesting. My mom took me there once. Maybe we can sell our things there."
"OK, let's go to the town," Ben agrees. "But how do we get there?"
They look around and see a bus. The bus has a sign that says "Town". They run to the bus and get on. They give the driver two coins and find a seat.
The bus starts to move. Lily and Ben look out the window. They see many new things. They see cars and trees and animals and bridges. They see a big river and a big park. They see a tall tower and a big clock. They are very excited.
"Look, Ben, look!" Lily says. "This is the town. It is so interesting. Do you think we can sell our things here?"
"I don't know, Lily, I don't know," Ben says. "But I want to see more. This is fun."
They smile and hold their things. They are happy. They are going to the town.

"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom says. "What is its name?"
"I don't know," Lily says. "Let's ask Mom."
They run inside and find Mom in the kitchen. They show her the bird through the window.
"Mom, what is that bird?" Tom asks.
"That is a toucan," Mom says. "It lives in the rainforest and eats fruits and nuts."
"Can we feed it?" Lily asks.
"Sure, you can try," Mom says. "But be careful, it might be shy or scared."
She gives them some grapes and nuts and tells them to go outside. Tom and Lily go to the garden and approach the bird slowly. They hold out their hands with the food.
"Hello, toucan," Tom says. "We have some grapes and nuts for you. Do you want some?"
The toucan looks at them with its big eyes. It hops closer and sniffs the food. Then it picks a grape with its beak and eats it. It makes a happy sound.
"Yay, it likes it!" Lily says. "Here, have some more."
The toucan eats more grapes and nuts from their hands. It flaps its wings and bobs its head. Tom and Lily giggle and smile. They feel happy to feed the toucan and learn a new word. They are curious children.

Sam was really sad, but Mike was really happy. He was so excited to have won the race. He shouted, "I won the race. This is so amazing!"

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shiny things. One day, they found a big, bright gem. It was red and sparkly, like a star.
"Wow, look at this!" Anna said. "It is so pretty!"
"Let me see!" Ben said. He tried to grab the gem from Anna's hand.
"No, it is mine!" Anna said. She held the gem tight. "I found it first!"
They started to pull and tug on the gem. They were both angry and loud.
A man was walking by. He heard the noise and saw the gem. He smiled and came closer.
"Hello, children," he said. "What do you have there?"
Anna and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at the man. He was tall and wore a hat and a coat. He had a bag on his shoulder.
"It is a gem," Anna said. "We found it in the sand."
"It is very beautiful," the man said. "Do you know what it is?"
Anna and Ben shook their heads.
"It is a ruby," the man said. "It is very rare and valuable. Do you want to see something amazing?"
Anna and Ben nodded.
The man opened his bag. He took out a big book. He opened it and showed them a page. It had a picture of a crown. It was gold and had many gems on it. One of them was a ruby, just like theirs.
"This is the crown of a king," the man said. "He lived in a distant land, long ago. He wore this crown on his head. He had many rubies like yours. He liked to display them and show off his power."
Anna and Ben looked at the picture. They were amazed. They had never seen anything like it.
"Can we keep our ruby?" Anna asked.
"Of course you can," the man said. "It is yours. You found it. But you have to share it. It is too precious to fight over. Can you do that?"
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for being mean. They nodded.
"Yes, we can," Ben said.
"Good," the man said. He smiled and closed his book. He put it back in his bag. He stood up and tipped his hat. "Have fun, children. And take good care of your ruby. It is a special gem."
He walked away. Anna and Ben watched him go. They held the ruby together. They felt happy and proud. They decided to display it in their room, where they could see it every day. "Yes, Ben, I want to help him. Let's give him a bath. Maybe he will be happy then." Anna says.
Anna and Ben go to the pond. They are careful not to scare the duck. They talk to him softly and gently. They splash some water on him. They rub his feathers with their hands. They wash away the dirt and the hurt. The duck quacks and flaps his wings. He looks clean and happy.
"Look, Anna, the duck is clean and happy. He is not dirty and sad anymore. He likes us. We are his friends." Ben says.
"Yes, Ben, the duck is clean and happy. We are his friends. We helped him. We gave him a bath. He likes us." Anna says.
